Member.Name: SetCustomCheckResult
Member.Description: Sets whether to report results from your SOLIDWORKS Design Check Custom Check validation macro as passed or failed.

Parameter.Name: vbIsCheckPassed
Parameter.Description: True to add your Custom Check to the Passed Checks results list and ignore sfArrayFailedItems, false to add your Custom Check to the Failed Checks results list and list sfArrayFailedItems

Parameter.Name: sfArrayFailedItems
Parameter.Description: Array of strings of failed items found by your SOLIDWORKS Design Checker Custom Check validation macro; array name must be enclosed within parentheses (see Example and Remarks)

Member.Returns:
One of the following <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.dsgnchk.dsgnchkError_e">dsgnchkError_e</see> enumerators:
0 = dsgnchkNOErr 8 = dsgnchkInvalidCallToAPI
Member.Remarks:
Create a Custom Check validation macro. Guidelines for creating this macro appear below. Additionally an example is linked to this topic that you can examine and test. Register the Custom Check macro with SOLIDWORKS Design Checker. See the SOLIDWORKS SOLIDWORKS Design Checker Help for details on how to register the macro. The macro is stored with the standards file. Check the document in SOLIDWORKS Design Checker using the standards file in which the Custom Check validation macro is stored. Guidelines for creating a Custom Check validation macro:
You can record the macro using a SOLIDWORKS macro recorder. You can have multiple procedures in your Custom Check validation macro. Only a zero-argument Custom Check procedure is supported. If your Custom Check validation macro returns true, then your Custom Check validation macro passed; if your Custom Check validation macro returns false, then your Custom Check validation macro failed. If you provide fully qualified names of the failed items, then these items can be shown highlighted when a user selects them in the results list by using a double array of strings with these characteristics:
Array has two dimensions. Upper dimension contains the size (number) of failed items ,and the lower dimension has a size of 2.For example:' EnumeratorsDim FailedItemsArr As StringReDim FailedItemsArr(0 To 2, 0 To 1) As String' Enumerators
0 To 2: reflects the upper dimension size (3) and means that there are 3 failures in the result. 0 To 1: reflects the lower dimension size (2) means that the lower dimension size is 2. It is not mandatory for the array to start with 0; the array can start with any dimension; e.g., (1 To 10) or (11 To 15) or (-5 To -2), etc. In the (X,0) positions of the array, you must pass the failed item's name. In the (X,1) positions of the array, you must pass the failed item's type string as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see>.For example:' DimensionFailedItemsArr(0, 0) = "RD2@Drawing View2"FailedItemsArr(0, 1) = "DIMENSION"FailedItemsArr(1, 0) = "RD1@Drawing View4"FailedItemsArr(1, 1) = "DIMENSION"FailedItemsArr(2, 0) = "My Failed Item 3"FailedItemsArr(2, 1) = "Annotation"' Dimension
Having a two-dimensional array or filling (X,1) positions is not mandatory. You can have a single-dimensional array and fill it with strings (i.e., failed entity names). If the type of failed entity is not the specified entity, then it is not shown as selected. If the type of failed entity is not specified or is incorrect, then it is ignored.

Member.Name: CalloutString
Member.Description: Gets or sets the hole callout string for this Advanced Hole element.
Member.Returns: Hole callout string (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedHoleFeatureData.CustomizeCallout">IAdvancedHoleFeatureData::CustomizeCallout</see> is set to true. The hole callout string is formatted as follows: LibraryName-SymbolName> callout_var1> callout_var2>... callout_varn> where:
LibraryName and SymbolName are defined in c:\ProgramData\SolidWorks\SolidWorks 20nn\lang\english\gtol.sym. callout_var1-n are callout variables. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetCalloutVariableString">IModelDocExtension::GetCalloutVariableString</see> to get the strings for hole callout variables defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swCalloutVariable_e">swCalloutVariable_e</see>. You can also find the hole callout variable strings by clicking Hole Callout > Callout Variables in the Advanced Hole PropertyManager. Note: You must include the right- and left-angle brackets and the hyphens when setting the elements of this property string: " "

Member.Name: LoadCriteria
Member.Description: Loads the specified query file and makes it the current advanced component selection criteria list.

Parameter.Name: CriteriaFileName
Parameter.Description: Path and filename of query file (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if query file loads, false if not
Member.Remarks:
Specify CriteriaFileName with either a *.xml file or a legacy *.sqy file. To create a *.xml query file, you can either:
Use the Advanced Component Selection dialog (Standard toolbar > Advanced Select) to export a query file in XML format. - or -
Open a txt file in Notepad and add content as follows:
Replace the attribute values in the and elements as required. Refer to the Assemblies > Basic Component Operations > Selecting Components > Advanced Component Selection > Search Criteria for Advanced Component Selection topic in the SOLIDWORKS help to see all the options for populating the Category (Category1 in the dialog), SubCategory (Category2 in the dialog), Condition, and Value attributes. In Favourites_Index specifies where the query appears at the end of the Select toolbar. This attribute corresponds to the row number in the Manage Searches tab of the dialog. In Name specifies "And" (default) or "Or" to indicate whether to logically AND or OR multiple Boolean elements in the Query element. This attribute corresponds to the And/Or column in the dialog. Add more and elements as needed to further constrain your query. Save the query file with a .xml extension. After calling this method, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedSelectionCriteria.Select">IAdvancedSelectionCriteria::Select</see> to select the assembly components that satisfy the query criteria.

Member.Name: SaveCriteria
Member.Description: Saves the current query to the specified XML file.

Parameter.Name: CriteriaFileName
Parameter.Description: Path and filename (*.xml) to which to save the current query

Member.Returns: True if current query is saved successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks: Call this method after <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedSelectionCriteria.AddItem2">adding</see> criteria to the current advanced component selection criteria list. As of SOLIDWORKS 2021, you can save queries only in XML format. As is done using the Advanced Component Selection dialog (Standard toolbar > Advanced Select), this method creates a query file in XML format with one or more and elements. Each element represents a particular search by Category (Category1 in the user interface) and SubCategory (Category2 in the user interface) to satisfy a Condition expression: ?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

Member.Remarks:
This method now supports all annotation types. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetType">IAnnotation::GetType</see> to determine the type of annotation. The array returned by this function may contain one or more objects of varying type. To determine the corresponding object type in the IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntites2 array, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityTypes">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityTypes</see>. COM applications can use QueryInterface to obtain the specific object from the LPUNKNOWN pointer.
Object Type Object Returned
swSelFACES <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">IFace2</see>
swSelEDGES <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">IEdge</see>
swSelVERTICES <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IVertex">IVertex</see>
swSelSKETCHSEGS <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see>
swSelSKETCHPOINTS <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchPoint">ISketchPoint</see>
swSelNOTHING NULL (annotation is dangling or unsupported)
You can associate annotations with some items not listed in the previous table (for example, origins). If this annotation is attached to one or more of those entities, then SOLIDWORKS returns a corresponding NULL in one of the array positions and IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityTypes indicates the unsupported entity by returning a corresponding swSelNOTHING value. COM applications that call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityCount2">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityCount2</see> include the NULL value in the total count of associated entities. Likewise, if an annotation has become disassociated from its geometry, then SOLIDWORKS returns a corresponding NULL in one of the array positions and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityTypes">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityTypes</see> indicates the dangling item by returning a corresponding swSelNOTHING value. If this annotation is not associated with any geometry (for example, a note without a leaderline), then SOLIDWORKS returns an empty array.

If this annotation is attached to one or more entities not listed in swSelectType_e, then this method and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.IGetAttachedEntityTypes">IAnnotation::IGetAttachedEntityTypes</see> return swSelNOTHING in a position in the array corresponding to the unlisted item. IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntities3 indicates an unsupported entity by returning a null value in the position in the array corresponding to the unsupported entity. COM applications that call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityCount3">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityCount3</see> include the null value in the total count of associated entities. If an annotation is disassociated from its geometry (i.e., dangling), then IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntities3 returns a null value in the position in the array corresponding to the dangling item, and this method returns swSelNOTHING in the position in the array corresponding to the dangling item. NOTE: If this annotation is not associated with any geometry, then this method and IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntities3 return empty arrays.

Member.Name: GetLeaderPointsAtIndex
Member.Description: Gets coordinate information about a specified leader on this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of leader within this annotation (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Array of objects (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Get Display Dimensions, GTols, and Surface-finish Symbols

Member.Remarks:
The index value is 0-based. Therefore, a valid index value is >= 0 Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderCount">IAnnotation::GetLeaderCount</see> to find out how many leaders are on this annotation. If the index value is invalid in Visual Basic for Applications (VBA), SOLIDWORKS returns an empty SafeArray or S_false. You must determine the number of points in the leader to use the data returned by this method. The number of points is a function of the number of segments in the leader. There can be one or two segments in a leader line, depending on whether or not it is a straight, bent, or underlined leader. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderStyle">IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle</see>to determine the number of points in the leader.
If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swNO_LEADER, then the number of points = 0. If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swSTRAIGHT and swUNDERLINED then the numberof points = 2. If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swBENT, then the number of points = 3. Additionally, for the COM interface, you must determine the number of points to allocate the appropriate size array for the return value. The number of points must also be passed to the method to help prevent overwrite problems if you have not allocated an array that is the correct size. If the number of points passed does not match what is found, SOLIDWORKS does not return any point information and returns S_false. The format of the return array is:
retval[0] = X-coordinate of first leader point retval[1] = Y-coordinate of first leader point retval[2] = Z-coordinate of first leader point
retval[3] = X-coordinate of second leader point retval[4] = Y-coordinate of second leader point retval[5] = Z-coordinate of second leader point
retval[6] = X-coordinate of third leader point retval[7] = Y-coordinate of third leader point retval[8] = Z-coordinate of third leader point You cannot directly set the leader coordinate information. The leader coordinates are computed based on the annotations text and attachment points. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetPosition">IAnnotation::GetPosition</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetPosition">IAnnotation::SetPosition</see> to get and set the text point.

Member.Name: GetPosition
Member.Description: Gets the position of this annotation.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The retval is an array of 3 doubles, the x, y, z origin of the annotation. If this method is not successful in retrieving the position of the annotation in Visual Basic for Applications (VBA), then the VARIANT SafeArray is empty (OLE Automation only), or the status value is S_false (COM only). Make sure that you check this value before using the returned position. The following table lists the types of annotations that this method supports and the position of the x, y, z origin. In a drawing, the x, y, z origin is relative to the origin of the drawing sheet (the lower-left corner of the sheet).
Type of Annotation Position of XYZ Origin
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Feature Symbols</see> Point where leader hits symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Target Symbols</see> Centerpoint of the circle that is attached to the leader
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display Dimensions</see> Point of leader attachment centered on a text box border / center point of bottom border of text box
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerances</see> Upper-left corner of the symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Notes</see> Upper-left corner of the text box
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish Symbols</see> Lower-left point of symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation">Table Annotation</see> Position of x,y,z determined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.AnchorType">ITableAnnotation::AnchorType</see>
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld Symbols</see> Left endpoint of the main horizontal line in the symbol
If you use this method on any other types of annotations, SOLIDWORKS takes no action and returns false.

The behavior of this method differs depending on the type of annotation.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum target</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum feature symbols</see>These symbols always use the document default setting for dimension text format todisplay text within the symbol. The index argument is not used and should be setto 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerance</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">display dimensions</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">simple notes</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">surface finish</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">weld symbols</see>These symbols can either use the document default setting to display text withinthe symbol (dimension text setting for the geometric tolerance symbols and displaydimensions, or note text setting for notes) or they can use a local format. The indexargument is not used and should be set to 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">Blocks</see> (and compound notes for documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier)These symbols might contain several different pieces of text; each piece can usethe document default setting for notes or a local format. The index argument identifiesthe text. The index value is 0-based. If the index value is invalid, then this methodreturns a Nothing or null pointer. To get the number of text or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat">ITextFormat</see> objects, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormatCount">IAnnotation::GetTextFormatCount</see>. Rich text formatIf a note contains embedded rich text information in the string, then this method returnsa text format that does not necessarily reflect what is displayed on the screen forthat note. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.HasMultipleFonts">INote::HasMultipleFonts</see> to determine if the note contains embeddedrich text information. ITextFormat is returned if it is for a local setting or for the documentdefault setting. To determine whether or not this annotation is using the documentdefault settings for text format, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetUseDocTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetUseDocTextFormat</see>. To set thetext format information, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see>.

Member.Name: GetTextFormatCount
Member.Description: Gets the number of text formats for this annotation.
Member.Returns: Number of text formats
Member.Remarks: The value returned by this method is intended to be used with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetUseDocTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetUseDocTextFormat</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetTextFormat</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.IGetTextFormat">IAnnotation::IGetTextFormat</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.ISetTextFormat">IAnnotation::ISetTextFormat</see>. The index input argument for these methods must be less than the number returned by this method. This value is not necessarily the same as the number of text objects within a symbol. For example, there are multiple text objects in a geometric tolerance symbol, but they all share the same text format so SOLIDWORKS returns 1. In fact, for all of the annotations except blocks (and compound notes in documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier), this method should return 1. For blocks and compound notes, each piece of text within the symbol has its own text format, so the return value should match the number of TextFormat objects.

Member.Name: GetUseDocTextFormat
Member.Description: Gets whether SOLIDWORKS is currently using the document default text format setting for this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Number indicating which text within this annotation to check (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if the setting is a document default setting, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The behavior of this method differs slightly depending on the type of annotation.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Target</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Feature</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish</see> SymbolsThese symbols always use the document default setting for dimension text format of the text objects within the symbol. Therefore, this method always returns True for these annotation types. The index argument is not used and should be set to 0.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerance</see> Symbols, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display Dimensions</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Simple Notes</see>These symbols can use the document default setting to display all of the text objects within the symbol (dimension text setting for the geometric tolerance symbols and display dimensions, or note text setting for notes), in which case this method returns True. They can also use a local format, in which case this method returns false. The index argument is not used and should be set to 0.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">Blocks</see> (and compound notes created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier)These symbols can contain several different pieces of text, each individually using the document default setting for notes or a local format. The index argument identifies the text. The index value is 0-based. If the index value is invalid, this method returns True. To get the number of text or text format objects, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormatCount">IAnnotation::GetTextFormatCount</see>. To get the text format object for this annotation, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetTextFormat</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.IGetTextFormat">IAnnotation::IGetTextFormat</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.ISetTextFormat">IAnnotation::ISetTextFormat</see>.

Member.Name: GetVisualProperties
Member.Description: Gets the visual properties of this annotation.
Member.Returns: Array of five longs or five integers (see Long vs. Integer and see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return value is the following array:
[color, style, width, layerID, layerOverride ] where:
color COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value can be 0 or -1 for default color.
style Line style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see>.
width Line width as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
layerID Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The Layer object can be obtainedby passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
layerOverride Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overriddenwith respect to the layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specificproperty or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1,style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if layerOverride was returned as 3, we knowthe color and style have been specifically set for this annotation and might notmatch the default values associated with this annotations layer.

You can associate annotations with additional items not listed in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see>. If this annotation is attached to one or more entities not listed in swSelectType_e, then this method and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityTypes">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityTypes</see> return swSelNOTHING in a position in the array corresponding to the unlisted item. IAnnotation::IGetAttachedEntities indicates an unsupported entity by returning a null value in the position in the array corresponding to the unsupported entity. COM applications that call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetAttachedEntityCount3">IAnnotation::GetAttachedEntityCount3</see> include the null value in the total count of associated entities. If an annotation is disassociated from its geometry (i.e., dangling), then IAnnotation::IGetAttachedEntities returns a null value in the position in the array corresponding to the dangling item, and this method returns swSelNOTHING in the position in the array corresponding to the dangling item. NOTE: If this annotation is not associated with any geometry, then this method and IAnnotation::IGetAttachedEntities return empty arrays.

Member.Name: IGetLeaderPointsAtIndex
Member.Description: Gets coordinate information about a specified leader on this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of leader within this annotation (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: PointCount
Parameter.Description: Number of (x,y,z) points to return in the array

Member.Returns: in-process, in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The index value is 0-based. Therefore, a valid index value is greater than or equal to 0, but less than the number of leaders on this annotation. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderCount">IAnnotation::GetLeaderCount</see> to find out how many leaders are on this annotation. If the index value is invalid in Visual Basic for Applications (VBA), then SOLIDWORKS returns an empty SafeArray or S_false. You must determine the number of points in the leader to use the data returned by this method. The number of points is a function of the number of segments in the leader. There can be one or two segments in a leader line, depending on whether or not it is a straight, bent, or underlined leader. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderStyle">IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle</see>to determine the number of points in the leader.
If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swNO_LEADER, then the number of points = 0. If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swSTRAIGHT and swUNDERLINED then the numberof points = 2. If IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle returns swBENT, then the number of points = 3. Additionally, for the COM interface, you must determine the number of points to allocate the appropriate size array for the return value. The number of points must also be passed to the method to help prevent overwrite problems if you have not allocated an array that is the correct size. If the number of points passed does not match what is found, SOLIDWORKS does not return any point information and returns S_false. The format of the return array is:
retval[0] = X-coordinate of first leader point retval[1] = Y-coordinate of first leader point retval[2] = Z-coordinate of first leader point
retval[3] = X-coordinate of second leader point retval[4] = Y-coordinate of second leader point retval[5] = Z-coordinate of second leader point
retval[6] = X-coordinate of third leader point retval[7] = Y-coordinate of third leader point retval[8] = Z-coordinate of third leader point You cannot directly set the leader coordinate information. The leader coordinates are computed based on the annotations text and attachment points. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetPosition">IAnnotation::GetPosition</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetPosition">IAnnotation::SetPosition</see> to get and set the text point.

Member.Name: IGetPosition
Member.Description: Gets the position of this annotation.
Member.Returns: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The retval is an array of 3 doubles, the x, y, z origin of the annotation. If this method is not successful in retrieving the position of the annotation, the status value is S_false (COM only). Make sure that you check this value before using the returned position. The following table lists the types of annotations that this method supports and the position of the x, y, z origin. In a drawing, the x, y, z origin is relative to the origin of the drawing sheet (the lower-left corner of the sheet).
Type of Annotation Position of XYZ Origin
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Feature Symbols</see> Point where leader hits symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Target Symbols</see> Centerpoint of the circle that is attached to the leader
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDimension">Dimensions</see> Upper-left corner of the text box of the dimension
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerances</see> Upper-left corner of the symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Notes</see> Upper-left corner of the text box
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish Symbols</see> Lower-left point of symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation">Table Annotations</see> Position of x,y,z determined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.AnchorType">ITableAnnotation::AnchorType</see>
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld Symbols</see> Left endpoint of the main horizontal line in the symbol
If you use this method on any other types of annotations, SOLIDWORKS takes no actionand returns false.

Member.Name: IGetSpecificAnnotation
Member.Description: Gets the specific underlying object associated with this annotation.
Member.Returns: Pointer to the IUnknown interface for the specific underlying annotation
Member.Remarks: If this annotation is a note, then this method returns the underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">INote</see>. Dispatch applications can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetType">IAnnotation::GetType</see> to determine the type of underlying object supported. For example, if the return value from IAnnotation::GetType is swWeldSymbol, then you know that you can use the Dispatch pointer returned from this method with the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">IWeldSymbol</see> class. COM applications can also use IAnnotation::GetType to determine the underlying object supported. Or, COM applications can use QueryInterface to determine which object is supported and get the interface from the LPUNKNOWN return value.

Member.Name: IGetTextFormat
Member.Description: Gets the text format for the specified text in this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Number indicating which text within this annotation to check

Member.Returns: Pointer to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat">ITextFormat</see> of the specified piece of text
Member.Remarks:
The behavior of this method differs depending on the type of annotation.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Target</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Feature Symbols</see>These symbols always use the document default setting for dimension text format todisplay text within the symbol. The index argument is not used and should be setto 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerance</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display Dimensions</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Simple Notes</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld Symbols</see>These symbols can either use the document default setting to display text withinthe symbol (dimension text setting for the geometric tolerance symbols and displaydimensions, or note text setting for notes) or they can use a local format. The indexargument is not used and should be set to 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">Blocks</see> (and compound notes in documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier)These symbols might contain several different pieces of text; each piece can usethe document default setting for notes or a local format. The index argument identifiesthe text. The index value is 0-based. If the index value is invalid, then this methodreturns a NULL pointer. To get the number of text or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat">ITextFormat</see> objects, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormatCount">IAnnotation::GetTextFormatCount</see>. Rich Text FormatIf a note contains embedded rich text information in the string, this method returnsa text format that does not necessarily reflect what is displayed on the screen forthat note. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.HasMultipleFonts">INote::HasMultipleFonts</see> to determine if the note contains embeddedrich text information. ITextFormat is returned if it is for a local setting or for the documentdefault setting. To determine whether or not this annotation is using the documentdefault settings for text format, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetUseDocTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetUseDocTextFormat</see>. To set thetext format information, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see>.

Member.Name: IGetVisualProperties
Member.Description: Gets the visual properties of this annotation.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of 5 longs (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The return value is the following array of longs:
[color, style, width, layerID, layerOverride ] where:
color COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value can be 0 or -1 for default color.
style Line style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see>.
width Line width as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
layerID Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The Layer object can be obtainedby passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
layerOverride Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overriddenwith respect to the layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specificproperty or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1,style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if layerOverride was returned as 3, we knowthe color and style have been specifically set for this annotation and might notmatch the default values associated with this annotations layer.

Member.Name: ISetTextFormat
Member.Signature: ISetTextFormat( System.int Index, System.bool UseDoc, TextFormat TextFormat )
Member.Description: Sets the text format information for the specified text within this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Number indicating which text within this annotation to check

Parameter.Name: UseDoc
Parameter.Description: True to use the document default setting for text format, false to not

Parameter.Name: TextFormat
Parameter.Description: Object to use for the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat">ITextFormat</see> on the specified piece of text

Member.Returns: True if this method is successful in setting the text format information, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The behavior of this method differs depending on the type of annotation.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Target</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Feature</see> SymbolsThese symbols always use the document default setting for dimension text format to display all of the text objects within the symbol. This method has no effect on the annotation. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerance</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display Dimensions</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Simple Notes</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld</see> SymbolsThese symbols can use the document default setting for display of all text objects within the symbol (dimension text setting for the geometric tolerance symbols and display dimensions, or note text setting for notes) or they can use a local format. The index argument is not used and should be set to 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">Blocks</see> (and compound notes in documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier)These symbols might contain several different pieces of text; each piece can use the document default setting for notes or a local format. The index argument identifies the text. The index value is 0 based. If the index value is invalid, then this method returns false. To get the number of text or TextFormat objects, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormatCount">IAnnotation::GetTextFormatCount</see>. Rich Text FormatIf a notes contains embedded rich text information in the string, then using this method to set a specific text format has no effect and returns false. If you use this method to set the note to use the document default text format, then all of the rich text font information is removed from the string.To set a specific text format for a note that contains embedded rich text information, perform these two steps. First use this method to set the document default. Then use this method to set the specific text format. If the useDoc argument is True, then the annotation is set to use the appropriate document default setting and ignores the textFormat argument, which should be set to NULL. To determine whether or not this annotation is using the document default settings for text format, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetUseDocTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetUseDocTextFormat</see>. To set the text format information, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.ISetTextFormat">IAnnotation::ISetTextFormat</see>. To see the effects of changing the text format information for this annotation, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">ModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>.

Member.Name: Layer
Member.Description: Gets or sets the layer used by this annotation. Layers are supported only in SOLIDWORKSdrawings.
Member.Returns: Name of the layer used for this annotation
Member.Remarks: In Drawing documents, annotations can be created on a specific layer. This property allows you to get or set the layer used by this annotation. You can also set an annotation to not be on any layer by specifying "" for theLayer. NOTE: The return value might be an empty string because an old document might not contain layers. This also occurs if annotations have been generated in a new document that does not have layers defined.

Member.Name: LayerOverride
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether the annotation has properties that override the default properties of the layer.
Member.Returns: Properties that have been overridden or should be overridden as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLayerOverride_e">swLayerOverride_e</see> (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Layers are currently supported only in SOLIDWORKS drawings. You should set this property only when you want to reset specific visual properties to the default visual properties of the owning layer. If you want to change or set specific values for the visual property of this item, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.Color">IAnnotation::Color</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.Style">IAnnotation::Style</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.Width">IAnnotation::Width</see>. In drawing documents, annotations can be created on a layer that has specific visual properties. By default, the annotation takes on the visual properties defined by the layer. However, for a specific annotation, you can override these visual properties (color, style, and width). When the annotation is not on any layer, this property returns an undefined value. You can use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.Layer">IAnnotation::Layer</see> property to determine the name of the layer that this annotation is on. If an empty string is returned by the Annotation::Layer property, then this property is not used. When you get this property, the returned bit value indicates which property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are:
color = 0x1
style = 0x2
width = 0x4 Therefore, if the value was returned as 3, you know color and style have been specifically set for this item and might not match the default values associated with this item's layer. When you set this property, the input bit value indicates which property or properties should maintain their current override values. Therefore, if the value is passed as 0x4, we know width should keep its current override value, and that color and style should be reset to use the color and style settings for the item's layer. If you pass 0, all visual properties are reset to use the default settings of the item's layer.

Member.Name: SetArrowHeadStyleAtIndex

Parameter.Description: 0-based index of leader within this annotation (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ArrowHeadStyle
Parameter.Description: Arrowhead style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swArrowStyle_e">swArrowStyle_e</see>

Member.Returns: Return status (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
A valid index value is greater than or equal to 0, but less than the number of leaders on this annotation. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetArrowHeadCount">IAnnotation::GetArrowHeadCount</see> to find out how many leaders are on this annotation. An index value of -1 is also valid, and indicates that this arrowhead style should be applied to all leaders on this annotation. If the index value isinvalid, SOLIDWORKS returns a retval of -2. If smart arrowhead style is enabled on this annotation, then this method cannot changethe arrowhead style of individual leaders, and retval is -3. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetSmartArrowHeadStyle">IAnnotation::GetSmartArrowHeadStyle</see> to determine if this flag is enabled or disabled. The return status of this method can have the following values:
If value equals... Then the arrowhead style was...
0 Successfully set
-1 Not set because of an unknown error
-2 Not set because of an invalid index value
-3 Not set because of smart arrowhead styles being enabled
-4 Not set because of an invalid arrowhead style value If leader display is enabled, then this method changes the visible model. To see thosechanges, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> to reddraw the graphics window. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetArrowHeadStyleAtIndex">IAnnotation::GetArrowHeadStyleAtIndex</see> to get the arrow head style of a specific leader.

Parameter.Description: True to enable dashed line leader display; false to enable solid-line leader (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Indicates whether the operation was successful (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Not all annotations support all styles of leaders or leader characteristics. Only notes, GTols, surface finish symbols, weld symbols, datum target symbols, and block instances support leaders of any kind.
Weld symbol leaders can be hidden, but are always bent; straight leaders (swSTRAIGHT) are not supported.
Datum target symbols can have straight or bent leaders, but cannot be hidden (swNO_LEADER is not supported).
Only notes support underline leaders (swUNDERLINED).
GTols are the only type of annotation that supports perpendicular bent leaders.
GTols and weld symbols are the only types of annotations that support all around leader symbols.
Datum target symbols are the only type of annotation that supports dashed leaders. This method sets the characteristics of the annotation, not the individual leaders. You can get or set these characteristics whether leaders are displayed.
Use... To...
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetDashedLeader">IAnnotation::GetDashedLeader</see> Determine whether this leader is a dashed line or a solid line.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderAllAround">IAnnotation::GetLeaderAllARound</see>
Determine whether all around symbol display is enabled or disabled.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderPerpendicular">IAnnotation::GetLeaderPerpendicular</see>
Determine whether perpendicular bent leader display is enabled or disabled.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderSide">IAnnotation::GetLeaderSide</see>
Get the leader attachment side setting.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetLeaderStyle">IAnnotation::GetLeaderStyle</see>
Get style of leader (hidden, straight, bent, or underline).
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetSmartArrowHeadStyle">IAnnotation::GetSmartArrowHeadStyle</see>
Determine whether smart arrowhead style is enabled or disabled.
You can set the leader side, smart arrowhead style, and bent leader values at any time. However, if leader display is disabled, you cannot affect the display of the annotation by setting these values. You can also set the perpendicular bent leader and all around symbol display at any time, but if bent leaders are disabled, you cannot affect the display of the annotation by setting these values. The return status of this operation can have the following values:
0 = Leader characteristics were successfully set
-1 = Leader characteristics were not set because of an unknown error
-2 = Leader attachment side setting is invalid
-3 = Leaders are not supported on this type of annotation
-4 = Leaders cannot be disabled on this type of annotation
-5 = Bent leaders cannot be disabled on this type of annotation
-6 = Underline style leaders are not allowed on this type of annotation If leader display is enabled, then this method changes the visible model.

Member.Name: SetPosition
Member.Signature: SetPosition( System.double X, System.double Y, System.double Z )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetPosition2">IAnnotation::SetPosition2</see>.

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: x origin of the annotation

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: y origin of the annotation

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: z origin of the annotation

Member.Returns: True if the position of the annotation was set, false if the operation was not successful
Member.Remarks:
The following table lists the types of annotations that this method supports and the position of the x, y, z origin. In a drawing, the x, y, z origin is relative to the origin of the drawing sheet (the lower-left corner of the sheet).
Type of Annotation Position of XYZ Origin
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum Feature Symbols</see> Point where leader hits symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum Target Symbols</see> Centerpoint of the circle that is attached to the leader
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display dimensions</see> Upper-left corner of the text box of the display dimension
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric Tolerances</see> Upper-left corner of the symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Notes</see> Upper-left corner of the text box
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud">Revision Clouds</see> Position of x,y,z determined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.Shape">IRevisionCloud::Shape</see>
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface Finish Symbols</see> Lower-left point of symbol
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation">Table Annotations</see> Position of x,y,z determined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.AnchorType">ITableAnnotation::AnchorType</see>
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">Weld Symbols</see> Left endpoint of the main horizontal line in the symbol
If you use this method on any other types of annotations, SOLIDWORKS takes no action and returns false. The position of an annotation can be subject to certain restrictions. These restrictions apply to setting the position through the user interface and using this method. One example of a restriction is a surface-finish symbol that is inserted directly on a face (that is, no leaders). It can only be moved within the borders of that face. If it is inserted directly on an edge, it can only be moved along that edge or extensions of that edge. Datum feature symbols have similar restrictions. If this method attempts to set a position of an annotation that violates any restrictions, the annotation is placed as near as possible to the specified position. The position of table annotations cannot be set if the table is anchored. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.Anchored">ITableAnnotation::Anchored</see> to determine if the table is anchored.
If a dimension has <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.OffsetText">offset text</see>, and you want to move... Then...
Dimension text, dimension line, and extension lines
Turn offset text off. Use this method to move the dimension text, dimension line, and extension lines. Turn offset text back on.
Dimension text only Use this method to move the dimension text. The dimension line and extension lines will not move.
Because radial and diametric dimensions are already attached to the end of a leader, this property is not available for these types of dimensions.

Member.Name: SetTextFormat
Member.Signature: SetTextFormat( System.int Index, System.bool UseDoc, System.object TextFormat )
Member.Description: Sets the text format for the specified text in this annotation.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Number indicating which text in this annotation to check

Parameter.Name: UseDoc
Parameter.Description: True to use the document default setting for text format, false to not

Parameter.Name: TextFormat
Parameter.Description: Object to use for the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat">text format</see> on the specified piece of text

Member.Returns: True if this method is successful in setting the text format information, false if not

Example.Name: Get Corresponding Objects in Assembly Component
Get Corresponding Objects in Assembly Component
Get Corresponding Objects in Assembly Component

Member.Remarks:
The behavior of this method differs depending on the type of annotation.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTargetSym">Datum target</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDatumTag">Datum feature</see> symbolsThese symbols always use the document default setting for dimension text format to display all of the text objects within the symbol. This method has no effect on the annotation. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">Geometric tolerance</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">Display dimensions</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">Simple notes</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">Surface finish</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IWeldSymbol">weld</see> symbols.These symbols can use the document default setting for display of all text objects within the symbol (dimension text setting for the geometric tolerance symbols and display dimensions, or note text setting for notes) or they can use a local format. The index argument is not used and should be set to 0. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">Blocks</see> (and compound notes in documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2015 and earlier)These symbols might contain several different pieces of text; each piece can use the document default setting for notes or a local format. The index argument identifies the text. The index value is 0-based. If the index value is invalid, then this method returns false. To get the number of text or TextFormat objects, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetTextFormatCount">IAnnotation::GetTextFormatCount</see>. Rich text formatIf a note contains embedded rich text information in the string, then using this method to set a specific text format has no effect and returns false. If you use this method to set the note to use the document default text format, then all of the rich text font information is removed from the string.To set a specific text format for a note that contains embedded rich text information, perform these two steps. First use this method to set the document default. Then use this method to set the specific text format. If the useDoc argument is true, then the annotation is set to use the appropriate document default setting and ignores the textFormat argument, which should be set to Nothing or null. To determine whether or not this annotation is using the document default settings for text format, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetUseDocTextFormat">IAnnotation::GetUseDocTextFormat</see>. To set the text format information, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetTextFormat">IAnnotation::SetTextFormat</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.ISetTextFormat">IAnnotation::ISetTextFormat</see>. To see the effects of changing the text format information for this annotation, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">ModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>.

Member.Remarks: There are several reasons why an annotation might or might not be visible on the screen. This property determines whether an annotation has been individually displayed or hidden if you selected and specifically hid the annotation or if you selected and specifically hid the dimensions of a feature. This property cannot determine whether an annotation is hidden if it is on a layer that is hidden (all annotations of this type are hidden) or if the feature that owns it is suppressed. Therefore, even though this method indicates that an annotation is visible, it might not necessarily be visible on the screen. If an annotation's visibility is set to swAnnotationHalfHidden, then that annotation is in a half-hidden state, which is not a permanent state. For example, during a Hide/Show Annotations operation in a drawing, a half-hidden annotation is displayed in gray if the interactive user selects to show all annotations. Any annotation set to swAnnotationHalfHidden is hidden when the interactive user finishes using Hide/Show Annotations. When you use this property to change the visibility of an annotation, you also cause changes to the visible model. To see those changes, redraw the graphics window using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>.

Parameter.Name: CompName
Parameter.Description: Path name of a loaded part or assembly to add as a component (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ConfigName
Parameter.Description: Name of the configuration from which to load the component (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: X coordinate of the component center

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: Y coordinate of the component center

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: Z coordinate of the component center

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see>
Member.Remarks: The specified file must be loaded in memory. A file is loaded into memory when you load the file in your SOLIDWORKS Design session (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc6">ISldWorks::OpenDoc6</see>) or open an assembly that already contains the file. If configName is empty or specifies a configuration that does not exist, then the current configuration is used. If you want to add the component at a position relative to the root component, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Transform2">IComponent2::Transform2</see> to reposition the component immediately after calling this method. Or, you can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AddComponents">IAssemblyDoc::AddComponents</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.IAddComponents2">IAssemblyDoc::AddComponents2</see> to specify the transform when inserting a component, insert as many components as you want at once, and rotate and scale the component through the transform matrix. IMPORTANT: The x, y, and z parameters of this method are relative to the bounding box of the component. Only use this method if you want to approximately position the component. Use IComponent2::Transform2 if you want to more precisely position the component.

Member.Signature: AddComponentConfiguration( System.string Name, System.string Comment, System.string AlternateName, System.int Options )
Member.Description: Adds a new configuration for the last selected assembly component.

Parameter.Name: Name
Parameter.Description: Name of new configuration

Parameter.Name: Comment
Parameter.Description: Comment displayed in Configuration Properties

Parameter.Name: AlternateName
Parameter.Description: Alternate configuration name; used if swConfigOption_UseAlternateName is set to true (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Options
Parameter.Description: Combination of one or more BOOLEAN configuration options as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swConfigurationOptions2_e">swConfigurationOptions2_e</see> (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration">IConfiguration</see>
Member.Remarks:
The Options argument can be a combination of any of the following values:
swConfigOption_SuppressByDefault True if you want to suppress newly added features and mates in this configuration, false if not
swConfigOption_HideByDefault - True if you want newly added components to be hidden, false if not
swConfigOption_MinFeatureManager True if you want newly added components to only display their component name in the FeatureManager design tree, false if you want newly added components to display their name and each of their features in the FeatureManager design tree
swConfigOption_DontActivate - True if you do not want the new configuration activated, false if not

Member.Name: AddComponents
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AddComponents3">IAssemblyDoc::AddComponents3</see>.

Parameter.Name: Names
Parameter.Description: Array of strings component file names

Parameter.Name: Transforms
Parameter.Description: Array of doubles of the component transforms

Member.Returns: Array of objects of newly created components
Member.Remarks: The array of file names represents all of the components that are added to the assembly. If there is more than one instance of a given component, make sure you add the file name of the component for each instance of the component. The array of transforms consists of [count x 16] doubles. There should be one transform for each component being added. TIP: See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc6">ISldWorks::OpenDoc6</see> for tips on how to avoid using large amounts of memory when opening up multiple parts to add to an assembly

Member.Name: AddComponents3
Member.Signature: AddComponents3( System.object Names, System.object Transforms, System.object CoordinateSystemNames )
Member.Description: Adds multiple components to the assembly.

Parameter.Name: Names
Parameter.Description: Array of full path names of components

Parameter.Name: Transforms
Parameter.Description: Array of transformation matrix doubles

Parameter.Name: CoordinateSystemNames
Parameter.Description: Array of coordinate system names

Member.Returns: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see> objects
Member.Remarks: Transforms contains an array of [(Names count) x 16] doubles. This parameter stores one transformation matrix of 16 doubles for each component in Names. If a component's transformation matrix is null, then the component is placed in the assembly such that the component's user-defined coordinate system coincides exactly with the default coordinate system of the assembly (no transformation). See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">IMathTransform</see> for details about transformation matrices. CoordinateSystemNames contains a user-defined coordinate system name for each component in Names. If a component's user-defined coordinate system is an empty string, then the component is placed in the assembly with respect to the default coordinate system of the component. TIP: See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc6">ISldWorks::OpenDoc6</see> for tips on how to avoid using large amounts of memory when opening up multiple parts to add to an assembly

Member.Remarks:
To specify a distance mate without limits, set the DistanceAbsUpperLimit and DistanceAbsLowerLimit arguments equal to the distance argument's value.
If MateTypeFromEnum is swMateDISTANCE or swMateANGLE when the mate is applied to the closest position that meets the mate condition specified by distance or angle, then setting Flip to true moves the assembly to the other possible mate position.
To add a mate:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ClearSelection2">IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2</see> before selecting entities to mate.

If MateTypeFromEnum is swMateCAMFOLLOWER, then use a selection mark of 8 for the cam-follower face. If MateTypeFromEnum is swMateWIDTH and uses tab selections, then use a selection mark of 16. If MateTypeFromEnum is anything else, then use a selection mark of 1.
Call this method.
Call IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2 after the mate is created. If nothing is preselected, then ErrorStatus is swAddMateError_IncorrectSelections, and nothing is returned.

Member.Signature: AddPipingFitting( System.string PathName, System.string ConfigName, System.short AlignmentIndex )
Member.Description: Adds a pipe fitting to the current piping assembly.

Parameter.Description: Full name and directory location of part file used for this fitting

Parameter.Name: ConfigName
Parameter.Description: Configuration within the fitting part file which should be used

Parameter.Description: Each fitting has a varying number of alignment positions; this value allows you to choose the alignment position

Member.Remarks: This method adds a piping fitting to the selected sketch point. The sketch must be the active sketch of the piping assembly. The alignmentIndex argument controls the alignment of the fitting. For example, you can align a t-piece in two ways: passing 0 aligns the t-piece one way, and passing 1 aligns it the other way. Member.Name: AddToFeatureScope
Member.Description: Adds a component to the scope of the currently selected assembly feature.

Parameter.Name: CompName
Parameter.Description: Name of component to add

Member.Returns: True if added successfully, false otherwise
Member.Remarks:
If no assembly feature is selected, then this method adds a component to a list for use with the next assembly feature created. Assembly features allow you to create a feature that affects multiple components in an assembly. For example, if you need a hole through two blocks so that you could bolt them together, you can create a hole as an assembly feature and make it go through both blocks. The scope of the assembly feature determines which components are effected by this feature. In other words, it describes which components can contain the feature. There are two ways to use the IAssemblyDoc::AddToFeatureScope method:
When an assembly feature is selected, IAssemblyDoc::AddToFeatureScope adds a component to the assembly feature's scope. Any component in the scope of the assembly feature can be affected by the assembly feature.
You can also use IAssemblyDoc::AddToFeatureScope to compile a group of components. The next assembly feature created (for example, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SimpleHole">IFeatureManager::SimpleHole</see>) affects each of the components in the compiled group. After completing these steps, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.UpdateFeatureScope">IAssemblyDoc::UpdateFeatureScope</see> to display the changes.

Member.Name: CreateMate
Member.Description: Creates a mate with the specified feature data object.

Parameter.Name: MateData
Parameter.Description: Mate-specific object (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see>
Member.Remarks:
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the base interface for the following mate-specific interfaces (an asterisk indicates that pre-selection of mate entities during mate creation is supported):
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAngleMateFeatureData">IAngleMateFeatureData</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICamFollowerMateFeatureData">ICamFollowerMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICoincidentMateFeatureData">ICoincidentMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConcentricMateFeatureData">IConcentricMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDistanceMateFeatureData">IDistanceMateFeatureData</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGearMateFeatureData">IGearMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IHingeMateFeatureData">IHingeMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData">ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILockMateFeatureData">ILockMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IParallelMateFeatureData">IParallelMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPerpendicularMateFeatureData">IPerpendicularMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileCenterMateFeatureData">IProfileCenterMateFeatureData</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRackPinionMateFeatureData">IRackPinionMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IScrewMateFeatureData">IScrewMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISlotMateFeatureData">ISlotMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISymmetricMateFeatureData">ISymmetricMateFeatureData</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITangentMateFeatureData">ITangentMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IUniversalJointMateFeatureData">IUniversalJointMateFeatureData</see> * <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IWidthMateFeatureData">IWidthMateFeatureData</see> To create a standard, advanced, or mechanical mate:
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMateData">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMateData</see> to access a MateFeatureData object. Set the general properties of the MateFeatureData object. Cast the MateFeatureData object to one of the mate-specific objects. Follow specific instructions in the Remarks of the mate-specific interface, set specific properties of the mate-specific object, and/or pre-select entities to mate for asterisked interfaces above. Call this method, passing in the mate-specific object. To create:
Misaligned concentric mates, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AddConcentricMateWithTolerance">IAssemblyDoc::AddConcentricMateWithTolerance</see>. Cylindrical distance mates, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AddDistanceMate">IAssemblyDoc::AddDistanceMate</see>.

swMateANGLE swMateCAMFOLLOWER swMateCOINCIDENT swMateCONCENTRIC swMateDISTANCE swMateGEAR swMateHINGE swMateLINEARCOUPLER swMateLOCK swMatePARALLEL swMatePERPENDICULAR swMatePROFILECENTER swMateRACKPINION swMateSCREW swMateSLOT swMateSYMMETRIC swMateTANGENT swMateUNIVERSALJOINT swMateWIDTH To create a mate, see the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblydoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks section.

Member.Name: EditConcentricMate
Member.Signature: EditConcentricMate( System.int AlignFromEnum, System.int ConcentricPositionType, System.bool ConcentricToleranceCheck, System.double ConcentricToleranceValue, out System.int ErrorStatus )
Member.Description: Edits a misaligned concentric mate.

Parameter.Name: AlignFromEnum
Parameter.Description: Type of mate alignment as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swMateAlign_e">swMateAlign_e</see>

Parameter.Name: ConcentricPositionType
Parameter.Description: Misaligned concentric mate position as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swConcentricAlignmentType_e">swConcentricAlignmentType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: ConcentricToleranceCheck
Parameter.Description: True to override the deviation, false to have SOLIDWORKS calculate the deviation

Parameter.Name: ConcentricToleranceValue
Parameter.Description: Maximum deviation; valid only when ConcentricToleranceCheck is true

Parameter.Name: ErrorStatus
Parameter.Description: Success or error as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAddMateError_e">swAddMateError_e</see>

Member.Remarks:
Select these entities before calling this method:
Two entities that define the misaligned concentric mate Misaligned concentric mate A parent non-misaligned (i.e., standard) concentric mate must already exist for the selected misaligned concentric mate. If a suitable parent concentric mate does not exist, then the selected misaligned concentric mate changes to a standard concentric mate. You can also change a misaligned concentric mate to a standard concentric mate using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.EditMate4">IAssemblyDoc::EditMate4</see>. After calling IAssemblyDoc::EditConcentricMate, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.EditRebuild3">IModelDoc2::EditRebuild3</see>.

Member.Remarks: The first selection should be the two items that are mated (that is, two faces, edge and face, and so on), and the third selection should be the mate feature to be edited. The mate feature must be selected last. The two mated items must be selected with a selection mark of 1. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectData">ISelectData</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> for details on using selection marks. If mateType is swMateDISTANCE or swMateANGLE when the mate is applied to the closest position that meets the mate condition specified by distance or angle, then setting flip to True moves the assembly to the other possible mate position. This method does not support editing Inplace mates.

Repair Mates Missing Same Mate Entity

Member.Remarks:
To edit:
Standard, advanced, and mechanical mates created using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see>, follow the steps to edit the mate in the Remarks of the mate's feature data interface. Misaligned concentric mates, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.EditConcentricMate">IAssemblyDoc::EditConcentricMate</see>. Distance mates, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.EditDistanceMate">IAssemblyDoc::EditDistanceMate</see>. If repairing all mates missing the same mate entity, then select the following items in the following order before calling this method:
Mate feature to repair. Two model items to mate (that is, two faces, edge and face, and so on). The two model items must be selected with a selection mark of 1. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectData">ISelectData</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> for details on using selection marks. If MateTypeFromEnum is swMateType_e.swMateDISTANCE or swMateType_e.swMateANGLE, and the mate is applied to the closest position that meets the mate condition specified by Distance or Angle, then setting Flip to true moves the components to the other possible mate position.
This method does not support editing Inplace mates.

Parameter.Description: Type of bounding box as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBoundingBoxOptions_e">swBoundingBoxOptions_e</see>

Member.Returns: Object containing the two diagonal points that bound the component; the array contains 6 doubles (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Assembly
Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Assembly
Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Assembly

Member.Remarks:
IMPORTANT: The values returned are approximate and should not be used for comparisonor calculation purposes. Furthermore, the bounding box may vary after rebuilding the model.The resulting box encloses the object, but it might not be the tightest box. The X, Y, Z points returned by SOLIDWORKS are the lower- and upper-diagonal corners that bound the component with the box sides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes. SOLIDWORKS returns box dimensions that enclose the object and are typically close to the minimum possible size. The return value is an array of doubles as follows:
[ XCorner1, YCorner1, ZCorner1, XCorner2, YCorner2, ZCorner2 ]

Member.Name: GetEditTarget
Member.Description: Gets the model document that is currently being edited.
Member.Returns: Object for the model document being edited
Member.Remarks: This method is useful when the user is performing an in-context edit of a part component because the currently active document returned from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.ActiveDoc">ISldWorks::ActiveDoc</see> might not be the document that the user is editing. For example, the user can use in-context editing to modify an assembly component. The active document is the assembly, but this method returns the IModelDoc2 for the component being edited. The IModelDoc2 object returned by this method might be that of the assembly if no part is being in-place edited. In other words, this method returns a valid pointer (non-NULL) even when user is not editing a part in-context. You can use the IModelDoc2 object returned by this method to determine which assembly component is being edited in-context. In general, you should not use this IModelDoc2 object for feature creation within the component part. Feature creation typically requires the IModelDoc2 of the active document. During feature creation, SOLIDWORKS automatically determines whether the feature should be created and owned by the active assembly, or if it is an in-context edit in which the feature should be created and owned by the component part.

Member.Name: IGetBox
Member.Description: Gets the bounding box.

Parameter.Name: Options
Parameter.Description: Type of bounding box as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBoundingBoxOptions_e">swBoundingBoxOptions_e</see>

Member.Returns: Two diagonal points that bound the object; the format is a pointer to an array of 6 doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
IMPORTANT: The values returned are approximate and should not be used for comparison or calculation purposes. Furthermore, the bounding box may vary after rebuilding the model.The resulting box encloses the object, but it might not be the tightest box. The X, Y, Z points returned by SOLIDWORKS are the lower- and upper-diagonal corners that bound the component with the box sides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes. SOLIDWORKS returns box dimensions that enclose the object and are typically close to the minimum possible size. The return value is an array of doubles as follows:
[ XCorner1, YCorner1, ZCorner1, XCorner2, YCorner2, ZCorner2 ]

Member.Name: IGetEditTarget2
Member.Description: Gets the model document that is currently being edited.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> being edited
Member.Remarks: This method is useful when the user is performing an in-context edit of a part component because the currently active document returned from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.ActiveDoc">ISldWorks::ActiveDoc</see> might not be the document that the user is editing. For example, the user can use in-context editing to modify an assembly component. The active document is the assembly, but this method returns the IModelDoc2 for the component being edited. The IModelDoc2 object returned by this method might be that of the assembly if no part is being in-place edited. In other words, this method returns a valid pointer (non-NULL) even when user is not editing a part in-context. You can use the IModelDoc2 object returned by this method to determine which assembly component is being edited in-context. In general, you should not use this IModelDoc2 object for feature creation within the component part. Feature creation typically requires the IModelDoc2 of the active document. During feature creation, SOLIDWORKS automatically determines whether the feature should be created and owned by the active assembly, or if it is an in-context edit in which the feature should be created and owned by the component part. COM applications need to release the IModelDoc2 object returned because this method increments the reference count on the IModelDoc2 object even if the edit target is the active document.

Member.Name: IReorderComponents
Member.Signature: IReorderComponents( System.int Count, ref Component2 Source, System.object Target, System.int Where )
Member.Description: Moves components to a different location in the FeatureManager tree.

Parameter.Name: Count
Parameter.Description: Number of items in the Source array

Parameter.Name: Source
Parameter.Description: Array of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">components</see> to move

Parameter.Name: Target
Parameter.Description: Target component or folder feature to which to move the components

Parameter.Name: Where
Parameter.Description: Where to move the components as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swReorderComponentsWhere_e">swReorderComponentsWhere_e</see>

Member.Returns: True if the components were moved, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The Source argument contains the components to reorder in the FeatureManager tree.
The order of the items in the array will be the order that the components appear after the reorder occurs. The components can only be moved within the same component of the model; you cannot move a component from a subassembly into the top level assembly.
The Where argument indicates where the Source should be moved relative to the Target as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swReorderComponentsWhere_e">swReorderComponentsWhere_e</see>. If the target is a feature, but not a folder feature, this method takes no action and returns false. Only folders that occur within the components section of the Assembly FeatureManager tree can be used; a folder that is among the body features will not be accepted. If the Where argument is specified as one of the two folder-related values, but the Target is a component, the method uses swReorderComponents_After.
