Member.Name: IOperations2
Member.Signature: IOperations2( System.int OperationType, Body2 ToolBody, out System.int ErrorCode )
Member.Description: Performs add, cut, and intersect (unite, subtract, and interfere) operations between two temporary bodies.

Parameter.Name: OperationType
Parameter.Description: Operation type as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swBodyOperationType_e">swBodyOperationType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: ToolBody
Parameter.Description: Pointer to the tool <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">body</see>

Parameter.Name: ErrorCode
Parameter.Description: Error indicator as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBodyOperationError_e">swBodyOperationError_e</see>; returns swBodyOperationNoError if SOLIDWORKS does not generate an error

Member.Returns: Resulting <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2">bodies enumeration</see>
Member.Remarks: If the target and tool bodies are the same in geometry, the result body of this method is NULL, and the return value is S_false. This method works with two temporary bodies; one is the target and one is the tool. The output is a list of bodies resulting from the operation. The two temporary bodies used in this function (the Body2 and ToolBody pointers) are invalid once the operation is complete. COM applications should release these two pointers after using this method. If your application needs to maintain these bodies, then you should make a copy of them using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.ICopy">IBody2::ICopy</see> before passing them to this routine. To perform a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swBodyOperationType_e">swBodyOperationType_e</see>.SWBODYINTERSECT between a sheet (surface) and a solid body, the sheet body must be the target body. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.Check3">IBody2::Check3</see> for both bodies before using this method to ensure that both bodies are valid solids. Using this method with invalid bodies can cause unexpected results. If a non-manifold error is returned, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.ResetEdgeTolerances">IBody2::ResetEdgeTolerances</see> to visit all of the edges in the body to reset their tolerances. Then use IBody2::Operations2 again.

Parameter.Name: OperationType
Parameter.Description:
One of the following operation types:
SWBODYADD
SWBODYCUT
SWBODYINTERSECT

Parameter.Name: ToolBody
Parameter.Description: Array of bodies

Parameter.Name: NumOfMatchingFaces
Parameter.Description: Number of matching faces

Member.Returns: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> formed by the operation
Member.Remarks:
The concept of match means that the caller tells the boolean operator beforehand which faces can be considered to coincide. Basically, the caller performs part of the boolean operation. Sometimes the application knows that two faces match because of the way the bodies are constructed; i.e., the application knows which faces are intended to match. Having a list of matching face pairs may allow the matched boolean operator to resolve other geometric operations that otherwise it would not be able to work out. In general, providing matched faces speeds up the boolean operation and makes results more reliable. The arguments FaceList1 and FaceList2 arguments can be empty lists. If matching face pairs are passed in, these faces must match such that:
the surface geometry is coinciding.
for each edge in a face, there is an edge in the other face that coincides

Member.Name: MatchedBoolean4
Member.Signature: MatchedBoolean4( System.int OperationType, System.object ToolBody, System.int NumOfMatchingFaces, System.object FaceList1, System.object FaceList2, System.double MatchingTolerance, out System.int ErrorCode )
Member.Description: Performs a matched boolean on the specified bodies and supports an optional list of faces that match exactly.

Parameter.Name: OperationType
Parameter.Description:
One of the following operation types:
SWBODYADD
SWBODYCUT
SWBODYINTERSECT

Parameter.Name: ToolBody
Parameter.Description: Array of bodies

Parameter.Name: NumOfMatchingFaces
Parameter.Description: Number of matching faces

Parameter.Name: FaceList1
Parameter.Description: First face list (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: FaceList2
Parameter.Description: Number of matching faces

Parameter.Name: MatchingTolerance
Parameter.Description: Tolerance to use to check matching faces

Parameter.Name: ErrorCode
Parameter.Description: Error indicated as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBodyOperationError_e">swBodyOperationError_e</see>

Member.Remarks:
The concept of match means that the caller tells the boolean operator beforehand which faces can be considered to coincide. Basically the caller performs part of the boolean operation. Sometimes the application knows that two faces match because of the way the bodies are constructed; i.e., the application knows which faces are intended to match. Having a list of matching face pairs may allow the matched boolean operator to resolve other geometric operations that otherwise it would not be able to work out. In general, providing matched faces speeds up the boolean operation and makes results more reliable. The arguments FaceList1 and FaceList2 arguments can be empty lists. If matching face pairs are passed in, these faces must match such that:
the surface geometry is coinciding.
for each edge in a face, there is an edge in the other face that coincides. If MatchingTolerance is less than 1.0e-8 or 0.0, then a default tolerance of 2.0e-6 is used. You decide the tolerance value based on the similarities and subtle differences between the two bodies. This method supports multibody parts.

Member.Name: MaterialPropertyValues2
Member.Description: Gets or sets the material properties for a body other than the base body in the active configuration.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The material values include the face color (R,G,B values), reflectivity (ambient, diffuse, specular, shininess), transparency, and emission. Valid settings are from 0 to 1 for all values. This property is intended to be used on bodies other than the base body and should follow a call to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.EnumRelatedBodies2">IPartDoc::EnumRelatedBodies2</see>. The format of the parameters or return values is an array of 9 doubles as follows:
[ R, G, B, Ambient, Diffuse, Specular, Shininess, Transparency, Emission ]
To see a color change, you must:
Specify R, G, and B, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. (These values are internally multiplied by 255.0 to determine the RGB color.) Specify the reflectivity properties (Diffuse, Specular, Shininess (1.0 - Specular spread/Blurriness)), each with a value greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0. Specify Ambient, Transparency and Emission, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. Refresh the graphics area after setting this property.

Example.Name: Create Solid Bodies Using Geometry and Topology
Cut Body in Half Using Macro Feature

Member.Remarks: If the target and tool bodies are the same in geometry, the result body of this method is NULL, and the return value is S_false. This method works with two temporary bodies; one is the target and one is the tool. The output is a list of bodies resulting from the operation. The two temporary bodies used in this function (the Body2 and ToolBody pointers) are invalid once the operation is complete. COM applications should release these two pointers after using this method. If your application needs to maintain these bodies, then you should make a copy of them using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.Copy">IBody2::Copy</see> before passing them to this routine. To perform a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swBodyOperationType_e">swBodyOperationType_e</see>.SWBODYINTERSECT between a sheet (surface) and a solid body, the sheet body must be the target body. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.Check3">IBody2::Check3</see> for both bodies before using this method to ensure that both bodies are valid solids. Using this method with invalid bodies can cause unexpected results. If a non-manifold error is returned, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.ResetEdgeTolerances">IBody2::ResetEdgeTolerances</see> to visit all of the edges in the body to reset their tolerances. Then use IBody2::Operations2 again.

Member.Name: SortCutList
Member.Description: Sorts the cut list.

Parameter.Name: CutListSortOptions
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICutListSortOptions">ICutListSortOptions</see>

Parameter.Name: IgnoreInvalidFacesOrFeatures
Parameter.Description: True to sort bodies ignoring any invalid excluded faces/features, false to not sort the bodies if there are invalid excluded faces/features (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if sorting is successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBodyFolder.GetCutListSortOptions">IBodyFolder::GetCutListSortOptions</see> to populate CutListSortOptions. This method applies the CutListSortOptions settings, sorts the cut list, and refreshes the cut list in the FeatureManager design tree. In the Cut List Sorting Options PropertyManager you select faces/features to exclude from sorting. If some of those selected faces/features to exclude are invalid, i.e., they are not of selection type BODYFEATURE or FACE or they cannot be excluded (see the end of this Remark), a dialog box pops up during the sort operation with: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Failed to exclude some of the selected faces in cut list sorting. Try selecting the corresponding features instead. Would you like to continue: Yes (Bodies will be sorted ignoring some of the excluded faces.) No (Bodies will not be sorted.) ---------------------------------------------------------- IgnoreInvalidFacesOrFeatures handles the situation when some of the body faces/features selected for exclusion (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICutListSortOptions.SetFacesOrFeaturesToExclude">ICutListSortOptions::SetFacesOrFeaturesToExclude</see>) can not be excluded. Set IgnoreInvalidFacesOrFeatures to:
True, to sort bodies ignoring any invalid excluded faces/features. False, to not sort the bodies if there are invalid excluded faces/features. If you set IgnoreInvalidFacesOrFeatures to false and there are invalid faces/features in the exclusion list, then this method will not sort the cut list. Other examples of faces and features that are invalid for exclusion:
Chamfers that remove an entire face. Suppressed features. Features that create new bodies from sketches, such as boss-extrude, revolve, and sweep. Certain sheet metal features. For more information, see the Sorting Cut Lists topics in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Remarks:
You must specify when to update an automatically generated cut list in a part document. However, an automatically generated cut list in a drawing is automatically updated when you open a drawing that references the cut list.
To find out if the part contains a weldment feature, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.IsWeldment">IPartDoc::IsWeldment</see>. If it does, then use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBodyFolder.GetAutomaticCutList">IBodyFolder::GetAutomaticCutList</see> to find out if automatic generation of a cut list is enabled.

Member.Name: GetConfigurationCount
Member.Description: Gets the number of configurations available to this BOM table or used in this BOM table.

Parameter.Name: OnlyVisible
Parameter.Description: True to get the number of configurations currently displayed in this table, false to get the total number of configurations available in this table

Member.Returns: Number of configurations in this BOM table or available to this BOM table
Member.Remarks:
The view associated with this BOM can contain a model with multiple configurations. For a top-level only style BOM table, there can be several Quantity columns, each showing the results for a different configuration. For the other styles of BOM tables, only a particular configuration can be shown in the table, and that configuration can be changed. To determine the style of the BOM table, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomFeature.TableType">IBomFeature::TableType</see>.
If OnlyVisible is...
Then the value returned is...
True
Number of configurations currently shown in the BOM table. For a top-level only style BOM table, this could be any number from 0 to the total number of configurations available. For the other styles of BOM tables, this value is always 1.
false
Total number of configurations available.
To get the configuration names, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomFeature.GetConfigurations">IBomFeature::GetConfigurations</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomFeature.IGetConfigurations">IBomFeature::IGetConfigurations</see>. Call this method before calling IBomFeature::IGetConfigurations to get the number of configurations.

Member.Name: SetColumnCustomProperty
Member.Description: Sets the custom property used to fill the values in a specified user-defined column.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Column for which to get the custom property

Parameter.Name: CustomProp
Parameter.Description: Custom property used to fill the values in this user-defined column

Member.Returns: True if the custom property is successfully set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
Use this method to create a user-defined column where each row in the column is automatically filled in with the custom property value for that particular configuration for that component. The default title for the column is the name of the custom property. If the specified custom property is not a valid custom property, then each row in the column remains empty.
To create a user-defined column that is not attached to a custom property; for example, you want to fill in each row of the column yourself, use this method with the CustomProp value specified as the title of the column.
To get the list of available custom properties, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomTableAnnotation.GetAllCustomProperties">IBomTableAnnotation::GetAllCustomProperties</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomTableAnnotation.IGetAllCustomProperties">IBomTableAnnotation::IGetAllCustomProperties</see>. The list of available custom properties includes all of the items in the BOM table, which includes items from the file summary items and file custom properties that have been set.
This method returns false if the column is not a user-defined column, and no action is taken.

Member.Description: Gets and sets whether to change BOM item numbers after sorting.
Member.Returns: True to preserve BOM item numbers, false to re-number them

Member.Name: ItemGroups
Member.Description: Gets and sets the categories into which the BOM table rows are grouped.
Member.Returns: Array of categories as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see> or null (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
You can set this property in one of two ways:
Specify null to indicate that the BOM table rows are not to be grouped into categories. Specify an array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see> enumerators to indicate that the BOM table rows are to be grouped into categories (assemblies, parts, user defined). For example, when you set this property to an array of three enumerators in the following order, assemblies are grouped first, parts are grouped next, and user-defined categories are grouped last:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see>.swBomTableSortItemGroup_Assemblies <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see>.swBomTableSortItemGroup_Parts <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see>.swBomTableSortItemGroup_Other To eliminate grouping into a category, do not include it in the array. For example, when you set this property to the following array, no assemblies are grouped, parts are grouped first, and user-defined categories are grouped last:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see>.swBomTableSortItemGroup_Parts <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBomTableSortItemGroup_e">swBomTableSortItemGroup_e</see>.swBomTableSortItemGroup_Other

Member.Remarks: After setting this property to true, you must call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomTableAnnotation.Sort">IBomTableAnnotation::Sort</see> to actually save the sort settings in the BOM table in the drawing. Thereafter, instead of setting all of the sorting parameters every time you instantiate a new IBomTableAnnotation for this table, you can simply call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBomTableAnnotation.ApplySavedSortScheme">IBomTableAnnotation::ApplySavedSortScheme</see> to re-sort the table using the sort settings saved in the BOM table.

Member.Name: Type
Member.Description: Gets or sets the type of chamfer feature.
Member.Returns: Type of chamfer as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swChamferType_e">swChamferType_e</see>
Member.Remarks: Both swChamferType_e.swChamferAngleDistance and swChamferType_e.swChamferDistanceDistance are edge chamfers. This means that all measurements are from edges. An angle-distance chamfer requires an angle and a distance; a distance-distance chamfer requires two distances, one for each side of the chamfered edge. A swChamferType_e.swChamferVertex chamfer only works on a vertex with three adjacent edges of the same convexity. A vertex chamfer requires three distances along three adjacent edges. For non-linear edges, this value is an arc length value; it is not a chordal value. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IVertex.EnumEdgesOriented">IVertex::EnumEdgesOriented</see> to determine the edge order used by this method. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Name: SetFeatureScope
Member.Signature: SetFeatureScope( System.bool FeatureScopeOption, System.bool AutoSelectBodies, System.object Bodies )
Member.Description: Sets the feature scope, whether to autoselect the affected bodies, and the affected bodies in this circular pattern feature.

Parameter.Name: FeatureScopeOption
Parameter.Description: True (default) to specify affected bodies, false to apply the pattern to all bodies every time the feature regenerates (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: AutoSelectBodies
Parameter.Description: True (default) to automatically select all bodies intersected by this pattern feature, false to specify affected bodies (see Remarks)

Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> to be affected; valid only if FeatureScopeOption is true and AutoSelectBodies is false

Member.Returns: True if feature scope set successfully, false if not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: If this method returns false, then default values for FeatureScopeOption and AutoSelectBodies are set. A subsequent call to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> creates the feature with a FeatureScopeOption of true and an AutoSelectBodies of true. After calling IFeature::ModifyDefinition, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetErrorCode2">IFeature::GetErrorCode2</see> to determine what's wrong and then take necessary remedial action. For more information, see the Circular Pattern PropertyManager topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Description: Sets the options for varying the spacing of pattern instances in this circular pattern feature.

Parameter.Description: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IInstanceToVaryOptions">IInstanceToVaryOptions</see>

Member.Returns: True if options successfully set, false if not

Member.Name: SkippedItemArray
Member.Description: Gets or sets the list of items to skip in this circular pattern feature.
Member.Returns: Array of integers representing the items to skip
Member.Remarks:
This array is 0-based. If you skip the third and fifth items, then the array looks like ArrayOut[0]=3 and ArrayOut[1]=5. To calculate the pattern instance numbers to skip: Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2

Member.Returns: Distance in radians between pattern instances in Direction 1

Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to allow pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to the base part in this circular pattern.
Member.Returns: True to allow the pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to enclosing geometry, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only when creating a pattern from a seed sketch. The seed sketch has:
An enclosing boundary of base geometry. Fully defined relations. Dimensions only for measurements that will not vary in the pattern instances. A driving dimension that is used to specify the direction of the circular pattern. If this property is true:
Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICircularPatternFeatureData.Axis">ICircularPatternFeatureData::Axis</see> with a driving dimension of the seed sketch. Pattern instances vary with and are constrained by the enclosing geometry. See the SOLIDWORKS Help > Parts and Features > Features > Patterns and Mirroring > Control and Modify Patterns > Vary Sketch topic. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Remarks: Pick points define the position of the entities to mate. If no pick points are specified, then entities are mated using default pick points. Member.Name: AddCommandItem2
Member.Signature: AddCommandItem2( System.string Name, System.int Position, System.string HintString, System.string ToolTip, System.int ImageListIndex, System.string CallbackFunction, System.string EnableMethod, System.int UserID, System.int MenuTBOption )
Member.Description: Adds a combination menu item and toolbar item to a CommandGroup.

Parameter.Name: Name
Parameter.Description: Name of the item to add to the CommandGroup

Parameter.Name: Position
Parameter.Description: Position of the item within the CommandGroup NOTE: Specify 0 to add this item to the beginning of the CommandGroup, or specify -1 to add it to the end of the CommandGroup. This argument specifies the position of the item in relation to its immediate parent item.

Parameter.Name: HintString
Parameter.Description: Text displayed in the SOLIDWORKS status bar when the pointer is on the item

Parameter.Name: ToolTip
Parameter.Description: ToolTip displayed when the pointer is on the item

Parameter.Name: ImageListIndex
Parameter.Description: Index number of the image for the item in the parent CommandGroup (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: CallbackFunction
Parameter.Description: Function to call when this item is selected (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: EnableMethod
Parameter.Description:
Optional function that controls the state of the item; if specified, then SOLIDWORKS calls this function before displaying the item
If your methodreturns... Then SOLIDWORKS...
0
Deselects and disables the item
1
Deselects and enables the item; this is the default state if no update function is specified
2
Selects and disables the item
3
Selects and enables the item
4 Not supported(see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UserID
Parameter.Description: User-defined command ID or 0 if not used

Parameter.Name: MenuTBOption
Parameter.Description: Command item type as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swCommandItemType_e">swCommandItemType_e</see>

Member.Returns: Index of the item within the CommandGroup as assigned by SOLIDWORKS
Member.Remarks: See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Add-in_Callbacks.htm">Add-in Callback and Enable Methods</see> to learn how to specify CallbackFunction and EnableMethod. ImageListIndex is 0-based. The size of the index is equal to number of the images in the image files for that CommandGroup. See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.IconList">ICommandGroup::IconList</see> for details. You can use -1 for ImageListIndex to specify that no icon is needed for a command item of type swCommandItemType_e.swMenuItem; however, command items of type swCommandItemType_e.swToolbarItem always need an icon.

Member.Name: IconList
Member.Description: Gets or sets the paths for the icons for the toolbar buttons and separators for this CommandGroup.
Member.Returns: Array of strings of the paths for the icons for the toolbar buttons and separators for this CommandGroup (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property supports scaling for high resolution screens with high resolution operating system scaling options. The array of strings of the paths to the image files can contain icons of the following sizes:
20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels Each image file (.bmp or .png) should contain all of the same-size icons for all of the buttons and separators for both parent and child toolbars. For example:
Each icon strip should use a 256-color palette. The order in which you specify the icons must be the same for this property and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.MainIconList">ICommandGroup::MainIconList</see>. For example, if you specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for this property, then you must specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for ICommandGroup::MainIconList.

Member.Name: LargeIconList
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.IconList">ICommandGroup::IconList</see>.
Member.Returns: Path for the bitmap or PNG files containing all of the large images of the toolbar buttons and separators for this CommandGroup
Member.Remarks: The bitmap or PNG file should contain all of the images for all of the large buttons and separators for this CommandGroup, in a single bitmap for both parent and child toolbars. Each image of each button must be 24x24. The images should use a 256-color palette. You can only set this property for the top-level CommandGroup.

Member.Name: LargeMainIcon
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.MainIconList">ICommandGroup::MainIconList</see>.
Member.Returns: Path of the large bitmap or PNG for this CommandGroup
Member.Remarks: The large bitmap or PNG must be 24x24 and use a 256-color palette.

Member.Name: MainIconList
Member.Description: Gets or sets the paths for the icons for the buttons for this CommandGroup.
Member.Returns: Array of strings of the paths for the icons for the buttons for this CommandGroup (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property supports scaling for high resolution screens with high resolution operating system scaling options. The array of strings for the paths to the image files can contain icons of the following sizes:
20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels Each image file (.bmp or .png) contains a single icon. Each icon should use a 256-color palette. The order in which you specify the icons must be the same for this property and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.IconList">ICommandGroup::IconList</see>. For example, if you specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for this property, then you must specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for ICommandGroup::IconList.

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandManager.CreateCommandGroup2">ICommandManager::CreateCommandGroup2</see>.

Parameter.Name: UserID
Parameter.Description: Unique user-defined ID for this CommandGroup

Parameter.Name: Title
Parameter.Description: Name of the CommandGroup to create (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ToolTip
Parameter.Description: ToolTip for this CommandGroup

Parameter.Name: Hint
Parameter.Description: Text displayed in SOLIDWORKS status bar when a user's mouse pointer is over this CommandGroup

Parameter.Name: Position
Parameter.Description: Position of the CommandGroup in the CommandManager for all document templates (see Remarks) NOTE: Specify 0 to add the CommandGroup to the beginning of the CommandMananger, or specify -1 to add it to the end of the CommandManager.

Member.Returns: Pointer to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup">ICommandGroup</see> object
Member.Remarks:
You can also use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasMenu">ICommandGroup::MenuPosition</see> to control the position of the CommandGroup in specific document templates.
If you change the definition of an existing CommandGroup (i.e., add or remove toolbar buttons), you must assign a new unique user-defined UserID to that CommandGroup. You must perform this action to avoid conflicts with any previously existing CommandGroupa and to allow for backward and forward compatibility of the CommandGroups in your application.
To add a CommandGroup to an existing SOLIDWORKS menu, specify the name of a parent menu in Title. For example, to add a CommandGroup to the Help menu, specify:Visual Basic: "&Help/MyApp Help" Visual C++ or C#: "&Help\\MyApp Help" NOTE: If you do not specify the name of a parent menu in Title, then the menu item appears on the Tools menu below the Xpress Products menu item.
You can turn off all menus or all toolbars for a CommandGroup . See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasMenu">ICommandGroup::HasMenu</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasToolbar">ICommandGroup::HasToolbar</see> for details.

Parameter.Name: UserID

Member.Remarks:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandManager.GetGroupDataFromRegistry">ICommandManager::GetGroupDataFromRegistry</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandManager.IGetGroupDataFromRegistry">ICommandManager::IGetGroupDataFromRegistry</see> before calling this method to determine how to set IgnorePreviousVersion. Set IgnorePreviousVersion to true to prevent SOLIDWORKS from saving the current toolbar setting to the registry, even if there is no previous version.
You can also use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasMenu">ICommandGroup::MenuPosition</see> to control the position of the CommandGroup in specific document templates.
If you change the definition of an existing CommandGroup (i.e., add or remove toolbar buttons), you must assign a new unique user-defined UserID to that CommandGroup. You must perform this action to avoid conflicts with any previously existing CommandGroups and to allow for backward and forward compatibility of the CommandGroups in your application.
To add a menu item for a CommandGroup to an existing SOLIDWORKS menu, specify the name of a parent menu in Title. For example, to add a CommandGroup to the Help menu, specify:Visual Basic: "&Help/MyApp Help" Visual C++ or C#: "&Help\\MyApp Help"
NOTE: If you do not specify the name of a parent menu in Title, then the menu item for the CommandGroup appears on the Tools menu below the Xpress Products menu item. You can turn off all menus or all toolbars for a CommandGroup. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasMenu">ICommandGroup::HasMenu</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandGroup.HasToolbar">ICommandGroup::HasToolbar</see> for details.

Parameter.Description: Function to call when the flyout is selected

Parameter.Name: UpdateCallbackFunction
Parameter.Description:
Optional update function that controls the state of the item; if specified, then SOLIDWORKS Design calls this function before displaying the item (see Remarks)
If this update function returns...
Then the SOLIDWORKS Design...
0
Disables the item
1
Enables the item; this is the default state if no update function is specified

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup">IFlyoutGroup</see>
Member.Remarks: After creating the flyout, display it on a CommandManager tab by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandTabBox.AddCommands">ICommandTabBox::AddCommands</see>. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.AddContextMenuFlyout">IFlyoutGroup::AddContextMenuFlyout</see> to add it to context menus. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.AddCommandItem">IFlyoutGroup::AddCommandItem</see> to add menu items to the flyout group. If any flyout menu items are enabled, then the flyout button cannot be disabled by the flyout group's UpdateCallbackFunction. The sensitivity of the top-level flyout button is always determined by its enabled menu items. Disabled flyout menu items do not appear in the flyout menu. If there are no flyout menu items, then control of the top-level flyout button is returned to the flyout group's UpdateCallbackFunction.

Member.Name: CreateFlyoutGroup2
Member.Signature: CreateFlyoutGroup2( System.int UserID, System.string Title, System.string ToolTip, System.string Hint, System.object MainIconList, System.object IconList, System.string CallbackFunction, System.string UpdateCallbackFunction )
Member.Description: Creates a new flyout in the CommandManager and context-sensitive menus.

Parameter.Name: UserID
Parameter.Description: Unique user-defined ID for the new flyout

Parameter.Name: Title
Parameter.Description: Name of the flyout to create

Parameter.Name: ToolTip
Parameter.Description: ToolTip for the new flyout

Parameter.Name: Hint
Parameter.Description: Text displayed in SOLIDWORKS Design status bar when a user's mouse pointer is over the flyout

Parameter.Name: MainIconList
Parameter.Description: Array of strings for the paths to the image files for this flyout button (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: IconList
Parameter.Description: Array of strings for the paths to the image files containing all of the flyout toolbar buttons and separators (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: CallbackFunction
Parameter.Description: Function to call when the flyout is selected

Parameter.Name: UpdateCallbackFunction
Parameter.Description:
Optional update function that controls the state of the item; if specified, then SOLIDWORKS calls this function before displaying the item (see Remarks)
If the updatefunction returns... Then SOLIDWORKS...
0 Disables the item
1 Enables the item; this is the default state if no update function is specified

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup">IFlyoutGroup</see>
Member.Remarks:
After creating the flyout, display it on a CommandManager tab by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandTabBox.AddCommands">ICommandTabBox::AddCommands</see>. Call:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.AddContextMenuFlyout">IFlyoutGroup::AddContextMenuFlyout</see> to add the flyout to context menus. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.AddCommandItem">IFlyoutGroup::AddCommandItem</see> to add menu items to the flyout group. If any flyout menu items are enabled, then the flyout button cannot be disabled by the flyout group's UpdateCallbackFunction. The sensitivity of the top-level flyout button is always determined by its enabled menu items. Disabled flyout menu items do not appear in the flyout menu. If there are no flyout menu items, then control of the top-level flyout button is returned to the flyout group's UpdateCallbackFunction. This method supports scaling for high resolution screens with high resolution operating system scaling options. The array of strings for the paths to the image files for MainIconList and IconList can contain images of the following sizes:
20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels The order in which you specify the image files must be the same for MainIconList and IconList. For example, if you specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels images for MainIconList, then you must specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels images for IconList. The images should use a 256-color palette.

The specified CommandManager tab is split into two. The left side is the original CommandManager tab box, and the right side is the new CommandManager tab box. The first button on the new CommandManager tab box is the button specified by CommandID.

Member.Description: Creates an enumerated list of bodies.
Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2">enumerated list of bodies</see>
Member.Remarks: The list contains only those bodies associated with reference surfaces. You get a list of bodies that are related to the model, but the list does not include the part body itself. A reference surface feature might consist of one or more surfaces sewn together. SOLIDWORKS represents each reference surface feature with two bodies: one to represent the front faces and one to represent the back faces. Each IBody2 object has one or more faces depending on whether the reference surface feature is a set of sewn surfaces or a single underlying surface. The corresponding faces for each body pair should have normal vectors that are opposite. To use the enumerated list, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2.Next">IEnumBodies2::Next</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2.Skip">IEnumBodies2::Skip</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2.Reset">IEnumBodies2::Reset</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumBodies2.Clone">IEnumBodies2::Clone</see>. If a component is suppressed or lightweight, this method might return NULL because the component has not been loaded into memory by SOLIDWORKS. For more information on lightweight components, see <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Work_with_Lightweight_Components.htm">Work With Lightweight Components</see>.

Member.Name: GetBody
Member.Description: Gets the body that belongs to this instance of this component.
Member.Returns: Body

Example.Name: Get Mass Properties of Assembly Component

Member.Remarks: This method returns a valid IBody2 object only for fully resolved components that reference an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc">IPartDoc</see>. For the root component, lightweight components or components that reference an AssemblyDoc, this method returns a NULL body object. However, if a component is in a multibody part, then this method returns the first body. For COM applications, this method returns the status code ITF_E_COMPONENTNOTRESOLVED. This method is different from the IPartDoc::Body method in that it recognizes assembly-level features and returns that information based on the component instance. IPartDoc::Body never recognizes assembly-level features because the feature information is kept with the assembly, not propagated down to the part file. For example, if PartABC is added to an assembly twice, then changes to that IPartDoc object would affect both instances of the assembly IComponent2. Likewise, querying information from that IPartDoc object will not recognize changes in the assembly that may have altered only one of the components (for example, an assembly-level feature was added to one of the components). However, the component object recognizes the two instances of PartABC as two distinct IComponent2 objects and returns its information from the assembly level. For example, one assembly configuration might have an assembly-level feature that cuts a hole through each of the components in the assembly. Using this method on each of the assembly components returns the body of each component with the hole feature that was applied in this particular configuration. If you switch to the configurationwithout the assembly-level hole and re-traverse the IComponent2 objects, then calling this method for each component returns the IBody2 object without the hole feature because it was applied in the other configuration. For more information on lightweight components, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSuppression">IComponent2::GetSuppression</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.SetSuppression2">IComponent2::SetSuppression2</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ResolveAllLightWeightComponents">IAssemblyDoc::ResolveAllLightWeightComponents</see>.

Member.Name: GetBox
Member.Description: Gets the bounding box for component.

Parameter.Name: IncludeRefPlanes
Parameter.Description: True includes reference planes with the returned bounding box, false does not

Parameter.Name: IncludeSketches
Parameter.Description: True includes sketches with the returned bounding box, false does not

Member.Returns: Object containing the two diagonal points that bound the component; the array contains 6 doubles

Example.Name: Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Components
Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Components
Get Assembly Bounding Box Using Components

Member.Remarks: The resulting box encloses the object, but it might not be the tightest box. The X, Y, Z points returned by SOLIDWORKS are the lower- and upper-diagonal corners that bound the component with the box sides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes. SOLIDWORKS returns box dimensions that enclose the component and are typically close to the minimum possible size. The return value is an array of doubles as follows: [ XCorner1, YCorner1, ZCorner1, XCorner2, YCorner2, ZCorner2 ] It is possible for this method to return a NULL VARIANT for Dispatch. This occurs if your application calls IComponent2::GetBox with a component that represented a subassembly and that subassembly is not loaded. The user interface behavior is the same. When the user selects a subassembly that is not loaded, there is no selection box around the subassembly. However, once the subassembly is loaded, there is a selection box. IMPORTANT: The values returned are approximate and should not be used for comparison or calculation purposes. Furthermore, the bounding box may vary after rebuilding the model.

Member.Name: GetChildren
Member.Description: Gets all of the children components of this component.
Member.Returns: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">components</see>

Example.Name: Get Display Dimensions, GTols, and Surface-finish Symbols
Get Names of Bodies in Multibody Part
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion

Member.Remarks:
If this assembly component is a part document, SOLIDWORKS returns NULL. If this assembly component is the root component or a subassembly, then this method returns the child components that belong to the assembly document. The typical order of calls needed in assembly traversal is:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> (called only once) <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent</see> (called only once) IComponent2::GetChildren (called recursively) You must call the IComponent2::GetChildren method recursively because it returns only the immediate (one level) children. It does not get child components of the sub-assemblies. For example, if one of the child components of a component is a sub-assembly that has its own children, those children are not returned by this method. You need to call this method again from that sub-assembly component to get its children. For a given component, this method returns all of the immediate child components. This includes suppressed, hidden, and lightweight components. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Visible">IComponent2::Visible</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSuppression">IComponent2::GetSuppression</see> to detect the component states. Results of an assembly traversal vary based on the configuration currently displayed in your main assembly and based on the configuration referenced by the subassembly component. The list of child components that this method returns can be different depending on which configuration is referenced by the component (see IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.ReferencedConfiguration">IComponent2::ReferencedConfiguration</see>). For example, if one configuration of your main assembly contains a suppressed subassembly, IComponent2::GetChildren returns an empty array when you call it from that suppressed subassembly component. As another example, a subassembly document (.sldasm file) can contain several configurations, each of which has varying states of suppression for its child components. When inserted into your main assembly, this subassemblydocument can reference any of these configurations. As a result, you might find that the child component suppression states vary based on which configuration is referenced by the subassembly component. NOTE: Components might not be returned in the same order from call to call.

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetModelDoc2">IComponent2::GetModelDoc2</see>.

Example.Name: Get Display Dimensions, GTols, and Surface-finish Symbols

Member.Remarks:
This method might return Nothing or null if:
a component is suppressed or lightweight. the component ID is not loaded into memory by SOLIDWORKS. For more information on lightweight components, see <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Work_with_Lightweight_Components.htm">Work With Lightweight Components</see>. When you use the IModelDoc2 object of a component, you do not have access to whatever uniqueness might exist for this instance of the assembly IComponent2. This occurs because the IModelDoc2 object goes back to the saved part file. By comparison, the IComponent2 object gathers information at the assembly level. This allows IComponent2 objects to recognize assembly-level changes made to a component instance (for example, assembly-level features and material changes). In addition, the IModelDoc2 object returned from this method represents the last-saved state. If the component part is currently open, then the IModelDoc2 object represents the state of the opened document. For example, if the component part is not open and it was last saved in the default configuration, then IComponent2::GetModelDocreturns a IModelDoc2 pointer representing that state. To get access to other configuration information (such as features and configuration properties), you must activate the part and show the desired configuration using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ShowConfiguration2">IModelDoc2::ShowConfiguration2</see>. If this component is the root component, then this method returns a NULL pointer. For more information, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent.</see>

This allows IComponent2 objects to recognize assembly-level changes made to a component instance (for example, assembly-level features and material changes). In addition, the IModelDoc2 object returned from this method represents the last-saved state. Member.Name: GetTessTriStrips
Member.Description: Gets the vertices that make up the shaded picture tessellation for this component.

Parameter.Name: NoConversion
Parameter.Description: True prohibits conversion to user units from system units, false does not

Member.Returns: Array (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Tessellation information is available only when the component is loaded as lightweight. These triangles are intended for graphical display purposes and do not represent a tessellation that could be used, for example, by a machining application. If you need the type of accuracy associated with a machining product, you should traverse the body faces and extract the topology and geometry data to create your own faceting. where:
FaceCount = number of faces on the body StripCount = total number of strips on the body VertexCount x 3 = total number of vertices. Multiplied by three to cover X,Y, and Z NumStrips = number of strips on a particular face VertexPerStrip = an array containing the number of vertex points on particular face strip VertexPoints = an array of X,Y,Z points for each vertex on the particular face strip Because the returned array elements are of type float, and FaceCount, StripCount, VertexCount, NumStrips, and the elements of VertexPerStrip are integers that have been packed into the return array elements, and you must <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_Visual_Basic_.NET_and_Visual_Basic.htm">unpack</see> them before you can use them. For example:
sa[0] = number of faces sa[1] = total number of strips sa[2] = total number of vertices x 3 (i.e., - data values)
For each face:
sa[3] = number of strips in this face sa[4] = number of vertices in first strip of this face sa[5] = number of vertices in second strip of this face
...
sa[3 + sa[3&cd; = number of vertices in last strip of this face
For each strip, i:
sa[3 + sa[3] + 1] = X value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 2] = Y value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 3] = Z value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 4] = X value of second vertex in this strip of the face
...
sa[3 + sa[3] + (sa[3+i] x 3)] = Z value of last vertex in this strip of the face

If you need the type of accuracy associated with a machining product, we recommend that you traverse the body faces and extract the topology and geometry data to create your own faceting. The format of the returned data is:
float x, y, z - first point in meters

Member.Name: IGetBody
Member.Description: Gets the body that belongs to this instance of this component.
Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">IBody2</see> object
Member.Remarks: This method returns a valid IBody2 object only for fully resolved components that reference an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc">IPartDoc</see>. For the root component, lightweight components or components that reference an AssemblyDoc, this method returns a NULL body object. However, if a component is in a multibody part, then this method returns the first body. For COM applications, this method returns the status code ITF_E_COMPONENTNOTRESOLVED. This method is different from the IPartDoc::Body method in that it recognizes assembly-level features and returns that information based on the component instance. IPartDoc::Body never recognizes assembly-level features because the feature information is kept with the assembly, not propagated down to the part file. For example, if PartABC is added to an assembly twice, then changes to that IPartDoc object would affect both instances of the assembly IComponent2. Likewise, querying information from that IPartDoc object will not recognize changes in the assembly that may have altered only one of the components (for example, an assembly-level feature was added to one of the components). However, the component object recognizes the two instances of PartABC as two distinct IComponent2 objects and returns its information from the assembly level. For example, one assembly configuration might have an assembly-level feature that cuts a hole through each of the components in the assembly. Using this method on each of the assembly components returns the body of each component with the hole feature that was applied in this particular configuration. If you switch to the configurationwithout the assembly-level hole and re-traverse the IComponent2 objects, then calling this method for each component returns the IBody2 object without the hole feature because it was applied in the other configuration. For more information on lightweight components, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSuppression">IComponent2::GetSuppression</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.SetSuppression2">IComponent2::SetSuppression2</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ResolveAllLightWeightComponents">IAssemblyDoc::ResolveAllLightWeightComponents</see>.

Member.Name: IGetBox
Member.Description: Gets the bounding box for component.

Parameter.Name: IncludeRefPlanes
Parameter.Description: True includes reference planes with the returned bounding box, false does not

Parameter.Name: IncludeSketches
Parameter.Description: True includes sketches with the returned bounding box, false does not

Member.Returns: Two diagonal points that bound the component; the format is a pointer to an array of 6 doubles
Member.Remarks: The resulting box encloses the object, but it might not be the tightest box. The X, Y, Z points returned by SOLIDWORKS are the lower- and upper-diagonal corners that bound the component with the box sides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes. SOLIDWORKS returns box dimensions that enclose the component and are typically close to the minimum possible size. The return value is an array of doubles as follows: [ XCorner1, YCorner1, ZCorner1, XCorner2, YCorner2, ZCorner2 ] It is possible for this method to return S_false for COM or a NULL VARIANT for Dispatch. This occurs if your application calls IComponent2::IGetBox with a component that represented a subassembly and that subassembly is not loaded. Once the subassembly is loaded, SOLIDWORKS returns the correct bounds and IComponent2::IGetBox returns S_OK. The user interface behavior is the same. When the user selects a subassembly that is not loaded, there is no selection box around the subassembly. However, once the subassembly is loaded, there is a selection box. IMPORTANT: The values returned are approximate and should not be used for comparison or calculation purposes. Furthermore, the bounding box may vary after rebuilding the model.

Member.Name: IGetChildren
Member.Description: Gets all of the children components of this component.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see> objects VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
If this assembly component is a part document, SOLIDWORKS returns NULL. If this assembly component is the root component or a subassembly, then this method returns the child components that belong to the assembly document. The typical order of calls needed in assembly traversal is:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> (called only once) <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent</see> (called only once) IComponent2::GetChildren (called recursively)
COM applications should use to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IGetChildrenCount">IComponent2::IGetChildrenCount</see> to determine the number of component children, which is the size of the array required to IComponent2::IGetChildren. Because IComponent2::IGetChildren returns an array, this code must be used in an in-process DLL. You must call the IComponent2::GetChildren method recursively because it returns only the immediate (one level) children. It does not get child components of the sub-assemblies. For example, if one of the child components of a component is a sub-assembly that has its own children, those children are not returned by this method. You need to call this method again from that sub-assembly component to get its children. For a given component, this method returns all of the immediate child components. This includes suppressed, hidden, and lightweight components. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Visible">IComponent2::Visible</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSuppression">IComponent2::GetSuppression</see> to detect the component states. Results of an assembly traversal vary based on the configuration currently displayed in your main assembly and based on the configuration referenced by the subassembly component. The list of child components that this method returns can be different depending on which configuration is referenced by the component (see IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.ReferencedConfiguration">IComponent2::ReferencedConfiguration</see>). For example, if one configuration of your main assembly contains a suppressed subassembly, IComponent2::GetChildren returns an empty array when you call it from that suppressed subassembly component. As another example, a subassembly document (.sldasm file) can contain several configurations, each of which has varying states of suppression for its child components. When inserted into your main assembly, this subassemblydocument can reference any of these configurations. As a result, you might find that the child component suppression states vary based on which configuration is referenced by the subassembly component. NOTE: Components might not be returned in the same order from call to call.

Member.Name: IGetModelDoc
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetModelDoc2">IComponent2::GetModelDoc2</see>.
Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">model document</see>
Member.Remarks:
This method might return NULL if:
a component is suppressed or lightweight. the component ID is not loaded into memory by SOLIDWORKS. For more information on lightweight components, see <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Work_with_Lightweight_Components.htm">Work With Lightweight Components</see>. When you use the IModelDoc2 object of a component, you do not have access to whatever uniqueness might exist for this instance of the assembly IComponent2. This occurs because the IModelDoc2 object goes back to the saved part file. By comparison, the IComponent2 object gathers information at the assembly level. This allows IComponent2 objects to recognize assembly-level changes made to a component instance (for example, assembly-level features and material changes). In addition, the IModelDoc2 object returned from this method represents the last-saved state. If the component part is currently open, then the IModelDoc2 object represents the state of the opened document. For example, if the component part is not open and it was last saved in the default configuration, then IComponent2::GetModelDocreturns a IModelDoc2 pointer representing that state. To get access to other configuration information (such as features and configuration properties), you must activate the part and show the desired configuration using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ShowConfiguration2">IModelDoc2::ShowConfiguration2</see>. If this component is the root component, then this method returns a NULL pointer. For more information, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.IGetRootComponent2">IConfiguration::IGetRootComponent2.</see>

Member.Name: IGetTessTriStripSize
Member.Description: Gets the array size of floats required to contain the data returned when calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetTessTriStrips">IComponent2::IGetTessTriStrips</see>.

Member.Remarks:

Member.Name: IGetTessTriStrips
Member.Description: Gets the vertices that make up the shaded picture tessellation for this component.

Parameter.Name: NoConversion
Parameter.Description: True prohibits conversion to user units from system units, false does not

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of floats (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
Tessellation information is available only when the component is loaded as lightweight. These triangles are intended for graphical display purposes and do not represent a tessellation that could be used, for example, by a machining application. If you need the type of accuracy associated with a machining product, you should traverse the body faces and extract the topology and geometry data to create your own faceting. where:
FaceCount = number of faces on the body StripCount = total number of strips on the body VertexCount x 3 = total number of vertices. Multiplied by three to cover X,Y, and Z NumStrips = number of strips on a particular face VertexPerStrip = an array containing the number of vertex points on particular face strip VertexPoints = an array of X,Y,Z points for each vertex on the particular face strip Because the returned array elements are of type float, and FaceCount, StripCount, VertexCount, NumStrips, and the elements of VertexPerStrip are integers that have been packed into the return array elements, and you must <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_Visual_Basic_.NET_and_Visual_Basic.htm">unpack</see> them before you can use them. For example:
sa[0] = number of faces sa[1] = total number of strips sa[2] = total number of vertices x 3 (i.e., - data values)
For each face:
sa[3] = number of strips in this face sa[4] = number of vertices in first strip of this face sa[5] = number of vertices in second strip of this face
...
sa[3 + sa[3&cd; = number of vertices in last strip of this face
For each strip, i:
sa[3 + sa[3] + 1] = X value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 2] = Y value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 3] = Z value of first vertex in this strip of the face sa[3 + sa[3] + 4] = X value of second vertex in this strip of the face
...
sa[3 + sa[3] + (sa[3+i] x 3)] = Z value of last vertex in this strip of the face

Member.Name: IMaterialPropertyValues
Member.Description: Gets or sets the material properties for the selected component in the active configuration.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles describing the material's values on this component (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The material values include the component color (R,G,B values), reflectivity (ambient, diffuse, specular, shininess), transparency, and emission. Valid values are from 0 to 1 for all values. The format of the parameters or return values is an array of doubles as follows: [ R, G, B, Ambient, Diffuse, Specular, Shininess, Transparency, Emission ] To see a color change, you must:
Specify R, G, and B, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. (These values are internally multiplied by 255.0 to determine the RGB color.) Specify the reflectivity properties (Diffuse, Specular, Shininess (1.0 - Specular spread/Blurriness)), each with a value greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0. Specify Ambient, Transparency and Emission, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. Refresh the graphics area after setting this property. This method returns an S_false HRESULT for COM implementations if the user has not explicitly modified this component from the material property values of the underlying part document. For example, the user can right-click a component in the FeatureManager design tree and select Component Properties to change the color. If the user has not done this, then this method returns NULL color information. The default component color can be obtained from the component's <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> object (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IGetModelDoc">IComponent2::IGetModelDoc</see>) using IModelDoc2::MaterialPropertyValues. Member.Name: MaterialPropertyValues
Member.Description: Gets or sets the material properties for the selected component in the active configuration.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles that describes the material values on this component (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The material values include the component color (R,G,B values), reflectivity (ambient, diffuse, specular, shininess), transparency, and emission. Valid values are from 0 to 1 for all values. The format of the parameters or return values is an array of doubles as follows: [ R, G, B, Ambient, Diffuse, Specular, Shininess, Transparency, Emission ] To see a color change, you must:
Specify R, G, and B, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. (These values are internally multiplied by 255.0 to determine the RGB color.) Specify the reflectivity properties (Diffuse, Specular, Shininess (1.0 - Specular spread/Blurriness)), each with a value greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0. Specify Ambient, Transparency and Emission, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. Refresh the graphics area after setting this property. This method returns a NULL VARIANT if the user has not explicitly modified this component from the material property values of the underlying part document. For example, the user can right-click a component in the FeatureManager design tree and select Component Properties to change the color. If the user has not done this, then this method returns NULL color information. The default component color can be obtained from the component's <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> object (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetModelDoc">IComponent2::GetModelDoc</see>) using IModelDoc2::MaterialPropertyValues. You might also want to check for specific face colors using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.MaterialPropertyValues">IFace2::MaterialPropertyValues</see>.

Member.Remarks:
This property returns a name that includes an instance number. For example: Part1-1 indicates that this is the first instance of the Part1 Component2. If you are examining a component that is within a subassembly, then this property returns a name that includes the full hierarchical path of component names. For example: subAssem1-2/Part1-1 indicates that this component (Part1) is the first instance within the subAssem1 Component2. It also shows that the second instance of subAssem1 is referenced. If you are setting the name of a component:
Before executing a name change, this property checks the swExtRefUpdateCompNames setting. If swExtRefUpdateCompNames is true, then the name change fails; if swExtRefUpdateCompNames is false, then the name change succeeds. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.GetUserPreferenceToggle">ISldWorks::GetUserPreferenceToggle</see> to change the swExtRefUpdateCompNames setting. Also, remember that some special characters are reserved by SOLIDWORKS, so be sure to use valid characters in the new name.
The component must be selected.

Member.Name: PresentationTransform
Member.Description: Gets or sets the component transform.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">Component transform</see>

Example.Name: Use Presentation Transforms to Move Component

Member.Remarks:
This property affects the graphical display; it does not affect the underlying model geometry. This property:
gets or sets the component transform for graphical display.
ignores all mate and in-context relationships. Only the display of the component on the screen is affected.
does not apply the transform to component geometry.
does not display any changes. To display changes, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>. This property's functionality is for graphical purposes only and does not affect solid models. For example, if you want to animate the explode steps for an assembly, then maintaining assembly mate and in-context relationships is not needed or desirable. You must first enable a presentation transform by setting <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.EnablePresentation">IAssemblyDoc::EnablePresentation</see> to true. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.RemovePresentationTransform">IComponent2::RemovePresentationTransform</see> removes any transform applied by IComponent2::PresentationTransform. Set IAssemblyDoc::EnablePresentation to false after calling IComponent2::RemovePresentationTransform. After calling this method, the component is next drawn in a position consistent with its underlying geometry (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Transform2">IComponent2::Transform2</see>).

Member.Name: ReferencedConfiguration
Member.Description: Gets or sets the active configuration used by this component.
Member.Returns: Name of the configuration

Example.Name: Get Names of Bodies in Multibody Part
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion
Traverse Assembly at Component and Feature Levels Using Recursion

Member.Remarks:
You can use this property to change the active configuration of:
a pattern seed component. pattern instance components, but only when the pattern's ForceUseSeedConfiguration property is set to false. When the configuration is changed, components might become suppressed or unsuppressed. This means that the array previously returned from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetChildren">IComponent2::GetChildren</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IGetChildren">IComponent2::IGetChildren</see> becomes invalid. If an application is traversing an assembly and calls IComponent2::ReferencedConfiguration, then it should stop the traversal and start again by getting the assembly's <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> and active configuration. The array previously returned from IComponent2::GetChildren or IComponent2::IGetChildren should be released before calling IComponent2::ReferencedConfiguration. To hold onto the changed component, you can perform an extra AddRef() on that component before freeing the array. After changing the referenced configuration, you must call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.EditRebuild3">IModelDoc2::EditRebuild3</see> to display the changes.

Member.Description: Sets the features, components, and feature references of a Smart Component.

Parameter.Name: FeaturesSelected
Parameter.Description: Array of boolean values indicating which features to enable in the Smart Component (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ComponentsSelected
Parameter.Description: Array of boolean values indicating which components to enable in the Smart Component (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Activate Smart Features in an Assembly
Activate Smart Features in an Assembly
Activate Smart Features in an Assembly

Member.Remarks:
A Smart Component is defined by its:
Components Features Feature references See the SOLIDWORKS Help for more information about Smart Components. Use this method to:
Change which features and components to enable in a Smart Component. Activate the Smart Features. Before calling this method:
Open an assembly that contains a Smart Component whose Smart Features have not yet been activated. Find the Smart Component in the assembly using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IsSmartComponent">IComponent2::IsSmartComponent</see>. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSmartComponentData">IComponent2::GetSmartComponentData</see> to obtain the current feature and component arrays for the Smart Component. Create two boolean arrays whose elements map one-to-one with the elements in the feature and component arrays. For each element in each boolean array, specify true if the corresponding feature or component is enabled in the Smart Component. Specify false if it is not. Set FeaturesSelected and ComponentsSelected with the corresponding boolean arrays. Create an array of reference entities (e.g., faces, edges, points) selected from the target assembly that map to the feature reference entities that were defined for the Smart Component. Set References to the array of reference entities. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISmartComponentFeatureData">ISmartComponentFeatureData</see> to:
Insert new features and components into a Smart Component. Delete features and components from a Smart Component.

Member.Remarks: This property affects the underlying model geometry and the display of the component. You must specify the transform in relation to the root component. This also applies when there is an in-context edit in progress. The transform is still with respect to the root component of the active assembly document, not with respect to the root component of the edit target. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.IGetRootComponent2">IConfiguration::IGetRootComponent2</see>. The destination component, or any component above it in the assembly tree, is moved so that the destination component's transform is set to the desired one. You can call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.Rebuild">IModelDoc2::Rebuild</see> with the swUpdateMates argument to rebuild the model after transforming a component. This is much faster than rebuilding all of the geometry for the model using the now obsolete IAssemblyDoc::EditRebuild. This property lets you violate existing mate relationships. If you place a component at an invalid location based on the mate definitions, then IModelDoc2::Rebuild recalculates existing mate relationships and moves your components to the closest valid location. After you change a component's transform, you can call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.UpdateBox">IAssemblyDoc::UpdateBox</see> to avoid clipping in shaded display mode.

Member.Signature: AddExplodeStep2( System.double ExplDist, System.int ExplDirIndex, System.bool ReverseDir, System.double ExplAng, System.int RotAxisIndex, System.bool ReverseAng, System.bool RotateAboutOrigin, System.bool AutoSpaceComponentsOnDrag, out System.int Error )
Member.Description: Adds a regular (translate and rotate) explode step to the explode view of the active configuration.

Parameter.Name: ExplDist
Parameter.Description: Distance in meters to move the components in this explode step

Parameter.Name: ExplDirIndex
Parameter.Description: Explode direction manipulator index as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swExplodeDirectionIndex_e">swExplodeDirectionIndex_e</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ReverseDir
Parameter.Description: True to reverse the explode direction, false to not

Parameter.Name: ExplAng
Parameter.Description: Angle in radians of component rotation (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: RotAxisIndex
Parameter.Description: Rotation manipulator index as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swRotationAxisIndex_e">swRotationAxisIndex_e</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ReverseAng
Parameter.Description: True to reverse the direction of ExplAng, false to not

Parameter.Name: RotateAboutOrigin
Parameter.Description: True if each component rotates about its origin, false if not (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: AutoSpaceComponentsOnDrag
Parameter.Description: True to automatically space components on drag, false to not (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Error
Parameter.Description: Error code as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swCreateExplodeStepError_e">swCreateExplodeStepError_e</see>

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep">Explode step</see>
Member.Remarks:
This method:
Is valid only for an active current explode view. To create an explode view, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AutoExplode">IAssemblyDoc::AutoExplode</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateExplodedView">IAssemblyDoc::CreateExplodedView</see>. Always clears the selection list. Does not work if the Explode PropertyManager is open. Does not work if any component is being edited in the context of the assembly. If AutoSpaceComponentsOnDrag is set to true, then RotateAboutOrigin is false and ExplAng is 0.0. Set AutoSpaceComponentsOnDrag to false to specify other values for RotateAboutOrigin and ExplAng. Before calling this method, you must:
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> to get the active configuration for the assembly. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ShowExploded2">IAssemblyDoc::ShowExploded2</see> to activate an explode view. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select:
Components to move with Mark = 1. (Optionally) An explode direction entity (cylindrical <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>, conical face, linear <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRefAxis">axis</see>) with Mark = 2. Either, both, or neither of the direction entity and ExplDirIndex can be set. If neither, then the Z-direction manipulator index is used. (Optionally) A rotation axis with Mark = 32. Valid only if RotateAboutOrigin is set to false. Either, both, or neither of the rotation axis and RotAxisIndex can be set. If neither, then the XY ring index is used.
