To create an explode view, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AutoExplode">IAssemblyDoc::AutoExplode</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateExplodedView">IAssemblyDoc::CreateExplodedView</see>. Always clears the selection list. Does not work if the Explode PropertyManager is open. Does not work if any component is being edited in the context of the assembly. Before calling this method, you must:
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> to get the active configuration for the assembly. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ShowExploded2">IAssemblyDoc::ShowExploded2</see> to activate an explode view. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select:
Components to move with Mark = 1. An explode direction entity (cylindrical <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>, conical face, linear <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRefAxis">axis</see>) with Mark = 34. A diverge direction entity (cylindrical face, conical face, linear edge, or axis) with Mark = 64. The selected entity must form an angle with the direction entity. If DivergeFromAxis is set to true and an invalid diverge direction is selected, then DivergeFromAxis is set to false, and the direction entity is set to null. If DivergeFromAxis is set to false, then the direction entity is set to null.

Member.Name: GetRootComponent
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent3">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent3</see>.
Member.Returns: Root component and an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see> object

Example.Name: Get Display Dimensions, GTols, and Surface-finish Symbols
Get Names of Bodies in Multibody Part
Traverse Assembly At Component and Feature Levels

Member.Remarks:
Because every assembly has at least one configuration, you can use this method to begin traversing an assembly and its components. This method returns a component object that is, essentially, a launching point for your assembly traversal. It is useful only for calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetChildren">IComponent2::GetChildren</see>. Most other IComponent2 object functions do not work with this root component object and return null or Nothing or an error condition. You can call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IsRoot">IComponent2::IsRoot</see> to determine if you have the root component. An IComponent2 object is based on the currently active configuration; one assembly configuration might suppress the component, while another might display it. Therefore, your traversal of IComponent2 objects might vary if you switch to a different configuration. The order of calls used in a typical assembly traversal is:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> (called only once) IConfiguration::GetRootComponent (called only once) IComponent2::GetChildren (called recursively) From the SOLIDWORKS API, the IConfiguration and IComponent2 objects provide access to all the child components, their transforms, their bodies, as seen in a specific assembly configuration. The component body objects and component transforms can vary based on the configuration; therefore, you should traverse components for each configuration. For example, one assembly configuration might include an assembly-level feature that cuts a hole through each of the components in the assembly. You can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetBody">IComponent2::GetBody</see> on each assembly component to get the body of each component with the hole feature that was applied in this configuration. If you switch to a configuration without the assembly-level hole and re-traverse the component objects, then IComponent2::IGetBody returns the body object without the hole feature. SOLIDWORKS generates an IAssemblyDoc <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DAssemblyDocEvents_RegenNotifyEventHandler">RegenNotify</see> event to indicate that a change might have taken place in one of your components. If you receive an IAssemblyDoc RegenNotify event, then you should re-traverse your components to be sure that your information is up-to-date. If this method is called from the configuration of a part document, SOLIDWORKS returns null or Nothing. You should use this method of assembly traversal to replace previous calls to the member class.

Member.Name: IGetRootComponent
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.IGetRootComponent2">IConfiguration::IGetRootComponent2</see>.

Member.Name: IGetRootComponent2
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetRootComponent3">IConfiguration::GetRootComponent3</see>.
Member.Returns: Pointer to the root component, an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see> object
Member.Remarks:
Because every assembly has at least one configuration, you can use this method to begin traversing an assembly and its components. This method returns a component object that is, essentially, a launching point for your assembly traversal. It is useful only for calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IGetChildren">IComponent2::IGetChildren</see>. Most other IComponent2 object functions do not work with this root component object and return NULL or an error condition. You can call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IsRoot">IComponent2::IsRoot</see> to determine if you have the root component. An IComponent2 object is based on the currently active configuration; one assembly configuration might suppress the component, while another might display it. Therefore, your traversal of IComponent2 objects might vary if you switch to a different configuration. The order of calls used in a typical assembly traversal is:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> (called only once) IConfiguration::IGetRootComponent 2(called only once) IComponent2::IGetChildren (called recursively) From the SOLIDWORKS API, the IConfiguration and IComponent2 objects provide access to all the child components, their transforms, their bodies, as seen in a specific assembly configuration. The component body objects and component transforms can vary based on the configuration; therefore, you should traverse components for each configuration. For example, one assembly configuration might include an assembly-level feature that cuts a hole through each of the components in the assembly. You can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.IGetBody">IComponent2::IGetBody</see> on each assembly component to get the body of each component with the hole feature that was applied in this configuration. If you switch to a configuration without the assembly-level hole and re-traverse the component objects, then IComponent2::IGetBody returns the body object without the hole feature. SOLIDWORKS generates an IAssemblyDoc <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DAssemblyDocEvents_RegenNotifyEventHandler">RegenNotify</see> event to indicate that a change might have taken place in one of your components. If you receive an IAssemblyDoc RegenNotify event, then you should re-traverse your components to be sure that your information is up-to-date. If this method is called from the configuration of a part document, SOLIDWORKS returns NULL. You should use this method of assembly traversal to replace previous calls to the member class.

Member.Name: IsLoaded
Member.Description: Gets whether a configuration is loaded.
Member.Returns: True if the configuration is loaded, false if not
Member.Remarks: When a configuration is activated, SOLIDWORKS loads it. For example, if a part or assembly document has three configurations named DC1, DC2, and DC3, and DC1 is the active configuration when you open the document, then this method will return true for DC1 and false for DC2 and DC3. If you activate the configuration named DC2, then this method will return true for DC1 and DC2 because DC1 was previously loaded. If you activate the configuration named DC3, then this method will return true for DC1, DC2, and DC3 because DC1 and DC2 were previously loaded and DC3 is now loaded.

Member.Name: SetConfigurationParams
Member.Signature: SetConfigurationParams( System.string ConfigName, ref System.object ParamNames, ref System.object ParamValues )
Member.Description: Sets the parameters for this configuration.

Parameter.Name: ConfigName
Parameter.Description: Name of the configuration (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ParamNames
Parameter.Description: Array of the names of the parameters for ConfigName (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ParamValues
Parameter.Description: Array of values for the parameters for ConfigName (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if the names and values of parameters for the specified configuration are set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
In ConfigName, if you specify the name of a configuration that:
does not exist, this method creates a new configuration with ParamNames and ParamValues. exists, this method sets that configuration with ParamNames and ParamValues. You can control these parameters in a part document:
Dimension values. Specify the dimension name in ParamNames for example, D1@Sketch1) and the value in ParamValues (for example, 60.0mm). Suppression state of features. Specify the feature name in ParamNames (for example, $STATE@Extrude2) and the suppression state in ParamValues (S=Suppressed or R=Resolved).

Member.Name: ConvertArcToBcurve
Member.Signature: ConvertArcToBcurve( System.object Center, System.object Axis, System.object Start, System.object End )
Member.Description: Gets the b-spline value representation of the arc.

Parameter.Name: Center
Parameter.Description: Array for the x, y, z coordinates of the center point of thearc

Parameter.Name: Axis
Parameter.Description: Array for the normal vector of the arc

Parameter.Name: Start
Parameter.Description: Array for the x, y, z coordinates of the start point of the arc

Parameter.Name: End
Parameter.Description: Array for the x, y, z coordinates of the end point of the arc

Member.Returns: Array for the b-spline representation of the arc
Member.Remarks:
Given coordinates of the center, start, end points and the normal vector of an arc, this method returns the b-spline representation of the arc. The returned data are doubles arranged in the following order:
dim, order Two integers packed into a double.
dim
Dimension of the control point data. If dim=3 (non-rational), control point coordinates are returned as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.....]. If dim=4 (rational), control point coordinates are returned as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,.....], where w is the weight for the point.
order
Order of the b-spline returned.
NumControlPoints, Periodic Two integers packed into a double.
NumControlPoints
Number of control points for the b-spline.
Periodic
True if the b-spline is periodic.
Knots Knot vectors. The Knot array contains (NumControlPoints + order) knot values. If the original curve is periodic, then the data is returned in a non-periodic form with extra knots inserted at the curve ends.
ControlPoints List of control points output in (NumControlPoints) vectors of dimension dim. For non-rational b-spline, control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........]. For rational b-spline, control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........], where w is the weight for the point.

order
Order of the b-spline returned.
NumControlPoints, Periodic Two integers packed into a double.
NumControlPoints
Number of control points for the b-spline.
Periodic
True if the b-spline is periodic.
Knots Knot vectors. The Knot array contains (NumControlPoints + order) knot values. If the original curve is periodic, then the data is returned in a non-periodic form with extra knots inserted at the curve ends.
ControlPoints List of control points output in (NumControlPoints) vectors of dimension dim. For non-rational b-spline, control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........]. For rational b-spline, control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........], where w is the weight for the point.

Member.Remarks: This method trims the curve from the start point to the end point in a parametric direction. It returns NULL if the curve is discontinued or non-linear between the points. If your application calls <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.CreateTrimmedSheet4">ISurface::CreateTrimmedSheet4</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.ICreateTrimmedSheet4">ISurface::ICreateTrimmedSheet4</see> to create a sheet with a boundary defined by arcs (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.CreateArc">IModeler::CreateArc</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.ICreateArc">IModeler::ICreateArc</see>) or lines (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.CreateLine">IModeler::CreateLine</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.ICreateLine">IModeler::ICreateLine</see>), then your application must first call this method to trim the arc and line curves before passing them to ISurface::CreateTrimmedSheet4 or ISurface::ICreateTrimmedSheet4. If your application calls ISurface::CreateTrimmedSheet4 or ISurface::ICreateTrimmedSheet4 to create a sheet with an elliptical boundary (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.CreateEllipse">IModeler::CreateEllipse</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.ICreateEllipse">IModeler::ICreateEllipse</see>), then you do not need to trim the elliptical curve before passing it to ISurface::CreateTrimmedSheet4 or ISurface::ICreateTrimmedSheet4.

Member.Name: GetBCurveParams5
Member.Signature: GetBCurveParams5( System.bool WantCubicIn, System.bool WantNRational, System.bool ForceNonPeriodic, System.bool IsClosed )
Member.Description: Gets a data object containing the parameters of a Bézier curve.

Parameter.Name: WantCubicIn
Parameter.Description: True to return cubic parameters, false to not

Parameter.Name: WantNRational
Parameter.Description: True to return non-rational parameters; false to return rational parameters

Parameter.Name: ForceNonPeriodic
Parameter.Description: True to convert the curve from periodic to nonperiodic, false to not (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: IsClosed
Parameter.Description: True for a closed curve, false for an open curve (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: An <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData">ISplineParamData</see> object (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: To control the accuracy of the curve data, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModeler.SetToleranceValue">IModeler::SetToleranceValue</see>. If a Bézier curve is closed (IsClosed = true) and periodic (ForceNonPeriodic = false), the seam at the juncture of the beginning and end of the curve is continuous and smooth. The data returned in this form contains a single knot at the juncture. If a Bézier curve is closed (IsClosed = true) and non-periodic (ForceNonPeriodic = true), the seam at the juncture is continuous, contains a cusp, and is not smooth. The data returned in this form contains multiple knots at each end of the curve. Obsolete versions of this method automatically treated closed Bézier curves as periodic. The cusp at the juncture of a closed non-periodic curve (e.g., a tear drop) was lost using these methods. This method provides more flexibility for specifying precisely which form of the curve to get to prevent unintentional data loss. This method returns the parameterization data of the Bézier curve in an ISplineParamData object instead of an array. Call the methods and properties of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData">ISplineParamData</see> to obtain the control points, knot points, dimension, order, and periodicity of the curve.

Member.Remarks: This method returns the curve as a series of segments, each of which has this form: (w0*a0 + w1*a1*t + w2*a2*t**2 + w3*a3*t**3) p(t) = -------------------------------------------- (w0 + w1*t + w2*t**2 + w3*t**3) Where w is the weight coefficient and a is the polynomial coefficient. The coefficients returned are vectors of dimensions "dim". For example, if the curve is rational, then dimension = 4, and the coefficients returned for each segment are as follows: (a0x,a0y,a0z,w0),(a1x,a1y,a1z,w1)... However, if the curve is returned as non-rational, then dimension = 3, and its coefficients are: (a0x,a0y,a0z),(a1x,a1y,a1z),... The size of the return value array is (3 + NumberKnots + NumberSegments x Order x Dimension). The array is as follows: [ packedDouble1, packedDouble2, packedDouble3, knot1, knot2,..., CoefficientsSegment1[Dimension], CoefficientsSegment2[Dimension],... ] where: packedDouble1: Integer pair containing Reserved and Order packedDouble2: Integer pair containing NumberSegments and Periodicity packedDouble3: Integer pair containing NumberKnots and Dimension knot1 knot2 ... CoefficientsSegment1[Dimension] CoefficientsSegment2[Dimension] ... The coefficients for each segment start with the constant term and end with the term of highest degree (for example, ConstantX, ConstantY, ConstantZ, AX, AY, AZ, BX, BY, BZ). The total number of coefficients is: (NumberSegments) x (Order) x (Dimension).

Member.Description: Gets the spline points for this curve.

Parameter.Name: ParamsArrayIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing the definition of the spline

Member.Returns: Array containing the spline points

Example.Name: Get Length of Spline or Elliptical Edge
Get Parameters and Spline Points for Curve

Member.Remarks:
For OLE Automation applications, the ParamsIn argument contains an array defining the spline. This array contains the values for propArray, knotsArray and cntrlPntCoordArray, all packed into a single array (propArray is packed as four integers into the first two elements of the array.) The contents of these arrays is described in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurve.IGetSplinePtsSize">ICurve::IGetSplinePtsSize</see>. The array returned contains the x, y, z location of the spline points:
[ x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2,....] Data passed into this method must satisfy the following requirements:
If the curve is periodic, it must not have any repeated knots. If the curve is non-periodic, it must only have repeated knots at its ends. The curve must be cubic or lower degree, non-rational, and have continuous firstand second derivatives. NOTE: For a linear or quadratic curve to satisfy these continuity requirements, it must consist of a single segment.

Member.Name: IConvertPcurveToBcurveSize
Member.Signature: IConvertPcurveToBcurveSize( System.int Dim, System.int Order, System.int Nsegs, ref System.double Coeffs, System.int Basis, ref System.double Xform, System.double ScaleFactor )
Member.Description: Creates a b-curve from piecewise data.

Parameter.Name: Dim
Parameter.Description:
Dimension of the curve:
3 = nonrational
4 = rational

Parameter.Name: Order
Parameter.Description: Order of the curve; minimum is 2 (linear)

Parameter.Name: Nsegs
Parameter.Description: Number of segments in the curve; must be at least 1

Parameter.Name: Coeffs
Parameter.Description: Array of coefficients

Parameter.Name: Basis
Parameter.Description: 0; not currently used

Parameter.Name: Xform
Parameter.Description: Transformation matrix to apply after conversion to b-curve

Parameter.Name: ScaleFactor
Parameter.Description: Units conversion factor to apply after conversion to b-curve

Member.Returns: Indicates that conversion succeeded or failed
Member.Remarks:
Dimension of coefficient vectors dim:
For rational curves dim = 4.
For non-rational curves dim = 3. Order of each segment of the curve order:
The order of the curve = degree + 1.
The minimum order is 2. Number of segments in the curve nseg:
There must be at least one segment (nseg >= 1).
Adjacent segments must meet. Coefficient data coeffs:
Contains order * nseg vectors of dimension dim. If dim = 3, then the vectors are 3-D vectors giving the x, y and z components. If dim = 4, then each vector has a weight (w) associated with it, and x, y, z and w components are supplied for each vector. The weights supplied must be greater than 0.
The coefficients are supplied in order, segment by segment.
The interpretation of the coefficients depends on the representation method chosen; this is determined by the value of the argument basis. Representation method basis: The expressions for each segment of the B-curve P(t) in the various representations are shown next. For generality, the rational form is given. The simplification to the non-rational form can be obtained by setting both the weights and the denominator equal to 1.0 Polynomial coefficients: The curve equation is given by a rational polynomial of order 'order': n n -- i / -- i P(t) = > w A t / > w t -- i i / -- i i=0 i=0 where n = order-1 A = polynomial coefficient i w = weight for A i i The polynomial coefficients are supplied starting with the constant term and ending with the term of highest degree.

Member.Name: SetFeatureScope
Member.Signature: SetFeatureScope( System.bool FeatureScopeOption, System.bool AutoSelectBodies, System.object Bodies )
Member.Description: Sets the feature scope, whether to autoselect the affected bodies, and the affected bodies in this curve-driven pattern feature.

Parameter.Name: FeatureScopeOption
Parameter.Description: True to specify affected bodies, false to apply the pattern to all bodies every time the feature regenerates (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: AutoSelectBodies
Parameter.Description: True to automatically select all bodies intersected by this pattern feature, false to specify affected bodies (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Bodies
Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> to be affected; valid only if FeatureScopeOption is true and AutoSelectBodies is false

Member.Returns: True if feature scope set successfully, false if not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: If this method returns false, then default values for FeatureScopeOption and AutoSelectBodies are set. A subsequent call to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> creates the feature with a FeatureScopeOption of true and an AutoSelectBodies of true. After calling IFeature::ModifyDefinition, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetErrorCode2">IFeature::GetErrorCode2</see> to determine what's wrong and then take necessary remedial action. For more information, see the Curve Driven Patterns and the Curve Driven Pattern PropertyManager topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Description: Gets or sets the skipped items for this curve-driven pattern feature.
Member.Returns: Array of integers representing the skipped items
Member.Remarks: This array is 0-based. If you skip the third and fifth items, then the array looks like ArrayOut[0]=3 and ArrayOut[1]=5. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Name: VarySketch
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to allow pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to enclosing geometry in this curve-driven pattern feature.
Member.Returns: True to allow pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to enclosing geometry, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only when creating a pattern from a seed sketch. The seed sketch has:
An enclosing boundary of base geometry. Fully defined relations. Dimensions only for measurements that will not vary in the pattern instances. A driving dimension that is used to specify the direction of the curve-driven pattern. If this property is true:
Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICurveDrivenPatternFeatureData.D1Direction">ICurveDrivenPatternFeatureData::D1Direction</see> with a driving dimension of the seed sketch. Pattern instances vary with and are constrained by the enclosing geometry. See the SOLIDWORKS Help > Parts and Features > Features > Patterns and Mirroring > Control and Modify Patterns > Vary Sketch topic. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Description: Gets whether the curve and edge are in the same direction.
Member.Returns: True if curve and edge are in the same direction, false if not
Member.Remarks: If this method returns False, then the curve and edge are in opposite directions. In that case, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.StartPoint">ICurveParamData::StartPoint</see> corresponds to the end of the edge, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.EndPoint">ICurveParamData::EndPoint</see> corresponds to the start of the edge.

Member.Name: StartPoint
Member.Description: Gets the x, y, and z coordinates for the start point of the curve.
Member.Returns: Array of three doubles
Member.Remarks: If <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.Sense">ICurveParamData::Sense</see> returns false, then the curve and edge are in opposite directions. In that case, start point corresponds to the end of the edge, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.EndPoint">ICurveParamData::EndPoint</see> corresponds to the start of the edge.

Member.Name: UMaxValue
Member.Description: Gets the maximum U parameter value.
Member.Returns: Maximum U parameter value
Member.Remarks: The minimum U parameter must always be smaller than the maximum U parameter. If the curve and edge are in opposite directions (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.Sense">ICurveParamData::Sense</see> returns false) and the minimum U parameter is larger than the maximum U parameter, then the parameters are in negative parameter space. For example, if ICurveParamData::Sense is false, minimum U parameter is 10, and maximum U parameter is 5, then <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.UMinValue">ICurveParamData::UMinValue</see> = -10 and ICurveParamData::UMaxValue = -5. To normalize the values in positive parameter space, swap the two U parameter values and then negate them, so that the values of the minimum U parameter is 5 and the maximum U parameter is 10. If the curve is closed and the curve starts and ends at the same point, then ICurveParamData::UMinValue and ICurveParamData::UMaxValue are a period apart.

Member.Name: UMinValue
Member.Description: Gets the minimum U parameter value.
Member.Returns: Minimum U parameter value
Member.Remarks: The minimum U parameter must always be smaller than the maximum U parameter. If the curve and edge are in opposite directions (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.Sense">ICurveParamData::Sense</see> returns false) and the minimum U parameter is larger than the maximum U parameter, then the parameters are in negative parameter space. For example, if ICurveParamData::Sense is false, minimum U parameter is 10, and maximum U parameter is 5, then ICurveParamData::UMinValue = -10 and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurveParamData.UMaxValue">ICurveParamData::UMaxValue</see> = -5. To normalize the values in positive parameter space, swap the two U parameter values and then negate them, so that the values of the minimum U parameter is 5 and the maximum U parameter is 10. If the curve is closed and the curve starts and ends at the same point, then ICurveParamData::UMinValue and ICurveParamData::UMaxValue are a period apart.

If you always want up-to-date data, then you should set UseCached to false. If the configuration is not previously activated, this method might take longer, as it loops through all of the model's configurations to find the specified custom property. When it finishes, the model might not be in its original configuration. To return the model to its original configuration, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ForceRebuild3">IModelDoc2::ForceRebuild3</see> after calling this method. This method does not preface the resolved evaluated values of external referenced documents with fromparent+, unlike the now obsolete ICustomPropertyManager::Get3.

Member.Name: IGetAxisPoints2
Member.Description: Gets the points that define the geometry of this datum origin.
Member.Returns:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of 8 doubles is 4 (X,Y) coordinates in drawing space:
The first coordinate (array items 0 and 1) is the start of the X leader portion of the symbol.
The second coordinate (array items 2 and 3) is the tip of the arrowhead on the X leader portion of the symbol.
The third coordinate (array items 4 and 5) is the start of the Y leader portion of the symbol.
The fourth coordinate (array items 6 and 7) is the tip of the arrowhead on the Y leader portion of the symbol. VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Name: ISetAxisPoints
Member.Description: Sets the points that define the geometry of this datum origin.

Parameter.Name: PointData
Parameter.Description: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of 4 doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Returns: True if the points are set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method gives you control over the shape of the symbol. The array of 4 doubles is 2 (X,Y) coordinates in drawing space:
The first coordinate (array items 0 and 1) is the tip of the arrowhead on the X leader portion of the symbol.
The second coordinate (array items 2 and 3) is the tip of the arrowhead on the Y leader portion of the symbol. The interactive user has this control via the selection drag handles of the symbol. This method returns a BOOLEAN indicating success or failure of the operation. The operation can fail if either of the coordinates is so close to the symbol origin that the symbol cannot be drawn properly. There must be:
Room to draw the arrow at the end of the origin leaders
A gap between the symbol origin and the beginning of the first leader. You can get:
Coordinates of the symbol origin using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetPosition">IAnnotation::GetPosition</see>.
Arrowhead length using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceDouble">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceDouble</see> - swDetailingArrowWidth
Gap using IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceDouble - swDetailingWitnessLineGap

Member.Name: Reattach
Member.Description: Attaches the datum origin to a different entity.
Member.Returns: True if the datum origin is attached to a different entity, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method:
Lets you manipulate the datum origin. It attaches the datum origin to the currently selected entity. Expects that only one entity (vertex, edge, or sketch point) is selected. That selected entity must be in the same view as the original entity to which the datum origin was attached.

Parameter.Description: Target area shape or style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swDatumTargetAreaShape_e">swDatumTargetAreaShape_e</see>

Member.Remarks:
If the target area style for this symbol is...
Then...
Point
There is one size value, which might be empty. Retrieve the text using an index value of 0. SOLIDWORKS displays the text in the upper half of the symbol, preceded by a diameter character.
Circle
There is one size value. Retrieve the text using an index value of 0. SOLIDWORKS displays the text in the upper half of the symbol, preceded by a diameter character.
Rectangle

Member.Name: SeedPosition
Member.Description: Gets or sets which pattern instance to use as the seed feature for this derived pattern feature.
Member.Returns: Pattern instance to use as the seed feature (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: The seed position is the index of a pattern instance, feature, or component that is part of an existing pattern and is used to drive the derived pattern feature. The total number of seed positions = total number of pattern instances in the pattern used to create the derived pattern feature. If the pattern used to create the derived pattern has pattern instances in Direction 1 and Direction 2, then the total number of seed positions = ((Number pattern instances in Direction 1) * (Number pattern instances in Direction 2) - 1). Setting the seed position outside of the range of pattern instances is silently rejected, and the seed position remains unchanged. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Name: GetArrowInfo
Member.Description: Gets the position of the arrows for this detail circle.
Member.Returns: Array containing the arrow position information
Member.Remarks: The section line in a drawing view has arrows at each end of the line. This method returns an array that contains 12 doubles, the (X, Y, Z) of the start and end point of one arrow, followed by the (X, Y, Z) of the start and end point of the other arrow. These values match some of the information in the array returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetSectionLineInfo2">IView::GetSectionLineInfo2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetSectionLineInfo2">IViewIGetSectionLineInfo2</see>; the arrow information near the middle of the array. The arrow information in that array also contains the arrow width, height, and style, which is not in the array returned by this method. To get this information using document preference settings, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceDouble">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceDouble</see> with swDetailingSectionArrowHeight, swDetailingSectionArrowWidth, or swDetailingSectionArrowLength, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceInteger">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceInteger</see> with swDetailingArrowStyleForDimensions.

Member.Name: GetLeaderInfo
Member.Description: Gets the leader information for this detail circle.
Member.Returns: Array (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
There can be 0, 1 or 2 lines in the leader line. If the GTol is not attached, there are 0 lines. Otherwise, leaders can use a straight leaderline (1 line) or a bent leaderline (2 lines). Your applications must infer the number of leader lines based on <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IsAttached">IGtol::IsAttached</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.HasExtraLeader">IGtol::HasExtraLeader</see>.
IsAttached() == false implies no leaderline, therefore, no leaderline points (PointCount=0). HasExtraLeader() == false means that this is a straight leaderline, therefore, 1 line (PointCount=2) HasExtraLeader() == True means that this is a bent leaderline, therefore, 2 lines (PointCount=3) Format of return information is the following array of doubles:
retval[0] = X-coordinate of first leader point retval[1] = Y-coordinate of first leader point retval[2] = Z-coordinate of first leader point retval[3] = X-coordinate of second leader point retval[4] = Y-coordinate of second leader point retval[5] = Z-coordinate of second leader point retval[6] = X-coordinate of third leader point retval[7] = Y-coordinate of third leader point retval[8] = Z-coordinate of third leader point

You can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDimension.ReadOnly">IDimension::ReadOnly</see> to determine if a dimension is read-only.

Member.Name: ReferencePoints
Member.Description: Gets or sets the reference points for this dimension.
Member.Returns: Reference points (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: The returned objects, the reference points, are actually <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathPoint">IMathPoint</see> objects. Reference point 1 and reference point 2 are valid for linear dimensions. Reference point 3 is the vertex for angular dimensions. This property does not distinguish between linear or angular dimensions or other types of dimensions. Three reference points are always returned. NOTE: When regenerating a <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/macro_features/Overview_of_Macro_Features.htm">macro feature</see>, this property gets and sets the reference points of a display dimension (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">IDisplayDimension</see> object). In all other cases, this property gets and sets the reference points of a dimension (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDimension">IDimension</see> object).

Member.Name: SetArcEndCondition
Member.Description: Sets the end conditions for linear dimensions that end on an arc.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of the endpoint on which to set the end condition; 1 is the first endpoint, 2 is the second endpoint

Parameter.Name: Condition
Parameter.Description: End condition as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swArcEndCondition_e">swArcEndCondition_e</see>

Member.Returns:
Indicates the success or failure of this method:
0 Command was successful; the arc end condition was set
-1 Command failed for an unknown reason; the arc end condition was not set
-2 Index parameter is invalid
-3 Condition parameter is invalid
-4 Endpoint 1 is not related to an arc
-5 Endpoint 2 is not related to an arc
Member.Remarks: Linear dimensions measure the distance from one point to another. If one or both of those points is on an arc, the point can be changed to the center point of the arc, the nearest point on the arc, or the furthest point on the arc. The arc end condition describes which point to use. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDimension.GetArcEndCondition">IDimension::GetArcEndCondition</see> to get the arc end conditions. To see the effects of changing the arc endpoint conditions, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> to redraw the graphics window.

Member.Name: GetAutoArcLengthLeader
Member.Description: Gets whether the leader style of this arc-length dimension is being automatically selected or selected by the user.
Member.Returns: True if the leader style is selected automatically , false if the leader style is selected by the user
Member.Remarks: The leader style of an arc-length dimension is specific to each display dimension. It can be parallel (the leaders are parallel to each other) or radial (the leaders are perpendicular to the extension line and would extend through the center of the arc). SOLIDWORKS can automatically select the style, or it can be specified by the user. Use IDisplayDimension::GetAutoArcLengthLeader to determine whether the leader type is selected automatically. This method gets the leader style stored on this display dimension. If this display dimension is set to select the leader type automatically, then this method might return a value that is different from what is displayed. This method applies to only arc length dimensions. It returns -1 if you run it on any other types of dimensions.

Member.Name: GetBentLeaderLength
Member.Description: Gets the length of the bent leader to use when displaying this dimension.
Member.Returns: Length of the bent leader in system units
Member.Remarks: This method returns the length of the bent leader regardless of how the dimension is currently being displayed. Even if the dimension is not currently being displayed with a bent leader, this method still returns the length. If the dimension is using the document default setting for dimension bent leader length, this method returns that value. You can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.GetUseDocBentLeaderLength">IDisplayDimension::GetUseDocBentLeaderLength</see> to determine if this dimension is using the document default setting for dimensionbent leader length or not.

Member.Name: GetBrokenLeader2

Member.Returns: Broken leader value as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swDisplayDimensionLeaderText_e">swDisplayDimensionLeaderText_e</see>
Member.Remarks: Dimension text can be displayed above a solid leader line or the dimension leader line can be broken with the text displayed either horizontal or aligned with the leader line. You can use this method to determine which setting is used by this display dimension. The setting can be local to the display dimension, or the display dimension might use the default document setting. This method returns a valid value only if it is using a local setting; if this display dimension uses the default document setting, it returns -1. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.SetBrokenLeader2">IDisplayDimension::SetBrokenLeader2</see> to set this value.

Member.Name: GetRoundToFraction
Member.Description: Gets whether the displayed dimension value is rounded off so that SOLIDWORKS can display it as a fraction.
Member.Returns: True rounds off the displayed dimension value to a fraction, false does not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: The unit display settings of a display dimension are controlled by a value that SOLIDWORKS stores in one of two places: on the owning document or on the individual display dimension. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.GetUseDocUnits">IDisplayDimension::GetUseDocUnits</see> to determine whether this IDisplayDimension uses the document default or a specific value set for this IDisplayDimension. If this display dimension uses local unit information, then the return value indicates whether the displayed value of this dimension is rounded off to a value that SOLIDWORKS can represent as a fraction. Fraction display is valid only for unit types swINCHES or swFEETINCHES. In all other cases, this method returns -1. Member.Remarks: For diameter dimensions, the second outside arrow is the arrow that appears on the opposite side of the arc from the dimension text. Display of this arrow is optional, and is controlled by a value stored in one of two places: on the owning document or on the individual display dimension. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.GetUseDocSecondArrow">IDisplayDimension::GetUseDocSecondArrow</see> to determine whether the document or the individual display dimension is controlling the second arrow display. The return value from this method is not valid when the document is controlling the display of second arrows. This method applies only to diameter dimensions. If this method is executed on any other type of dimension, SOLIDWORKS returns false. type

data

Circle

6
Filled dot
4 doubles; (x, y, z) center point and radius The size of the array is the size of the expected returned array.

Member.Returns: True if each dimension runs in a direction closest to the baseline, false if all dimensions run in the same direction (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
If this property is... Then...
True No angle dimension in the angular running dimension is greater than 180⁰ from the baseline, and each angle is measured from a direction that is closest to the baseline.
False The running direction of all angle dimensions is determined by the first angle dimension added. For example, if the user places the baseline dimension at the top of the part, clicking on a feature to the right of the baseline dimension forces all subsequent angular dimensions to be measured clockwise from the baseline. This property corresponds to the Run bidirectionally check box in the Witness/Leader Display panel of the Leaders tab of the Dimension PropertyManager page that appears when you right-click in a drawing and select More Dimensions > Angular Running Dimension.

Member.Name: Scale2
Member.Description: Gets or sets the scale value that is applied to the dimension value of this non-associative distance dimension.
Member.Returns: Scale applied to the dimension value
Member.Remarks: This scale value applies only to non-associative distance dimensions, such as those created using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.CreateLinearDim4">IDrawingDoc::CreateLinearDim4</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.CreateDiamDim4">IDrawingDoc::CreateDiamDim4</see>. For these dimensions, SOLIDWORKS multiplies the actual dimension measurement by this scale value to get the dimension value that is displayed on the screen. For any other types of dimensions (such as associative dimensions or angular measurement dimensions), setting the scale factor has no effect and getting the scale factor will always return 1. The scale value must be greater than 0. This has no effect in the OLE interface, and returns S_false in the COM interface. After using this property, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> to redraw the graphics window to see your changes.

Member.Name: SetArcLengthLeader
Member.Description: Sets the leader style of this arc-length dimension.

Parameter.Name: AutoLeader
Parameter.Description: True if the leader style is automatically selected, false if the leader style isselected by the user

Parameter.Name: LeaderType
Parameter.Description: Leader style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swArcLengthLeaderType_e">swArcLengthLeaderType_e</see> if autoLeader is false

Member.Returns:
Return status:
0
Command was successful, leader style values were set
-1
Command failed for an unknown reason, no leader style values were set
-2
Specified leader style value is not valid
Member.Remarks: The leader style of an arc length dimension is specific to each display dimension. The leader style can be parallel (the leaders are parallel to each other) or radial (the leaders are perpendicular to the extension line and would extend through the center of the arc). The style can be selected automatically by SOLIDWORKS, or specified by the user. If the autoLeader value is passed in as True to automatically select the leader style, then SOLIDWORKS ignores the leaderStyle value. This method applies only to arc length dimensions. Member.Name: SetUnits
Member.Signature: SetUnits( System.bool UseDoc, System.int UType, System.int FractBase, System.int FractDenom, System.bool RoundToFraction )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.SetUnits2">IDisplayDimension::SetUnits2</see>.

Parameter.Name: UseDoc
Parameter.Description: True uses the document settings for units, false uses the setting values passed to the arguments (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UType
Parameter.Description: Unit display setting as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLengthUnit_e">swLengthUnits_e</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAngleUnit_e">swAngleUnits_e</see>

Parameter.Name: FractBase
Parameter.Description: Decimal or fraction display setting as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFractionDisplay_e">swFractionDisplay_e</see>

Parameter.Name: FractDenom
Parameter.Description: Denominator for fraction display

Parameter.Name: RoundToFraction
Parameter.Description: True rounds values to the nearest fraction, false displays fractions only if the values are exact

Member.Returns: Return status (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The unit display settings of a display dimension are controlled by a value stored in one of two places: on the owning document, or on the individual display dimension. This method allows you to determine which setting to use, the document default or the values specified by UType, FractBase, FractDenom, and RoundToFraction. If the UseDoc argument is true, then the display dimension unit information follows the document settings, and SOLIDWORKS ignores the remaining arguments. SOLIDWORKS also removes any local settings so that if you switch back to the local settings, they are set to default values. The UType argument indicates the units. Depending on the type of dimension (angular or linear), this parameter takes a value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLengthUnit_e">swLengthUnits_e</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAngleUnit_e">swAngleUnits_e</see>. If the specified value is invalid, SOLIDWORKS does not change the existing setting and returns an error in the return value. The FractBase argument indicates whether the dimension is displayed as a fraction or a decimal. This must take a value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFractionDisplay_e">swFractionDisplay_e</see>. SOLIDWORKS displays this value as a fraction only if it can be precisely represented as a fraction based on the fraction denominator setting specified in FractDenom. However, if the RoundToFraction argument is true, then SOLIDWORKS forces fraction display by rounding the value to the nearest fraction. The FractDenom argument indicates the fraction precision by specifying the largest fraction denominator used (for example, 4 for 1/4 or 32 for 1/32). Fraction display is valid only if UType is swINCHES or swFEETINCHES. The return value indicates the success or failure of this function. It may take one of the following values:
-2
Command failed because UType is invalid
-1
Command failed for an unknown reason
0
Command was successful After using this method, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> to redraw the graphics window to see your changes.

However, if the RoundToFraction argument is true, then SOLIDWORKS displays the dimension rounded to the nearest fraction. FractDenom indicates the fraction precision by specifying the largest fraction denominator used (for example, 4 for 1/4 or 32 for 1/32). Fraction display is valid only if UType is swINCHES or swFEETINCHES. The return value indicates the success or failure of this method as follows:
If Return Value is... Then this method...
2 Failed because UType is invalid
1 Failed for an unknown reason
0 Succeeded After using this method, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> to redraw the graphics window to see your changes.

Member.Name: AutoRepair
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to automatically repair non-critical custom properties errors in the file to be opened.
Member.Returns: True to automatically repair custom properties errors, false to not (default) (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDocumentSpecification.Silent">IDocumentSpecification::Silent</see> is set to true. If the document to be opened has a non-critical data error, the non-critical data error may or may not be repaired, depending on how you set this property and other conditions. If you set this property to true, and the file to open has non-critical data corruption in:
The custom properties area, the repair proceeds, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc7">ISldWorks::OpenDoc7</see> returns the document with warning, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFileLoadWarning_e">swFileLoadWarning_e</see>.swFileLoadWarning_AutomaticRepair. An area other than custom properties, the document is not repaired. The following files are created in c:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp:
Repaired_file_name.sld* Backup of file_name.sld* If you set this property to false, and the file to open has non-critical data corruption:
The document is not repaired. The document does not open. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc7">ISldWorks::OpenDoc7</see> fails and returns null with error code, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFileLoadError_e">swFileLoadError_e</see>.FileRequiresAutoRepair. If critical data corruption exists in the file, and you set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDocumentSpecification.CriticalDataRepair">IDocumentSpecification::CriticalDataRepair</see> to true to handle critical data corruption:
Non-critical data corruptions are ignored and not repaired. Repairing critical errors necessitates obliterating all non-critical data. Use For C++ only, VARIANT_TRUE (-1) automatically repairs the file, and VARIANT_FALSE (0) does not.

Member.Name: CriticalDataRepair
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to automatically repair critical data errors in the file to be opened.
Member.Returns: True to automatically repair critical data errors, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDocumentSpecification.Silent">IDocumentSpecification::Silent</see> is set to true. If you set this property to true, and the file to open has critical data corruption:
Critical data repair proceeds. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc7">ISldWorks::OpenDoc7</see> returns the document with warning, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFileLoadWarning_e">swFileLoadWarning_e</see>.swFileLoadWarning_CriticalDataRepair. All non-critical data errors are ignored, because repairing critical errors obliterates all non-critical data in the file. If set to true, this property instructs SOLIDWORKS to repair critical data by importing Parasolid bodies into a new file. The repaired file contains only Parasolid bodies. The following files are created in c:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp:
Repaired_file_name.sld* Backup of file_name.sld* If you set this property to false, and the file to open has critical data corruption:
The document does not open. ISldWorks::OpenDoc7 fails and returns null with error code, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFileLoadError_e">swFileLoadError_e</see>.FileRequiresCriticalDataRepair. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDocumentSpecification.AutoRepair">IDocumentSpecification::AutoRepair</see> to handle non-critical data corruption of files. For C++ only, VARIANT_TRUE (-1) automatically repairs the file, and VARIANT_FALSE (0) does not.

Member.Description: Gets the position of the arrows for the section line.
Member.Returns: Array of objects (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The section line in a drawing view has arrows at each end of the line. This method returns an array that consists of 12 doubles, the (X, Y, Z) of the start and end point of one arrow followed by the (X, Y, Z) of the start and end point of the other arrow. These values are the same as some of the information in the array returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetSectionLineInfo2">IView::GetSectionLineInfo2</see>. The arrow information in that array also contains the arrow width, height and style. That information is not included in the array returned by this method, but you can get it from the document preference settings because these values are controlled only at the document level, not on an individual section line basis. See:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceDouble">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceDouble</see> with swDetailingSectionArrowHeight, swDetailingSectionArrowWidth, or swDetailingSectionArrowLength <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceInteger">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceInteger</see> with swDetailingArrowStyleForDimensions

Member.Remarks:

Each coordinate pair consists of 6 doubles, the (X, Y, Z) coordinate of each end point of the segment. These values are the same as some of the information in the array returned by the<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetSectionLineInfo2">IView::IGetSectionLineInfo2</see>. The line segment information in that array also contains the line style. The array returned by this method does not contain that information because it is a document-level setting, and cannot be controlled per section line. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceInteger">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceInteger</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SetUserPreferenceInteger">IModelDocExtension::SetUserPreferenceInteger</see> with swLineFontSectionLineStyle to get or set that value.

Member.Name: IGetTextInfo
Member.Description: Gets the location of the section line text.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of 3 doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks: The section line in a drawing view usually has a piece of text near each end of the line, typically the section view label (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrSection.GetLabel">IDrSection::GetLabel</see>). The array returned by this method consists of 6 doubles, the (X, Y, Z) origin of one text followed by the (X, Y, Z) origin of the other text. The origin is the upper-left corner of the text. These values are the same as some of the information in the array returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetSectionLineInfo2">IView::IGetSectionLineInfo2</see>. The text information in that array also contains the text height. This method returns an array that does not include that information, but you can get it using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrSection.IGetTextFormat">IDrSection::IGetTextFormat</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITextFormat.CharHeight">ITextFormat::CharHeight</see>.

Member.Name: ISetLineInfo
Member.Signature: ISetLineInfo( System.int Count, ref System.double PLineInfo )
Member.Description: Sets the location (both position and arrow heads) of the section line.

Parameter.Name: Count
Parameter.Description: Number of the point coordinates of the section line

Parameter.Name: PLineInfo
Parameter.Description: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Returns: True if the location is set, false if not
Member.Remarks: The PLineInfo argument is an array consisting of several coordinate pairs and is of the same format as the array returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrSection.IGetLineInfo">IDrSection::IGetLineInfo</see>. The number of coordinate pairs is determined by the number of line segments in the section line. Each coordinate pair consists of 6 doubles, the x,y,z coordinate ofeach end point of the segment. The formatted array should include the start point and end point of each line segment, including the z position even though the z position is irrelevant. Any section line containing more than one segment contains at least one set of duplicate points. These points represent the end point of one line segment and the coincident start point of another line segment. If you change either set of points, then you must change the other set of points at the same time. These points must always becoincident when calling this method. To update the section view, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.EditRebuild3">IModelDoc2::EditRebuild3</see> after calling this method.

Member.Remarks: This method is more precise than the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDragOperator.DragAsUI">IDragOperator::DragAsUI</see> method. IDragOperator::DragAsUI is more like an interactive drag operation performed in the SOLIDWORKS 2001Plus software and it may give better graphics performance than IDragOperator::Drag. You will see an improvement in performance when this method is used in the default state. If <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDragOperator.CollisionDetectionEnabled">collision detection</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDragOperator.DynamicClearanceEnabled">clearance</see> is enabled, then the original mode is used. This method is more efficient than making multiple calls to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.SetTransformAndSolve2">IComponent2::SetTransformAndSolve</see> because this method reuses the solver. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDragOperator.UseAbsoluteTransform">IDragOperator::UseAbsoluteTransforms</see> to set the transforms type to absolute or relative. If the desired orientation set by this method was not honored and remedial action occurred, then the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDragOperator.DragCorrected">IDragOperation::DragCorrected</see> property is set. This method returns false if the drag cannot be performed. This typically occurs because of a collision.

Member.Description: Gets or sets the name of the layer on which the component resides in the view.
Member.Returns: Name of the layer on which this component resides
Member.Remarks:
If you specify... Then...
Empty string Name of the component's layer is set to None or to the name of the default layer.

Member.Name: LayerOverride
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether the drawing component has properties that override the default properties of the layer.
Member.Returns: Properties that have been overridden or should be overridden as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLayerOverride_e">swLayerOverride_e</see> (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Get Components' Properties in Drawing View

Member.Remarks:
Currently, only SOLIDWORKS drawing documents support layers. You should set this property only when you want to reset specific visual properties to the default visual properties of the owning layer. If you want to change or set specific values for the visual property of this component, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingComponent.Style">IDrawingComponent::Style</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingComponent.Width">IDrawingComponent::Width</see>. In drawing documents, components can be created on a layer that has specific visual properties. By default, the component takes on the visual properties defined by the layer. However, for a specific component, you can override these visual properties (style or width). When the component is not on any layer, this property returns an undefined value. You can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingComponent.Layer">IDrawingComponent::Layer</see> to determine the name of the layer that this component is on. If an empty string is returned by this property, then this property is not used. When you get this property, the returned bit value indicates which properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are:
color = 0x1
style = 0x2
width = 0x4 Therefore, if the return value is returned as 2, then you know style has been specifically set for this component and might not match the default value associated with this component's layer. When you set this property, the input bit value indicates which properties should maintain their current override values. Therefore, if the return value is passed as 0x4, you know width should keep its current override value and style should be reset to use the style settings for the component's layer. If you pass 0, all visual properties are reset to use the default settings of the component's layer.

Member.Name: AutoDimension
Member.Signature: AutoDimension( System.int EntitiesToDimension, System.int HorizontalScheme, System.int HorizontalPlacement, System.int VerticalScheme, System.int VerticalPlacement )
Member.Description: Automatically dimensions the selected drawing view.

Parameter.Name: EntitiesToDimension
Parameter.Description: Entities to dimension as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimEntities_e">swAutodimEntities_e</see>

Parameter.Name: HorizontalScheme
Parameter.Description: Horizontal dimensioning scheme as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimScheme_e">swAutodimScheme_e</see>

Parameter.Name: HorizontalPlacement
Parameter.Description: Placement relative to the drawing view as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimHorizontalPlacement_e">swAutodimHorizontalPlacement_e</see>

Parameter.Name: VerticalScheme
Parameter.Description: Vertical dimensioning scheme as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimScheme_e">swAutodimScheme_e</see>

Parameter.Name: VerticalPlacement
Parameter.Description: Placement relative to the drawing view as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimVerticalPlacement_e">swAutodimVerticalPlacement_e</see>

Member.Returns: swAutodimStatusSuccess if the view is automatically dimensioned; see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swAutodimStatus_e">swAutodimStatus_e</see> for reasons for possible failures
Member.Remarks:
This method requires information about the:
drawing view to autodimension. This information can be supplied by selecting the drawing view to use. No mark is necessary.If a drawing view is not selected, then this method attempts to determine the drawing view information from the other entities that are selected. If no other selections exist, then this method defaults to using the first drawing view, which is consistent with how the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface works.
datums to use for the dimensioning baseline. These can be supplied by selecting a vertical edge, vertical sketch line, vertex, or sketch point as the datum for the horizontal dimensioning scheme. Mark the selection with swAutodimMarkHorizontalDatum from <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swAutodimMark_e">swAutodimMark_e</see>. Similarly a horizontal edge, horizontal sketch line, vertex, or sketch point should be selected and marked with swAutodimMark_e.swAutodimMarkVerticalDatum for defining the datum for the vertical dimensioning scheme. If only one of these datums is supplied, only the appropriate dimensions are created for that datum.Instead of selecting the horizontal and vertical datum separately, you can select a vertex or sketch point to use to define both datums. Mark the selected vertex or sketch point selection with swAutodimMark_e.swAutodimMarkOriginDatum. If no datums are selected, then this method automatically uses the left- and bottom-most entities in the view to determine default datums, which is consistent with how the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface works.
entities to autodimension. This information is supplied by the entitiesToDimension argument and the selected entities marked with swAutodimMark_e.swAutodimMarkEntities. The entitiesToDimension argument takes a value from the swAutodimEntities_e enumeration:
swAutodimEntitiesSelected indicates that only selected entities marked with a value of swAutodimMarkEntities are considered for autodimensioning.
swAutodimEntitiesAll indicates that all entities in the drawing view are autodimensioned.
swAutodimEntitiesBasedOnPreselect indicates that SOLIDWORKS figures out what to do based on the selected entities marked with swAutodimMarkEntities. If any exist, then autodimension them, just like swAutodimEntitiesSelected. If none exist, then autodimension all entities, just like swAutodimEntitiesAll.Supported entities for dimensioning are lines, points, vertices, faces, and sketch entities.

Member.Description: Gets or sets the background processing option for this drawing.
Member.Returns: Background processing option as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBackgroundProcessOption_e">swBackgroundProcessOption_e</see> (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Fire Notifications for Background Processing Events
Fire Notifications for Background Processing Events
Fire Notifications for Background Processing Events

Member.Remarks:
SOLIDWORKS recommends that you only use this property with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.IsBackgroundProcessingCompleted">ISldWorks::IsBackgroundProcessingCompleted</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.EnableBackgroundProcessing">ISldWorks::EnableBackgroundProcessing</see> when you can quickly open a drawing document via the user interface, but that same drawing takes significantly more time to open programmatically. To more efficiently and programmatically open a drawing document that requires a lot of CPU time and no user input:
Set ISldWorks::EnableBackgroundProcessing to true. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DSldWorksEvents_BackgroundProcessingStartNotifyEventHandler">ISldWorks Event BackgroundProcessingStartNotify</see> to handle the background processing start event. Open the drawing document by calling either <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc6">ISldWorks::OpenDoc6</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.OpenDoc7">ISldWorks::OpenDoc7</see>. Set IDrawingDoc::BackgroundProcessingOption to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBackgroundProcessOption_e">swBackgroundProcessOption_e</see>.swBackgroundProcessing_DeferToApplication. Call ISldWorks::IsBackgroundProcessingCompleted repeatedly, which polls the status of the open operation Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DSldWorksEvents_BackgroundProcessingEndNotifyEventHandler">ISldWorks Event BackgroundProcessingEndNotify</see> to handle the background processing end event. When the open operation is finished, set ISldWorks::EnableBackgroundProcessing to false.

Member.Name: CreateCompoundNote
Member.Signature: CreateCompoundNote( System.double Height, System.double X, System.double Y, System.double Z )
Member.Description: Obsolete for documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2016 and later. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockDefinition">ISketchBlockDefinition</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISketchBlockInstance">ISketchBlockInstance</see>. Creates and returns a compound note.

Parameter.Name: Height
Parameter.Description: Note height in meters

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: x location of note in meters

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: y location of note in meters

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: z location of note in meters

Member.Returns: Newly created compound note
Member.Remarks: A compound note is a note that can contain multiple text strings and sketch geometry. Compound notes are equivalent to a user-defined symbol. After creating a compound note, you can use the other compound note methods to add text and sketch geometry to the object. This object appears to the end-user as though it were one item. If the user selects the compound note and drags it, all of the entities and text move together. Because a compound note can have multiple pieces of text, many of the compound note methods require that you specify the index value of the text. For example, the first piece of text added to the compound note using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.AddText">INote::AddText</see> has index number 1, the second text added has index number 2, and so on. SOLIDWORKS adds the note to the view of the current selection, so you must make a selection before you call this method.

Member.Name: CreateDrawViewFromModelView3
Member.Signature: CreateDrawViewFromModelView3( System.string ModelName, System.string ViewName, System.double LocX, System.double LocY, System.double LocZ )
Member.Description: Creates a drawing view on the current drawing sheet using the specified model view.

Parameter.Name: ModelName
Parameter.Description: Full pathname of the model document for which to create the drawing view (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ViewName
Parameter.Description: Name of the model view from which to create the drawing view (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: LocX
Parameter.Description: x location of drawing view center in meters

Parameter.Name: LocY
Parameter.Description: y location of drawing view center in meters

Parameter.Name: LocZ
Parameter.Description: z location of drawing view center in meters

Member.Returns: Pointer to the newly create <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView">IView</see> object
Member.Remarks:
This method:
Places the center of the view at the specified location.
Uses the <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/swconst/SO_Drawings.htm">swAutomaticScaling3ViewDrawings</see> setting to set the view scale. If this setting is set to True, then when a new drawing view is inserted, that view automatically scales to fit nicely on the drawing sheet. If there are no views on the sheet, the sheet scale is changed to the appropriate scale, and the view created uses the sheet scale. If a model document is currently open in SOLIDWORKS and you don't know its full pathname, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetPathName">IModelDoc2::GetPathName</see> to populate ModelName. Include the .sldprt or .sldasm extension in the pathname.
ViewName must exactly match the name of the model view. For example, the names of the standard views begin with an asterisk. This asterisk is part of the view name and must be included (for example, "*Front").

Member.Name: CreateViewport3
Member.Signature: CreateViewport3( System.double LowerLeftX, System.double LowerLeftY, System.short SketchSize, System.double Scale )
Member.Description: Creates a an empty view in a drawing.

Parameter.Name: LowerLeftX
Parameter.Description: x value for lower-left coordinate for the view

Parameter.Name: LowerLeftY
Parameter.Description: y value for lower-left coordinate for the view

Parameter.Name: SketchSize
Parameter.Description: Approximate number of entries

Parameter.Name: Scale
Parameter.Description: Scale to use for the view

Member.Returns: Pointer to the newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView">IView</see> object
Member.Remarks:
You cannot set the size of an empty view or resize it. Instead, resizing of the view occurs automatically when you add sketch or model geometry to the view.
The center of the empty view is computed from the specified lower-left corner and default values for the upper-right corner. The latter is set to (0.001, 0.001). The center is computed as follows:
center = lower-left_corner + (upper-right_corner - lower-left_corner) / 2.0
To move the view, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.Position">IView::Position</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IPosition">IView::IPosition</see>.
The default SketchSize value is 0. If you are creating more than 500 sketch entities, specify a value instead of using the default.
After you use this method, you can create sketch entities in the new view. One advantage is that users can move the entities around the drawing by dragging the view instead of selecting all the entities.

Member.Remarks: This method only deletes cosmetic threads in a drawing of an assembly; this method does not delete cosmetic threads in a drawing of a part. Member.Returns: Array containing the line font information (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method breaks down the line font into its individual segment lengths. Lines are repeating patterns of space and solid segments. The segCount argument returns the number of segments that define the pattern, and segLengths[] specifies the length of each segment. A negative length value indicates space. For example:
Solid line: segCount = 1, segLenghts[] = {0.5} Dashed line: segCount = 2, segLengths[] = {0.25, -0.25} VARIANT format:
double segCount - Number of segments in the pattern double segLengths[segCount] - Length of each segment

Member.Name: GetViews
Member.Description: Gets the all of the views, including the sheets, in this drawing document.
Member.Returns: An array of arrays (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return value is an array of arrays with a length equal to the number of sheets in the drawing document. Each of those arrays is a list of views with the first view in the list being the sheet itself. If there are multiple sheets in the drawing document, then the order in which the sheets are returned is undetermined. So, the active sheet and its views might not be returned in the first array. For example, when there are three sheets in the drawing document:
One sheet contains 6 views, so first array has this number of elements = 7 (sheet + 6 views)
Another sheet contains 2 views, so second array has this number of elements = 3 (sheet + 2 views)
Another sheet contains no views, so third array has this number of elements = 1 (sheet + 0 views)

Member.Description: Obsolete for documents created in SOLIDWORKS 2016 and later. Creates and returns a compound note.

Parameter.Name: Height
Parameter.Description: Note height in meters

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: x location of note in meters

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: y location of note in meters

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: z location of note in meters

Member.Returns: Pointer to the newly created compound <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">note</see>
Member.Remarks: A compound note is a note that can contain multiple text strings and sketch geometry. Compound notes are equivalent to a user-defined symbol. After creating a compound note, you can use the other compound note methods to add text and sketch geometry to the object. This object appears to the end-user as though it were one item. If the user selects the compound note and drags it, all of the entities and text move together. Because a compound note can have multiple pieces of text, many of the compound note methods require that you specify the index value of the text. For example, the first piece of text added to the compound note using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.AddText">INote::AddText</see> has index number 1, the second text added has index number 2, and so on. SOLIDWORKS adds the note to the view of the current selection, so you must make a selection before you call this method.

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array containing the names of the drawing sheets in this drawing of size Count VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The argument Count is used to help prevent memory overwrites. First call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.GetSheetCount">IDrawingDoc::GetSheetCount</see> to get the number of sheets in this drawing. Then use its return value to dimension the return value array. This method compares the number of sheets in this part with the value passed in.
If the actual number of sheets is...
Then...
Larger than the value passed in
no sheets are returned, and status returns S_ERROR.
Smaller than this value
the names of all of the sheets in the return value is returned and changes Count to reflect the actual number of sheets.
