Member.Returns: Pointer to the newly created freeform <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see>
Member.Remarks:
The SOLIDWORKS API Freeform-related methods are intended to journal the actions performed by an interactive user while creating the feature. Because user interaction is required to create a Freeform feature, fully automating the creation of it is not possible using the SOLIDWORKS API.
The typical steps performed by an interactive user to create a Freeform feature are:
Select the face to form. NOTE: The face must have four sides.
Add curves on the selected face. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformCurveData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformCurveData</see>.
Add points on the curves. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformPointData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformPointData</see>.Interactively pull or push the points to change the shape of the selected face.
Insert the Freeform feature. Corresponds to this method, IFeatureManager::InsertFreeform. Record a macro while interactively creating a Freeform feature, then examine the macro to see the order in which the Freeform-related methods are recorded.

Member.Remarks:
The SOLIDWORKS API Freeform-related methods are intended to journal the actions performed by an interactive user while creating the feature. Because user interaction is required to create a Freeform feature, fully automating the creation of it is not possible using the SOLIDWORKS API.
The typical steps performed by an interactive user to create a Freeform feature are:
Select the face to form.
Add curves on the selected face. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformCurveData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformCurveData</see>.
Add points on the curves. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformPointData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformPointData</see>.
Specify boundary continuity. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformBoundaryContinuity">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformBoundaryContinuity</see>.Interactively pull or push the points to change the shape of the selected face.
Insert the Freeform feature. Corresponds to this method, IFeatureManager::InsertFreeform2. Record a macro while interactively creating a Freeform feature, then examine the macro to see the order in which the Freeform-related methods are recorded.

Member.Remarks: Before calling this method, select the entity to use as the ground plane using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByRay">IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>. Call this method to insert a ground plane at each level of a plant assembly. Ground planes are used as reference geometry when inserting published assets at each level. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ActivateGroundPlane">IAssemblyDoc::ActivateGroundPlane</see> to activate the ground plane on the level where you want to insert a published asset; the asset's ground face snaps to the assembly's activated ground plane. Components with magnetic mates snap only to components that are also on the active ground plane. Only one ground plane can be active at a given time in each assembly configuration. See Large Assemblies > Facility Layout in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Name: InsertMidSurface
Member.Signature: InsertMidSurface( Body2 PBodyIn, ModelDoc2 PPartDocIn, System.double Placement, System.bool KnitFlag )
Member.Description: Inserts a midsurface feature.

Parameter.Name: PBodyIn
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">Body</see> in the context of an assembly; otherwise, null or Nothing (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: PPartDocIn
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">Model document</see> in the context of an assembly; otherwise, null or Nothing (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Placement
Parameter.Description: Value from -1 to 1 that indicates the desired location of the midsurface relative to the face pair; a value of 0.0 places the midsurface equally between the face pair

Parameter.Name: KnitFlag
Parameter.Description: True to sew all the reference surfaces (neutral sheets) into a single sheet (surface) body, false for the midsurface feature to contain individual reference surface geometry

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3">midsurface feature</see>
Member.Remarks: The pPartDocIn parameter is the component's model document where you want to add the midsurface feature, and the pBody parameter is the body of that component. A midsurface feature is calculated from the solid body in your part document. This method first finds all parallel pairs of faces from the part solid. For each pair of parallel faces found, it creates a neutral reference surface between the two faces. The placement position of the reference surface is controlled by the placement parameter. This process repeats itself until all parallel body faces are processed. At the end of this process, all the reference surfaces are sewn into a single reference surface if knitFlag is set to true. The hierarchy of a midsurface feature is a midsurface feature contains one or more reference surfaces. If sewn successfully using the KnitFlag = True option, then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface. Each reference surface is considered a sheet body. The sheet body has the normal topology that you would expect to find on a body object (for example, faces, edges, and so on). See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3">IMidSurface3</see> for methods that provide access to this topology.

Member.Name: InsertMoldCoreCavitySolids
Member.Signature: InsertMoldCoreCavitySolids( System.double Dist1, System.double Dist2, System.bool Setback, System.double Angle )
Member.Description: Creates a core/cavity solid feature.

Parameter.Name: Dist1
Parameter.Description: Length of the extrusion in Direction 1

Parameter.Name: Dist2
Parameter.Description: Length of the extrusion in Direction 2

Parameter.Name: Setback
Parameter.Description: True to enable setback surface, false to not

Parameter.Name: Angle
Parameter.Description: Draft angle for the setback surface

Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see> object
Member.Remarks:
To use this method:
The Parting Line feature must exist.
The parting surface must be generated.
The part must be separated into core and cavity (sheet bodies).
A sketch describing the outline of the mold block must exist. The sketch must be perpendicular to the pull direction. Usually, the sketch is a rectangle that includes the part (core and cavity). The location of the sketch plane specifies the parting plane in the setback surface option.
Without the setback surface option, the parting surface must extend beyond the block sketch so that the parting surface is cut off by the block.
With the setback surface option, the parting surface should be included within the block sketch. The parting plane (sketch plane) cannot intersect with the parting surface. Therefore, the parting plane must be either higher or lower than the parting surface. From the parting surface, a set of ruled surfaces is generated to be trimmed by the parting plane.

Parameter.Name: Angle
Parameter.Description: Draft angle in radians

Parameter.Description: True to flip the direction of the draft (the draft direction is determined by theselected direction, which could be a planar face, a reference plane, an edge, ortwo vertices; if you refer to the last argument in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>,then these items have a selection mark of 1; the faces to draft have a selectionmark of 2, and the draft edges have a selection mark of 4), false to not

Parameter.Description: True if this is an edge draft and the user selects edges to draft, false if thisis a face draft and the user selects faces to draft (SOLIDWORKS automatically selectsthe faces next to the edge to be drafted)

Parameter.Name: PropType
Parameter.Description:
Propagation type:
0 = no propagation 1 = propagate to the next tangent faces that share the base neutral plane; valid for edge draft or neutral plane draft 2 = propagate to all faces that are a neighbor of the neutral plane 3 = propagate to all faces that a neighbor of the neutral plane on all inner loops (for example, all faces of a pocket or a boss) 4 = propagate to all faces that are a neighbor of the neutral plane on the outer loop (for example, the sides of a box with the bottom face as the neutral plane)

Parameter.Name: IsStepDraft
Parameter.Description: True if the draft is a step draft, false if not

Parameter.Name: IsBodyDraft

Parameter.Name: Closed
Parameter.Description: True closes the loft, false leaves the loft open; if true and you selected less that three profiles, any selected guide curves must be closed curves

Parameter.Name: KeepTangency
Parameter.Description: True maintains the tangency as seen in the section curves, false does not If the section curves are tangent, then you have the option to specify whether the resulting faces are also tangent; when generating tangent surfaces, SOLIDWORKS maintains planar and cylindrical surface shapes if the section curves exhibit these characteristics

Parameter.Name: ForceNonRational
Parameter.Description: True obtains smoother surfaces, false does not

Parameter.Name: TessToleranceFactor
Parameter.Description: Factor that controls the number of intermediate sections used for loft with centerline; the default value is 1.0; the greater the value, the more intermediate sections are created

Parameter.Name: StartMatchingType
Parameter.Description:
Tangency type at the start profile:
0 = none
1 = tangent to the normal of the profile
2 = tangent to a selected vector
3 = tangency to all the adjacent faces sharing an edge with the start profile
4 = tangent to some of the selected faces sharing an edge with the start profile (not available)

Parameter.Name: EndMatchingType
Parameter.Description:
Tangency type at the end profile:
0 = none
1 = tangent to the normal of the profile
2 = tangent to a selected vector
3 = tangency to all the adjacent faces sharing an edge with the start profile
4 = tangent to some of the selected faces sharing an edge with the start profile (not available)

Parameter.Name: EndTangentLength
Parameter.Description: End tangent length

Parameter.Description: True is one direction, false is the opposite

Parameter.Name: Thickness1

Parameter.Name: Thickness2
Parameter.Description: Thickness value for the second direction

Parameter.Name: ThinType
Parameter.Description:
Thin wall type:
0 = One direction
1 = One direction reverse
2 = Mid-plane
3 = Two direction

Parameter.Name: Merge
Parameter.Description: True merges the results in a multibody part, false does not

Parameter.Name: UseFeatScope
Parameter.Description: True if the feature only affects selected bodies, false if the feature affects all bodies

Parameter.Description: True to automatically select all bodies and have the feature affect those bodies, false to select the bodies the feature affects

Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see> object
Member.Remarks:
Selection of guide curves and centerline is optional. However, you must select the profiles in an order consistent with the desired direction of the loft. Because a solid is being created, the section profiles must be closed. It is best to use guide curves, especially when you select profiles in the FeatureManager design tree. You can use any number of profiles; however, if you select only one profile, then any selected guide curves must be closed curves. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the profiles and guide curves. Set the mark for:
profile selections to 1
any guide curve selection to 2
centerline selection to 4
start tangency vector selection to 8
start tangency faces selection to 16 (not available)
end tangency vector selection to 32
end tangency faces selection to 64 (not available) NOTE: Linear edge, sketch line, axis, plane and planar faces are qualified for tangency vector sections. When UseAutoSelect is false, the user must select the bodies that the feature will affect.

Member.Name: InsertRevolvedRefSurface
Member.Signature: InsertRevolvedRefSurface( System.double Angle, System.bool ReverseDir, System.double Angle2, System.int RevType )
Member.Description: Creates a revolved reference surface by revolving a profile around a centerline.

Parameter.Name: Angle
Parameter.Description: Angle of revolution in radians

Parameter.Name: ReverseDir
Parameter.Description: Angle is positive or negative (True or false)

Parameter.Name: Angle2
Parameter.Description: Angle of revolution in radians

Parameter.Name: RevType
Parameter.Description: Type of revolution (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Pointer to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see> object
Member.Remarks:
Make the selections using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> before calling this method. See the SOLIDWORKS Help for information about what entities are valid for selection.
The RevType argument can be one of these values:
0 = One direction revolution.
1 = MidPlane revolution. For this type of revolve, the angle specification specifies the full revolution. The angle to revolve is (angle/2) on either side of the sketch. The ReverseDir argument has no effect.
2 = Two direction revolution. For a two direction revolve, Angle is the angle to revolve in Direction1 and Angle2 is the angle to revolve in Direction2. This method does not support 3D sketches.

Parameter.Name: Text
Parameter.Description: Text for note

Parameter.Name: FeatureOwner
Parameter.Description: Macro feature for this note

Member.Returns: Point to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">INote</see> object
Member.Remarks:
The note is for display purposes only and cannot be modified by the end user. For example, you could display the note to inform an end user that editing or deleting the macro feature is prohibited.
You associate the note with the specified macro feature in:
VB by using this method in the code that generates the macro feature and by setting swMacroFeatureSecurityEnableNote in the <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Security_Function.htm">macro feature's security function</see>. You should also include the conditions under which to display the note.
C++ by using this method in the code that generates the macro feature and by setting swMacroFeatureSecurityEnableNote for the Options argument of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swpublished.ISwComFeature.Security">ISwComFeature::Security</see> in the <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Security_Function.htm">macro feature's security function</see>. You should also include the conditions under which to display the note.

Member.Remarks:
Before calling this method to create a sheet metal gusset feature, you must pre-select faces, lines, edges, vertices, or points as follows:
To... Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select...
Specify the legs of the gusset feature
Two flat faces of a bend. - or -
Two flat faces adjacent to a cylindrical bend face. - or -
One cylindrical bend face. - or -
One flat face and one non-planar face adjacent to a toroidal bend. - or -
One toroidal bend face.
Optionally orient the gusset section plane
One linear edge or sketch segment that is perpendicular to the gusset section plane. If you do not pre-select either entity, then the method uses the bend line adjacent to the gusset legs as the reference.
Optionally position the gusset section plane
One vertex, sketch point, or reference point. If you do not pre-select any one of these entities, then you must set BOffset to true and specify DOffset for an assumed reference point. For insertion of the first gusset, the assumed reference point is on the end of the sheet metal bend. For second and subsequent gusset insertions, the assumed reference point is on the edge of the gusset last inserted. Instead of pre-selecting the references and calling this method, you can pass the references as arrays to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertSheetMetalGussetFeature2">IFeatureManager::InsertSheetMetalGussetFeature2</see>.
If ProfDimType = 1, to dimension the gusset profile using... Specify...
Both legs of the gusset
DLength of d1 leg DHeight of d2 leg BUseAngle = false BFlipSides = true to swap d1 and d2 legs during dimensioning
d1 leg and the angle it forms with the gusset
DLength of d1 leg DAngle of angle formed by gusset intersecting d1 leg BUseAngle = true BFlipSides = true to swap d1 and d2 legs during dimensioning
d2 leg and the angle it forms with the gusset

Member.Name: InsertSlicing
Member.Signature: InsertSlicing( System.object SlicingData, out System.int Errors )
Member.Description: Creates and inserts slicing into the FeatureManager design tree.

Parameter.Name: SlicingData
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISlicingData">ISlicingData</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Errors
Parameter.Description: Errors as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swInsertSlicingError_e">swInsertSlicingError_e</see>

Member.Returns: Array of sketch and reference plane objects
Member.Remarks:
This method invokes the Slicing tool. For more information, refer to SOLIDWORKS Help > Parts and Features > Controlling Parts > Slicing Tool. Before calling this method:
Pre-select in the graphics area a planar entity (to create a linear pattern of slices) or a combination of a linear entity and a point entity (to create an angular pattern of slices whose axis is the linear entity). Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.GetSlicingData">IFeatureManager::GetSlicingData</see> to get an ISlicingData object. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISlicingData.PlaneReferences">ISlicingData::PlaneReferences</see> if step 1 is not performed. Specify a planar entity or a combination of a linear entity and a point entity as specified in step 1. Set other ISlicingData properties. Populate SlicingData with the ISlicingData object. After calling this method:
Use the array of sketch and reference plane objects returned by this method to perform further work. If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISlicingData.AddSlicingPlanesAndSketchesToFolder">ISlicingData::AddSlicingPlanesAndSketchesToFolder</see> was set to true, then a Slice1 folder in the FeatureManager design tree is created containing the slicing planes and sketches. You can edit the slicing planes and sketches individually as needed. Delete the Slice1 folder and its contents to remove slicing from the model.

Member.Signature: InsertSweepSurface2( System.bool Propagate, System.short TwistCtrlOption, System.bool KeepTangency, System.bool BAdvancedSmoothing, System.short StartMatchingType, System.short EndMatchingType, System.short PathAlign, System.bool UseFeatScope, System.bool UseAutoSelect, System.double TwistAngle, System.bool BMergeSmoothFaces )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertSweepSurface3">IFeatureManager::InsertSweepSurface3</see>.

Parameter.Name: Propagate
Parameter.Description: True propagates the sweep to the next edge, false causes the sweep to occur only on the selected edge; to propagate to the next edge, the next edge must be tangent to the current edge

Parameter.Name: TwistCtrlOption
Parameter.Description: Twist control option as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTwistControlType_e">swTwistControlType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: KeepTangency
Parameter.Description: If the sweep section has tangent segments, then true to cause the corresponding surfaces in the resulting sweep to be tangent, false to not

Parameter.Name: BAdvancedSmoothing
Parameter.Description: If the sweep section has circular or elliptical arcs, then true to approximate the sections and smooth the surfaces, false to not

Parameter.Name: StartMatchingType
Parameter.Description: Tangency type as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTangencyType_e">swTangencyType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: EndMatchingType
Parameter.Description: Tangency type as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTangencyType_e">swTangencyType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: PathAlign
Parameter.Description: Align path type (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UseFeatScope
Parameter.Description: True if the feature only affects selected bodies, false if the feature affects all bodies

Parameter.Name: UseAutoSelect
Parameter.Description: True to automatically select all bodies and have the feature affect those bodies, false to select the bodies the feature affects (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: TwistAngle
Parameter.Description: If TwistCtrlOption set to swTwistControlType_e.swTwistControlConstantTwistAlongPath, then specify end twist angle

Parameter.Name: BMergeSmoothFaces
Parameter.Description: True to merge smooth faces, false to not

Member.Returns: Pointer to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see> object
Member.Remarks:
Because you are creating a surface, the sections can be open. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the profile and sweep curves. The mark for:
1 = Profile selection
2 = Guide curve selection, if provided
4 = Sweep path The PathAlign argument is available when TwistCtrlOption is set to swTwistControlFollowPath and can take one of these values:
0 = None; no correction (default)
2 = Direction vector; a plane, planar face, or line defines the path
3 = All faces; includes neighboring faces When UseAutoSelect is false, the user must select the bodies that the feature will affect.

Member.Description: Obsolete. See Remarks.

Parameter.Name: Propagate
Parameter.Description: True propagates the sweep to the next edge, false causes the sweep to occur only on the selected edge; to propagate to the next edge, the next edge must be tangent to the current edge

Parameter.Name: TwistCtrlOption
Parameter.Description: Twist control option as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTwistControlType_e">swTwistControlType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: KeepTangency
Parameter.Description: If the sweep section has tangent segments, then true to cause the corresponding surfaces in the resulting sweep to be tangent, false to not

Parameter.Name: BAdvancedSmoothing
Parameter.Description: If the sweep section has circular or elliptical arcs, then true to approximate the sections and smooth the surfaces, false to not

Parameter.Description: Tangency type as defined in swTangencyType_e

Parameter.Description: Align path type (see Remarks)

Parameter.Description: True if the feature only affects selected bodies, false if the feature affects all bodies

Parameter.Description: True to automatically select all bodies and have the feature affect those bodies, false to select the bodies the feature affects (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: TwistAngle
Parameter.Description: If TwistCtrlOption set to swTwistControlType_e.swTwistControlConstantTwistAlongPath, then specify end twist angle

Parameter.Name: BMergeSmoothFaces
Parameter.Description: True to merge smooth faces, false to not

Parameter.Name: CircularProfile
Parameter.Description: True to use a circular profile, false to use the selected sketch profile or solid body

Parameter.Name: CircularProfileDiameter
Parameter.Description: If CircularProfile is true, then specify the diameter of the circular profile

Parameter.Name: Direction
Parameter.Description: Direction as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swSweepDirection_e">swSweepDirection_e</see> (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">Feature</see>
Member.Remarks:
SOLIDWORKS 2018 introduces a new sweep architecture, making this method obsolete. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Sweep_Features_and_SweepFeatureData_Objects.htm">Sweep Features and SweepFeatureData Objects</see> to create this sweep surface. Because you are creating a surface, the sections can be open. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the sketch profile and sweep curves. Specify these marks:
1 = Sketch profile
2 = Guide curve, if provided
4 = Sweep path The PathAlign argument is available when TwistCtrlOption is set to swTwistControlType_e.swTwistControlFollowPath and can take one of these values:
0 = None; no correction (default)
2 = Direction vector; a plane, planar face, or line defines the path
3 = All faces; includes neighboring faces When UseAutoSelect is false, the user must select the bodies that the feature will affect.
Direction only applies to sketch profiles and only when the sketch profile is not coincident with an end of the path.

Member.Name: PostSplitBody
Member.Signature: PostSplitBody( System.object BodiesToMark, System.bool ConsumeCut, System.object Origins, System.object SavePaths )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.PostSplitBody2">IFeatureManager::PostSplitBody2</see>.

Parameter.Name: BodiesToMark
Parameter.Description: Bodies to mark for the split operation

Parameter.Name: ConsumeCut
Parameter.Description: True to remove the bodies from the part, false to not

Parameter.Name: Origins
Parameter.Description: Array of origins of the bodies to save

Parameter.Name: SavePaths
Parameter.Description: Array of paths and filenames of part documents to which to save BodiesToMark

Member.Returns: Pointer to the split-body <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see>
Member.Remarks:
To create a split-body feature:
Select the entities to use to split the part into multiple bodies.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.PreSplitBody">IFeatureManager::PreSplitBody</see> to get all of the bodies created by splitting the part.
Call this method to create the split-body feature. The size of the BodiesToMark, Origins, and SavePaths arrays must be equal and greater than 0. If you pass an empty path and filename for a body, then that body is only marked and not saved. It remains with the original part.
To find out if the bodies in a split-body feature were consumed, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplitBodyFeatureData.Consume">ISplitBodyFeatureData::Consume</see>.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName">IFeature::GetTypeName</see> return:
Split for a feature that was created by splitting a part into multiple parts by using either this method or the Split feature in the user interface. You can access a split-body feature's data using the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISplitBodyFeatureData">ISplitBodyFeatureData</see> interface.
SplitBody for a body created by splitting a part and saving the body to a part. You cannot access the data of a split body saved to a part.

Member.Name: PostSplitBody2
Member.Signature: PostSplitBody2( System.object BodiesToMark, System.bool ConsumeCut, System.object Origins, System.object SavePaths, System.string OverrideTemplateName )
Member.Description: Creates a Split feature.

Parameter.Name: BodiesToMark
Parameter.Description: Array of bodies to mark for the split operation

Parameter.Name: ConsumeCut
Parameter.Description: True to remove the bodies from the part, false to not

Parameter.Name: Origins
Parameter.Description: Array of origins of the bodies to save

Parameter.Name: SavePaths
Parameter.Description: Array of paths and filenames of the part documents to which to save BodiesToMark

Parameter.Name: OverrideTemplateName
Parameter.Description: Path and filename of the part or assembly template that overrides the default (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Split <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see>
Member.Remarks:
To create a Split feature:
Select the entities to use to split the part into multiple bodies.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.PreSplitBody">IFeatureManager::PreSplitBody</see> to get all of the bodies created by splitting the part.
Call this method to create the Split feature. The size of the BodiesToMark, Origins, and SavePaths arrays must be equal and greater than 0. If you pass an empty path and filename for a body, then that body is only marked, is not saved to a separate part document, and remains with the original part.
OverrideTemplateName overrides the default part or assembly template that is specified in Tools > Options > System Options > File Locations. The template is applied to all new part or assembly files created during the split operation.
To find out whether the bodies in a Split feature are consumed, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplitBodyFeatureData.Consume">ISplitBodyFeatureData::Consume</see>.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName">IFeature::GetTypeName</see> return:
Split for a feature that was created by splitting a part into multiple parts by using either this method or the Split feature in the user interface. You can access a split-body feature's data using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISplitBodyFeatureData">ISplitBodyFeatureData</see>.
SplitBody for a body created by splitting a part and saving the body to a part. You cannot access the data of a split body saved to a part.

Member.Name: SetFreeformBoundaryContinuity
Member.Description: Sets the boundary continuity for this Freeform feature.

Parameter.Name: BoundaryIndex
Parameter.Description: 0-based index of the boundary to modify (i.e., a value ranging from 0 to (Number of face boundaries-1))

Parameter.Name: Continuity
Parameter.Description: -1 = Movaeable 0 = Contact 1 = Tangenet 2= Curvature

Member.Remarks:
The SOLIDWORKS API Freeform-related methods are intended to journal the actions performed by an interactive user while creating the feature. Because user interaction is required to create a Freeform feature, fully automating the creation of it is not possible using the SOLIDWORKS API.
The typical steps performed by an interactive user to create a Freeform feature are:
Select the face to form.
Add curves on the selected face. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformCurveData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformCurveData</see>.
Add points on the curves. Corresponds to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.SetFreeformPointData">IFeatureManager::SetFreeformPointData</see>.
Specify boundary continuity. Corresponds to IFeatureManager::SetFreeformBoundaryContinuity.Interactively pull or push the points to change the shape of the selected face.
Insert the Freeform feature. Corresponds to this method, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertFreeform2">IFeatureManager::InsertFreeform2</see>. Record a macro while interactively creating a Freeform feature, then examine the macro to see the order in which the Freeform-related methods are recorded.

Member.Description: Gets or sets whether or not to merge results.
Member.Returns: True for merged results, false for non-merged results
Member.Remarks: If the fill surface displays in an unwanted direction while merging results, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.ReverseDirection">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::ReverseDirection</see> to reverse the direction of the fill surface.

Member.Name: OptimizeSurface
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether or not to optimize the patch.
Member.Returns: True for optimized patch, false for non-optimized patch
Member.Remarks: You can only adjust the quality of the resolution of a patch when the patch is not optimized. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.ResolutionControl">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::ResolutionControl</see> for details.

Member.Name: ReleaseSelectionAccess
Member.Description: Releases access to selections that define this fill-surface feature.
Member.Remarks:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.AccessSelections">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::AccessSelections</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.IAccessSelections">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::IAccessSelections</see> put the model into a rollback state to allow access to the selections that define the fill-surface feature.
Use this method to restore the rollback state if you did not modify the fill-surface feature, or use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IModifyDefinition2">IFeature::IModifyDefinition2</see> if you did modify the fill-surface feature.

Member.Name: ResolutionControl
Member.Description: Gets and sets the quality of the resolution of the fill-surface feature.
Member.Returns: Valid values: 1, 2, and 3 (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Adjusting the quality of the resolution is only available for patches that are not optimized. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.OptimizeSurface">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::OptimizeSurface</see> for details.
Specifying a higher value:
Increases the number of patches defining the surface
Improves the quality of the surface profile
Increases processing time
Increases the size of the file

Member.Name: ReverseDirection
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether or not to reverse direction while merging results.
Member.Returns: True to reverse direction while merging results, false to not
Member.Remarks: When patching a solid with a fill surface, there are often two possible results. Use this method to reverse direction while merging results if the fill surface displays in an unwanted direction. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.Merge">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::Merge</see> for details about merging results.

Member.Name: ReverseSurface
Member.Description: Gets or sets direction of the surface patch.
Member.Returns: True reverses the direction of the surface patch, false does not
Member.Remarks:
This property is dynamic and is only available when:
All boundary curves are coplanar
No constraint points exist
No interior constraints
Fill surface is nonplanar

Member.Description: Switches the boundary face of the curvature control of the patch.

Member.Name: TryToFormSolid
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to form a solid.
Member.Returns: True if trying to form solid, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The behavior for this option depends on the boundaries.
When all the boundaries belong to the same solid body, you can use the surface fill to patch the solid.
If at least one of the edges is an open sheet edge and you merge results, then the fill knits with the surfaces to which the edges belong. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.Merge">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::Merge</see> for details about merging results.
If all the boundary entities are open edges, then a solid may be created. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.GetPatchBoundary">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::GetPatchBoundary</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.IGetPatchBoundary">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::IGetPatchBoundary</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.SetPatchBoundary">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::SetPatchBoundary</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFillSurfaceFeatureData.ISetPatchBoundary">IFillSurfaceFeatureData::ISetPatchBoundary</see> for details about boundary entities.

Member.Signature: AddCommandItem( System.string Name, System.string HintString, System.int ImageListIndex, System.string CallbackFunction, System.string UpdateCallbackFunction )
Member.Description: Adds an item to a flyout menu.

Parameter.Name: Name
Parameter.Description: Name of the item to add to the flyout

Parameter.Name: HintString
Parameter.Description: Text displayed in the SOLIDWORKS status bar when the pointer is on the item

Parameter.Name: ImageListIndex
Parameter.Description: Index of the image in the icon list (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UpdateCallbackFunction
Parameter.Description:
Optional function that controls the state of the item; if specified, then SOLIDWORKS calls this function before displaying the item
If UpdateCallbackFunction returns...
Then SOLIDWORKS...
0
Deselects and disables the item
1
Deselects and enables the item; this is the default state if no update function is specified
2
Selects and disables the item
3
Selects and enables the item
4 Hides the item(see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Index of the item within the flyout as assigned by SOLIDWORKS
Member.Remarks: See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Add-in_Callbacks.htm">Add-in Callback and Enable Methods</see> to learn how to specify CallbackFunction and UpdateCallbackFunction. Flyouts are created at runtime. Call this method from the callback method defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICommandManager.CreateFlyoutGroup">ICommandManager::CreateFlyoutGroup</see>. ImageListIndex is 0-based. The size of the index is equal to the number of images in the large or small graphic file for that flyout. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.LargeIconList">IFlyoutGroup::LargeIconList</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.SmallIconList">IFlyoutGroup::SmallIconList</see> for details.

Member.Name: IconList
Member.Description: Gets or sets the paths for the icons for the toolbar buttons for this flyout.
Member.Returns: Array of strings of the paths for the icons for the toolbar buttons for this flyout (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property supports scaling for high resolution screens with high resolution operating system scaling options. The array of strings for the paths to the image files can contain icons of the following sizes:
20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels Each image file (.bmp or .png) should contain all of the same-size icons for all of the buttons. For example:
Each icon strip should use a 256-color palette. The order in which you specify the icons must be the same for this property and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.MainIconList">IFlyoutGroup::MainIconList</see>. For example, if you specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for this property, then you must specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for IFlyoutGroup::MainIconList.

20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels Each image file (.bmp or .png) contains a single icon. Each icon should use a 256-color palette. The order in which you specify the icons must be the same for this property and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFlyoutGroup.IconList">IFlyoutGroup::IconList</see>. For example, if you specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for this property, then you must specify an array of paths to 20 x 20 pixels, 32 x 32 pixels, and 40 x 40 pixels icons for IFlyoutGroup::IconList.

Parameter.Description: Name of the menu item to add; including parent menu names, e.g., subMenuString@menuString (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Position
Parameter.Description: Position of the existing menu item before which to insert the new menu item; the first menu item is at position 0; if Position is 1, the new menu item is appended to the end of the menu (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if menu item was successfully added, false if not
Member.Remarks:
If the name of a parent menu name is not specified in Menu, then:
the menu item appears on the Tools menu below the XPress products menu item. Position is ignored. This method is only valid when the application is implemented as a DLL, not as an EXE.

Member.Name: AddMenuItem
Member.Signature: AddMenuItem( System.string Menu, System.string Item, System.int Position, System.string CallbackFcnAndModule )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFrame.AddMenuItem2">IFrame::AddMenuItem2</see>.

Member.Name: AddMenuItem2
Member.Signature: AddMenuItem2( System.string Menu, System.string Item, System.int Position, System.string CallbackFcnAndModule, System.string BitmapFileName )
Member.Description: Adds a menu item and bitmap or a separator to an existing menu.

Parameter.Name: Menu
Parameter.Description: Name of the menu to which to add this menu item

Parameter.Name: Item
Parameter.Description: Name of menu item (including accelerator key "&"); if Item is null or empty, then this method adds a separator

Parameter.Name: Position
Parameter.Description: Position at which to add the new menu item; the first item is at position 0; if Position is 1, the new menu item is added to the end of the list

Parameter.Name: CallbackFcnAndModule
Parameter.Description: Function called when user clicks the menu item (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: BitmapFileName
Parameter.Description: Path and filename of the bitmap for the menu item

Member.Returns: True if menu item is added, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method only works for the C++ application implemented as a DLL, not as an EXE. Any function exposed as a callback from a menu item must be declared as an EXPORT or included in your .def file. You can add a new menu item to any one of the four frames (main frame, part frame, assembly frame, or drawing frame). To do this, you must get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFrame">IFrame</see> object when the desired frame is active. For example, if you want your menu to be available when a part document is active, then call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.Frame">ISldWorks::Frame</see> when a part is first loaded or created, and use that IFrame object to call this method. Once you add your menu to the part frame, you do not need to do it again during the current SOLIDWORKS Design session. The CallbackFcnAndModule argument specifies which function to call when this menu item is selected by the user. The syntax is as follows: "dllname@function@updatefunction,hintstring" where:
dllname
Name of your library as specified in the project .def file. The actual DLL filename and the definition in the .def file must be the same.
function
Name of the function that gets called when the user clicks the menu item. This function must also be declared as an EXPORT in your .def file. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Add-in_Callbacks.htm">Add-in Callback and Enable Methods</see> to learn how to specify your function.
updatefunction
Optional argument that controls the state of the button. If specified, then SOLIDWORKS Design calls this function before the button is displayed. Define your updatefunction to return an integer and declare it as an EXPORT or included in your .def file. The display of the button is controlled by the return value of the function as follows:
return 0 - Menu item is unchecked and disabled.
return 1 - Menu item is unchecked and enabled. This is the default menu state if no update function is specified.
return 2 - Menu item is checked and disabled.
return 3 - Menu item is checked and enabled. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Add-in_Callbacks.htm">Add-in Callback and Enable Methods</see> to learn how to specify your updatefunction.
hintstring
Optional argument that contains a text hint displayed in the SOLIDWORKS Design status bar when the user moves the mouse over this menu item. If hintstring is specified, then it must be preceded by a comma. For example: "Userdll@AddBox@checkForUserSelects,Add a box"

Member.Name: AddMenuPopupIcon
Member.Signature: AddMenuPopupIcon( System.int DocType, System.int SelectType, System.string HintString, System.string CallbackFcnAndModule, System.string CustomNames, System.string BitmapFilePath )
Member.Description: Adds an icon to a context-sensitive menu of a C++ SOLIDWORKS add-in.

Parameter.Name: DocType
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swDocumentTypes_e">Document type</see> to which to add the context-sensitive menu icon

Parameter.Name: SelectType
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">Selection type</see> to which to add the context-sensitive menu icon

Parameter.Name: HintString
Parameter.Description: Text displayed in the SOLIDWORKS status bar when the user moves the mouse over the icon

Parameter.Name: CallbackFcnAndModule
Parameter.Description: Function called when user clicks the context-sensitive menu icon (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: CustomNames
Parameter.Description: Names of custom feature types (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: BitmapFilePath
Parameter.Description: Path and file name of the bitmap for the context-sensitive menu icon

Member.Returns: True if the context-sensitive menu icon is added, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method is supported in C++ applications only, and it only works for C++ applications implemented as .dll files, not as .exe files. Any function exposed as a callback from an context-sensitive menu icon must be declared as an EXPORT or included in your .def file. The CallbackFcnAndModule argument specifies which function to call when the shortcut menu icon is clicked by the user. The syntax is as follows: dllname@function where:
dllname
Name of your library as specified in the project .def file. The actual file name and the definition in the .def file must be the same.
function
Name of the function that gets called when the user clicks the icon. This function must also be declared as an EXPORT in your .def file. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Add-in_Callbacks.htm">Add-in Callback and Enable Methods</see> to learn how to implement your callback function.
CustomNames is a semi-colon separated list of the names of the custom feature types. This argument is applicable only if SelectType is a custom feature type (like swSelATTRIBUTES); in the case of swSelATTRIBUTES, set this field to the name of the attribute definition.

Member.Name: GetLeaderAtIndex2
Member.Description: Gets information about the specified leader on this GTol.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of the leader

Member.Returns: Array (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: A GTol can have a straight leader (1 segment) or a bent leader (2 segments), or it might have a perpendicular leader, which can have either 2 or 3 segments, depending on the situation. The returned array contains the point information to define the leader. It contains the x,y,z coordinates for each vertex in the leader. It can contain up to 12 doubles (4 sets of x,y,z values). Examine the return value to determine the number of items in the leader coordinate information. The size of the array is either 6 (1 segments), 9 (2 segments), or 12 (3 segments).

Member.Returns: Number of leaders on the GTol

Member.Name: GetLeaderInfo
Member.Description: Gets information describing the layout of the GTol leader lines.
Member.Returns: Array (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
There can be 0, 1 or 2 lines with the leader line. If the GTol is not attached, then there are 0 lines. Otherwise, the GTol can have a straight leaderline (1 line) or a bent leaderline (2 lines). The caller must infer the number of leader lines based on <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IsAttached">IGtol::IsAttached</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.HasExtraLeader">IGtol::HasExtraLeader</see>.
IGtol::IsAttached() == false implies no leaderline; therefore, there are no leaderline points (PointCount=0).
IGtol::HasExtraLeader() == false means that this is a straight leaderline; therefore, there is 1 line (PointCount=2).
IGtol::HasExtraLeader() == True means that this is a bent leaderline; therefore, there are 2 lines (PointCount=3). The format of return information is the following array of doubles: retval[0] = X-coordinate of first leader point retval[1] = Y-coordinate of first leader point retval[2] = Z-coordinate of first leader point
retval[3] = X-coordinate of second leader point retval[4] = Y-coordinate of second leader point retval[5] = Z-coordinate of second leader point
retval[6] = X-coordinate of third leader point retval[7] = Y-coordinate of third leader point retval[8] = Z-coordinate of third leader point Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.GetLeaderCount">IGtol::GetLeaderCount</see> to see how many leaders are on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">IGTol</see> object.

Member.Remarks: A GTol can have a straight leader (1 segment) or a bent leader (2 segments), or it might have a perpendicular leader, which can have either 2 or 3 segments, depending on the situation. The returned array contains the point information to define the leader. It contains the x,y,z coordinates for each vertex in the leader. It can contain up to 12 doubles (4 sets of x,y,z values). Member.Name: IGetSymArcs
Member.Description: Gets an array that defines all arcs in the symbol.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: Indexed position of the symbol

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
Each arc in the symbol is defined by three points: center, arc start, and arc end. Format of return information is the following array of doubles: For the ith arc: retval[9 * i + 0] = X-coordinate of center point retval[9 * i + 1] = Y-coordinate of center point retval[9 * i + 2] = Z-coordinate of center point
retval[9 * i + 3] = X-coordinate of arc start point retval[9 * i + 4] = Y-coordinate of arc start point retval[9 * i + 5] = Z-coordinate of arc start point
retval[9 * i + 6] = X-coordinate of arc end point retval[9 * i + 7] = Y-coordinate of arc end point retval[9 * i + 8] = Z-coordinate of arc end point

Member.Name: IGetSymCircles
Member.Description: Gets an array that defines all circles in the symbol.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: Indexed position of the symbol

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
Each circle in the symbol is defined by its radius and center point. Format of return information is the following array of doubles. For the ith circle:
retval[4 * i] = radius retval[4 * i + 1] = X-coordinate of center point retval[4 * i + 2] = Y-coordinate of center point retval[4 * i + 3] = Z-coordinate of center point

Member.Name: IGetSymEdgeCounts
Member.Description: Gets an array of the number of lines, arcs and circles in the specified symbol.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: Indexed position of the symbol

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of shorts (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks: Format of return information is the following array of short integers: retval[0] = Line count retval[1] = Arc count retval[2] = Circle count retval[3] = Text count For more information, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IGetSymText">IGtol::IGetSymText</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IGetSymTextPoints">IGtol::IGetSymTextPoints</see>.

Member.Name: IGetSymLines
Member.Description: Gets an array that defines all lines in the symbol.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: Indexed position of the symbol

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
Each line in the symbol is defined by two points. Format of return information is the following array of doubles: For the ith line:
retval[6 * i + 0] = X-coordinate of first point retval[6 * i + 1] = Y-coordinate of first point retval[6 * i + 2] = Z-coordinate of first point
retval[6 * i + 3] = X-coordinate of second point retval[6 * i + 4] = Y-coordinate of second point retval[6 * i + 5] = Z-coordinate of second point

Member.Name: IGetSymText
Member.Description: Gets the symbol text.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swGtolGeomCharSymbol_e">Symbol index</see> number used by SOLIDWORKS

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of strings. The size of the array is based on the number of text pieces in this GTol. This number can be determined using TextCount returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IGetSymEdgeCounts">IGtol::IGetSymEdgeCounts</see>. VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Name: IGetSymTextPoints
Member.Description: Gets the text points for the specified symbol.

Parameter.Name: SymIdx
Parameter.Description: Indexed position of the symbol

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The size of the return array is based on the number of text pieces in this GTol, which you can determine using the return value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IGetSymEdgeCounts">IGtol::IGetSymEdgeCounts</see>. The format of the returned data is an array of doubles: retval[0] - X location of text 1 retval[1] - Y location of text 1 retval[2] - Z location of text 1
retval[3] - X location of text 2 retval[4] - Y location of text 2 retval[5] - Z location of text 2
retval[ (n*3-3)] - X location of text n retval[ (n*3-2)] - Y location of text n retval[ (n*3-1)] - Z location of text n

Member.Remarks: The return value is the following array of doubles: [ textPtX, textPtY, textPtZ ] where the text position values are offset values from the origin of this <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">IGTol</see> object.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: 0-based index of the piece of text

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Name: IGetWitnessLine
Member.Description: Gets the extension line that connects the leader of this geometric tolerance with the entity that is being dimensioned.
Member.Returns:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to array of six doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
As you drag a geometric tolerance leader off an entity, SOLIDWORKS dynamically builds a witness or extension line that connects the leader to the entity. The return value is the following array of six doubles: [ startPt[3], endPt[3] ] where:
startPt[3] = x,y,z start point coordinates of the witness line
endPt[3] = x,y,z end point coordinates of the witness line

<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IsAttached">IGtol::IsAttached</see> to determine whether this symbol is currently using a leader. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.HasExtraLeader">IGtol::HasExtraLeader</see> to determine whether this symbol is using a bent leader. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.GetLeaderSide">IGtol::GetLeaderSide</see> to determine where the leader is attached to the symbol. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetLeader">IGtol::SetLeader</see> to set the characteristics of the leader on this symbol.

<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.IsAttached">IGtol::IsAttached</see> to determine whether this symbol is currently using a leader. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.HasExtraLeader">IGtol::HasExtraLeader</see> to determine whether this symbol is using a bent leader. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.GetLeaderSide">IGtol::GetLeaderSide</see> to determine where the leader is attached to the symbol. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetLeader">IGtol::SetLeader</see> to set the characteristics of the leader on this symbol.

Member.Description: Sets the symbols for the specified frame.

Parameter.Name: FrameNumber
Parameter.Description: Feature control frame 1 for first

Parameter.Name: GCS
Parameter.Description: Geometric tolerance symbol (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: TolDia1
Parameter.Description: Diameter symbol exists for tolerance 1 (True or false)

Parameter.Name: TolMC1
Parameter.Description: Material condition symbol for tolerance 1 (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: TolDia2
Parameter.Description: Diameter symbol exists for tolerance 2 (True or false)

Parameter.Name: TolMC2
Parameter.Description: Material condition symbol for tolerance 2 (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: DatumMC1
Parameter.Description: Material condition symbols for primary datum (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: DatumMC2
Parameter.Description: Material condition symbols for secondary datum (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: DatumMC3
Parameter.Description: Material condition symbols for tertiary datum (see Remarks)

Member.Remarks:
This method is valid only if this Gtol was created in a version of SOLIDWORKS earlier than 2022. GTol symbols are defined in C:\ProgramData\SolidWorks\SolidWorks 20nn\lang\english\gtol.sym. Reference this file to specify GCS, TolMC1, TolMC2, DatumMC1, DatumMC2, and DatumMC3 in LibraryName-SymbolName> format. Examples:
GCS = "" (Position symbol in the ISO Geometric Tolerancing Symbols library) TolMC1 = "" (Least Material Condition symbol in the Modifying Symbols library) After calling this method, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetFrameValues2">IGtol::SetFrameValues2</see> to specify tolerance and datum values.

Member.Name: SetFrameValues2
Member.Signature: SetFrameValues2( System.short FrameNumber, System.string Tol1, System.string Tol2, System.string Datum1, System.string Datum2, System.string Datum3 )
Member.Description: Sets the geometric tolerance values and datum references in the specified frame of this GTol symbol.

Parameter.Name: FrameNumber
Parameter.Description: Symbol frame number; 1 for first frame (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Tol1
Parameter.Description: Tolerance 1 value

Parameter.Name: Tol2
Parameter.Description: Tolerance 2 value

Parameter.Name: Datum1
Parameter.Description: Primary datum with material conditions (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Datum2
Parameter.Description: Secondary datum with material conditions (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Datum3
Parameter.Description: Tertiary datum with material conditions (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if frame values are set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method is valid only if this Gtol was created in a version of SOLIDWORKS earlier than 2022. Before calling this method, call:
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetFrameSymbols2">IGtol::SetFrameSymbols2</see> to specify the GTol symbol for this frame. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.GetFrameCount">IGtol::GetFrameCount</see> to specify FrameNumber. Geometric tolerance and material condition symbols are defined in C:\ProgramData\SolidWorks\SolidWorks 20nn\lang\english\gtol.sym. Inspect this file as you specify Datum1, Datum2, and Datum3 in LibraryName-SymbolName> format. For example, for datum tags A, B, and C: bRet = aGTol.SetFrameValues2(1, "0.2", "", "B-A-C", "B-C", "C-A")
sets the first symbol frame of this GTol with:
Tolerance 1 = 0.2 Primary datum = B-A-C Secondary datum = B-C Teritiary datum = C-A

Member.Name: AssignTagPrefix
Member.Signature: AssignTagPrefix( System.int Index, System.string TagPrefix, System.int ApplyTo )
Member.Description: Prefixes the manual datum tags of specified holes with specified text.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of row to which to apply TagPrefix

Parameter.Name: TagPrefix
Parameter.Description: Prefix to apply

Parameter.Name: ApplyTo
Parameter.Description: Apply to other holes as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_e">swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_e</see> (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if prefix successfully assigned, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method:
is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IHoleTable.TagStyle">IHoleTable::TagStyle</see> is set to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swHoleTableTagStyle_e">swHoleTableTagStyle_e</see>.swHoleTable_ManualTags. corresponds to the functionality of the Assign Tag Prefix dialog that pops up when you right-click on a hole table row of a manual tag. If ApplyTo is specified with swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_e:
swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_OnlySpecifiedHole, then only the hole as specified by Index is assigned TagPrefix. swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_AllHolesOfSameSize, then all holes that are the same size as the hole specified by Index are assigned TagPrefix. When TagPrefix is assigned to only the hole as specified by Index, the numbering of all holes of the same size changes. For example, if:
A model view has six holes of two different sizes, and the hole table manual tags are initially labeled: AA1, AA2, AA3, AA4, BB1, BB2
Specify Index with the row index of AA1. Specify TagPrefix with "AB". Specify ApplyTo with swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_e.swHoleTableTagPrefixApply_OnlySpecifiedHole. After calling this method:
The hole table manual tags are re-labeled: AB1, AA1, AA2, AA3, BB1, BB2 Notice that AA1 is re-labeled to AB1, and AA2 - AA4 are re-numbered to AA1 - AA3. BB1 and BB2 are unchanged.

Member.Remarks: Because many of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation">ITableAnnotation</see> APIs apply to all parts of a table annotation that has been split, you might not want all of the table annotations when just one table annotation would be sufficient. Thus, for this method, you might want to specify 1 for Count so that a single value is returned. Or, you can call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IHoleTable.GetTableAnnotationCount">IHoleTable::GetTableAnnotationCount</see> if you want the total number of table annotations, including any splits, for this hole table feature.

Member.Name: SetImportLayerToSheetFormat
Member.Description: Sets whether the specified visible layers are imported to the sheet format or drawing sheet.

Parameter.Name: Layers
Parameter.Description: Array of strings of the names of the layers (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: SheetFormat
Parameter.Description: True to import the specified visible layers to the sheet format, false to import them to the drawing sheet

Member.Returns: True of importing the specified visible layers was successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method only supports importing to a drawing; it does not support importing to a part sketch.
The Layers argument can contain either a string or an array of strings, where the strings are the layer names with which to work. You can also specify the argument as empty, which indicates all layers. If this method is not used, the default behavior is to import all layers to the drawing sheet.
The import to sheet or sheet format Boolean is the same for all sheets that are imported; you cannot specify it on a sheet-by-sheet basis.
Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) Example To import all layers on all sheets to drawings sheets in SOLIDWORKS (this is the default behavior):
boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerToSheetFormat (emptyVariant, false)
To import layers "A" and "B" to the drawing sheet and the remaining layers to the sheet format:
boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerToSheetFormat (emptyVariant, True) layerName(0) = "A" layerName(1) = "B" layerVariant = layerName boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerToSheetFormat ((layerVariant), false)

Member.Name: SetImportLayerVisibility
Member.Description: Sets whether the specified layers are imported hidden or visible.

Parameter.Name: Layers
Parameter.Description: Array of strings of the names of the layers (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Visibility
Parameter.Description: Visibility of the layers as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swImportDxfDwg_LayerVisibility_e">swImportDxfDwg_LayerVisibility_e</see>

Member.Returns: True if setting the visibility of these layers is successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method only supports importing to a drawing; it does not support importing to a part sketch.
The Layers argument can contain either a string or an array of strings, where the strings are the layer names with which to work. You can also specify the argument as empty, which indicates all layers. If this method is not used, the default behavior is to import all layers with the same visibility as they have in the DXF/DWG file.
The layer visibility is the same for all sheets that are imported; you cannot specify the layer visibility on a sheet-by-sheet basis.
Hidden layers are always imported to the drawing sheet.
You should first specify the behavior that applies to all layers, using an empty VARIANT, because this overrides any information you have previously entered for specific layers. Then, you should use this method with layer names in the VARIANT, to override that default behavior on a layer-by-layer basis. Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) Example To import all layers with the same visibility as in the DXF/DWG file (this is the default behavior): boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerVisibility (emptyVariant, swImportDxfDwg_LayerMaintain)
To import layer "A" hidden and the remaining layers visible: boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerVisibility (emptyVariant, swImportDxfDwg_LayerVisible) layerName = "A" layerVariant = layerName
boolstatus = ImportDxfDwgData.SetImportLayerVisibility ((layerVariant), swImportDxfDwg_LayerHidden)

Member.Name: SetBody
Member.Description: Modifies the wire body for this imported curve feature.

Parameter.Name: DispBody
Parameter.Description: Wire <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">body</see>

Member.Remarks:
Wire bodies contain wires, loops, coedges, edges, and vertices. Wires typically represent profiles, construction lines, and center lines of swept shapes. Wires can also represent wire frames that, when surfaced, form shells. The following methods create wire bodies:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge.CreateWireBody">IEdge::CreateWireBody</see>

Member.Name: GetD1ModifiedSpacingValue
Member.Description: Gets the spacing in Direction 1 of the specified modified pattern instance.

Parameter.Name: Instance
Parameter.Description: Pattern instance number (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Spacing value in Direction 1
Member.Remarks:
To specify Instance, you can use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IInstanceToVaryOptions.GetModifiedInstances">IInstanceToVaryOptions::GetModifiedInstances</see> to learn which pattern instances are modified. To calculate Instance:
Ensure that the D2PatternSeedOnly property in the pattern feature data object is set to false. Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2

Member.Description: Sets the interfering components and their transforms.

Parameter.Name: ComponentList
Parameter.Description: Array of interfering <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">components</see>

Parameter.Name: TransformList
Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">transforms</see>

Example.Name: Set Components and Transforms for Interference Detection
Set Components and Transforms for Interference Detection
Set Components and Transforms for Interference Detection

Member.Remarks: You must pass in absolute transforms to this method. If you want to transform a component incrementally before interference detection, then you must multiply that incremental transform by the component's existing transform before passing in the resultant transform. To produce the effect of identity transforms on components (i.e., the components do not move while participating in interference detection), the transforms for those components passed in can be null or Nothing. However, passing in null or Nothing for all of the transforms is interpreted as invalid input. NOTE: A null or Nothing is interpreted as the component’s existing transform (i.e., an identity incremental transform).

Member.Name: GetID
Member.Description: Gets the layer ID for this layer.
Member.Returns: Layer ID for this layer
Member.Remarks:
A layer ID:
is unique within the drawing. is persistent across SOLIDWORKS Design sessions and never changes, even if you <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILayer.Name">change the name of the layer</see>. can be used to identify a specific layer when multiple layers exist in a drawing. cannot be assigned by applications or users. is not the same as a <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/overview/Persistent_Reference_IDs.htm">persistent reference ID</see>. You can get a layer using its persistent reference ID, but you cannot get a layer using this method.

Member.Returns: Layer name

Member.Name: Printable
Member.Description: Gets and sets whether this layer is printed when the drawing document is printed.
Member.Returns: True if the layer is printable, false if the layer is not visible (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Always call this property after setting <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILayer.Visible">ILayer::Visible</see> to the opposite state, because setting ILayer::Visible might change the state of ILayer::Printable. It is not possible to make a layer printable if it is not visible. To ensure that ILayer::Visible and ILayer::Printable are set to the desired states, perform the following steps in this order:
Set ILayer::Visible. Get the state of ILayer::Printable. Set ILayer::Printable if necessary.

Member.Name: Visible
Member.Description: Gets or sets the visibility of this layer.
Member.Returns: True if the layer is visible, false if the layer is not visible (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
After setting this property to the opposite state, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILayer.Printable">ILayer::Printable</see> to check its state, because setting ILayer::Visible might change the state of ILayer::Printable. To ensure that ILayer::Visible and ILayer::Printable are set to the desired states, perform the following steps in this order:
Set ILayer::Visible. Get the state of ILayer::Printable. Set ILayer::Printable if necessary.

Member.Name: SetFeatureScope
Member.Signature: SetFeatureScope( System.bool FeatureScopeOption, System.bool AutoSelectBodies, System.object Bodies )
Member.Description: Sets the feature scope, whether to autoselect the affected bodies, and the affected bodies in this linear pattern feature.

Parameter.Name: FeatureScopeOption
Parameter.Description: True to specify affected bodies, false to apply the pattern to all bodies every time the feature regenerates (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: AutoSelectBodies
Parameter.Description: True to automatically select all bodies intersected by this pattern feature, false to specify affected bodies (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Bodies
Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> to be affected; valid only if FeatureScopeOption is true and AutoSelectBodies is false

Member.Returns: True if feature scope set successfully, false if not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: If this method returns false, then default values for FeatureScopeOption and AutoSelectBodies are set. A subsequent call to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> creates the feature with a FeatureScopeOption of true and an AutoSelectBodies of true. After calling IFeature::ModifyDefinition, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetErrorCode2">IFeature::GetErrorCode2</see> to determine what's wrong and then take necessary remedial action. For more information, see the Linear Patterns and the Linear Pattern PropertyManager topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Name: SkippedItemArray
Member.Description: Gets or sets the items skipped in this linear pattern feature.
Member.Returns: Array of integers representing skipped items
Member.Remarks:
The array is 0-based. If you skip the third and fifth items, then the array looks like ArrayOut[0]=3 and ArrayOut[1]=5. To calculate the pattern instance numbers to skip: Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2

Member.Name: StructureSystemToPatternArray
Member.Description: Gets or sets the structure systems to pattern in this linear pattern feature.
Member.Returns: Array of <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemFolder">IStructureSystemFolder</see>s
Member.Remarks: This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILinearPatternFeatureData.BodyPattern">ILinearPatternFeatureData::BodyPattern</see> is true. Use the setter of this property to change structure systems only after the linear pattern feature has been created. Before using this property in .NET code, read <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/IDispatch_Object_Arrays_as_Input_in_.NET.htm">IDispatch Object Arrays as Input in .NET</see>. To remove a structure system from the pattern, set this property to a DispatchWrapper array containing one null element. For more information, see the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Pattern and Mirror Support topic.

Member.Name: VarySketch
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to allow the pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to enclosing geometry in this linear pattern feature.
Member.Returns: True to allow the pattern instances of a seed sketch to vary in relation to enclosing geomtry, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only when creating a pattern from a seed sketch. The seed sketch has:
An enclosing boundary of base geometry. Fully defined relations. Dimensions only for measurements that will not vary in the pattern instances. A driving dimension that is used to specify the direction of the linear pattern. If this property is true:
Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILinearPatternFeatureData.D1Axis">ILinearPatternFeatureData::D1Axis</see> with a driving dimension of the seed sketch. Pattern instances vary with and are constrained by the enclosing geometry. See the SOLIDWORKS Help > Parts and Features > Features > Patterns and Mirroring > Control and Modify Patterns > Vary Sketch topic. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property.

Member.Name: GetModifiedInstance
Member.Signature: GetModifiedInstance( System.int Instance, out System.double D1Distance, out System.double D1NominalVal, out System.double D2Distance, out System.double D2NominalVal )
Member.Description: Gets the modified values for the specified pattern instance in this linear component pattern feature.

Parameter.Name: Instance
Parameter.Description: Pattern instance number (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: D1Distance
Parameter.Description: Distance from the pattern seed in Direction 1

Parameter.Name: D1NominalVal
Parameter.Description: Offset from the nominal position of Instance in Direction 1

Parameter.Name: D2Distance
Parameter.Description: Distance from the pattern seed in Direction 2

Parameter.Name: D2NominalVal
Parameter.Description: Offset from the nominal position of Instance in Direction 2

Member.Remarks:
To specify Instance, you can use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.GetModifiedInstances">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::GetModifiedInstances</see> to learn which pattern instances are modified. To calculate Instance:
Ensure that <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.D2PatternSeedOnly">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::D2PatternSeedOnly</see> is set to false. Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2

Member.Remarks:
To modify a feature in a... Then...
Part
TopDoc argument is the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> for the part Component argument is NULL
Assembly
TopDoc is the IModelDoc2 object for the assembly Component argument is the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">IComponent2</see> object in which the feature is to be modified This method puts the model into a rollback state to allow access to the selections that define this feature. Member.Returns: True if the pattern instance is modified successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks:
To calculate Instance:
Ensure that <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.D2PatternSeedOnly">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::D2PatternSeedOnly</see> is set to false. Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2
