If you set this property to true, you can also set:
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.RotationAngle">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::RotationAngle</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.RotationAxis">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::RotationAxis</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.ReverseAxisOfRotation">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::ReverseAxisOfRotation</see> <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.FixedAxisOfRotation">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::FixedAxisOfRotation</see> See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property. Member.Remarks: This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.RotateInstances">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::RotateInstances</see> is true. For more information, see the Linear Component Pattern PropertyManager topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Member.Name: RotationAxis
Member.Description: Gets or sets the axis of rotation of components in this linear component pattern feature.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRefAxis">Axis</see>, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISketchLine">line</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see> around which the pattern components rotate
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.RotateInstances">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::RotateInstances</see> is true. The rotation axis must be parallel to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.D1Axis">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::D1Axis</see>. Use:
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.FixedAxisOfRotation">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::FixedAxisOfRotation</see> to specify whether all instances of components rotate about this rotation axis.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData.ReverseAxisOfRotation">ILocalLinearPatternFeatureData::ReverseAxisOfRotation</see> to reverse the direction of this rotation axis. You cannot edit this property to null or Nothing after the feature is first created with a rotation axis. If you try, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> returns false and the feature does not roll back. To roll back the feature, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ForceRebuild3">IModelDoc2::ForceRebuild3</see> or move the rollback bar in the user interface to before and after the feature. See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this property. For more information, see the Linear Component Pattern PropertyManager topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Example.Name: Get Number of Instances Skipped in Driving Feature
Get Number of Instances Skipped in Driving Feature
Get Number of Instances Skipped in Driving Feature

Member.Remarks:
This array is 0-based. If you skip the third and fifth components, then the array looks like ArrayOut[0]=3 and ArrayOut[1]=5. To calculate the pattern instance numbers to skip: Calculate: For a bi-directional pattern: I = n2 * (i - 1) + (j - 1) For a uni-directional pattern: I = i - 1 where:
I = pattern instance number n2 = number of instances in Direction 2 i = index for Direction 1 j = index for Direction 2

Member.Name: EnumCoEdges
Member.Description: Enumerates the coedges in a loop.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumCoEdges">Coedges enumeration</see>
Member.Remarks: The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICoEdge">ICoEdge</see> objects are returned in a CW or CCW manner based on the direction of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2">ILoop2</see>. The loop direction is determined as follows: if a loop is viewed along its direction, with the face normal pointing upwards, then the face that owns the loop is to the left. This means that inner loops are CW and outer loops are CCW. To determine if a loop is an outer loop, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IsOuter">ILoop2::IsOuter</see>. The coedge direction always aligns with the direction of the ILoop2.

Member.Name: EnumEdges
Member.Description: Enumerates the edges in a face.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumEdges">Edges enumeration</see>
Member.Remarks: The edge objects are returned in a CW or CCW manner based on the direction of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2">ILoop2</see>. The loop direction is determined as follows: if a loop is viewed along its direction, with the face normal pointing upwards, then the face that owns the loop is to the left. This means that inner loops are CW and outer loops are CCW. To determine if a loop is an outer loop, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IsOuter">ILoop2::IsOuter</see>. Because an edge is shared by multiple loops, the edge direction may be opposite to the direction of the ILoop2. To check this, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge.EdgeInFaceSense">IEdge::EdgeInFaceSense</see>.

The loop direction is determined as follows: if a loop is viewed along its direction, with the face normal pointing upwards, then the face that owns the loop is to the left. This means that inner loops are CW and outer loops are CCW. To determine if a loop is an outer loop, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IsOuter">ILoop2::IsOuter</see>. Because an edge is shared by multiple loops, the edge direction might be opposite to the direction of the ILoop2. To check this, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge.EdgeInFaceSense">IEdge::EdgeInFaceSense</see>. If the loop is a singular loop, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.GetVertices">ILoop2::GetVertices</see> to get its position (a single vertex). ILoop2::GetEdges returns an empty array if the loop is singular.

Member.Name: IGetEdges
Member.Description: Gets all the edges in the loop.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see> that make up the loop VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks: The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">IEdge</see> objects are returned in a CW or CCW manner based on the direction of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2">ILoop2</see>. The loop direction is determined as follows: if a loop is viewed along its direction, with the face normal pointing upwards, then the face that owns the loop is to the left. This means that inner loops are CW and outer loops are CCW. To determine if a loop is an outer loop, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IsOuter">ILoop2::IsOuter</see>. Because an edge is shared by multiple loops, the edge direction might be opposite to the direction of the ILoop2. To check this, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge.IEdgeInFaceSense2">IEdge::IEdgeInFaceSense2</see>. If the loop is a singular loop, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IGetVertices">ILoop2::IGetVertices</see> to get its position (a single vertex). LIoop2::GetEdges returns an empty array if the loop is singular.

The loop direction is determined as follows: if a loop is viewed along its direction, with the face normal pointing upwards, then the face that owns the loop is to the left. This means that inner loops are CW and outer loops are CCW. To determine if a loop is an outer loop, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2.IsOuter">ILoop2::IsOuter</see>. Publish Text and Custom Properties from Theme to MBD 3D PDF
Publish Text and Custom Properties from Theme to MBD 3D PDF

Member.Remarks:
SOLIDWORKS Model Based Definition (MBD) is an integrated drawingless manufacturing solution for SOLIDWORKS. Typical steps for generating a SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using the SOLIDWORKS API are:
Get the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData">MBD3DPdfData object</see> using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetMBD3DPdfData">IModelDocExtension::GetMBD3DPdfData</see>. Set the path and file name of the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF theme using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.ThemeName">IMBD3DPdfData::ThemeName</see>. Get standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetMoreViews</see>. Set standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetMoreViews</see>. Get and set text and custom properties in the theme using the array of objects returned by this method. Set the path for the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.FilePath">IMBD3DPdfData::FilePath</see>. Generate the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.PublishTo3DPDF">IModelDocExtension::PublishTo3DPDF</see>. See the SOLIDWORKS Help for details about MBD.

Member.Name: EnableMultiBodyConsume
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to replace the original edit body with multiple solid bodies created during regeneration of a multibody macro feature.
Member.Returns: True to replace the original edit body with multiple solid bodies, false to not
Member.Remarks: This method was designed to work specifically with macro features that generate multiple solid bodies. The <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Rebuild_Function.htm">rebuild</see> function of a macro feature creates or regenerates the macro feature in the FeatureManager design tree. By default, if the rebuild function creates multiple solid bodies, it appends the new solid bodies to the original edit body in the Solid Bodies folder of the FeatureManager design tree. Always set this property to true in the rebuild function when working with macro features involving multiple input or output bodies.

Member.Name: GetEditTargetTransform
Member.Description: Gets the transform of the component where the macro feature resides if at least one selection in the macro feature belongs to a different component.
Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">Math transform</see> of the component where the macro feature resides if at least one selection in the macro feature belongs to a different component, or NULL if all of the selections in the macro feature belong to the component where the macro feature resides
Member.Remarks:
When <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Rebuild_Function.htm">regenerating a macro feature</see> in a part that is a component in an assembly, you cannot get the component's transform where the macro feature resides because you cannot get the component using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.GetComponent">IEntity::GetComponent</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.IGetComponent2">IEntity::IGetComponent2</see> in a part document. However, you may need the component's transform because references from other components to it often need to be transformed. This method provides this transform. If there are no external references among the macro feature selections (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.GetSelections3">IMacroFeatureData::GetSelections3</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.IGetSelections3">IMacroFeatureData::IGetSelections3</see>), then this method returns NULL. If there are external references among the macro feature selections, then this method returns the transform of the component where the macro feature resides.
For example, if the macro feature includes a selection box in which the user can select a face, and the user selects a face on a different component, then this method can get the component's transform where the macro feature resides. However, if all of the selections in the macro feature belong to the component where the macro feature resides, then this method returns NULL because you probably will not need the transform. See also <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Macro_Features_and_Component_Transforms.htm">Macro Features and Component Transforms</see>.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this method.

Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">transforms</see> for the selections' components

Example.Name: Cut Body in Half Using Macro Feature

Member.Remarks:
When a macro feature is inserted in-context and an entity on a different component is selected, you may need to know that component's transform.
If the assembly is the active document, then you can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.GetComponent">IEntity::GetComponent</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Transform2">IComponent2::Transform2</see> to get the component's transform.
However, if the part for the component is open for editing and a <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Edit_Definition_Function.htm">macro feature is being edited</see>, then you must use IMacroFeatureData::GetSelections3 to get the component's transform. This method returns the transform and the selection. If the selection belongs to the same part as the macro feature, then NULL is returned. See also <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Macro_Features_and_Component_Transforms.htm">Macro Features and Component Transforms</see>.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this method.

Number of strings in array Types of images in this order Image format and sizes
Three
Regular Suppressed Highlighted
Windows bitmap (*.bmp) format 16 pixels wide X 18 pixels high
Nine NOTES:
This size array is only valid for macro features created in parts, assemblies, and drawings in SOLIDWORKS 2017 and later. SOLIDWORKS displays the appropriate images based on the current DPI setting of the display device.
Regular small Suppressed small Highlighted small Regular medium Suppressed medium Highlighted medium Regular large Suppressed large Highlighted large
Windows bitmap (*.bmp) format Recommended sizes are:
Small: 20 pixels wide X 20 pixels high Medium: 32 pixels wide X 32 pixels high Large: 40 pixels wide X 40 pixels high You can specify either the full path name or just the file name for the strings; for example, c:\bitmaps\icon1.bmp or icon1.bmp.

Member.Name: IGetSelections3
Member.Signature: IGetSelections3( System.int SelCount, out System.object Objects, out System.int ObjectTypes, out System.int SelMarks, out View DrViews, out MathTransform ComponentXForms )
Member.Description: Gets the selected objects for the macro feature.

Parameter.Name: SelCount
Parameter.Description: Number of selected objects

Parameter.Name: Objects
Parameter.Description: Array of selected objects of size SelCount

Parameter.Name: ObjectTypes
Parameter.Description: Array of the selected object types as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see> of size SelCount

Parameter.Name: SelMarks
Parameter.Description: Array of marks associated with the selected objects of size SelCount

Parameter.Name: DrViews
Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView">drawing views</see> of size SelCount

Parameter.Name: ComponentXForms
Parameter.Description: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMathTransform">transforms</see> for the selections' components VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Remarks:
Before calling this method, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.GetSelectionCount">IMacroFeatureData::GetSelectionCount</see> to determine the size of the arrays. When a macro feature is inserted in-context and an entity on a different component is selected, you may need to know that component's transform.
If the assembly is the active document, then you can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.IGetComponent2">IEntity::IGetComponent2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Transform2">IComponent2::Transform2</see> to get the component's transform.
However, if the part for the component is open for editing and a <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Edit_Definition_Function.htm">macro feature is being edited</see>, then you must use IMacroFeatureData::GetSelections3 to get the component's transform. This method returns the transform and the selection. If the selection belongs to the same part as the macro feature, then NULL is returned. See also <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Macro_Features_and_Component_Transforms.htm">Macro Features and Component Transforms</see>.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details on using this method.

Member.Name: ISetIconFiles
Member.Signature: ISetIconFiles( System.int IconCount, ref System.string IconFiles )
Member.Description: Sets the file names for the icons for this macro feature.

Parameter.Name: IconCount
Parameter.Description: Number of files for the icons

Parameter.Name: IconFiles
Parameter.Description:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of the file names for the icons (see Remarks)
VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Member.Remarks:
The array of the file names for IconFiles can contain either three or nine strings.
Number of strings in array Types of images in this order Image format and sizes
Three
Regular Suppressed Highlighted
Windows bitmap (*.bmp) format 16 pixels wide X 18 pixels high
Nine NOTES:
This size array is only valid for macro features created in parts, assemblies, and drawings in SOLIDWORKS 2017 and later. SOLIDWORKS displays the appropriate images based on the current DPI setting of the display device.
Regular small Suppressed small Highlighted small Regular medium Suppressed medium Highlighted medium Regular large Suppressed large Highlighted large
Windows bitmap (*.bmp) format Recommended sizes are:
Small: 20 pixels wide X 20 pixels high Medium: 32 pixels wide X 32 pixels high Large: 40 pixels wide X 40 pixels high You can specify either the full path name or just the file name for the strings; for example, c:\bitmaps\icon1.bmp or icon1.bmp. If you change the bitmaps after inserting them with a macro feature into a SOLIDWORKS document, then the new bitmaps are not displayed until you exit and restart SOLIDWORKS.

Member.Name: Provider
Member.Description: Gets or sets the error message to display in the What's Wrong dialog when a non-embedded macro feature fails to rebuild due to missing files.
Member.Returns: Error message
Member.Remarks:
This property allows you to replace the generic error message that appears in the What's Wrong dialog with a more detailed error message when this non-embedded macro feature fails to load or rebuild due to missing files. Possible causes of macro feature rebuild failure:
The model contains this COM-based macro feature, but the rebuild, edit, and security callbacks exist in an add-in that SOLIDWORKS cannot locate. The model references this non-embedded macro feature which exists in a VBA macro that SOLIDWORKS cannot locate. Third-party DLLs, add-in files, or other files associated with this non-embedded macro feature are missing. NOTE: All files required by embedded macro features are serialized with the model, so File not found errors do not occur for embedded macros, and this property need not be set for them.

Use this method to restore the rollback state if you did not modify the feature or use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IModifyDefinition2">IFeature::IModifyDefintion2</see> if you did.

Member.Description: Gets the density of selected components/bodies.

If the density varies across components in a model:
Density = ( Mass / Volume ) If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents">IMassProperty2::IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents</see> is reset, then call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.Recalculate">IMassProperty2::Recalculate</see> before using this property.

Member.Name: PrincipalAxesOfInertia
Member.Description: Gets the principal axis of inertia for the specified axis.

Parameter.Name: Axis
Parameter.Description: 0 = x axis 1 = y axis 2 = z axis

Member.Returns: Zero-based array of size 3 (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method returns:
A vector that represents the specified Axis: lx, ly, or lz.
Metric units unless explicitly specified otherwise. If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassPropertyOverrideOptions.OverrideMomentsOfInertia">IMassPropertyOverrideOptions::OverrideMomentsOfInertia</see> is true or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents">IMassProperty2::IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents</see> is reset, then call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.Recalculate">IMassProperty2::Recalculate</see> before using this property.

Member.Name: PrincipalMomentsOfInertia
Member.Description: Gets the principal moments of inertia.
Member.Returns: Array of size 3 (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This property returns metric units unless explicitly specified otherwise.
The return value is a 0-based array of doubles:
[ Px, Py, Pz ]
If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassPropertyOverrideOptions.OverrideMomentsOfInertia">IMassPropertyOverrideOptions::OverrideMomentsOfInertia</see> is true or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents">IMassProperty2::IncludeHiddenBodiesOrComponents</see> is reset, then call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMassProperty2.Recalculate">IMassProperty2::Recalculate</see> before using this property.

Member.Name: GetCurrentMisalignedDeviation
Member.Description: Gets the current misalignment deviation for the misaligned concentric mate.
Member.Returns: Current misalignment deviation
Member.Remarks: If the current deviation of misalignment is greater than <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetMaximumMisalignedDeviation">IMate2::GetMaximumMisalignedDeviation</see>, then the mate fails to solve. The current deviation and the maximum deviation are cumulative across both concentric mates in the Hole Set. For example, if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetConcentricAlignmentType">IMate2::GetConcentricAlignmentType</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swConcentricAlignmentType_e">swConcentricAlignmentType_e</see>.swConcentricAlignSymmetric, the deviation from both holes is summed before comparison with the maximum deviation.

Member.Remarks: Call this method before calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.MateEntity">IMate2::MateEntity</see> to get the number of entities in the mate.

Member.Name: GetMaximumMisalignedDeviation
Member.Description: Gets the maximum allowed misalignment deviation for this misaligned concentric mate.
Member.Returns: Maximum allowed misalignment deviation
Member.Remarks: If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetCurrentMisalignedDeviation">IMate2::GetCurrentMisalignedDeviation</see> is greater than the value returned by this method, then the mate fails to solve. The current deviation and the maximum deviation are cumulative across both concentric mates in the Hole Set. For example, if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetConcentricAlignmentType">IMate2::GetConcentricAlignmentType</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swConcentricAlignmentType_e">swConcentricAlignmentType_e</see>.swConcentricAlignSymmetric, the deviation from both holes is summed before comparison with the maximum deviation.

Parameter.Description: Maximum allowed misalignment deviation

Member.Remarks: This method is valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetUseMisalignedDeviationDocumentProperty">IMate2::GetUseMisalignedDeviationDocumentProperty</see> returns false. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.SetUseMisalignedDeviationDocumentProperty">IMate2::SetUseMisalignedDeviationDocumentProperty</see> to set UseDocumentProperty to false if you want to use this method to set the maximum misaligned deviation for this mate. If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetCurrentMisalignedDeviation">IMate2::GetCurrentMisalignedDeviation</see> is greater than the value set by this method, then the mate fails to solve. The current deviation and the maximum deviation are cumulative across both concentric mates in the Hole Set. For example, if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.GetConcentricAlignmentType">IMate2::GetConcentricAlignmentType</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swConcentricAlignmentType_e">swConcentricAlignmentType_e</see>.swConcentricAlignSymmetric, the deviation from both holes is summed before comparison with the maximum deviation.

Member.Name: EntityParams
Member.Description: Gets the parameters for this mate entity.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles representing the mate entity parameters (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return value is the following array of doubles: [ pointX, pointY, pointZ, vectorI, vectorJ, vectorK, radius1, radius2 ] where
pointX is the X location of this mate entity in the assembly model space
pointY is the Y location of this mate entity in the assembly model space
pointZ is the Z location of this mate entity in the assembly model space
vectorI is the i component of the assembly mate vector
vectorJ is the j component of the assembly mate vector
vectorK is the k component of the assembly mate vector
radius1 is the value for the first radius
radius2 is the value for the second radius To define the mate entity, the following information is returned based on the mate type. All coordinate information is given in terms of the assembly coordinate system where the mate resides.
Mate Type
Returned
swMatePoint
pointX, pointY, pointZ
swMateLine
pointX, pointY, pointZ, vectorI, vectorJ, vectorK where the point is a point on the line and the vector represents the line direction.
swMatePlane
pointX, pointY, pointZ, vectorI, vectorJ, vectorK where the point is a point on the plane and the vector represents the plane normal.
swMateCylinder
pointX, pointY, pointZ, vectorI, vectorJ, vectorK, radius1 where the point is a point on the cylinder axis and the vector represents the cylinder axis.
swMateCone
pointX, pointY, pointZ, vectorI, vectorJ, vectorK, radius1, radius2 where the point is a point on the cone axis and the vector represents the cone axis.
To get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMateEntity2">IMateEntity2</see> interface, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMate2.MateEntity">IMate2::MateEntity</see>.

Example.Name: Align Assembly Component to Assembly Origin and Planes
Use Presentation Transforms to Move Component

Member.Remarks:
Transformation matrix data: |a b c . n | |d e f . o | |g h i . p | |j k l . m | The SOLIDWORKS transformation matrix is stored as a homogeneous matrix of 16 elements, ordered as shown. The first 9 elements (a to i) are elements of a 3x3 rotational sub-matrix, the next 3 elements (j,k,l) define a translation vector, and the next 1 element (m) is a scaling factor. The last 3 elements (n,o,p) are unused in this context. The 3x3 rotational sub-matrix represents 3 axis sets:
row 1 for x-axis components of rotation row 2 for y-axis components of rotation row 3 for z-axis components of rotation The 3 axes are constrained to be orthogonal and unified so that they produce a pure rotational transformation. Reflections can also be added to these axes by setting the components to negative. The rotation sub-matrix coupled with the lower-left translation vector and the lower-right corner scaling factor creates an affine transformation, which is a transformation that preserves lines and parallelism; i.e., maps parallel lines to parallel lines. If the 3 axis sets of the 3x3 rotational sub-matrix are not orthogonal or unified, then they are automatically corrected according to the following rules:
If any axis is 0, or any two axes are parallel, or all axes are coplanar, then an identity matrix replaces the rotational sub-matrix.
All axes are corrected to be of unit length.
The axes are built to be orthogonal to each other in the prioritized order of Z, X, Y (X is orthogonal to Z, Y is orthogonal to Z and X).

Member.Name: SurfaceFromMesh
Member.Signature: SurfaceFromMesh( System.int SurfaceType, System.double FacetTolerance, System.double ExtendSurfaceSize, out System.int ErrorCode )
Member.Description: Creates a surface from the selected facets in this mesh body.

Parameter.Name: SurfaceType
Parameter.Description: Type of surface to create as defined by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swSurfaceTypes_e">swSurfaceTypes_e</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: FacetTolerance
Parameter.Description: 0.0 (High tolerance) <= Percent facet selection <= 100.0 (Low tolerance)

Parameter.Name: ExtendSurfaceSize
Parameter.Description: Extension in meters of the surface body to fit the selected facets and geometric shape

Parameter.Name: ErrorCode
Parameter.Description: 0 if successful, -1 if not

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">IBody2</see>
Member.Remarks:
This method:
is analogous to the Insert menu > Mesh > Surface From Mesh functionality in the user interface. creates a Surface-From-MeshX feature in the FeatureManager design tree. Before calling this method, select as many facets in the mesh body as are needed to create the type of surface. SurfaceType can be one of only swSurfaceTypes_e.:
PLANE_TYPE SPHERE_TYPE CYLINDER_TYPE CONE_TYPE For more information, see the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Parts and Features > Graphics Mesh and Mesh BREP Bodies > Creating a Surface from Mesh Feature topic.

Member.Name: GetFirstFace
Member.Signature: GetFirstFace( out System.object FromFace1Disp, out System.object FromFace2Disp, out System.double Thickness )
Member.Description: Gets the first face in this midsurface feature and three other items.

Parameter.Name: FromFace1Disp
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Parameter.Name: FromFace2Disp
Parameter.Description: Parallel <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see> to FromFace1Disp on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Distance between the two parallel faces, FromFace1Disp and FromFace2Disp

Member.Returns: First <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see> in this midsurface feature
Member.Remarks:
The first two return values are the two faces from the original part body that were used to generate this midsurface face.
The next return value is the thickness (in meters) between the two parallel faces from the original part body.
The last return value is the first face in this midsurface feature. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetNextFace">IMidSurface3::GetNextFace</see> to get the next neutral face in this midsurface feature.

Member.Name: GetFirstFaceArray
Member.Description: Gets the first face and the thickness between the faces.

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Thickness between the faces

Member.Returns: First <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>
Member.Remarks:
A separator is needed between the front faces and back faces. Thus, a NULL always exists between the front and back faces.
For example, if there are five faces in the model, then the mid-surface has five faces. To get the five faces:
Call IMidSurface3::GetGetFirstFaceArray once.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetNextFaceArray">IMidSurface3::GetNextFaceArray</see> four times. At each call, the data is arranged as follows if there is one front face in the array: [Neutral face], [front face], NULL, [back face] If there are more than one front face in the array, then the data is arranged as follows: [Neutral face], [front face1, front face2], NULL, [back face1, back face2]
To get the next face from the original paired faces, call IMidSurface3::GetNextFaceArray.

Member.Name: GetFirstFacePair
Member.Signature: GetFirstFacePair( out System.double Thickness, out System.object PartnerFaceDisp )
Member.Description: Gets the first pair of parallel faces in this midsurface feature and the thickness (in meters) between the two faces.

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Distance between these two parallel faces

Parameter.Name: PartnerFaceDisp
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face
Member.Remarks: The two faces returned by this method are the two parallel faces from the original part body that were used to generate the first neutral face in this midsurface feature. This method is similar to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetFirstFace">IMidSurface3::GetFirstFace</see>, except this method does not return the neutral face. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetNextFacePair">IMidSurface3::GetNextFacePair</see> to get the next pair of faces in this midsurface feature.

Member.Name: GetFirstNeutralSheet
Member.Description: Gets the first reference surface in this midsurface feature.
Member.Returns: First reference surface sheet <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">body</see> in this midsurface feature
Member.Remarks: Each reference surface in the midsurface feature is considered to be a sheet body. If the reference surfaces are sewn together during the creation of the midsurface feature (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.InsertMidSurfaceExt">IModelDoc2::InsertMidSurfaceExt</see>), then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface sheet body. The sheet body returned from this method has the normal topology that you would expect to find on a body (for example, faces, edges, and so on). See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">IBody2</see> object for methods that provide access to this topology. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetNextNeutralSheet">IMidSurface3::GetNextNeutralSheet</see> to get the next reference surface in this midsurface feature.

Member.Name: GetNeutralSheetCount
Member.Description: Gets the total number of reference surfaces found in this midsurface feature.
Member.Returns: Number of reference surface sheet bodies found in this midsurface feature
Member.Remarks: Each reference surface in the midsurface feature is considered to be a sheet body. If the reference surfaces are sewn together during the creation of our midsurface feature, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertMidSurface">IFeatureManager::InsertMidSurface</see>, then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface sheet body.

Member.Name: GetNextFace
Member.Signature: GetNextFace( out System.object FromFace1Disp, out System.object FromFace2Disp, out System.double Thickness )
Member.Description: Gets the next neutral face in this midsurface feature.

Parameter.Name: FromFace1Disp
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Parameter.Name: FromFace2Disp
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Distance between the two parallel faces, FromFace1Disp and FromFace2Disp

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> in this midsurface feature
Member.Remarks:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetFirstFace">IMidSurface3::GetFirstFace</see> before calling this method to get the first neutral face. This method returns the next neutral face in this midsurface feature along with three other items.
The first two return values are the two faces from the original part body that were used to generate this neutral midsurface face.
The next return value is the thickness (in meters) between the two parallel faces from the original part body.
The last return value is the neutral face in this midsurface feature.

Member.Name: GetNextFaceArray
Member.Description: Gets the next face from the original paired faces and the thickness between the faces.

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Thickness between the faces

Member.Returns: Next <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>
Member.Remarks:
A separator is needed between the front faces and back faces. Thus, a NULL always exists between the front faces and the back faces. For example, if there are five faces in the model, then the mid-surface has five faces. To get the five faces:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetFirstFaceArray">IMidSurface3::GetGetFirstFaceArray</see> once.
Call IMidSurface2::GetNextFaceArray four times. At each call, the data is arranged as follows if there is one front face in the array: [Neutral face], [front face], NULL, [back face] If there are more than one front face in the array, then the data is arranged as follows: [Neutral face], [front face1, front face2], NULL, [back face1, back face2]
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetFirstFaceArray">IMidSurface3::GetFirstFaceArray</see> to get the first face from the original paired faces.

Member.Name: GetNextFacePair
Member.Signature: GetNextFacePair( out System.double Thickness, out System.object PartnerFaceDisp )
Member.Description: Gets the next pair of parallel faces in this midsurface feature and the thickness (in meters) between the two faces.

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Distance between theses two parallel faces

Parameter.Name: PartnerFaceDisp
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">Face</see> on the original part body used in generating the neutral face
Member.Remarks: The two faces returned are the two parallel faces from the original part body that were used to generate the neutral face in this midsurface feature. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetFirstFacePair">IMidSurface3::GetFirstFacePair</see> to get the first pair of faces used in this midsurface feature. This method is similar to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.GetNextFace">IMidSurface3::GetNextFace</see>, except this method does not return the neutral face.

Member.Name: GetNextNeutralSheet
Member.Description: Gets the next reference surface in this midsurface feature.
Member.Returns: Next reference surface sheet <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">body</see> in this midsurface feature
Member.Remarks: Each reference surface in the midsurface feature is considered a sheet body. If the reference surfaces are sewn together during the creation of the midsurface feature (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertMidSurface">IFeatureManager::InsertMidSurface</see>), then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface sheet body. If this is the case, then this method returns NULL. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface2.GetNeutralSheetCount">IMidSurface2::GetFirstNeutralSheet</see> to get the first and only reference surface sheet body. The sheet body returned from this method has the normal topology that you would expect to find on a body (for example, faces, edges, and so on). See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">IBody2</see> object for methods that provide access to this topology.

The next return value is the thickness (in meters) between the two parallel faces from the original part body.
The last return value is the first face in this midsurface feature. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.IGetNextFace">IMidSurface3::IGetNextFace</see> to get the next neutral face in this midsurface feature.

Member.Name: IGetFirstFaceArray
Member.Signature: IGetFirstFaceArray( out Face2 FromFrontFaceListDisp, out System.int SizeOfFrontFaceList, out Face2 FromFaceBackListDisp, out System.int SizeOfBackFaceList, out System.double Thickness )
Member.Description: Gets the first face and the thickness between the faces.

Parameter.Name: FromFrontFaceListDisp
Parameter.Description:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of front <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">faces</see>
VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Parameter.Name: SizeOfFrontFaceList
Parameter.Description: Number of front faces

Parameter.Name: FromFaceBackListDisp
Parameter.Description: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of back <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">faces</see> VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.

Parameter.Name: SizeOfBackFaceList
Parameter.Description: Number of back faces

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Thickness between the faces

Member.Returns: First <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>
Member.Remarks:
A separator is needed between the front faces and back faces. Thus, a NULL always exists between the front faces and the back faces.
For example, if there are five faces in the model, then the mid-surface has five faces. To get the five faces:
Call IMidSurface3::IGetGetFirstFaceArray once.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface3.IGetNextFaceArray">IMidSurface3::IGetNextFaceArray</see> four times. At each call, the data is arranged as follows if there is one front face in the array: [Neutral face], [front face], NULL, [back face] If there are more than one front face in the array, then the data is arranged as follows: [Neutral face], [front face1, front face2], NULL, [back face1, back face2] To get the next face from the original paired faces, call IMidSurface3::IGetNextFaceArray.

Member.Remarks: Each reference surface in the midsurface feature is considered to be a sheet body. Member.Description: Creates a display dimension at the specified location for selected entities.

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: Dimension text location in meters

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: Dimension text location in meters

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: Dimension text location in meters

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">dimension</see>
Member.Remarks: Before calling this method, you must select the entities for which to add a display dimension. If extension lines are needed during dimensioning because the selected entities do not unambiguously define what needs to be dimensioned, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.AddDimension">IModelDocExtension::AddDimension</see> instead of this method. To dimension, make selections based on location and not name. For example, creating an angular dimension between two lines gets different results based on which line endpoints are selected. Therefore, if you are using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the entities for dimensioning, then you should specify the X, Y, and Z selection coordinates. You must also leave the object name argument empty, because if you pass the object name to IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2, then the selection routines use the object name instead of the coordinates to locate that item. NOTE: To change the angle in an angular dimension to its supplementary angle, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.SupplementaryAngle">IDisplayDimension::SupplementaryAngle</see>. Because coordinates are ignored when the object name is passed, the dimensioning routines are not able to use a specific selection location for the dimension. This causes unpredictable results during dimension creation. IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 randomly selects the line endpoint. You should only use this method on visible documents. Before using this method, check to see if the document is visible by using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.Visible">ISldWorks::Visible</see>. When you use this method, you might also want to use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.SetUserPreferenceToggle">ISldWorks::SetUserPreferenceToggle</see> with swInputDimValOnCreate to suppress the dialog box that lets the user type a dimension value.

Member.Name: AddFeatureMgrView3
Member.Signature: AddFeatureMgrView3( ref System.int Bitmap, ref System.int AppView, System.string ToolTip, System.int WhichPane )
Member.Description: Adds the specified tab to the FeatureManager design tree view.

Parameter.Name: Bitmap
Parameter.Description: Pointer to the bitmap that you want to use for the FeatureManager design tree tab; the bitmap should be no larger than 16x18; this standard pointer is created by performing a New on Cbitmap

Parameter.Name: AppView
Parameter.Description: Pointer to an existing view that you want to use as your FeatureManager design tree view. If you do not have an existing view, then use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelViewManager.CreateFeatureMgrView2">IModelViewMgr::CreateFeatureMgrView2</see>, which returns a view handle

Parameter.Name: ToolTip
Parameter.Description: ToolTip string

Parameter.Name: WhichPane
Parameter.Description: Pane in which to add the view as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFeatMgrPane_e">swFeatMgrPane_e</see>

Member.Returns: True if the FeatureManager design tree view tab is added successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method:
is valid only for x86 applications.
is not valid in the context of the Microsoft .NET Framework; it is only valid for old-style add-ins, which are now obsolete. Instead, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelViewManager.CreateFeatureMgrControl3">IModelViewManager::CreateFeatureMgrControl3</see>, which allows you to provide the ProgID or CLSID of an ActiveX control to use in the new tab for the FeatureManager design tree.
is identical to the earlier version, IModelDoc2::AddFeatureMgrView2, except that this method provides the ability to place the new tab on either the top or bottom pane. The pane may or may not be visible. However, the tab is added to the specified pane. Only the values swFeatMgrPaneTop and swFeatMgrPaneBottom from swFeatMgrPane_e should be used as inputs in the whichPane argument. Under certain conditions, for example while the Surface, Extend command is active in the user interface, SOLIDWORKS locks the bottom pane and does not allow the activation of any other tab. If your application needs the ability to activate your new tab at all times, consider adding it either to the top pane or to both panes. If you add it to the top pane only, it may not be apparent to the user until the top pane is made visible.
If you have an existing CView, this method adds that view as a new FeatureManager design tree view. This method also provides a parameter for adding a tab, which the user clicks to activate your view.
The FeatureManager design tree view added to this document is not persistent. In other words, the FeatureManager design tree view is not stored with this document and must be recreated upon reloading the document.
This method does not receive <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatMgrView.ActivateView">IFeatMgrView::ActivateNotify</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatMgrView.DeActivateView">IFeatMgrView::DeactivateNotify</see> events.
This view is generated by you and can be drawn into as you desire. However, because you generated this view, you are responsible for deleting it. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.DeleteFeatureMgrView">IModelDoc2::DeleteFeatureMgrView</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteFeatureMgrViewx64">IModelDocExtension::DeleteFeatureMgrViewx64</see> for details on how to delete your Feature Manager view.

Supported types of Object1 and Object2 include <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see>:
swSelFACES (face)
swSelEDGES (edge)
swSelVERTICES (vertex)
swSelSKETCHSEGS (sketch segment)
swSelDATUMPLANES (reference plane)

Model entity measurements are based on the model origin
Measured object cannot be a temporary geometric entity

+1 : Go from the start point to the end point in a counter-clockwise direction
-1 : Go from the start point to the end point in a clockwise direction

Member.Returns: Newly created arc (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method creates a partial arc in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. You can check for an active sketch using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>. For COM applications, the object pointer returned from this method can be used to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. The underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchArc">ISketchArc</see> object can be obtained using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchArc object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call ISketchSegment or ISketchArc functions. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> increase performance during entity creation by adding entities directly to the SOLIDWORKS database.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB also avoids some of the peculiarities involved with creating entities via the user interface, such as inferencing, automatic relations, and snapping to the grid. Adding entities directly to the database also increases the performance of this API. When you are done creating entities, it is important to call IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(false), to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.
This method also works with IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded. If you have called IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True), additional performance can be gained by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) to disable immediate display of entities as they are added to the database. When you are done creating all of your sketch entities, you must redraw your document window (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>) to see the entities that you added. You should also restore the original display settings by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(True).

Member.Remarks:
This method creates a partial arc in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. You can check for an active sketch using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>. For COM applications, the object pointer returned from this method can be used to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. The underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchArc">ISketchArc</see> object can be obtained using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchArc object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call ISketchSegment or ISketchArc functions. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> increase performance during entity creation by adding entities directly to the SOLIDWORKS database.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB also avoids some of the peculiarities involved with creating entities via the user interface, such as inferencing, automatic relations, and snapping to the grid. Adding entities directly to the database also increases the performance of this API. When you are done creating entities, it is important to call IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(false), to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.
This method also works with IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded. If you have called IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True), additional performance can be gained by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) to disable immediate display of entities as they are added to the database. When you are done creating all of your sketch entities, you must redraw your document window (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>) to see the entities that you added. You should also restore the original display settings by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(True). To create a circle using a center point and radius, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateCircleByRadius2">IModelDoc2::CreateCircleByRadius2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ICreateCircleByRadius2">IModelDoc2::ICreateCircleByRadius2</see>. To create a partial arc, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateArc2">IModelDoc2::CreateArc2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ICreateArc2">IModelDoc2::ICreateArc2</see>.

Member.Signature: CreateClippedSplines( System.object ParamsIn, System.double X1, System.double Y1, System.double X2, System.double Y2 )
Member.Description: Creates one or more sketch spline segments that are clipped against a given (x1, y1), (x2, y2) rectangle. This rectangle lies in the space of the active 2D sketch.

Parameter.Name: ParamsIn
Parameter.Description: See Remarks

Parameter.Name: X1
Parameter.Description: x component of the lower corner of the clipping rectangle

Parameter.Name: Y1
Parameter.Description: y component of the lower corner of the clipping rectangle

Parameter.Name: X2
Parameter.Description: x component of the upper corner of the clipping rectangle

Parameter.Name: Y2
Parameter.Description: y component of the upper corner of the clipping rectangle

Member.Returns: Array of newly created sketch segments
Member.Remarks:
The rectangle lies in the space of the active 2D sketch. The results are undefined for calls made in an active 3D sketch. The ParamsIn argument in Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) is a SafeArray of size (4 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles) as follows: [ Dimension, Order, NumControlPoints, Periodicity, knot1, knot2,..., ControlPoint1[Dimension], ControlPoint2[Dimension],... ] where: Dimension, Order, NumControlPoints, and Periodicity are integer values. The size of the knot array is determined by ( NumControlPoints + Order ). The size of the control point array is based upon the curve dimension:
If Dimension = 3, then ControlPoint is an array of 3 doubles ( x, y, z ).
If Dimension = 4, then ControlPoint is an array of 4 doubles ( x, y, z, w ) where w = weight.

Member.Returns: Newly created ellipse
Member.Remarks:
This method creates a partial arc in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. You can check for an active sketch using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>. For COM applications, the object pointer returned from this method can be used to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. The underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchArc">ISketchArc</see> object can be obtained using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchArc object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call ISketchSegment or ISketchArc functions. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> increase performance during entity creation by adding entities directly to the SOLIDWORKS database.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB also avoids some of the peculiarities involved with creating entities via the user interface, such as inferencing, automatic relations, and snapping to the grid. Adding entities directly to the database also increases the performance of this API. When you are done creating entities, it is important to call IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(false), to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.
This method also works with IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded. If you have called IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True), additional performance can be gained by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) to disable immediate display of entities as they are added to the database. When you are done creating all of your sketch entities, you must redraw your document window (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>) to see the entities that you added. You should also restore the original display settings by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(True). To create a partial ellipse, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateEllipticalArcByCenter">IModelDoc2::CreateEllipticalArcByCenter</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateEllipticalArcByCenterVB">IModelDoc2::CreateEllipticalArcByCenterVB</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ICreateEllipticalArcByCenter">IModelDoc2::ICreateEllipticalArcByCenter</see>.

This method uses the current document setting for displaying the reference plane. If display of reference planes is disabled, then you do not see the reference plane on the screen. This method does not select the reference plane after it is created. Objects that are selected before running this method are still selected when the method completes, not the newly created reference plane.
This method returns an IRefPlane object. This object can then be used for subsequent operations on the reference plane feature. Having a IRefPlane object may not be useful, except that it is a feature, which is an entity, so methods available on those objects are available. For an OLE user, those functions are directly accessible; for a COM user, those functions are available via QueryInterface. For example, to select the reference plane, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.Select4">IEntity::Select4</see>.

Member.Remarks:
The resulting plane is not parametric. The planes normal vector is calculated using the cross product of the vectors (P2 - P1) and (P3 - P1), respectively. The x-axis of the planes' coordinate system are a vector from P1 to P2 or a vector projected from the x-axis of the global coordinate system onto the plane. The useGlobal argument denotes whether to align the x-axis of the plane with global orientation.
If useGlobal...
Then x-axis of the...
True
global (model) coordinate system is projected onto the plane. That vector is used to determine the direction of the plane's x-axis. This does not reorient the plane. Instead, it rotates the plane coordinate system about P1 until the x-axis of the plane aligns with the projected vector. P1, P2, and P3 are still required because they define the plane.
false
plane is aligned based on your input points, P1 and P2. This method creates the plane in the model that is currently being edited. This behavior is consistent with the other plane creation methods, but it is different from the original IModelDoc2::CreatePlaneFixed, which created the plane in this model, regardless of whether a component was currently being edited.

Member.Name: CreateSpline
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchManager.CreateSpline">ISketchManager::CreateSpline</see>.

Parameter.Name: PointData
Parameter.Description: Set of X,Y,Z point coordinates to use in creating the spline (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Newly created spline
Member.Remarks: This method creates a spline in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see> to check if the sketch active. The PointData array is a set of, at least, two X, Y, Z values. The X value for the start point of the spline is PointData[0], the Y value for the start point is PointData[1], and the Z value for the start point is PointData[2]. The X value for the next point is PointData[3], and so on. For the COM interface, the total number of points in the array must be passed in. For the OLE interface, the total number of points are determined automatically, by taking the UBound of the PointData VARIANT and dividing by 3, so be careful to dimension that array correctly. For COM applications, you can use the object pointer returned from this method to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. You can obtain the underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> object by using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchSpline object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call SketchSegment or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchEllipse">ISketchEllipse</see> APIs. This method does not work with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see>. It always adds the spline directly to the database (as if IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True) was in effect), and you must redraw your document window to see the entities that you added (as if IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) was in effect). In 2D sketches, SOLIDWORKS ignores the Z value in PointData.

Member.Name: CreateSplineByEqnParams
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchManager.CreateSplineByEqnParams">ISketchManager::CreateSplineByEqnParams</see>.

Parameter.Name: ParamsIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing an array of doubles to use in creating the spline

Member.Returns: Newly created spline
Member.Remarks: The parameters are provided as three arrays, which for OLE automation are packed into a single SafeArray, which is packed as follows: [ Dimension, Order, Number of control Points, Periodicity, knot1, knot2,...,ControlPoint1[Dimension], ControlPoint2[Dimension],... ] Pass the control point coordinates to this routine in sketch space. The Z value is interpreted as 0. In certain situations, you must transform your B-curve parameters to sketch space using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ModelToSketchTransform">ISketch::ModelToSketchTransform</see>. NOTE: The curve can be either periodic or non-periodic. If the generated spline is a closed spline, then it must be flagged as periodic. Additionally, splines generated in sketches must be G1 continuous. If the data passed to this method does not generate a G1 continuous spline, then it is rejected and a spline is not created. If your data is not G1 continuous, then you must split the spline into multiple G1 segments and call this method for each segment. For the OLE interface, you can use the returned object pointer directly to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> interface or its base class, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see>. This method does not work with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see>. It always adds the spline directly to the database (as if IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True) is in effect), and you must redraw your document window to see the entities that you added (as if IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) is in effect). To create 3D splines, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.InsertCurveFilePoint">IModelDoc2::InsertCurveFilePoint</see> and related functions.

Member.Name: FeatureByPositionReverse
Member.Description: Gets the nth from last feature in the document.

Parameter.Name: Num
Parameter.Description: Number of feature from the last feature in the FeatureManager design tree; 0 is the last feature in FeatureManager design tree

Member.Returns: Pointer to the nth from last <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see> in the document

Example.Name: Specify IGES Levels and Values, Then Import IGES File
Specify IGES Levels and Values, Then Import IGES File
Specify IGES Levels and Values, Then Import IGES File

Member.Remarks:
This method returns features in the current order for the model, and this order changes when the model is edited. Your application should not assume that:
features retain the same relative or absolute position throughout the model’s lifetime. For example, you should not assume that Sketch1 always appears before Sketch2. any feature has a specific name. Because features can be renamed, you cannot assume that the first reference plane feature is named Plane1. When traversing the FeatureManager design tree, your application should use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetSpecificFeature2">IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2</see> to identify specific features instead of relying solely on <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see>. This method returns features in the model definition order, which is not the same as the order displayed in the user interface. See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITreeControlItem">ITreeControlItem</see> for details. Because SOLIDWORKS does not guarantee the name or positioning of default features, your application should not make any assumptions in this area. If your application is trying to access geometric features (i.e., sketches, fillets, bosses, reference surfaces, etc.) using IModelDoc2::FeatureByPositionReverse, then it is safest to determine the number of default features at the top and bottom of the list for each particular document. This could be done once for each document by traversing the FeatureManager design tree using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.FirstFeature">IModelDoc2::FirstFeature</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetNextFeature">IFeature::GetNextFeature</see>. Based on the feature type, IFeature::GetTypeName, you can recognize where new features will be placed in the FeatureManager design tree upon creation. For example, a new fillet is created at position (n-1) where n is the total number of features in the part. Therefore, to obtain this feature, then specify 1 for PositionFromEnd. This allows you to obtain the newly created fillet feature which is 1 from the bottom of the list. If you are using this method to obtain the last feature object created by your application, then, as a precaution, you might also want to check the feature count immediately before your feature creation and immediately after your feature creation. If the feature count has increased by 1, then it is relatively safe to assume that only your application has modified the document and added a feature. However, this is not a guaranteed methodology because another third-party applications might be running and might have also modified your document. Feature count can be determined by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetFeatureCount">IModelDoc2::GetFeatureCount</see>. However, IModelDoc2::GetFeatureCount does not recognize Sheet-Metal and Flat-Pattern folders as features in the FeatureManager design tree. Sheet-Metal and Flat-Pattern folders were introduced in SOLIDWORKS 2013. To access the first feature in the FeatureManager design tree and sub-features, use IModelDoc2::FirstFeature and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::GetFirstSubFeature</see> methods, respectively. IModelDoc2::FeatureByPositionReverse can access suppressed features.

Member.Name: FirstFeature
Member.Description: Gets the first feature in the document.
Member.Returns: First <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see> in the document

Example.Name: Get All Sheet Metal Feature Data
Traverse Assembly and Hide All Sketches

Member.Remarks:
This method:
is identical to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.FirstFeature">IPartDoc::FirstFeature</see>, but is available on the IModelDoc2 interface to include access to assemblies and drawings. can access the first feature even if it is suppressed. returns features in the current order for the model, and this order changes when the model is edited. Your application should not assume that:
features retain the same relative or absolute position throughout the model’s lifetime. For example, you should not assume that Sketch1 always appears before Sketch2. any feature has a specific name. Because features can be renamed, you cannot assume that the first reference plane feature is named Plane1. When traversing the FeatureManager design tree, your application should use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetSpecificFeature2">IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2</see> to identify specific features instead of relying solely on <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see>. This method returns features in the model definition order, which is not the same as the order displayed in the user interface. See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITreeControlItem">ITreeControlItem</see> for details. To access the next feature in the FeatureManager design tree and subfeatures, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetNextFeature">IFeature::GetNextFeature</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetNextFeature">IFeature::IGetNextFeature</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::GetFirstSubFeature</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::IGetFirstSubFeature</see> methods, respectively.

Member.Name: ForceReleaseLocks
Member.Description: Releases the locks that a file system places on a file when it is opened and detaches that file from the file system.
Member.Returns: 1 if locks are released, 0 if not
Member.Remarks: This method only supports part and assembly documents; it does not support drawing documents. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.CloseAndReopen">ISldWorks::CloseAndReopen</see> for details about closing and reopening a drawing document without unloading its references from memory. You must call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ReloadOrReplace">IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace</see> after calling IModelDoc2::ForceReleaseLocks to re-attach the detached file to the file system. If you do not call IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace after calling IModelDoc2::ForceReleaseLocks, then you will experience problems with OLE objects (e.g., design tables). IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace re-attaches the detached file to the file system; however, any changes made to the detached file are not preserved unless you save the file to disk before calling IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace. CAUTION: This method is intended to be used by PDM systems. Using this method incorrectly could corrupt your data.

Member.Remarks: Calling this method on a drawing document returns a list of all the parts and assemblies used in the drawing. If you set Traverseflag to True, then each of the parts within the assembly file is also returned in this array of strings. Because a derived mirror part is generated from another part, the list of model dependencies returned by this method would include the original part used to generate the derived mirror part. Library features are completely unassociated. They do not require the library nor do they update when changes are made to the library feature. Therefore, this method does not return library features. If you use this method with an assembly that contains two documents, Part1 and SubAssem1, an example of what might be returned is: [ "Part1", "C:\temp\Part1.SLDPRT", "SubAssem1", "c:\temp\SubAssem1.SLDASM" ] If Traverseflag is set to True, then all the documents contained in SubAssem1.ASM are returned. Also, suppressed components are recognized and returned by this method as a dependent file. If AddReadOnlyInfo is set to True, then a string of True or false is added to the list of strings. If Part1 is read-only, then the resulting set of strings would be: [ "Part1", "C:\temp\Part1.SLDPRT", "True", "SubAssem1", "c:\temp\SubAssem1.SLDASM", "" ] NOTE: For assemblies containing suppressed or lightweight components, file references (return value from this method) point to the as-saved component reference because the actual component has not been loaded into memory. Because the suppressed and lightweight components have not actually been loaded, the current search criteria has not been applied to update the file references. Setting Searchflag to True vs. false, causes this method to apply the current search criteria rules to locate the particular reference and may result in a different return value. Likewise, unsuppressing or resolving these components causes the current search criteria to be applied and updates the assembly's component references in memory, if necessary. When calling this method with Seachflag set to True, you can explicitly set the search folders first. This is important because this method uses the current SOLIDWORKS directory as its second search criteria. Because the user may have interactively opened files from some random directory, you cannot be certain the current SOLIDWORKS directory is pointing to the desired location. You may want to consider setting the search folders to that of the document being used in this method.

Member.Name: GetGridSettings
Member.Description: Gets the current grid settings.
Member.Returns: Current grid settings (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return format is the following array of doubles: [ dispGrid, gridSpacing, snap, dotStyle, nMajor, nMinor, angleSnap, angleUnit, minorAuto ] where:
dispGrid - can be interpreted as a BOOLEAN: True if grid displayed, false otherwise
gridSpacing - snap distance
snap - can be interpreted as a BOOLEAN: True if snap to grid is on, false otherwise
dotStyle - can be interpreted as a BOOLEAN: True if dotted grids, false otherwise
nMajor - number of minors in major
nMinor - number of snaps in minor
angleSnap - can be interpreted as a BOOLEAN: True if snap to angle is on, false otherwise
angleUnit - value of angle to which to snap
minorAuto - an be interpreted as a BOOLEAN: True if the minor grids are set automatically, false otherwise

Member.Name: GetPopupMenuMode
Member.Description: Gets the current pop-up menu mode.
Member.Returns:
Current pop-up menu mode:
0 - Default shortcut mode. This presents end users with options to Select Other, manipulate the view, access the properties dialog of the selected item, and so on. 1 - End users are presented with a limited set of choices including Select Other and Clear Selection. This mode is typically seen when a SOLIDWORKS dialog is active and the end user is restricted to entity selection.
Member.Remarks: When end users click the right-mouse button when the pointer is on an entity in the graphics window, they are presented with one of two distinct menu sets. These menu sets have been defined as mode 0 and mode 1. Using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetPopupMenuMode">IModelDoc2::SetPopupMenuMode</see>, your application can simulate the same shortcut menu behavior as in the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface. If you have a dialog that requires end-user selection of entities, you can set the pop-up menu mode to 1 to simulate SOLIDWORKS behavior. Your application should always set the menu mode back to its previous value. You can determine the previous value by calling the IModelDoc2::GetPopupMenuMode before calling IModelDoc2::SetPopupMenuMode.
