Member.Name: GetRayIntersectionsPoints
Member.Description: Gets the intersection point information generated by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.RayIntersections">IModelDoc2::RayIntersections</see>.
Member.Returns: Array containing the hit points (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The array returned contains information about each hit of each ray on the given bodies, in the following format: For each intersection found:
(double) BodyIndex: index in BodiesIn array of the body that was hit
(double) RayIndex: index in VectorsIn array of rays
(double) IntersectionType: type of intersection found. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swRayPtsResults_e">swRayPtsResults_e</see> . Entry/Exit information (swRayPtsResultsENTER and swRayPtsResultsEXIT) are only returned when swRayPtsOptsENTRY_EXIT is specified in the options argument in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.RayIntersections">IModelDoc2::RayIntersections</see> call. If more than one intersection type is found, then the IntersectionType contains an OR'd set of values from the swRayPtsResults_e enumeration.
(double) x,y,z: coordinates of hit point
(double) nx,ny,nz: normal (optionally appears when swRayPtsOptsNORMALS is specified in the Options argument in the IModelDoc2::RayIntersections call).

Member.Name: GetRayIntersectionsTopology
Member.Description: Gets the topology intersections generated by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.RayIntersections">IModelDoc2::RayIntersections</see>.
Member.Returns: Array of containing the hit points (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: This method only returns information if the swRayPtsOptsTOPOLS option was specified in the Options argument of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.RayIntersections">IModelDoc2::RayIntersections</see>. The array returned contains information about each entity hit of each ray on the given bodies. The topology hit can be coordinated with the hit point using the BodyIndex return value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints</see>. You can determine the type of item hit (face, edge or vertex) by checking the IntersectionType return value in the IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints.

Many operations cause this flag to be set, and you can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetSaveFlag">IModelDoc2::SetSaveFlag</see> to set this flag. is set to true if the document was created in an older version of SOLIDWORKS. is set to true for assemblies only when a subassembly has been saved. Member.Name: GetTessellationQuality
Member.Description: Gets the shaded-display image quality number for the current document.
Member.Returns: 0 Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method returns a number (QualityNum) that corresponds to the degree of tessellation of curved surfaces for shaded rendering output. Tools > Options > Document Properties > Image Quality includes a field that sets the maximum chordal deviation. QualityNum and the maximum chordal deviation (in meters) are coupled and inversely proportional as follows: var = TessMin + QualityNum*((TessMax-TessMin)/100) Deviation = 0.025 * (BodyDiameter * 2) / var; where:
TessMin = 6 TessMax = 166 0 QualityNum (returned by this method) BodyDiameter is the diagonal distance across the bounds of the part box. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.GetPartBox">IPartDoc::GetPartBox</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.IGetPartBox">IPartDoc::IGetPartBox</see> for more information. You can also get the maximum chordal deviation using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swUserPreferenceDoubleValue_e">swUserPreferencesDouble_e</see>.swImageQualityShadedDeviation. To get the image quality number, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swUserPreferenceIntegerValue_e">swUserPreferenceInteger_e</see>.swImageQualityShaded. NOTE: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetTessellationQuality">Setting the degree of tessellation</see> to a higher value results in:
finer tessellation, increased file size, slower graphics performance, and increased memory usage.

Member.Name: GetUnits
Member.Description: Gets the current unit settings, fraction base, fraction value, and significant digits.
Member.Returns: Array of 5 shorts (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The format of the returned data is an array of shorts: [ LengthUnit, FractionBase, FractionValue, SignificantDigits, RoundToFraction ] where:
LengthUnit = current model units as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLengthUnit_e">swLengthUnit_e</see>.
FractionBase = decimal or fraction as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swFractionDisplay_e">swFractionDisplay_e</see>; fractional units are only valid if the model units are set to swINCHES or swFEETINCHES.
FractionValue = denominator value if using fractional units.
SignificantDigits = significant digits if using decimal units.
RoundToFraction = flag denoting whether or not to round to the fraction; for example, if 4 was the denominator value and the actual value was .27, it is rounded to .25 You can also use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.LengthUnit">IModelDoc2::LengthUnit</see>, which provides access to the LengthUnit parameter.

Member.Name: GetUpdateStamp
Member.Description: Gets the current update stamp for this document.
Member.Returns: Current update stamp value for this document
Member.Remarks: The update stamp is an integer form of a time stamp. The update stamp is incremented for model state changes (i.e., suppress or unsuppress, configuration changes, feature changes, etc.) and for geometric changes (i.e., anything that requires a rebuild). This time stamp is not incremented for operations such as color changes, feature or configuration name changes, etc.

Member.Name: IAddDimension2
Member.Signature: IAddDimension2( System.double X, System.double Y, System.double Z )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.AddDimension">IModelDocExtension::AddDimension</see>.

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: Dimension text location in meters

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: Dimension text location in meters

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension">dimension</see>
Member.Remarks: You should only use this method on the visible document. Before using this method, you can check to see if the document is visible by using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.Visible">ISldWorks::Visible</see>. Dimensions are created based on selection location. For example, creating an angular dimension between two lines gets different results based on which line endpoints are selected. Therefore, if you are using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the entities for dimensioning, then you should specify the XYZ selection coordinates. You must also leave the object name argument empty, because if you pass the object name to IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2, then the selection routines tries to locate that item without using the coordinates. Because coordinates are ignored when the object name is passed, the dimensioning routines are not able to use a specific selection location for the dimension. This causes unpredictable results in your dimension creation because you cannot be sure which line endpoint is selected by IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2. When you use this method, you might also want to use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.SetUserPreferenceToggle">ISldWorks::SetUserPreferenceToggle</see> swInputDimValOnCreate to suppress the dialog box that lets the user enter the dimension value.

Supported input object types include:

Member.Name: ICreateArc2
Member.Signature: ICreateArc2( System.double XC, System.double YC, System.double Zc, System.double Xp1, System.double Yp1, System.double Zp1, System.double Xp2, System.double Yp2, System.double Zp2, System.short Direction )
Member.Description: Creates an arc based on a center point, a start, an end point, and a direction.

Parameter.Name: XC
Parameter.Description: X value of the circle center point in meters

Parameter.Name: YC
Parameter.Description: Y value of the circle center point in meters

Parameter.Name: Zc
Parameter.Description: Z value of the circle center point in meters

Parameter.Name: Xp1
Parameter.Description: X value of the start point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Yp1
Parameter.Description: Y value of the start point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Zp1
Parameter.Description: Z value of the start point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Xp2
Parameter.Description: X value of the end point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Yp2
Parameter.Description: Y value of the end point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Zp2
Parameter.Description: Z value of the end point of the arc in meters

Parameter.Name: Direction
Parameter.Description:
+1 : Go from the start point to the end point in a counter-clockwise direction
-1 : Go from the start point to the end point in a clockwise direction

Member.Returns:
This method creates a partial arc in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. You can check for an active sketch using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>. For COM applications, the object pointer returned from this method can be used to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. The underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchArc">ISketchArc</see> object can be obtained using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchArc object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call ISketchSegment or ISketchArc functions. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> increase performance during entity creation by adding entities directly to the SOLIDWORKS database.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB also avoids some of the peculiarities involved with creating entities via the user interface, such as inferencing, automatic relations, and snapping to the grid. Adding entities directly to the database also increases the performance of this API. When you are done creating entities, it is important to call IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(false), to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.
This method also works with IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded. If you have called IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True), additional performance can be gained by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) to disable immediate display of entities as they are added to the database. When you are done creating all of your sketch entities, you must redraw your document window (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>) to see the entities that you added. You should also restore the original display settings by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(True).

Member.Remarks:
This method creates a partial arc in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. You can check for an active sketch using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>. For COM applications, the object pointer returned from this method can be used to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. The underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchArc">ISketchArc</see> object can be obtained using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchArc object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call ISketchSegment or ISketchArc functions. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> increase performance during entity creation by adding entities directly to the SOLIDWORKS database.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB also avoids some of the peculiarities involved with creating entities via the user interface, such as inferencing, automatic relations, and snapping to the grid. Adding entities directly to the database also increases the performance of this API. When you are done creating entities, it is important to call IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(false), to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.
This method also works with IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded. If you have called IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True), additional performance can be gained by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) to disable immediate display of entities as they are added to the database. When you are done creating all of your sketch entities, you must redraw your document window (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see>) to see the entities that you added. You should also restore the original display settings by calling IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(True). To create a circle using a center point and a point on the circle, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateCircle2">IModelDoc2::CreateCircle2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ICreateCircle2">IModelDoc2::ICreateCircle2</see>. To create a partial arc, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.CreateArc2">IModelDoc2::CreateArc2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ICreateArc2">IModelDoc2::ICreateArc2</see>.

Member.Description: Creates one or more sketch spline segments that are clipped against a given (x1, y1), (x2, y2) rectangle. This rectangle lies in the space of the active 2D sketch.

Parameter.Name: PropArray
Parameter.Description: See Remarks

Parameter.Name: KnotsArray
Parameter.Description: See Remarks

Parameter.Name: CntrlPntCoordArray
Parameter.Description: See Remarks

Parameter.Name: X1
Parameter.Description: x component of the lower corner of the clipping rectangle

Parameter.Name: Y1
Parameter.Description: y component of the lower corner of the clipping rectangle

Parameter.Name: X2
Parameter.Description: x component of the upper corner of the clipping rectang

Parameter.Name: Y2
Parameter.Description: y component of the upper corner of the clipping rectang

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEnumSketchSegments">sketch segments enumeration</see>
Member.Remarks:
The rectangle lies in the space of the active 2D sketch. The results are undefined for calls made in an active 3D sketch.
The arrays are as follows:
PropArray = [ Dimension, Order, NumControlPoints, Periodicity ]
KnotsArray = [ NumControlPoints + Order ]
CntrlPntCoordArray = [ NumControlPoints * Dimension ] If Dimension = 3, then CntrlPntCoordArray is an array of 3 doubles ( x, y, z ). If Dimension = 4, then CntrlPntCoordArray is an array of 4 doubles ( x, y, z, w ) where w = weight.

Member.Remarks:
This method uses the current document setting for displaying the reference plane. If display of reference planes is disabled, then you do not see the reference plane on the screen. If display of reference planes is enabled, then you see it. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceToggle">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceToggle</see> swDisplayPlanes and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SetUserPreferenceToggle">IModelDocExtenison::SetUserPreferenceToggle</see> swDisplayPlanes get or set this display preference.
This method does not select the reference plane after it is created. Objects that are selected before running this method are still selected when the method completes, not the newly created reference plane.
This method returns an IRefPlane object. This object can then be used for subsequent operations on the reference plane feature. Having a IRefPlane object may not be useful, except that it is a feature, which is an entity, so methods available on those objects are available. For an OLE user, those functions are directly accessible; for a COM user, those functions are available via QueryInterface. For example, to select the reference plane, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.Select4">IEntity::Select4</see>.

Member.Remarks:
The resulting plane is not parametric. The planes normal vector is calculated using the cross product of the vectors (P2 - P1) and (P3 - P1), respectively. The x-axis of the planes' coordinate system are a vector from P1 to P2 or a vector projected from the x-axis of the global coordinate system onto the plane. The useGlobal argument denotes whether to align the x-axis of the plane with global orientation.
If useGlobal...
Then x-axis of the...
True
global (model) coordinate system is projected onto the plane. That vector is used to determine the direction of the plane's x-axis. This does not reorient the plane. Instead, it rotates the plane coordinate system about P1 until the x-axis of the plane aligns with the projected vector. P1, P2, and P3 are still required because they define the plane.
false
plane is aligned based on your input points, P1 and P2. This method creates the plane in the model that is currently being edited. This behavior is consistent with the other plane creation APIs, but it is different from the original IModelDoc2::ICreatePlaneFixed, which created the plane in this model, regardless of whether a component was currently being edited.

For example, to select the reference plane, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.Select4">IEntity::Select4</see>.

Member.Name: ICreateSpline
Member.Signature: ICreateSpline( System.int PointCount, ref System.double PointData )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchManager.ICreateSpline">ISketchManager::ICreateSpline</see>.

Parameter.Name: PointCount
Parameter.Description: Number of points in the pointData array

Parameter.Name: PointData
Parameter.Description: Set of X,Y,Z point coordinates to use in creating the spline (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">spline</see>
Member.Remarks: This method creates a spline in the active 2D sketch. If a sketch is not active, then a new sketch is created. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see> to check if the sketch active. The PointData array is a set of, at least, two X, Y, Z values. The X value for the start point of the spline is PointData[0], the Y value for the start point is PointData[1], and the Z value for the start point is PointData[2]. The X value for the next point is PointData[3], and so on. For the COM interface, the total number of points in the array must be passed in. For the OLE interface, the total number of points are determined automatically, by taking the UBound of the PointData VARIANT and dividing by 3, so be careful to dimension that array correctly. For COM applications, you can use the object pointer returned from this method to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface. You can obtain the underlying <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> object by using QueryInterface on the returned ISketchSegment object. OLE applications can define a new ISketchSegment or ISketchSpline object using the returned Dispatch pointer. Visual Basic applications interpret the pointer for you automatically, so you can use the returned object to call SketchSegment or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchEllipse">ISketchEllipse</see> APIs. This method does not work with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see>. It always adds the spline directly to the database (as if IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True) was in effect), and you must redraw your document window to see the entities that you added (as if IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) was in effect). In 2D sketches, SOLIDWORKS ignores the Z value in PointData.

Member.Name: ICreateSplineByEqnParams
Member.Signature: ICreateSplineByEqnParams( ref System.int PropArray, ref System.double KnotsArray, ref System.double CntrlPntCoordArray )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchManager.ICreateSplineByEqnParams">ISketchManager::ICreateSplineByEqnParams</see>.

Parameter.Name: PropArray
Parameter.Description: Includes dimension, order, number of control points, periodicity

Parameter.Name: KnotsArray
Parameter.Description: knot1, knot2, and so on

Parameter.Name: CntrlPntCoordArray
Parameter.Description: ontrolpoint1[dimension], controlpoint2[dimension], and so on

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">spline</see>
Member.Remarks:
The PropArray array contains four integers (placed in the first four doubles in a Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) SafeArray):
Dimension
Order
Number of Control Points
Periodicity ( True or false ) The KnotsArray contains doubles with (Number of Control Points + Order) elements. The size of the CntrlPntCoordArray array is based upon the curve dimension.
Dimension = 2 then each Control Point is an array of 2 doubles ( x, y )
Dimension = 3 then each Control Point is an array of 3 doubles ( x, y, z)
Dimension = 4 then each Control Point is an array of 4 doubles ( x, y, z, w ) where w = weight Pass the control point coordinates to this routine in sketch space. The Z value is interpreted as 0. In certain situations, you must transform your B-curve parameters to sketch space using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ModelToSketchTransform">ISketch::ModelToSketchTransform</see>. NOTE: If the generated spline is a closed spline, then it must be flagged as periodic. Additionally, splines generated in sketches must be G1 continuous. If the data passed to this method does not generate a G1 continuous spline, then it is rejected and a spline is not created. If your data is not G1 continuous, then you must split the spline into multiple G1 segments and call this method for each segment. You can use the returned object pointer directly to call any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> interface, or use QueryInterface to obtain the pointer to the ISketchSpline and any APIs on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> interface. This method does not work with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see>. It always adds the spline directly to the database (as if IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB(True) is in effect), and you must redraw your document window to see the entities that you added (as if IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded(false) is in effect). To create 3D splines, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.InsertCurveFilePoint">IModelDoc2::InsertCurveFilePoint</see> and related functions.

Member.Name: IFeatureByPositionReverse
Member.Description: Gets the nth from last feature in the document.

Parameter.Name: Num
Parameter.Description: Number of feature from the last feature in the FeatureManager design tree; 0 is the last feature in FeatureManager design tree

Member.Returns: Pointer to the nth from last <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see> in the document
Member.Remarks:
This method returns features in the current order for the model, and this order changes when the model is edited. Your application should not assume that:
features retain the same relative or absolute position throughout the model’s lifetime. For example, you should not assume that Sketch1 always appears before Sketch2. any feature has a specific name. Because features can be renamed, you cannot assume that the first reference plane feature is named Plane1. When traversing the FeatureManager design tree, your application should use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetSpecificFeature2">IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2</see> to identify specific features instead of relying solely on <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see>. This method returns features in the model definition order, which is not the same as the order displayed in the user interface. See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITreeControlItem">ITreeControlItem</see> for details. Because SOLIDWORKS does not guarantee the name or positioning of default features, your application should not make any assumptions in this area. If your application is trying to access geometric features (i.e., sketches, fillets, bosses, reference surfaces, etc.) using IModelDoc2::IFeatureByPositionReverse, then it is safest to determine the number of default features at the top and bottom of the list for each particular document. This could be done once for each document by traversing the FeatureManager design tree using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.FirstFeature">IModelDoc2::IFirstFeature</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IFirstFeature">IModelDoc2::IFirstFeature</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetNextFeature">IFeature::IGetNextFeature</see>. Based on the feature type, IFeature::GetTypeName, you can recognize where new features will be placed in the FeatureManager design tree upon creation. For example, a new fillet is created at position (n-1) where n is the total number of features in the part. Therefore, to obtain this feature, then specify 1 for PositionFromEnd. This allows you to obtain the newly created fillet feature which is 1 from the bottom of the list. If you are using this method to obtain the last feature object created by your application, then, as a precaution, you might also want to check the feature count immediately before your feature creation and immediately after your feature creation. If the feature count has increased by 1, then it is relatively safe to assume that only your application has modified the document and added a feature. However, this is not a guaranteed methodology because another third-party applications might be running and might have also modified your document. Feature count can be determined by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetFeatureCount">IModelDoc2::GetFeatureCount</see>. However, IModelDoc2::GetFeatureCount does not recognize Sheet-Metal and Flat-Pattern folders as features in the FeatureManager design tree. Sheet-Metal and Flat-Pattern folders were introduced in SOLIDWORKS 2013. To access the first feature in the FeatureManager design tree and sub-features, use IModelDoc2::IFirstFeature and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::IGetFirstSubFeature</see> methods, respectively. IModelDoc2::IFeatureByPositionReverse can access suppressed features.

Member.Name: IFirstFeature
Member.Description: Gets the first feature in the document.
Member.Returns: First <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see> in the document

Example.Name: Get Names of Creators of Features

Member.Remarks:
This method:
is identical to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.FirstFeature">IPartDoc::FirstFeature</see>, but is available on the IModelDoc2 interface to include access to assemblies and drawings. can access the first feature, even if it is suppressed. returns features in the current order for the model, and this order changes when the model is edited. Your application should not assume that:
features retain the same relative or absolute position throughout the model’s lifetime. For example, you should not assume that Sketch1 always appears before Sketch2. any feature has a specific name. Because features can be renamed, you cannot assume that the first reference plane feature is named Plane1. When traversing the FeatureManager design tree, your application should use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName2">IFeature::GetTypeName2</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetSpecificFeature2">IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2</see> to identify specific features instead of relying solely on <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see>. This method returns features in the model definition order, which is not the same as the order displayed in the user interface. See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITreeControlItem">ITreeControlItem</see> for details. To access the next feature in the FeatureManager design tree and subfeatures, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetNextFeature">IFeature::GetNextFeature</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetNextFeature">IFeature::IGetNextFeature</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::GetFirstSubFeature</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IGetFirstSubFeature">IFeature::IGetFirstSubFeature</see> methods, respectively.

Member.Name: IGet3rdPartyStorage
Member.Description: Gets the IStream interface to the specified third-party stream inside this SOLIDWORKS Design document.

Parameter.Name: StringIn
Parameter.Description: Name of the stream; the name should be less than 30 characters and must be unique and qualified among all parties choosing to store within the current session

Parameter.Name: IsStoring
Parameter.Description: True if you are storing data, false if you are reading data

Member.Returns: IUnknown (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Call this interface when a SaveToStorageNotify or LoadFromStorageNotify notification is received. Do not call this method to save or load from storage in reaction to the FileSaveNotify or FileOpenNotify2 events. During a file-open operation, your application receives a LoadFromStorageNotify event if you have registered for document notifications. When you receive this event, it is safe to open your Stream for reading using IModelDoc2::IGet3rdPartyStorage. When a file is fully loaded, you can call this method for reading your data at any time. This provides you with access to read your storage node whenever needed. However, it is not a good idea to attempt this while in the middle of a FileSaveNotify or FileOpenNotify2 as unforeseen conflicts can occur. If your application is loaded in the middle of a SOLIDWORKS Design session, then you can traverse all open documents using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.EnumDocuments2">ISldworks::EnumDocuments2</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.IGetFirstDocument2">ISldWorks::IGetFirstDocument2</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetNext">IModelDoc2::IGetNext</see> and read the storage from all existing open documents. From that point on, your application can use the LoadFromStorageNotify event to recognize when new documents have been opened and need reading. For storage writing, IModelDoc2::IGet3rdPartyStorage interface is locked unless the SaveToStorageNotify event has been sent. Therefore, you can only write to your storage when the file is actually being saved and your application has received the SaveToStorageNotify event. Your call to IModelDoc2::IGet3rdPartyStorage must be followed by a call to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IRelease3rdPartyStorage">IModelDoc2::IRelease3rdPartyStorage</see>. This must be done even when you fail to obtain a Stream and the return value from IModelDoc2::IGet3rdPartyStorage is NULL. If you fail to call IModelDoc2::IRelease3rdPartyStorage, the third-party node may remain locked and prevent future access. You are not required to call IModelDoc2::IRelease3rdPartyStorage, under any circumstance, if you called IModelDoc2::IGet3rdPartyStorage in reaction to one of the SaveToStorageNotify or LoadFromStorageNotify events. However, calling IModelDoc2::IRelease3rdPartyStorage excessively does not cause problems. As work progresses during an active session and you have information that needs to be stored, you may want to flag the document as dirty using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetSaveFlag">IModelDoc2::SetSaveFlag</see>. This causes a Save Changes? prompt to display if the user tries to close the file without saving. If the user clicks Yes to this prompt, then your application receives the SaveToStorageNotify event. NOTE: The name given to the storage stream should be registered so that no conflicts occur. Once registered, the stream name is reserved exclusively for your application. Passing the unique ID string and a flag to determine if data is being stored or loaded returns an IUnknown pointer. You must then use QueryInterface() to get the IStream interface. The stream is used for serialization and then released in the third-party code.
SwRootStorage --| | |-- ThirdPty --| | |-- |-- |-- : : : |--
The IStream object used by the third party is written to IStream objects under an IStorage object called ThirdPty in the SOLIDWORKS compound document. Each third party writes to a single IStream object whose name is assigned by SOLIDWORKS. NOTE: If you are using serialization, then be careful with the standard MFC macros; otherwise, you may get messages like Unexpected File Format after your application is unloaded. One way of using IMPLEMENT_SERIAL is: IMPLEMENT_SERIAL( CCustomAttr, CObject, VERSIONABLE_SCHEMA|0 )

Member.Name: IGetRayIntersectionsPoints
Member.Description: Gets the intersection point information generated by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IRayIntersections">IModelDoc2::IRayIntersections</see>.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array containing the hit points (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The array returned contains information about each hit of each ray on the given bodies, in the following format: For each intersection found:
(double) BodyIndex: index in BodiesIn array of the body that was hit
(double) RayIndex: index in VectorsIn array of rays
(double) IntersectionType: type of intersection found. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swRayPtsResults_e">swRayPtsResults_e</see> . Entry/Exit information (swRayPtsResultsENTER and swRayPtsResultsEXIT) are only returned when swRayPtsOptsENTRY_EXIT is specified in the options argument in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IRayIntersections">IModelDoc2::IRayIntersections</see> call. If more than one intersection type is found, then the IntersectionType contains an OR'd set of values from the swRayPtsResults_e enumeration.
(double) x,y,z: coordinates of hit point
(double) nx,ny,nz: normal (optionally appears when swRayPtsOptsNORMALS is specified in the Options argument in the IModelDoc2::RayIntersections call).

Member.Name: IGetRayIntersectionsTopology
Member.Description: Gets the topology intersections generated by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IRayIntersections">IModelDoc2::IRayIntersections</see>.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array containing the hit entities (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks: This method only returns information if the swRayPtsOptsTOPOLS option was specified in the Options argument of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.RayIntersections">IModelDoc2::RayIntersections</see>. The array returned contains information about each entity hit of each ray on the given bodies. The topology hit can be coordinated with the hit point using the BodyIndex return value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsPoints</see>. You can determine the type of item hit (face, edge or vertex) by checking the IntersectionType return value in the IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsPoints.

Member.Name: IInsertGtol
Member.Description: Creates a new geometric tolerance symbol (GTol) in this document.
Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">GTol</see>
Member.Remarks: The leader attachment points for the newly created GTol object come from the selections made before calling this method. The initial location of the symbol is near the selection location. If there are no selections, then the GTol does not have a leader, is free standing, and is initially at the origin of the model or drawing. This method creates an empty symbol. To fill in the text and symbols of this GTol, use the pointer returned by this method to access the various get and set methods of the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">IGTol</see> interface, such as <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetFrameSymbols2">IGtol::SetFrameSymbols2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.SetFrameValues">IGtol::SetFrameValues</see>. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IGtol.GetAnnotation">IGtol::GetAnnotation</see> to retrieve the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation">IAnnotation</see> object.

Member.Name: IInsertMidSurfaceExt
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertMidSurface">IFeatureManager::IInsertMidSurface</see>.

Parameter.Name: Placement
Parameter.Description: Value from -1 to 1 that indicates the desired location of the midsurface relative to the face pair; a value of 0.0 places the midsurface equally between the face pair

Parameter.Name: KnitFlag
Parameter.Description: True to sew all the reference surfaces (neutral sheets) into a single sheet (surface) body, false for the midsurface feature to contain individual reference surface geometry

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface2">Mid-surface feature</see>
Member.Remarks: A midsurface feature is calculated from the solid body in your part document. This method first finds all parallel pairs of faces from the part solid. For each pair of parallel faces found, it creates a neutral reference surface between the two faces. The placement position of the reference surface is controlled by the placement parameter. This process repeats itself until all parallel body faces are processed. At the end of this process, all the reference surfaces are sewn into a single reference surface if knitFlag is set to True. The hierarchy of a midsurface feature is: A midsurface feature contains one or more reference surfaces. If sewn successfully using the knitFlag = True option, then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface. Each reference surface is considered a sheet body. The sheet body has the normal topology that you would expect to find on a body object (for example, faces, edges, and so on). See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface2">IMidSurface2</see> object for methods that provide access to this topology.

Member.Name: ILightSourcePropertyValues
Member.Description: Gets and sets the light source property values.

Parameter.Name: ID
Parameter.Description: Light source ID

Member.Returns:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of 19 doubles containing the light source properties (see Remarks)
VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported
Member.Remarks:
The light source ID ranges from 0 to n, where n = (the total number of light sources - 1). To get the total number of light sources, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetLightSourceCount">IModelDoc2::GetLightSourceCount</see>. The return values for this property is the following array of 19 doubles: [ type, Intensity, Color[3], Position[3], Direction[3], coneAngle, falloff[3], Ambient, Specular, isDisabled, SpotExponent ]
where:
type = an integer packed into a double that represents the light source type where valid types are taken from openGL definitions (LIGHT_EYE, LIGHT_AMBIENT, LIGHT_SPOT, LIGHT_POINT, LIGHT_DISTANT)
Intensity = Light-source intensity (diffuseness) where values range from 0 to 1.
Color[3] = Light-source color in the form of an array of 3 doubles (R, G, B) where values range from 0 to 1.
Position[3] = Light-source position for spot lights in the form of an array of 3 doubles (X, Y, Z) in model space.
Direction[3] = Light-source direction in the form of an array of 3 doubles (i, j, k)
coneAngle = Light-source cone half angle in degrees where valid values are from 0 to 90 and 180.
falloff[3] = Light-source falloff in the form of an array of 3 doubles (Kc, Kl, Kq). These values result in changes in light intensity as the distance between the light position and the vertex change. NOTE: The falloff[3] values are not supported in SOLIDWORKS 2011 and later.The result is driven by the following equation: [ 1 / (Kc + D*Kl + D*D*Kq ) ] where: D = the distance.between the light's position and the vertex Kc = constant attenuation Kl = linear attenuation Kq = quadratic attenuation
Ambient = light-source ambient Intensity
Specular = light-source specular Intensity
isDisabled = an integer packed into a double. True means that the light is disabled and false means the light is not disabled.
SpotExponent = spot exponentNOTE: The SpotExponent value is not supported in SOLIDWORKS 2011 and later.

Member.Name: IMultiSelectByRay
Member.Signature: IMultiSelectByRay( ref System.double PointIn, ref System.double VectorIn, System.double RadiusIn, System.int TypeWanted, System.bool Append )
Member.Description: Selects multiple objects of the specified type that are intersected by a ray from point (x,y,z in meters) in direction vector (x,y,z) within a distance radius.

Parameter.Name: PointIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing 3 doubles that define the start point of the ray

Parameter.Name: VectorIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing 3 doubles that define the direction of the ray

Parameter.Name: RadiusIn
Parameter.Description: Radius of the ray in meters

Parameter.Name: TypeWanted
Parameter.Description: Type of objects to select as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: Append
Parameter.Description: True to append the selections to the current selection list, false to not

Member.Returns: True if an object is selected, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method:
Defines a cylindrical region of infinite length that begins at PointIn, runs parallel to VectorIn, and has a radius of RadiusIn. If you specified edges or vertices, then any edge or vertex found within the selection cylinder is selected.
Selects only entity objects, which include faces, edges, and vertices. You cannot use this function to select sketches. When selecting face entities, RadiusIn is ignored and a cylinder of infinitely small radius is used.

Member.Name: IRayIntersections
Member.Signature: IRayIntersections( ref Body2 BodiesIn, System.int NumBodies, ref System.double BasePointsIn, ref System.double VectorsIn, System.int NumRays, System.int Options, System.double HitRadius, System.double Offset )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.RayIntersections">IModelDocExtension::RayIntersections</see>.

Parameter.Name: BodiesIn
Parameter.Description: Array <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> that are hit by the rays (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: NumBodies
Parameter.Description: Number of bodies in the BodiesIn array

Parameter.Name: BasePointsIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing the x,y,z base points of each ray

Parameter.Name: VectorsIn
Parameter.Description: Array containing the direction vectors of each ray

Parameter.Name: NumRays
Parameter.Description: Number of rays specified; this should be equal to the number of elements in the (basePointsIn / 3) or (vectorsIn / 3) arrays

Parameter.Name: Options
Parameter.Description: Number of options as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swRayPtsOpts_e">swRayPtsOpts_e</see>

Parameter.Name: HitRadius
Parameter.Description: Radius of hit cylinder used mainly in grazing cases to establish a hit

Parameter.Name: Offset
Parameter.Description: Length tolerance to use to establish whether a hit on a face represents the entry or exit of the ray from the body (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Number of intersections found
Member.Remarks:
The method performs the intersection operations between the specified bodies and the ray vectors. To get the results (a set of intersection points, intersection normals, and the bodies that were hit from your bodiesIn array) of the intersection operations, you must call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetRayIntersectionsTopology">IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionTopology</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsTopology">IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsTopology</see>. Information returned by IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints, IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints, IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionTopology, and IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsTopology depends partially on the value of the options argument. Valid values can be concatenated together using bitwise operations. See IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints or IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints to see which data is always output regardless of the values specified in the options argument. For the COM interface, the return value, the intersection count, must be used in determining the size of arrays to allocate for return values from IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsPoints and IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsTopology.
For each ray that hits an edge or a vertex, the offset distance is added in both the positive and negative directions along the ray and the points computed are tested for spatial inclusion in the hit body. This determines if the ray was entering, leaving, or just grazing the body at the hit point. Entry and exit onto faces can be computed does not require such an offset.

Member.Name: ISketchSplineByEqnParams
Member.Signature: ISketchSplineByEqnParams( ref System.int PropArray, ref System.double KnotsArray, ref System.double CntrlPntCoordArray )
Member.Description: Creates a spline on the active 2D sketch using the specified b-curve parameters.

Parameter.Name: PropArray
Parameter.Description: Includes dimension, order, number of control points, and periodicity

Parameter.Name: KnotsArray
Parameter.Description: knot1, knot2, and so on

Parameter.Name: CntrlPntCoordArray
Parameter.Description: controlpoint1[dimension], controlpoint2[dimension], and so on

Member.Returns: True if created successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The PropArray argument contains 4 integers packed into the first two doubles in the array:
Dimension
Order
Number of Control Points
Periodicity ( True or false ) The KnotsArray argument is an array of doubles with (Number of Control Points + Order) elements. The size of the CntrlPntCoordArray array is based upon the curve dimension:
Dimension = 2 then each control point is an array of 2 doubles ( x, y )
Dimension = 3 then each control point is an array of 3 doubles ( x, y, z)
Dimension = 4 then each control point is an array of 4 doubles ( x, y, z, w ) where w = weight The parameters are provided as 3 arrays, which for COM applications are passed separately. Pass control point coordinates to this method in sketch space. The Z value is interpreted as 0. In certain situations, you must transform your b-curve parameters to sketch space with the help of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ModelToSketchTransform">ISketch::ModelToSketchTransform</see>. NOTE: If the spline being generated is a closed spline, then it must be flagged as periodic. In addition, splines generated in sketches must be G1 continuous. If the data passed to this method does not generate a G1 continuous spline, then it is rejected and a spline is not created.

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.InsertLoftRefSurface2">IModelDoc2::InsertLoftRefSurface2</see>.

Member.Name: InsertLoftRefSurface2
Member.Signature: InsertLoftRefSurface2( System.bool Closed, System.bool KeepTangency, System.bool ForceNonRational, System.double TessToleranceFactor, System.short StartMatchingType, System.short EndMatchingType )
Member.Description: Creates a loft surface from the selected profiles, centerline, and guide curves.

Parameter.Name: Closed
Parameter.Description: True for closed loft, false for open loft; if True, then you must have at least three profiles selected, and if you are using guide curves, the guide curves must be closed

Parameter.Name: KeepTangency
Parameter.Description: If the section curves are tangent, then you have the option to specify whether the resulting surfaces are also be tangent; specify True to maintain the tangency as seen in the section curves, false otherwise; when generating tangent surfaces, SOLIDWORKS maintains planar and cylindrical surface shapes if the section curves exhibit these characteristics

Parameter.Name: ForceNonRational
Parameter.Description: True to force the resulting surface to be non-rational, false to not

Parameter.Name: TessToleranceFactor
Parameter.Description: Factor to control the number of intermediate sections used for loft with centerline; default value is 1.0; the greater the variable, the more intermediate sections created

Parameter.Name: StartMatchingType
Parameter.Description: Tangency type at the start profile (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: EndMatchingType
Parameter.Description: Tangency type at the end profile (see Remarks)

Member.Remarks:
Selection of guide curves and centerline is optional; however, selection of the profiles must be in an order consistent with the desired direction of the loft. Because you are creating a surface, the section profiles can be open. Use of guide curves is strongly recommended, especially when selection of profiles is done in the FeatureManager design tree. You can use any number of profiles; however, if you have selected only one profile, then any selected guide curves must be closed curves. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the profiles and guide curves. The mark for:
profile selections should be 1
any guide curve selection, if provided, should be 2
centerline selection, if provided, should be 4
start tangency vector selection, if provided, should be an 8
start tangency faces selection, if provided, should be a 16 (not available currently
end tangency vector selection, if provided, should be a 32
end tangency faces selection, if provided, should be a 64 (not available currently) Linear edge, sketch line, axis, plane and planar faces are qualified for tangency vector sections. The tangency types can be one of the following:
0 =
none
1 =
tangent to the normal of the profile
2 =
tangent to a selected vector
3 =
tangency to all the adjacent faces sharing an edge with the start profile
4 =
tangent to some of the selected faces sharing an edge with the start profile (not available at this moment).

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertMidSurface">IFeatureManager::InsertMidSurface</see>.

Parameter.Name: Placement
Parameter.Description: Value from -1 to 1 that indicates the desired location of the midsurface relative to the face pair; a value of 0.0 places the midsurface equally between the face pair

Parameter.Name: KnitFlag
Parameter.Description: True to sew all the reference surfaces (neutral sheets) into a single sheet(surface) body, false for the midsurface feature to contain individual reference surface geometry

Member.Returns: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface2">Mid-surface feature</see>
Member.Remarks: A midsurface feature is calculated from the solid body in your part document. This method first finds all parallel pairs of faces from the part solid. For each pair of parallel faces found, it creates a neutral reference surface between the two faces. The placement position of the reference surface is controlled by the placement parameter. This process repeats itself until all parallel body faces are processed. At the end of this process, all the reference surfaces are sewn into a single reference surface if knitFlag is set to True. The hierarchy of a midsurface feature is: A midsurface feature contains one or more reference surfaces. If sewn successfully using the knitFlag = True option, then the midsurface feature contains only one reference surface. Each reference surface is considered a sheet body. The sheet body has the normal topology that you would expect to find on a body object (for example, faces, edges, and so on). See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMidSurface2">IMidSurface2</see> object for methods that provide access to this topology.

Example.Name: Create Block Definition and Insert Block Instance
Create Block Definition and Insert Block Instance
Create Block Definition and Insert Block Instance

Member.Remarks:
If you use a symbol in Text, it must be formatted as: LibraryName-SymbolName> where LibraryName and SymbolName are in the SOLIDWORKS text file C:\ProgramData\SolidWorks\SolidWorks 20nn\lang\english\gtol.sym. NOTE: You must include the right- and left-angle brackets and separate LibraryName and SymbolName with a hyphen; for example, . The leader attachment points for the new note come from the selections made before calling this method. The initial location of the note will be near the selection location. If there are no selections, the note:
Does not have a leader
Is free standing
Is at the origin of the model or drawing This method creates a default note. To adjust the display characteristics of this note, you should use the pointer that is returned by this method to access the properties and get and set methods of the Note object, such as <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.SetBalloon">INote::SetBalloon</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.Angle">INote::Angle</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.LockPosition">INote::LockPosition</see>. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.GetAnnotation">INote::GetAnnotation</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.IGetAnnotation">INote::IGetAnnotation</see> to retrieve the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation">IAnnotation</see> object.

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.InsertStackedBalloon">IModelDocExtension::InsertStackedBalloon</see>.

Parameter.Name: Style
Parameter.Description: Balloon style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBalloonStyle_e">swBalloonStyle_e</see>

Parameter.Description: Text in the balloon

Parameter.Name: LowerTextStyle
Parameter.Description: Text style for the lower text of the balloon as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swBalloonTextContent_e">swBalloonTextContent_e</see>

Parameter.Name: LowerText
Parameter.Description: Text in the lower part of the balloon when Style = swBS_SplitCirc

Member.Returns: Newly created <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">note</see>
Member.Remarks: This method adds a single balloon note attached to the pre-selected entity. The note is located near the pre-selection. This method returns a Note object, which you can then use to access the note; for example, setting the font of the note text or setting the position of the Note. You can stack notes on the Note object returned by this method. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote.GetBalloonStack">INote::GetBalloonStack</see> with this note to get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBalloonStack">IBalloonStack</see> object. You can control various properties of the stack, such as the direction and size. You can also use the BalloonStack to stack more balloons on this first balloon. If the balloon style is split circle, both the lower- and upper-text arguments are used. If the balloon style is anything other than split circle, the upper-text arguments are used and the lower-text arguments are ignored. If the text style is item number or quantity, the note text is determined through the pres-selected entity to which this note is attached and the corresponding text argument is ignored. If the pre-selection is just a location on the drawing, not an entity, then the text style should be custom and you must specify the text to use.

Member.Name: IsTessellationValid
Member.Description: Gets whether the current set of facets is valid.
Member.Returns: True if the facet data is valid; false if not
Member.Remarks: This method captures operations that invalidate the current set of facets, but does not send a RegenNotify event. For example, if the user changes the rendering tolerance, the RegenNotify event is not sent. However, the current set of facets would be invalid. This action triggers a RepaintNotify from which you can call this method before attempting to use your current set of facet data. If false is returned, then valid facet information would not be available until SOLIDWORKS completes a repaint operation (RepaintPostNotify). In other words, SOLIDWORKS does not have any valid facet information at this time, and any facet data obtained in earlier calls is invalid.

Member.Name: LightSourcePropertyValues
Member.Description: Gets and sets the light source property values.

Parameter.Name: ID
Parameter.Description: Light source ID

Member.Returns: Array of 19 doubles containing the light source properties (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The light source ID ranges from 0 to n, where n = (the total number of light sources - 1). To get the total number of light sources, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetLightSourceCount">IModelDoc2::GetLightSourceCount</see>. The return values for this property is the following array of 19 doubles: [ type, Intensity, Color[3], Position[3], Direction[3], coneAngle, falloff[3], Ambient, Specular, isDisabled, SpotExponent ]
where:
type = an integer packed into a double that represents the light source type where valid types are taken from openGL definitions (LIGHT_EYE, LIGHT_AMBIENT, LIGHT_SPOT, LIGHT_POINT, LIGHT_DISTANT)
Intensity = Light-source intensity (diffuseness) where values range from 0 to 1.
Color[3] = Light-source color in the form of an array of 3 doubles (R, G, B) where values range from 0 to 1.
Position[3] = Light-source position for spot lights in the form of an array of 3 doubles (X, Y, Z) in model space.
Direction[3] = Light-source direction in the form of an array of 3 doubles (i, j, k)
coneAngle = Light-source cone half angle in degrees where valid values are from 0 to 90 and 180.
falloff[3] = Light-source falloff in the form of an array of 3 doubles (Kc, Kl, Kq). These values result in changes in light intensity as the distance between the light position and the vertex change. NOTE: The falloff[3] values are not supported in SOLIDWORKS 2011 and later.The result is driven by the following equation: [ 1 / (Kc + D*Kl + D*D*Kq ) ] where: D = the distance.between the light's position and the vertex Kc = constant attenuation Kl = linear attenuation Kq = quadratic attenuation
Ambient = light-source ambient Intensity
Specular = light-source specular Intensity
isDisabled = an integer packed into a double. True means that the light is disabled and false means the light is not disabled.
SpotExponent = spot exponentNOTE: The SpotExponent value is not supported in SOLIDWORKS 2011 and later.

Member.Name: MultiSelectByRay
Member.Signature: MultiSelectByRay( System.object DoubleInfoIn, System.int TypeWanted, System.bool Append )
Member.Description: Selects multiple objects of the specified type that are intersected by a ray from point (x,y,z in meters) in direction vector (x,y,z) within a distance radius.

Parameter.Name: DoubleInfoIn
Parameter.Description: Array of 7 doubles:3 for the start point of the ray, 3 for the direction of the ray, and 1 for the radius

Parameter.Name: TypeWanted
Parameter.Description: Type of objects to select as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSelectType_e">swSelectType_e</see>

Parameter.Name: Append
Parameter.Description: True to append the selections to the current selection list, false to not

Member.Returns: True if an object is selected, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method:
Defines a cylindrical region of infinite length that begins at pointIn, runs parallel to VectorIn, and has a radius of RadiusIn. If you specified edges or vertices, then any edge or vertex found within the selection cylinder is selected.
Selects only entity objects, which include faces, edges, and vertices. You cannot use this function to select <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch">ISketch</see> objects.When selecting face entities, RadiusIn is ignored and a cylinder of infinitely small radius is used.

Member.Name: RayIntersections
Member.Signature: RayIntersections( System.object BodiesIn, System.object BasePointsIn, System.object VectorsIn, System.int Options, System.double HitRadius, System.double Offset )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.RayIntersections">IModelDocExtension::RayIntersections</see>.

Parameter.Name: BodiesIn
Parameter.Description: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">bodies</see> that are hit by the rays (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: BasePointsIn
Parameter.Description: Array of doubles containing the x,y,z base points of each ray

Parameter.Name: VectorsIn
Parameter.Description: Array of doubles containing the direction vectors of each ray

Parameter.Name: Options
Parameter.Description: Number of options as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swRayPtsOpts_e">swRayPtsOpts_e</see>

Parameter.Name: HitRadius
Parameter.Description: Radius of hit cylinder; this is used mainly in grazing cases to establish a hit

Parameter.Name: Offset
Parameter.Description: Length tolerance to use to establish whether a hit on a face represents the entry or exit of the ray from the body (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Number of intersections found
Member.Remarks: The method performs the intersection operations between the specified bodies and the ray vectors. To get the results (a set of intersection points, intersection normals, and the bodies that were hit from your bodiesIn array) of the intersection operations, you must call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsPoints">IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetRayIntersectionsTopology">IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionTopology</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetRayIntersectionsTopology">IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsTopology</see>. Information returned by IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints, IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints, IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionTopology, and IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionsTopology depends partially on the value of the options argument. Valid values can be concatenated together using bitwise operations. See IModelDoc2::GetRayIntersectionsPoints or IModelDoc2::IGetRayIntersectionPoints to see which data is always output regardless of the values specified in the options argument. For each ray that hits an edge or a vertex, the offset distance is added in both the positive and negative directions along the ray and the points computed are tested for spatial inclusion in the hit body. This determines if the ray was entering, leaving, or just grazing the body at the hit point. Entry and exit onto faces can be computed does not require such an offset.

Member.Name: ReloadOrReplace
Member.Signature: ReloadOrReplace( System.bool ReadOnly, System.string ReplaceFileName, System.bool DiscardChanges )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.ReloadOrReplace">IModelDocExtension::ReloadOrReplace</see>.

Parameter.Name: ReadOnly
Parameter.Description: True to set the model document read-only after reload or replace, false to allow write access

Parameter.Name: ReplaceFileName
Parameter.Description: Replacement model document; null or Nothing to reload the current model document

Parameter.Name: DiscardChanges
Parameter.Description: True to discard changes made to the current model document, false to abort operation if the model document was changed (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Error codes as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swComponentReloadError_e">swComponentReloadError_e</see>
Member.Remarks:
The model to reload or replace must be open in its own window frame.
This method does not reload or replace the model if the top assembly has been opened invisibly. In that case, make the model visible by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.Visible">IModelDoc2::Visible</see> before calling this method.
You must call IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace after calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ForceReleaseLocks">IModelDoc2::ForceReleaseLocks</see>, which detaches a file from the file system, to re-attach a detached file to the file system. If you do not call IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace after calling IModelDoc2::ForceReleaseLocks, then you will experience problems with OLE objects (e.g., design tables). Any changes made to a file while it is detached are not preserved unless you save the file to disk before calling IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace. Additionally if you set IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace's DiscardChanges parameter to false and you made changes to a detached file that you are attempting to re-attach to the file system, then IModelDoc2::ReloadOrReplace will fail. DiscardChanges must be set to true to re-attach a detached file. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.CloseAndReopen">ISldWorks::CloseAndReopen</see> to perform a similar function with drawing documents.

Member.Description: Sets the property values of the selected edge.

Member.Returns: True if edge properties successfully changed, false if not
Member.Remarks:
If the edge...
Then this method...
Does not have a name
Sets the name.
Has a name
Does not change the name and returns false. This behavior is intended to prevent a program from renaming an edge that is referenced in some other location. For example, if an assembly contains a mate to an edge on a part, then a name is automatically assigned to that edge. If you change that name, then there is no guarantee that the mate remains valid. Therefore, when using entity names, you should first check to see if the entity is already named, and if so, use the existing name. If no name exists for the edge, then you can give the edge a name.

Member.Name: SelectedFaceProperties
Member.Signature: SelectedFaceProperties( System.int RgbColor, System.double Ambient, System.double Diffuse, System.double Specular, System.double Shininess, System.double Transparency, System.double Emission, System.bool UsePartProps, System.string FaceName )
Member.Description: Sets the material property values of the selected face.

Parameter.Name: RgbColor
Parameter.Description: Face color (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UsePartProps
Parameter.Description: True if the face inherits the Part properties, false if not

Parameter.Name: FaceName
Parameter.Description: Name of the face

Member.Returns: True if face properties successfully changed, false if not
Member.Remarks:
To see a color change, you must:
Specify the reflectivity properties (Diffuse, Specular, Shininess (1.0 - Specular spread/Blurriness)), each with a value greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0. Specify Ambient, Transparency and Emission, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. Refresh the graphics area after calling this method. You can use the FaceName argument to set the name for this face. If the face has a name, then this method does not change the name and returns false. This behavior is intended to prevent a program from renaming a face that is referenced in some other location. For example, if an assembly contains a mate to a face on a part, then a name is automatically assigned to that face. If you change that name, then there is no guarantee that the mate will still be valid. Therefore, when using entity names, you should first check to see if the entity is already named, and, if so, use the existing name. If no name exists for the face, then you can assign the face a name.

Member.Signature: SelectedFeatureProperties( System.int RgbColor, System.double Ambient, System.double Diffuse, System.double Specular, System.double Shininess, System.double Transparency, System.double Emission, System.bool UsePartProps, System.bool Suppressed, System.string FeatureName )
Member.Description: Sets the property values of the selected feature.

Parameter.Name: RgbColor
Parameter.Description: Color of feature (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Ambient
Parameter.Description: 0.0 <= Ambient value <= 1.0

Parameter.Name: Diffuse
Parameter.Description: 0.0 < Diffuse value <= 1.0

Parameter.Name: Specular

Parameter.Description: 0.0 <= Transparency value <= 1.0

Parameter.Name: Emission
Parameter.Description: 0.0 <= Emission value <= 1.0

Parameter.Name: UsePartProps
Parameter.Description: True if the feature inherits the properties from the part, false if not

Parameter.Name: Suppressed
Parameter.Description: True if the feature is suppressed, false if not

Parameter.Name: FeatureName
Parameter.Description: Name of the feature

Member.Returns: True if feature's properties are successfully set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
To see a color change, you must:
Specify the reflectivity properties (Diffuse, Specular, Shininess (1.0 - Specular spread/Blurriness)), each with a value greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0. Specify Ambient, Transparency and Emission, each with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. Refresh the graphics area after calling this method. This method is different from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SelectedEdgeProperties">IModelDodc2::SelectedEdgeProperties</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SelectedFaceProperties">IModelDoc2::SelectedFaceProperties</see> in that it allows you to change the name of this feature. All features have names; however, a face or edge typically has a name only if it is being referenced. Because it is dangerous to change the name of a referenced object, you cannot programmatically change the names of faces or edges. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.SetEntityName">IPartDoc::SetEntityName</see> for additional information. This method requires that the feature to be selected. To select the feature programmatically, you can use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> and pass in the feature name and the appropriate object type (for example, "BODYFEATURE", "ATTRIBUTE", "PLANE", "SKETCH", and so on) and the selection coordinates 0,0,0. To determine the feature name and object type, use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Name">IFeature::Name</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName">IFeature::GetTypeName</see> methods, respectively.

Member.Name: SetAddToDB
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchManager.AddToDB">ISketchManager::AddToDB</see>.

Parameter.Name: Setting
Parameter.Description: True to add items directly to the SOLIDWORKS database, false if not

Example.Name: Calculate Closest Distance Between Model Components

Member.Remarks: One of the benefits of adding sketch entities directly to the database is that you can avoid grid and entity snapping. For example, if you create a sketch line whose endpoint is near another entity or near a grid point, the new line endpoint snaps to the other item or grid point. Setting ModelDoc2::SetAddToDB to True avoids this behavior during sketch entity creation. IModelDoc2::SetAddToDb and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> also increase performance during sketch entity creation. IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded requires that IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB is True. If you want to constrain all the sketch entities after creation, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ConstrainAll">ISketch::ConstrainAll</see>. After setting IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB to True, you must set it back to false to restore SOLIDWORKS to its normal operating mode.

Member.Name: SetConsiderLeadersAsLines
Member.Description: Sets a flag on the document that indicates whether the display data of a leader should be included as lines when the lines are retrieved from a view or annotation in this document.

Parameter.Name: LeadersAsLines
Parameter.Description: True to return leaders as line data, false to not

Member.Returns: Original value of the flag before calling this method
Member.Remarks: The various GetLeaderCount and GetLeaderAtIndex methods that are found on several different annotations return the information about where the vertices of the leader are located. GetLineCount and GetLinesAtIndex also return the leader information as part of its line information. Depending on what your program is trying to accomplish and which methods it is using, this duplication of information may not be desirable. This method controls this behavior by setting a flag on the document that indicates whether or not the leader information is returned as part of the line information or not. Initially, when a document is opened, the flag is set to True, so that existing applications work as they have always worked. If you do not want to get back leader information as part of the line information, call this method and set the value to false. The flag is not saved with the document, so you must specifically set it to false whenever you do not want leaders as part of the line information. The various GetArrowHeadCount and GetArrowHeadAtIndex methods are also affected. When this flag has been set to false so that leaders are not considered as lines, the arrowhead information for the arrowheads on those leaders is not returned. However, GetArrowHeadInfo still returns valid information. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetConsiderLeadersAsLines">IModelDoc2::GetConsiderLeadersAsLines</see> to determine the current behavior.

Parameter.Name: Setting
Parameter.Description: True to display new sketch entities when added, false to note

Member.Remarks:
The sketch entities appear on the screen after performing <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GraphicsRedraw2">IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.EditRebuild3">IModelDoc2::EditRebuild3</see> is performed. Also, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetAddToDB">IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB</see> must be True to use this method's settings. This display setting remains even after your program run has ended. Therefore, it is recommended that you reset this parameter to True at the end of your program. For example, if you have ended your program and the display is set to false, then the user would have difficulty performing selections and newly created entities would not be seen until a redraw or a rebuild. NOTES:
IModelDoc2::GraphicsRedraw2 is much faster than ModelDoc2::EditRebuild3.
IModelDoc2::SetAddToDB and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.SetDisplayWhenAdded">IModelDoc2::SetDisplayWhenAdded</see> also increase performance during sketch entity creation.

Member.Name: SetPopupMenuMode
Member.Description: Sets the pop-up menu mode.

Parameter.Name: ModeIn
Parameter.Description: Pop-up menu mode (see Remarks)

Member.Remarks:
When end users press the right-mouse button on an entity in the graphics window, they are be presented with one of two menu sets. These menu sets are defined as mode 0 and mode 1. Mode
0 - Default shortcut mode. This mode presents the end user with options to Select Other, manipulate the view, access the properties dialog of the selected item, and so on.
1 - The end-user is presented with a limited set of choices including Select Other and Clear Selection. This mode is typically seen when a SOLIDWORKS dialog is active and the user is restricted to entity selection. Using this method, you can simulate the same shortcut menu behavior as in the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface. If you have a dialog that requires user selection of entities, you can set the pop-up menu mode to 1 to simulate SOLIDWORKS behavior. Your application should always set the menu mode back to its previous value. To determine the previous behavior, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetPopupMenuMode">IModelDoc2::GetPopupMenuMode</see> prior to calling to this method.

Member.Name: SetReadOnlyState
Member.Description: Sets whether this document is read-only or read-write.

Parameter.Name: SetReadOnly
Parameter.Description: True to set this document to be read-only, false to set this document to read-write

Member.Returns: True if method executes successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks: If the file is opened as read-write, specifying read-only should work except if it is a new file that has not yet been saved. If the file is opened as read-only in SOLIDWORKS, then specifying read-write only changes the internal SOLIDWORKS state (not the access rights on disk) and only succeeds if it would be possible to open this file with write access. If the file is read-only on disk or if another user has it open with write access, then this method does not change the internal state to writeable; the document remains read-only.
