Member.Name: GetLeaderAtIndex
Member.Description: Gets information about the specified leader on this surface finish symbol.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of leader

Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
There can be 0, 1 or 2 lines used with the leader line. If the surface-finish sysmbol is not attached then, there are 0 lines; otherwise, you can have a straight leaderline (1 line) or a bent leaderline (2 lines). You must infer the number of leader lines based on <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.IsAttached">ISFSymbol::IsAttached</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.HasExtraLeader">ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader</see>.
ISFSymbol::IsAttached == false implies no leaderline and no leaderline points (PointCount=0).
ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader == false means that this is a straight leaderline and 1 line (PointCount=2)
ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader == true means that this is a bent leaderline and 2 lines (PointCount=3) Format of return information is the following array of doubles:
retval[0] = x-coordinate of first leader point
retval[1] = y-coordinate of first leader point
retval[2] = z-coordinate of first leader point
retval[3] = x-coordinate of second leader point
retval[4] = y-coordinate of second leader point
retval[5] = z-coordinate of second leader point
retval[6] = x-coordinate of third leader point
retval[7] = y-coordinate of third leader point
retval[8] = z-coordinate of third leader point
Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.GetLeaderCount">ISFSymbol::GetLeaderCount</see> to see how many leaders there are on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">ISFSymbol</see> object.

Member.Name: IGetLeaderAtIndex
Member.Signature: IGetLeaderAtIndex( System.int Index, out System.int PointCount )
Member.Description: Gets information about the specified leader on this surface finish symbol.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of the line where the index begins at 0

Parameter.Name: PointCount
Parameter.Description: Number of (x,y,z) points returned in the array

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
There can be 0, 1 or 2 lines used with the leader line. If the surface-finish sysmbol is not attached then, there are 0 lines; otherwise, you can have a straight leaderline (1 line) or a bent leaderline (2 lines). You must infer the number of leader lines based on <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.IsAttached">ISFSymbol::IsAttached</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.HasExtraLeader">ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader</see>.
ISFSymbol::IsAttached == false implies no leaderline and no leaderline points (PointCount=0).
ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader == false means that this is a straight leaderline and 1 line (PointCount=2)
ISFSymbol::HasExtraLeader == true means that this is a bent leaderline and 2 lines (PointCount=3) Format of return information is the following array of doubles:
retval[0] = x-coordinate of first leader point
retval[1] = y-coordinate of first leader point
retval[2] = z-coordinate of first leader point
retval[3] = x-coordinate of second leader point
retval[4] = y-coordinate of second leader point
retval[5] = z-coordinate of second leader point
retval[6] = x-coordinate of third leader point
retval[7] = y-coordinate of third leader point
retval[8] = z-coordinate of third leader point
Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol.GetLeaderCount">ISFSymbol::GetLeaderCount</see> to see how many leaders there are on the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISFSymbol">ISFSymbol</see> object.

Member.Description: Adds a third-party CPropertyPage to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISWPropertySheet">ISWPropertySheet</see> and adds an ActiveX control on top of the page.

Parameter.Name: Title
Parameter.Description: Title of CPropertyPage

Parameter.Description: Name, ProgID, or CLSID of the ActiveX control (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: LicenseKey
Parameter.Description: License key for the ActiveX control

Member.Returns: Index of CPropertyPage on ISWPropertySheet
Member.Remarks:
Typically, this method is called from the ISldWorks <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DSldWorksEvents_PropertySheetCreateNotifyEventHandler">PropertySheetCreateNotify</see> event handler. See the Example section.
The ProgID argument accepts any of these values:
OLE short name or ProgID for the class; for example, "MSCAL.Calendar". The name must match the name registered by the control.
String form of a CLSID, contained within braces, for example, "{9DBAFCCF-592F-101B-85CE-00608CEC297B}". See also <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/overview/Keystrokes_and_Accelerator_Keys_and_ActiveX_Modeless_Dialogs_and_PropertyManager_Pages.htm">Keystrokes and Accelerator Keys in ActiveX Modeless Dialogs and PropertyManager Pages</see>.

Member.Name: RevolutionType
Member.Description: Gets or sets the type of revolution to specify for this screw mate.
Member.Returns: Type of revolution as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swScrewMateDistanceOptions_e">swScrewMateDistanceOptions_e</see>
Member.Remarks:
If you set this property to swScrewMateDistanceOptions_e:
swDistancePerRevolution, then specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IScrewMateFeatureData.RevolutionVal">IScrewMateFeatureData::RevolutionVal</see> with the distance that one component translates for each revolution of the other component. swRevolutionsPerUnitLength, then specify IScrewMateFeatureData::RevolutionVal with the number of revolutions of one component for each unit length that the other component translates.

Member.Name: RevolutionVal
Member.Description: Gets or sets either the number of revolutions one component makes for each unit length that the other component translates or the distance that one component translates for each revolution of the other component.
Member.Returns: Revolution value (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IScrewMateFeatureData.RevolutionType">IScrewMateFeatureData::RevolutionType</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swScrewMateDistanceOptions_e">swScrewMateDistanceOptions_e</see>:
swDistancePerRevolution, then specify this property with the distance that one component translates for each revolution of the other component. swRevolutionsPerUnitLength, then specify this property with the number of revolutions of one component for each unit length that the other component translates. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swUserPreferenceIntegerValue_e">swUserPreferencesIntegerValue_e</see>.swUnitsLinear to a unit length as defined in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swLengthUnit_e">swLengthUnit_e</see>.

Member.Name: UnChainMemberPairs
Member.Description: Gets and sets whether to chain member pairs to create this secondary structure system member.
Member.Returns: True to pair each member passed in <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISecondaryMemberBetweenPointsFeatureData.SetMemberPairs">ISecondaryMemberBetweenPointsFeatureData::SetMemberPairs</see> to the previous member passed, false to pair consecutive members only
Member.Remarks:
If this property is set to true, each primary member passed to ISecondaryMemberBetweenPointsFeatureData::SetMemberPairs pairs with the previous primary member to create a new member pair. For the list of members A,B,C,D,E,F: If this property is set to true, then 5 member pairs are created: A -- B B -- C C -- D D -- E E -- F
If this property is set to false, then only 3 member pairs are created: A -- B C -- D E -- F

Member.Name: GraphicsOnlySection
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to generate a graphics-only section view.
Member.Returns: True to generate a graphics-only section view, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property corresponds to the Graphics-only section check box on the Section View PropertyManager page. When a section view is created, the model is rebuilt. If the model is very large and complex, rebuilding the model slows down the creation of the section view. This property indicates whether to rebuild the model when a section view is created. When this property is set to true:
Keep cap color check box is selected and inactivated on the Section View PropertyManager page. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISectionViewData.KeepCapColor">ISectionViewData::KeepCapColor</see> returns only true; setting to false is ignored. Model is not rebuilt, and the section view is quickly generated.

Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to color the caps of section views.
Member.Returns: True to color the caps of section views, false to not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: This property is valid only if <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISectionViewData.ShowSectionCap">ISectionViewData::ShowSectionCap</see> is true and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISectionViewData.GraphicsOnlySection">ISectionViewData::GraphicsOnlySection</see> is false.

Member.Returns: True to validate and return a status for newly created section bodies, false to not
Member.Remarks: By default, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelViewManager.CreateSectionView">IModelViewManager::CreateSectionView</see> returns whether it successfully created a section view. Set this property to true to have <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelViewManager.CreateSectionView">IModelViewManager::CreateSectionView</see> check and return whether it successfully created the section bodies.

Member.Description: Adds the specified object to the selection list.

Parameter.Name: Object
Parameter.Description: Object to add to the selection list (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: SelectData
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectData">ISelectData</see>

Member.Returns: True if successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.CreateSelectData">ISelectionMgr::CreateSelectData</see> to specify SelectData. To add objects to a selection list without pre-selecting the objects in the user interface:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.SuspendSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList</see> to suspend the current selection list, preserving its contents and starting a new selection list. Call ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObject or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObjects">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObjects</see> to populate the new selection list. Process the objects in the new selection list. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.ResumeSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::ResumeSelectionList</see> to reinstate the suspended selection list. To programmatically pre-select objects in the user interface and add them to a selection list, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>.

Member.Name: AddSelectionListObjects
Member.Description: Adds the specified objects to the selection list.

Parameter.Name: Objects
Parameter.Description: Array of objects to add to the selection list (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: SelectData
Parameter.Description: <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectData">ISelectData</see>

Member.Returns: Number of objects added to the selection list
Member.Remarks:
For VB.NET and C# applications, specify Objects as an array of System.Runtime.InteropServices.DispatchWrappers. See the examples and <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/IDispatch_Object_Arrays_as_Input_in_.NET.htm">IDispatch Object Arrays as Input in .NET</see> for more information. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.CreateSelectData">ISelectionMgr::CreateSelectData</see> to specify SelectData. To add objects to a selection list without preselecting the objects in the user interface:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.SuspendSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList</see> to suspend the current selection list, preserving its contents and starting a new selection list. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObject">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObject</see> or ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObjects to populate a new selection list. Process the objects in the new selection list. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.ResumeSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::ResumeSelectionList</see> to reinstate the suspended selection list. To programmatically preselect objects in the user interface and add them to a selection list, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>.

Member.Name: GetSelectionPoint2
Member.Description: Gets the selected point in model space coordinates from the currently selected object.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index position with in the current list of selected items, where AtIndex ranges from 1 to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObjectCount2">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObjectCount2</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Mark
Parameter.Description:
-1 = All selections regardless of marks
0 = only the selections without marks
Any other value = Value that was used to mark and select an object

Member.Returns: Array of 3 doubles (x,y,z)
Member.Remarks:
The index starts at 1, even when using C++. However, if you specify -1 for the Index argument, then the Mark argument is ignored and the dynamically highlighted view is selected if dynamic highlighting is turned on. See also IAssemblyDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DAssemblyDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, IDrawingDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DDrawingDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, and IPartDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DPartDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>. The point returned from ISelectionMgr::GetSelectionPoint2 or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectionPoint2">ISelectionMgr::IGetSelectionPoint2</see> cannot lie on the object that was selected. For example, the user can select an edge when the edge is within the pick radius of their mouse cursor. However, to get a point on a face, edge, or vertex, use that object's GetClosestPointOn method.
To do this, get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">IFace2</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">IEdge</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IVertex">IVertex</see> object using the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see> method, and then use that object to call GetClosestPointOn. Pass the X,Y,Z values returned from ISelectionMgr::GetSelectionPoint2 or ISelectionMgr::IGetSelectionPoint2, and the GetClosestPointOn method will return the closest X,Y,Z point that is on the face, edge, or vertex.
If the selected object is sketch geometry, then the coordinates returned are in sketch space. The coordinates are 2D and related to the origin of the sketch that owns the selected geometry.

Member.Description: Gets the selection point projected on to the active sketch and returned in sketch space.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index position with in the current list of selected items, where AtIndex ranges from 1 to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObjectCount2">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObjectCount2</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Mark
Parameter.Description: -1 = All selections regardless of marks 0 = only the selections without marks Any other value that was used to mark and select an object

Member.Returns: Array of 3 doubles (x,y,z)
Member.Remarks:
The selection point is projected on to the currently active sketch, resulting in a z value of 0.00. If a sketch is not currently active, then the return value is the same as that returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectionPoint2">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectionPoint2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.IGetSelectionPoint2">ISelectionMgr::IGetSelectionPoint2</see>. You can determine if a sketch is active by checking for a Nothing or null return value from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.GetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::GetActiveSketch2</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.IGetActiveSketch2">IModelDoc2::IGetActiveSketch2</see>.
The index starts at 1. However, if you specify -1 for the Index argument, then the Mark argument is ignored and the dynamically highlighted view is selected if dynamic highlighting is turned on. See also IAssemblyDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DAssemblyDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, IDrawingDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DDrawingDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, and IPartDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DPartDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>.

Member.Name: ResumeSelectionList
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.ResumeSelectionList2">ISelectionMgr::ResumeSelectionList2</see>.
Member.Remarks:
To add objects to a selection list without preselecting the objects in the user interface:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.SuspendSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList</see> to suspend the current selection list, preserving its contents and starting a new selection list. To populate a new selection list, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObject">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObject</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObjects">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObjects</see>.NOTE: To add objects in a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet">selection set</see> in a new selection list, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet.Select">ISelectionSet::Select</see>. Process the objects in the new selection list. Call ISelectionMgr::ResumeSelectionList to reinstate the suspended selection list. To programmatically preselect objects in the user interface and add them to a selection list, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>.

Member.Name: ResumeSelectionList2
Member.Description: Reinstates the previously suspended selection list.

Parameter.Name: Append
Parameter.Description: True to append the new selection list to the suspended selection list and resume the combined selection list, false to just resume the suspended selection list

Member.Remarks:
To add objects to a selection list without pre-selecting the objects in the user interface:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.SuspendSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList</see> to suspend the current selection list, preserving its contents and starting a new selection list. To populate the new selection list, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObject">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObject</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObjects">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObjects</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>.NOTE: To add objects in a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet">selection set</see> to a new selection list, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet.Select">ISelectionSet::Select</see>. Process the objects in the new selection list. Call this method to reinstate the suspended selection list, setting Append to true to append the new selection list.

Member.Signature: SetSelectionPoint2( System.int Index, System.int Mark, System.double X, System.double Y, System.double Z )
Member.Description: Sets the selection point in model space.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index position with in the current list of selected items, where AtIndex ranges from 1 to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObjectCount2">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObjectCount2</see> (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: Mark
Parameter.Description:
-1 = All selections regardless of marks
0 = only the selections without marks
Any other value = Value that was used to mark and select an object

Parameter.Name: X
Parameter.Description: x coordinate of the selection point

Parameter.Name: Y
Parameter.Description: y coordinate of the selection point

Parameter.Name: Z
Parameter.Description: z coordinate of the selection point

Member.Returns: True if the position of the selection point is set, false if not
Member.Remarks: This method allows an application to provide an XYZ position to a selected object at the given index in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr">ISelectionMgr</see> object. This XYZ position represents a world-coordinate location in the context of that ISelectionMgr object. The index starts at 1, even when using C++. However, if you specify -1 for the Index argument, then the Mark argument is ignored and the dynamically highlighted view is selected if dynamic highlighting is turned on. See also IAssemblyDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DAssemblyDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, IDrawingDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DDrawingDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>, and IPartDoc event <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.DPartDocEvents_DynamicHighlightNotifyEventHandler">DynamicHighlightNotify</see>.

Member.Name: SuspendSelectionList
Member.Description: Suspends the current selection list.
Member.Returns: 0 if the suspended list is empty, 1 if not
Member.Remarks:
To add objects to a selection list without preselecting the objects in the user interface:
Call ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList to suspend the current selection list, preserving its contents and starting a new selection list. To populate a new selection list, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObject">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObject</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.AddSelectionListObjects">ISelectionMgr::AddSelectionListObjects</see>.NOTE: To add objects in a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet">selection set</see> to a new selection list, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionSet.Select">ISelectionSet::Select</see>. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.ResumeSelectionList">ISelectionMgr::ResumeSelectionList</see> to reinstate the suspended selection list. To programmatically preselect objects in the user interface and add them to a selection list, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see>. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ClearSelection2">IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2</see> works like ISelectionMgr::SuspendSelectionList to clear the selection list. Unlike IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2, this method preserves the list for future reinstatement.

Member.Description: Inserts a family table in this drawing sheet.

Parameter.Name: AttachToAnchorPoint
Parameter.Description: True to insert the family table at the existing family table anchor point, false to anchor the table at the point specified by X and Y

Parameter.Description: True to use all configurations, false to only use ConfigArray configurations

Parameter.Description: Array of configurations to use; valid only if UseAllConfigs is false

Parameter.Name: ItemNumberStart
Parameter.Description: Starting item number

Parameter.Name: ItemNumberIncrement
Parameter.Description: Item number increment

Parameter.Name: FollowConfigTreeOrder
Parameter.Description: True to follow the configuration tree order, false to not

Member.Returns: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFamilyTableAnnotation">IFamilyTableAnnotation</see>
Member.Remarks: Family tables display the variations in part and assembly configurations or custom properties in table format. By default, the family table templates are in install_dir\lang\language and have a filename extension of .sldfamtbt. The template and table must be of the same type. Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISheet.SetProperties2">ISheet::SetProperties2</see>.

Parameter.Name: PaperSz
Parameter.Description: Paper size as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swDwgPaperSizes_e">swDwgPaperSizes_e</see>

Parameter.Description: Template as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swDwgTemplates_e">swDwgTemplates_e</see>

Parameter.Name: Scale1
Parameter.Description: Scale numerator

Parameter.Name: Scale2
Parameter.Description: Scale denominator

Parameter.Name: FirstAngle
Parameter.Description: True if you want first angle projection, false if not

Parameter.Name: Width
Parameter.Description: Custom paper width if PaperSz = swDwgPaperSizes_e.swDwgPapersUserDefined

Parameter.Name: Height
Parameter.Description: Custom paper height if PaperSz = swDwgPaperSizes_e.swDwgPapersUserDefined

Member.Remarks:
If you specify a custom template, then the current custom template is used by this sheet until you call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISheet.SetTemplateName">ISheet::SetTemplateName</see> and pass in a different custom template name.
NOTE: If Templ does not match the PaperSz specification, then you get a template that does not fit the paper size. This parameter does not override the PaperSz setting. Also, if you change the scale of the sheet using Scale1 and Scale2, then any drawing view that is set to use the sheet's scale takes the new scale setting. You can also use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISheet.SetSize">ISheet::SetSize</see> to set the size of the sheet and the standard sheet size.

However, you cannot specify the scaling of the position or text height of the annotations. Instead, both of these methods automatically scale the position of the annotations but do not scale the text height of the annotations when the drawing is changed.

Member.Name: SetRadius
Member.Description: Sets the bend radius in this gauge table.

Parameter.Description: Bend radius

Parameter.Name: Override
Parameter.Description: True to override an existing value, false to not (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if bend radius successfully set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
If Override is:
true, then specify an override bend radius in Radius. false, then specify Radius using one of the default bend radii for the current gauge number from the gauge table. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters.GetAvailableRadii">ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters::GetAvailableRadii</see> to choose a value for Radius.

Member.Name: SetThickness
Member.Description: Sets the gauge thickness in this gauge table.

Parameter.Name: Thickness
Parameter.Description: Gauge thickness

Parameter.Name: Override
Parameter.Description: True to override an existing value, false to not (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if gauge thickness successfully set, false if not
Member.Remarks:
If Override is:
true, then specify Thickness using an override gauge thickness. You should also use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters.SetRadius">ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters::SetRadius</see> to override the bend radius. false, instead of calling this method use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters.GetAvailableGaugeNumbers">ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters::GetAvailableGaugeNumbers</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters.SetCurrentGaugeNumber">ISheetMetalGaugeTableParameters::SetCurrentGaugeNumber</see> to change the current gauge number. Each gauge number has a default thickness.

Member.Name: ActionDirection
Member.Description: Gets or sets the direction of the force.
Member.Returns:
Along an axis defined by an edge or a plane
Along the line-of-sight between two points
Member.Remarks: The way you define the directions of your forces depends on which forces you are creating. If you are creating an action-only force, the force direction remains fixed with respect to some part in your model, either a moving part or the ground part. In this case, you can define the force direction using one vector defined by an edge or a plane. If you are creating an action/reaction force, then the direction along which you want the force applied is defined by the line between two points in your model and is constantly changing throughout the simulation. In this case, you can define the force direction as the line between the two points.

Fire Events for External Output Time Step Changes

Member.Remarks:
If the EntitiesToDimension argument takes the value swAutodimEntitiesSelected, then use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> with a mark value of swAutodimMarkEntities to select the sketch entities to dimension.
You can supply datums for horizontal and vertical dimensioning schemes. Select and mark a unique vertical edge, vertex, sketch point, or vertical sketch line as the datum for the horizontal dimensioning scheme, using swAutodimMarkHorizontalDatum as the mark value. Similarly, select a unique horizontal edge, vertex, sketch point, or horizontal sketch line as the datum for the vertical dimensioning scheme, using swAutodimMarkVerticalDatum as the mark value. It is an error to supply just one datum as indicated by the status value swAutodimStatus_DatumNotSupplied.

Member.Signature: CheckFeatureUse( System.int FeatureType, out System.int OpenCount, out System.int ClosedCount )
Member.Description: Checks to see if this sketch is valid for use in creating a specified feature.

Parameter.Name: FeatureType
Parameter.Description: Determine if this type of feature can be created as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSketchCheckFeatureProfileUsage_e">swSketchCheckFeatureProfileUsage_e</see>

Parameter.Name: OpenCount
Parameter.Description: Number of open contours found in this sketch

Parameter.Name: ClosedCount
Parameter.Description: Number of closed contours found in this sketch

Member.Returns: swSketchCheckFeatureStatus_OK if this sketch can be used to create the specified feature; see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSketchCheckFeatureStatus_e">swSketchCheckFeatureStatus_e</see> for possible failure values

Example.Name: Determine If Sketch Suitable for Feature

Member.Remarks: This method is equivalent to the SOLIDWORKS interactive tool Check Sketch for Feature Usage. See the SOLIDWORKS Help for details. The OpenCount and ClosedCount arguments are output values. If this method returns swSketchCheckFeatureStatus_OK, meaning that the sketch can be used to create the specified feature, then these two arguments contain useful information. If this method returns something else, then OpenCount and ClosedCount both return 0. If the featureType value is not valid, this method returns swSketchCheckFeatureStatus_UnknownError.

Member.Returns: Number of arcs in the sketch

Member.Name: GetArcs
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetArcs2">ISketch::GetArcs2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetArcs2">ISketch::IGetArcs2</see>.

Member.Name: GetArcs2
Member.Description: Gets all of the arcs in the sketch.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles containing the arcs in the sketch (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
To determine the number of arcs, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetArcCount">ISketch::GetArcCount</see>. Return value is an array of doubles with the format: [ Color, Type, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, [Start], [End], [Center] Rotation Dir ] where
Color - COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
Type - Line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a line style and line weight.
Line Font - Line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
Line Width - Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
Layer ID - Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
Layer Override - Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if Layer Override was returned as 3, the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
Start[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the start point.
End[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the end point. If the arc is closed, then End[3] is the same point as the Start.
Center[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the center point.
Rotation Dir - Rotational direction (CW = -1, CCW = 1) This set of data repeats for each arc in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumArcs * 16).

Member.Description: Gets the edges for a sketch that has one contour.

Parameter.Name: Xform
Parameter.Description: Array of size 16 doubles representing the transform

Member.Returns: Array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see>
Member.Remarks:
This method supports sketches with one contour only. For sketches with multiple contours, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchContours">ISketch::GetSketchContours</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSketchContours">ISketch::IGetSketchContours</see> and then <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchContour.GetEdges">ISketchContour::GetEdges</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchContour.IGetEdges">ISketchContour::IGetEdges</see>.
Specifying the unit transform returns the edges in the space of the sketch.
If your application is expecting the returned edges to be in the context of the model's coordinate system, then xform should be the inverse of the transform returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ModelToSketchTransform">ISketch::ModelToSketchTransform</see>.

Member.Name: GetEllipses3
Member.Description: Gets all of the ellipses in the sketch.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchEllipse">ISketchEllipse</see> objects. The return values are in an array of doubles: [ Color, LineType, LineFont, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, StartPt[3], EndPt[3], CenterPt[3], MajorPt[3], MinorPt[3],Direction ... ] where:
Color :
COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
LineType :
Line type. Valid returns are defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a lineStyle and lineWeight.
LineFont :
Value is used for polyline font information. This value can be used as an input to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.GetLineFontInfo2">IDrawingDoc::GetLineFontInfo2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.GetLineFontName2">IDrawinDoc::GetLineFontName2</see>.
LineWidth :
Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
LayerID:
Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. Obtain the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
LayerOverride:
Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
StartPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse start point
EndPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse end point. If the ellipse is closed, then this will be the same point as the StartPt.
CenterPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse center point.
MajorPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing a point on the ellipse and on the major axis.
MinorPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing a point on the ellipse and on the minor axis.
Direction :
-1 for clockwise, +1 for counterclockwise
This set of data repeats for each ellipse in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumEllipses * 20). To determine the number of ellipses, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetEllipseCount">ISketch::GetEllipseCount</see>.

Member.Remarks: The return value is the following array of doubles: [ Color, Type, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, [Start], [End] ] where all data values are returned as doubles: Color = COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color. Type = line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a line style and line weight. Line Font = line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see>. Line Width = integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>. Layer ID = integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. Obtain the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>. Layer Override = integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride is returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer. Start[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the line start point. End[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the line end point. This set of data repeats for each line in the sketch. The number of doubles returned is (lineCount * 12). To determine the number of lines in the sketch, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetLineCount2">ISketch::GetLineCount2</see>. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchLine">ISketchLine</see> objects.

Member.Description: Gets all of the parabolas in the sketch.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchParabola">ISketchParabola</see> objects. The return values are in an array of doubles: [ Color, LineType, LineStyleIndex, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, StartPt[3], EndPt[3], FocusPt[3], ApexPt[3] ] where: Color = COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color. LineType = line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a line style and line weight. LineStyleIndex = line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see>. LineWidth = integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>. LayerID = integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. Obtain the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>. LayerOverride = integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer. StartPt[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the parabola start point. EndPt[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the parabola end point. FocusPt[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the parabola focus point. ApexPt[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the parabola apex point. This set of data repeats for each parabola in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumParabolas * 18). To determine the number of parabolas, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetParabolaCount">ISketch::GetParabolaCount</see>.

Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplineParams2">ISketch::GetSplineParams2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplineParams2">ISketch::IGetSplineParams2</see>.

Member.Name: GetSplineParams2
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplineParams3">ISketch::GetSplineParams3</see>.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> objects.
The return value is an array of doubles containing data for all the splines in the sketch:
[ packedDouble1, packedDouble2, ControlPoint1[Dimension elements], ControlPoint2[Dimension elements],... knot1, knot2,..., packedDouble3, packedDouble4, packedDouble5, ]
packedDouble1 and packedDouble2
The first two array elements for each spline contain four integer values holding information that describes the rest of the data in that spline's parameters:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
0
Dim
Order
1
nCtrlPoints
Periodic
where:
Dim is the number of dimensions in which the spline is defined
Order is the order of the spline
nCtrlPoints is the number of control points
Periodic is 1 for a closed spline or 0 for an open spline NOTE: For information about unpacking double arrays into integer pairs, see:
<see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_Visual_Basic_.NET_and_Visual_Basic.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Paris in VB.NET and Visual Basic</see> <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/PackedIntegersCPlusPlus.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Pairs in C++</see> <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_C_.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Pairs in C#</see>
ControlPoint# The ControlPoint data (in the sketch coordinate system) follows the two packed data elements.
knots# The number of knots depends on whether the spline is periodic or not:
Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + 1
Non-Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + Order
packedDouble3, packedDouble4, and packedDouble5 The last three array elements for each spline contain five integer values holding style and layer information:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
i
Color
lineStyle
i+1
lineWidth
Layer
i+2
layerOverride
Not used
where:
i is the index following the last Knot or [2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim]
Color is the COLORREF value describing the color used for the ith spline
lineStyle is the line style used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration
lineWidth is line width used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration
Layer is an integer index to the layer that the ith spline is on
layerOverride is integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden or should be overridden.
Therefore, the size of the data for each spline is given by: 2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim + 3

Member.Name: GetSplines
Member.Description: Gets information for each spline by tessellation instead of by interpolation as is done by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplinesInterpolate">ISketch::GetSplinesInterpolate</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplinesInterpolate">ISketch::IGetSplinesInterpolate</see>.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> objects. The returned array of doubles has the format: [ [ Color, LineType, NumSplinePoints, [x,y,z] ] ] This complete set of data repeats itself for each spline found in the sketch. For each spline, the array returned contains the color, the line type, the number of spline points in the spline, and the X,Y,Z value for each of those points. Therefore, the [x,y,z] parameter is an array of NumSplinePoints, which may vary in size from spline to spline. The [x,y,z] points for each spline are not the same as the points used to generate the spline. This method tessellates the spline based on the display quality and places points along the spline appropriately. LineType may take one of the values in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>.

Member.Name: GetSplinesInterpolate
Member.Description: Gets the spline points by interpolation instead of by tessellation as is done by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplines">ISketch::GetSplines</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplines">ISketch::IGetSplines</see>.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: The return value is an array of doubles formatted as: [ [NumSplinePoints, [x, y, z] ], ] This complete set of data repeats itself for each spline found in the sketch. For each spline, the array returned contains the number of spline points in the spline, and the X,Y,Z value for each of those points. The [x,y,z] parameter is an array of NumSplinePoints. For example, if your sketch has two splines and each spline has three points, then the data would be in the following format: [ 3, x1_1, y1_1, z1_1, x2_1, y2_1, z2_1, x3_1, y3_1, z3_1, 3, x1_2, y1_2, z1_2, x2_2, y2_2, z2_2, x3_2, y3_2, z3_2 ] The [x,y,z] points for each spline are the same points used to generate the spline.

Member.Name: GetUserPoints
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetUserPoints2">ISketch::GetUserPoints2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetUserPoints2">ISketch::IGetUserPoints2</see>.

Member.Name: GetUserPoints2
Member.Description: Gets all of the user points in this sketch.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)

Example.Name: Get Sketch Points and Their Persistent IDs

Member.Remarks:
The return value is an array of doubles with this format: [ Color, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, ptLoc[3] ] where:
Color = COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
Line Font = line style. Valid line styles can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
Line Width = integer value defining the line width. Valid width values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration.
Layer ID = integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
Layer Override = integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
ptLoc[3] = an array of doubles (x, y, z) describing the point location This set of data repeats for each user point in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumPts * 8). To determine the number of points in the sketch, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetUserPointsCount">ISketch::GetUserPointsCount</see>. Member.Name: IGetArcs2
Member.Description: Gets all of the arcs in the sketch.

Parameter.Name: ArraySize
Parameter.Description: Number of arcs in the sketch

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles containing the arcs in the sketch (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
To determine the number of arcs, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetArcCount">ISketch::GetArcCount</see>. Return value is an array of doubles with the format: [ Color, Type, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, [Start], [End], [Center] Rotation Dir ] where
Color - COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
Type - Line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a line style and line weight.
Line Font - Line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
Line Width - Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
Layer ID - Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
Layer Override - Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if Layer Override was returned as 3, the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
Start[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the start point.
End[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the end point. If the arc is closed, then End[3] is the same point as the Start.
Center[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the center point.
Rotation Dir - Rotational direction (CW = -1, CCW = 1) This set of data repeats for each arc in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumArcs * 16).

Member.Name: IGetContourEdges
Member.Signature: IGetContourEdges( ref System.double Xform, System.int EdgeCount )
Member.Description: Gets the edges for a sketch that has one contour.

Parameter.Name: Xform
Parameter.Description: Sketch entities, edges

Parameter.Name: EdgeCount
Parameter.Description: Number of edges

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see> VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
This method supports sketches with one contour only. For sketches with multiple contours, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchContours">ISketch::GetSketchContours</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSketchContours">ISketch::IGetSketchContours</see> and then <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchContour.GetEdges">ISketchContour::GetEdges</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchContour.IGetEdges">ISketchContour::IGetEdges</see>.
To get the number of edges, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetContourEdgeCount">ISketch::GetContourEdgesCount</see> before calling this method.
Specifying the unit transform returns the edges in the space of the sketch.
If your application is expecting the returned edges to be in the context of the model's coordinate system, then xform should be the inverse of the transform returned by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.ModelToSketchTransform">ISketch::ModelToSketchTransform</see>.

Member.Remarks:

The return values are in an array of doubles: [ Color, LineType, LineFont, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, StartPt[3], EndPt[3], CenterPt[3], MajorPt[3], MinorPt[3],Direction ... ] where:
Color :
COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
LineType :
Line type. Valid returns are defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A line type is a combination of a lineStyle and lineWeight.
LineFont :
Value is used for polyline font information. This value can be used as an input to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.GetLineFontInfo2">IDrawingDoc::GetLineFontInfo2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.GetLineFontName2">IDrawinDoc::GetLineFontName2</see>.
LineWidth :
Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
LayerID:
Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. Obtain the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
LayerOverride:
Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
StartPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse start point
EndPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse end point. If the ellipse is closed, then this will be the same point as the StartPt.
CenterPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse center point.
MajorPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing a point on the ellipse and on the major axis.
MinorPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing a point on the ellipse and on the minor axis.
Direction :
-1 for clockwise, +1 for counterclockwise
This set of data repeats for each ellipse in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumEllipses * 20). To determine the number of ellipses, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetEllipseCount">ISketch::GetEllipseCount</see>.

Member.Name: IGetSplineParams2
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplineParams3">ISketch::IGetSplineParameters3</see>.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> objects. The return value is an array of doubles containing data for all the splines in the sketch:
[ packedDouble1, packedDouble2, ControlPoint1[Dimension elements], ControlPoint2[Dimension elements],... knot1, knot2,..., packedDouble3, packedDouble4, packedDouble5, ]
packedDouble1 and packedDouble2
The first two array elements for each spline contain four integer values holding information that describes the rest of the data in that spline's parameters:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
0
Dim
Order
1
nCtrlPoints
Periodic
where:
Dim is the number of dimensions in which the spline is defined
Order is the order of the spline
nCtrlPoints is the number of control points
Periodic is 1 for a closed spline or 0 for an open spline ControlPoint# The ControlPoint data (in the sketch coordinate system) follows the two packed data elements.
knots# The number of knots depends on whether the spline is periodic or not:
Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + 1
Non-Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + Order
packedDouble3, packedDouble4, and packedDouble5 The last three array elements for each spline contain five integer values holding style and layer information:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
i
Color
lineStyle
i+1
lineWidth
Layer
i+2
layerOverride
Not used
where:
i is the index following the last Knot or [2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim]
Color is the COLORREF value describing the color used for the ith spline
lineStyle is the line style used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration
lineWidth is line width used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration
Layer is an integer index to the layer that the ith spline is on
layerOverride is integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden or should be overridden.
Therefore, the size of the data for each spline is given by: 2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim + 3

Parameter.Name: ForceNonPeriodic
Parameter.Description: True to attempt to convert all non-periodic splines to periodic, false to not

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> objects. The return value is an array of doubles containing data for all the splines in the sketch:
[ packedDouble1, packedDouble2, ControlPoint1[Dimension elements], ControlPoint2[Dimension elements],... knot1, knot2,..., packedDouble3, packedDouble4, packedDouble5, ]
packedDouble1 and packedDouble2
The first two array elements for each spline contain four integer values holding information that describes the rest of the data in that spline's parameters:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
0
Dim
Order
1
nCtrlPoints
Periodic
where:
Dim is the number of dimensions in which the spline is defined
Order is the order of the spline
nCtrlPoints is the number of control points
Periodic is 1 for a closed spline or 0 for an open spline ControlPoint# The ControlPoint data (in the sketch coordinate system) follows the two packed data elements.
knots# The number of knots depends on whether the spline is periodic or not:
Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + 1
Non-Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + Order
packedDouble3, packedDouble4, and packedDouble5 The last three array elements for each spline contain five integer values holding style and layer information:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
i
Color
lineStyle
i+1
lineWidth
Layer
i+2
layerOverride
Not used
where:
i is the index following the last Knot or [2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim]
Color is the COLORREF value describing the color used for the ith spline
lineStyle is the line style used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration
lineWidth is line width used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration
Layer is an integer index to the layer that the ith spline is on
layerOverride is integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden or should be overridden.
Therefore, the size of the data for each spline is given by: 2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim + 3

Member.Name: IGetSplines
Member.Description: Gets information for each spline by tessellation instead of by interpolation as is done by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplinesInterpolate">ISketch::GetSplinesInterpolate</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplinesInterpolate">ISketch::IGetSplinesInterpolate</see>.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks: See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchSegments">ISketch::GetSketchSegments</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchSegments">ISketch::IEnumSketchSegments</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSegment">ISketchSegment</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchSpline">ISketchSpline</see> objects. The returned array of doubles has the format: [ [ Color, LineType, NumSplinePoints, [x,y,z] ] ] This complete set of data repeats itself for each spline found in the sketch. For each spline, the array returned contains the color, the line type, the number of spline points in the spline, and the X,Y,Z value for each of those points. Therefore, the [x,y,z] parameter is an array of NumSplinePoints, which may vary in size from spline to spline. The [x,y,z] points for each spline are not the same as the points used to generate the spline. This method tessellates the spline based on the display quality and places points along the spline appropriately. LineType may take one of the values in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>.

Member.Name: IGetSplinesInterpolate
Member.Description: Gets the spline points by interpolation instead of by tessellation as is done by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplines">ISketch::GetSplines</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSplines">ISketch::IGetSplines</see>.
Member.Returns:
in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks)
VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported
Member.Remarks: To determine the size of the array returned, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSplinesInterpolate">ISketch:GetSplineInterpolateCount</see>. The return value is an array of doubles formatted as: [ [NumSplinePoints, [x, y, z] ], ] This complete set of data repeats itself for each spline found in the sketch. For each spline, the array returned contains the number of spline points in the spline, and the X,Y,Z value for each of those points. The [x,y,z] parameter is an array of NumSplinePoints. For example, if your sketch has two splines and each spline has three points, then the data would be in the following format: [ 3, x1_1, y1_1, z1_1, x2_1, y2_1, z2_1, x3_1, y3_1, z3_1, 3, x1_2, y1_2, z1_2, x2_2, y2_2, z2_2, x3_2, y3_2, z3_2 ] The [x,y,z] points for each spline are the same points used to generate the spline.

Member.Description: Gets all of the user points in this sketch.

Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
The return value is an array of doubles with this format: [ Color, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, ptLoc[3] ] where:
Color = COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
Line Font = line style. Valid line styles can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
Line Width = integer value defining the line width. Valid width values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration.
Layer ID = integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
Layer Override = integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
ptLoc[3] = an array of doubles (x, y, z) describing the point location This set of data repeats for each user point in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumPts * 8). To determine the number of points in the sketch, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetUserPointsCount">ISketch::GetUserPointsCount</see>. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.GetSketchPoints2">ISketch::GetSketchPoints2</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IGetSketchPoints2">ISketch::IGetSketchPoints2</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketch.IEnumSketchPoints">ISketch::IEnumSketchPoints</see> for access to individual <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISketchPoint">ISketchPoint</see> objects.

Member.Name: GetRotationDir
Member.Description: Gets the rotation direction of this sketch arc.
Member.Returns: Rotation direction with respect to the normal of the arc's sketch plane (counterclockwise = 1, clockwise = -1) (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method determines the direction that the sketch proceeds around this arc, beginning at the arc's start point and ending at the arc's end point. The direction is with respect to the normal of the arc's sketch plane and not with respect to the viewer.
If the normal to the arc's sketch plane is... And the normal to the arc is... And this method returns... It means that...
(0, 0, -1) (0, 0, 1) 1 (counterclockwise)
With respect to its sketch plane's normal (from behind the screen), the arc travels counterclockwise from its start point to its end point. Note that from the perspective of the viewer (in front of the screen), the arc travels clockwise from its start point to its end point.

Member.Name: GetArcs
Member.Description: Gets information about all of the arcs in the block definition.
Member.Returns: Array containing an array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Return value is an array of doubles with the format: [ Color, Type, Line Font, Line Width, Layer ID, Layer Override, [Start], [End], [Center] Rotation Dir ] where
Color - COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
Type - Line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A LineType is a combination of a line style and line weight.
Line Font - Line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
Line Width - Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
Layer ID - Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerID</see>.
Layer Override - Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
Start[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the start point.
End[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the end point. If the arc is closed, then End[3] is the same point as Start.
Center[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the center point.
Rotation Dir - Rotational direction (CW = -1, CCW = 1) This set of data repeats for each arc in the sketch. The size of the array is (NumArcs * 16).

Member.Name: GetEllipses
Member.Description: Gets the information about all of the ellipses in this block definition.
Member.Returns: Array containing an array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return values are in an array of doubles: [ Color, LineType, LineFont, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, StartPt[3], EndPt[3], CenterPt[3], MajorPt[3], MinorPt[3],Direction ... ] where:
Color :
COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
LineType :
Line type. Valid returns are defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A lineType is a combination of a lineStyle and lineWeight.
LineFont :
Value is used for polyline font information. This value can be used as an input to the GetLineFontInfo2 and GetLineFontName2.
LineWidth :
Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
LayerID:
Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. Obtain the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
LayerOverride:
Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
StartPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse start point
EndPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse end point. If the ellipse is closed, then this will be the same point as the StartPt.
CenterPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the ellipse center point.
MajorPt[3] :
Array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing a point on the ellipse and on the major axis.
MinorPt[3] :

Member.Name: GetSplineParams
Member.Description: Gets all the parameters of the splines in the sketch block definition.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles, containing spline parameters (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
The return value is an array of doubles containing data for all the splines in the sketch block definitioni. The first two array elements for each spline contain 4 integer values holding information that describes the rest of the data in that splines parameters:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
0
Dim
Order
1
nCtrlPoints
Periodic
where:
Dim is the number of dimensions the spline is defined in
Order is the order of the spline
nCtrlPoints is the number of control points
Periodic is 1 for a closed spline or 0 for an open spline The number of knots depends on whether the spline is periodic or not:
Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + 1
Non-Periodic:
numKnots = nCtrlPoints + Order
The last three array elements for each spline contain 5 integer values holding style and layer information:
Spline Element
Packed Data
low part
high part
i
Color
lineStyle
i+1
lineWidth
Layer
i+2
layerOverride
Not used
where:
i is the index following the last Knot or [2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim]
Color is the COLORREF value describing the color used for the ith spline
lineStyle is the line style used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration
lineWidth is line width used for the ith spline. Valid values can be found in the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see> enumeration
Layer is an integer index to the layer that the ith spline is on
layerOverride is integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden or should be overridden. Therefore, the size of the data for each spline is given by: 2 + numKnots + numControlPointDoubles * Dim + 3 The ControlPoint data (in the sketch coordinate system) follows the 2 packed data elements, the Knot points, and, finally, the last 3 packed data elements. Subsequent splines follow one another in the array. [ packedDouble1, packedDouble2, ControlPoint1[Dimension elements], ControlPoint2[Dimension elements],... knot1, knot2,..., packedDouble3, packedDouble4, packedDouble5, ] For information about unpacking double arrays into integer pairs, see:
<see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_Visual_Basic_.NET_and_Visual_Basic.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Paris in Visual Basic.NET and Visual Basic</see> <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/PackedIntegersCPlusPlus.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Pairs in C++</see> <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Unpacking_Double_Arrays_into_Integer_Pairs_in_C_.htm">Unpacking Double Arrays into Integer Pairs in C#</see>
