Member.Name: AccessSelections
Member.Description: Gains access to the selection lists on the PropertyManager page of a Smart Component.

Parameter.Name: ShowPMP
Parameter.Description: True to display the PropertyManager page, false to not (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if the selections where successfully accessed, false if not
Member.Remarks:
ShowPMP only controls the display of the PropertyManager page. This method allows access to the PropertyManager page selection lists regardless of whether the PropertyManager page is displayed. The selection lists have marks as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e">swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e</see>. This method opens the training assembly in which this Smart Component is defined. To delete a feature or component from a Smart Component:
Open the Smart Component in SOLIDWORKS.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> on the "Smart Feature" to get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISmartComponentFeatureData">ISmartComponentFeatureData</see> object.
Call this method to open the training assembly of the Smart Component.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.ActiveDoc">ISldWorks::ActiveDoc</see> to set an assembly document variable.
To get a specific feature or component, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see>(index, mark), where mark is defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e">swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e</see> and index is the position of the item in the selection list.
Select an already selected feature or component to delete it from its selection list. If the object returned by ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6 is a:
feature, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Select2">IFeature::Select2</see> to delete that feature from the feature selection list.
component, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.Select4">IComponent2::Select4</see> to delete that component from the component selection list.
Close the training assembly and release access to the selection lists. To insert a feature or component into a Smart Component:
Open the Smart Component in SOLIDWORKS.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> on the "Smart Feature" to get the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISmartComponentFeatureData">ISmartComponentFeatureData</see> object.
Call this method to open the training assembly of the Smart Component.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.ActiveDoc">ISldWorks::ActiveDoc</see> to point to the training assembly. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to specify the feature or component you want to insert, setting Mark to an option in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e">swSmartComponentSelectionTypes_e</see>. Close the training assembly and release access to the selection lists. To close the training assembly and release access to the selection lists on the PropertyManager page:
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISmartComponentFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">ISmartComponentFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> if you did not insert or delete features and components. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IModifyDefinition2">IFeature::IModifyDefinition2</see> to rebuild the Smart Component if you inserted or deleted features and components.

Member.Name: ReleaseSelectionAccess
Member.Description: Releases access to the selection lists of a Smart Component.
Member.Remarks:
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISmartComponentFeatureData.AccessSelections">ISmartComponentFeatureData::AccessSelections</see> opens the training assembly in which this Smart Component is defined and allows access to the selection lists on the PropertyManager page of the SmartComponent. To close the training assembly:
Call this method if you did not insert or delete features and components. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IModifyDefinition2">IFeature::IModifyDefinition2</see> to rebuild the Smart Component if you inserted or deleted features and components.

Member.Name: GetKnotPoints
Member.Description: Gets the knot vector for the spline.

Parameter.Name: KnotPoints
Parameter.Description: Array of double values between 0 and 1, inclusive (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if successful, false if not
Member.Remarks: Before calling this method, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.KnotPointsCount">ISplineParamData::KnotPointsCount</see> to get the size of the KnotPoints array. Together with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.GetControlPoints">control points</see>, knots determine the shape and smoothness of a spline. The knot vector divides the parametric space into intervals or knot spans. These intervals may be uniform or non-uniform. Each interval governs a different control point.

Member.Name: GetSegments
Member.Description: Gets the coefficients of all of the piecewise polynomials of a spline.

Parameter.Name: Segments
Parameter.Description: Array of doubles (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method works only with P-spline parameterization data. Before calling this method, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICurve.GetPCurveParams2">ICurve::GetPCurveParams2</see> to obtain the P-spline parameterization data object for the curve. Each pair of spline control points defines one segment of a curve. Each segment is typically represented by a cubic polynomial. This method returns a one-dimensional array containing doubles that are the coefficients of all of the piecewise cubic polynomials of the spline. The segment coefficients are stored in the Segments array in order of increasing variable exponent: (constants)(first degree coefficients)(second degree coefficients)(third degree coefficients) etc. For example, if the spline segments are represented by cubic rational (dim=4) polynomials in parametric form, (w0*a0 + w1*a1*t + w2*a2*t**2 + w3*a3*t**3) p(t) = -------------------------------------------- (w0 + w1*t + w2*t**2 + w3*t**3) where w0, w1, w2, w3 are weighting coefficients and a0, a1, a2, a3 are vector coefficients, then the Segments array stores (dimension(4) X order(4)) = 16 coefficients: (a0x,a0y,a0z,w0)(a1x,a1y,a1z,w1)(a2x,a2y,a2z,w2)(a3x,a3y,a3z,w3). If the spline segments are represented by cubic non-rational (dim=3) polynomials, then the Segments array stores (dimension(3) X order(4)) = 12 coefficients:
(a0x,a0y,a0z)(a1x,a1y,a1z)(a2x,a2y,a2z)(a3x,a3y,a3z0). The total number of coefficients returned by this method is: (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.SegmentCount">segment count</see>) x (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.Order">order</see>) x (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.Dimension">dimension</see>)

Member.Name: Layer
Member.Description: Gets the index of the layer in which this spline is drawn.
Member.Returns: Index of layer of spline, -1 if layer not defined

Member.Name: LayerOverride
Member.Description: Gets the spline's properties that override the default properties of the layer.
Member.Returns: Properties that have been overridden or should be overridden as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLayerOverride_e">swLayerOverride_e</see> (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Layers are only supported in drawing documents. Splines can be created on a layer that has specific visual properties. By default, the spline takes on the visual properties defined by the layer. However, for a specific spline, these visual properties can be overridden (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.Color">ISplineParamData::Color</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.LineStyle">ISplineParamData::LineStyle</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.LineWidth">ISplineParamData::LineWidth</see>). This property gets or sets whether the default visual properties of the layer are used by this spline. When the spline is not on any layer, the value this property returns is undefined. You can use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISplineParamData.Layer">ISplineParamData::Layer</see> property to determine the name of the layer, if any, that this spline is on. If an empty string is returned by the ISplineParamData::Layer property, then this property is not used. When you get this property, the returned bit value indicates which property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are:
color = 0x1
style = 0x2
width = 0x4 Therefore, if the value was returned as 3, you know color and style have been specifically set for this item and might not match the default values associated with this item's layer. When you set this property, the input bit value indicates which property or properties should maintain their current override values. Therefore, if the value is passed as 0x4, we know width should keep its current override value, and that color and style should be reset to use the color and style settings for the item's layer. If you pass 0, all visual properties are reset to use the default settings of the item's layer.

Member.Remarks:
If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedHoleFeatureData.UseBaselineDimensions">IAdvancedHoleFeatureData::UseBaselineDimensions</see> is set to false, and:
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedHoleElementData.EndCondition">IAdvancedHoleElementData::EndCondition</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swEndConditions_e">swEndConditions_e</see>.swEndCondBlind, then this property specifies the equation for the depth of the Blind end condition. If this property is set to swStraightTapeHoleEquation_e.swStraightTapHoleEquation_UserDefinedValue, then use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedHoleElementData.BlindDepth">IAdvancedHoleElementData::BlindDepth</see> to set the custom Blind depth of this hole element. IAdvancedHoleElementData::EndCondition is specifically set to anything other than Blind, then this property is not valid. If IAdvancedHoleFeatureData::UseBaselineDimensions is set to true, then:
the end condition automatically becomes swEndConditions_e.swEndCondOffsetFromSurface, - and -
this property specifies the equation for the offset distance. If this property is set to swStraightTapHoleEquation_e.swStraightTapHoleEquation_UserDefinedValue, then use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAdvancedHoleElementData.OffsetDistance">IAdvancedHoleElementData::OffsetDistance</see> to set the custom offset distance of this hole element.

Member.Name: AddTrimmingLoop
Member.Signature: AddTrimmingLoop( System.int NCrvs, System.object VOrder, System.object VDim, System.object VPeriodic, System.object VNumKnots, System.object VNumCtrlPoints, System.object VKnots, System.object VCtrlPointDbls )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.AddTrimmingLoop2">ISurface::AddTrimmingLoop2</see>.

Member.Name: AddTrimmingLoop2
Member.Signature: AddTrimmingLoop2( System.int NCrvs, System.object VOrder, System.object VDim, System.object VPeriodic, System.object VNumKnots, System.object VNumCtrlPoints, System.object VKnots, System.object VCtrlPointDbls, System.object UvRange )
Member.Description: Creates a trimming loop out of specified surface parametric UV-curves and adds it to a list of such loops.

Parameter.Name: NCrvs
Parameter.Description: Number of surface parametric (UV) curves constituting the loop and the size of each of the VOrder, VDim, VPeriodic, VNumKnots, VNumControlPnts arrays

Parameter.Name: VOrder
Parameter.Description: Array containing NCrvs longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++) representing orders of the curves (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VDim
Parameter.Description: Array containing NCrvs longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++) representing dimensions (2, 3, or 4) of the control points of the curves (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VPeriodic
Parameter.Description: Array containing NCrvs longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++) representing whether the curve is periodic (1) or non-periodic (0) (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VNumKnots
Parameter.Description: Array containing NCrvs longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++) representing number of knots on the curves (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VNumCtrlPoints
Parameter.Description: Array containing NCrvs longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++) representing number of control points on the curves (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VKnots
Parameter.Description: Knot vector array of doubles, where TotalNumKnots = (TotalNumKnots + VNumKnots[i]) for i = 1 to NCrvs (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: VCtrlPointDbls
Parameter.Description: Control point coordinate array of doubles, where TotalNumCPCoords = (TotalNumCPCoords + (VDim[i] * VNumCtrlPoints[i])) for i = 1 to NCrvs (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: UvRange
Parameter.Description: Array of four doubles representing U Low, U High, V Low, and V High (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: True if successful in adding a trimming loop to the surface, false if not
Member.Remarks:
The list of trimming loops is created by a previous call to one of the base surface creation functions, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateRevolutionSurface">IBody2::CreateRevolutionSurface</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreatePlanarSurface">IBody2::CreatePlanarSurface.</see> The information on each UV-curve is in b-spline form (knots and control point coordinates) and is compacted into two arrays, VKnots and VCtrlPointDbls. Order of each curve in VOrder is, at a minimum, 2. A second order curve is a linear curve. For each curve in VNumCtrlPoints, VOrder, and VNumKnots, (NumCtrlPoints >= Order) and (NumKnots = NumCtrlPoints + Order). Dim for each curve in VDim specifies the dimension of each CtrlPointDbl set in VCtrlPointDbls. This method expects 2D-polynomial (X,Y) or 2D-rational (X,Y,Weight) curves to be passed as trimming curves. However, you can set a flag so that this method accepts 3D-polynomial (X,Y,Z) or 3D-rational (X,Y,Z,Weight) trim curves. To do this, negate the absolute value of the first value in the VDim array. For example, if the first VDim value is 3, set it to -3. When you do this, 3D trim curves are expected. If Dim is:
2, specify (X,Y) control points in each CtrlPointDbl set. -2, specify (X,Y,Z) control points in each CtrlPointDbl set. 3, specify (X,Y,Weight) control points in each CtrlPointDbl. -3, specify (X,Y,Z,Weight) control points in each CtrlPointDbl. Multiplicity of a knot is the number of times it is repeated in the knot vector. There are specific rules around number of knots, knot multiplicity, and curve order. For example, if a curve's Periodic value is:
0 (non-periodic), there must be (NumCtrlPoints + Order) knots and the maximum multiplicity of any knot is Order. 1 (periodic), there must be (NumCtrlPoints + 1) knots and the maximum multiplicity of any knot is Order. If a knot has multiplicity greater than 1, repetitions must occur at the end of the knot vector. If you do not want to specify a UV range, use null or Nothing in the UvRange array elements. After calling this method to add a trimming loop, you can generate the trimmed surface by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateTrimmedSurface">IBody2::CreateTrimmedSurface</see>. You can create a body from trimmed surfaces using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateBodyFromSurfaces">IBody2::CreateBodyFromSurfaces</see>. NOTE: It is highly recommended that you consult other resources for the mathematics behind b-splines, knots, knot multiplicity, and control points before attempting to use this method.

Member.Name: Evaluate
Member.Signature: Evaluate( System.double UParam, System.double VParam, System.int NumUDeriv, System.int NumVDeriv )
Member.Description: Evaluates the surface, given the u and v parameters of the surface.

Parameter.Name: UParam
Parameter.Description: Value of u parameter

Parameter.Name: VParam
Parameter.Description: Value of v parameter

Parameter.Name: NumUDeriv
Parameter.Description: Number of u derivatives required

Parameter.Name: NumVDeriv
Parameter.Description: Number of v derivatives required

Member.Returns:
This method returns the evaluated point, normal, and derivatives with respect to u and v up to order NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs, respectively. If NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs are 0, then no derivatives are returned. For more information on the valid u and v parameters of the surface, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Parameterization">ISurface::Parameterization</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IParameterization">ISurface::IParameterization</see>. Also, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.FaceInSurfaceSense">IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense</see> to check to see if the normal of the face is in the same direction or in the opposite direction of the surface normal. The evaluation returns the following array of (3 *((( NumUDerivs +1) * (NumVDerivs + 1)) + 1 )) doubles: [ evaluatedPoint[3], evaluatedDerivatives[xx], evaluatedNormal[3] ] where: evaluatedPoint[3] = point representing the evaluated X,Y,Z point in meters evaluatedDerivatives[xx] = array of vectors representing the derivatives where the nth derivative wrt u (i NumUDerivs) and the nth derivative wrt v (j NumVDerivs) would be vector number ( i + (NumUDerivs + 1) * j ) - 1 in the evaluatedDerivatives array. If NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs are 0, then no derivatives are returned. evaluatedNormal[3] = a vector representing the evaluated normal The following table describes the number of derivatives that can be requested based on the surface type. If you request more derivatives than allowed, then this method returns all data as zeros. To determine the surface type, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Identity">ISurface::Identity</see>.
U Derivatives
0
1
2
0
a
a
b
V Derivatives
1
a
a
c
2
b
c
d
where:
a - All surface types
b - All surface types except blend surfaces
c - All surface types except blend surfaces and offset surfaces
d - All surface types except blend surfaces but offset surfaces will only return 0th, 1st, and 2nd derivatives (the uncalculated 3rd and 4th derivatives are returned as 0 vectors). For example, if you specified 2 derivatives in both u and v, then an array containing 10 vectors is returned. The returned data is in model space coordinates. [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du P(u,v)/dudu] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv P(u,v)/dududv] [P(u,v)/dvdv P(u,v)/dudvdv P(u,v)/dududvdv] [N(u,v)] where:
du the partial derivative in the u direction
dv the partial derivative in the v direction
N(u,v) the normal vector
Each P() represents a model space point or vector depending on the entry in the array If you request 2 derivatives for u and 1 for v, then an array containing 7 vectors is returned: [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du P(u,v)/dudu] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv P(u,v)/dududv] [N(u,v)] If u = 1 and v = 2, then: [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv] [P(u,v)/dvdv P(u,v)/dudvdv] [N(u,v)]

Member.Remarks: This method calculates the normal, the principal directions, and the principal curvatures, of the surface at the specified point. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.FaceInSurfaceSense">IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense</see> to check the directions of the face normal and surface normal. IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense returns true when the face normal and surface normal point in opposite directions, and false when they point in the same direction. The return value is the following array of eleven doubles: [surfNorm[i, j, k], principalDir1[i, j, k], principalDir2[I, j, k], principalCurvature1, principalCurvature2 ] where: surfNorm[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the surface normal principalDir1[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the first principal direction principalDir2[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the second principal direction principalCurvature1 = first principal curvature principalCurvature2 = second principal curvature Principal Curvature 1 is the minimum normal curvature at the point (largest radius). Principal Curvature 2 is the maximum normal curvature at the point. The tangent direction producing Principal Curvature 1 is called the first principal direction, and the tangent direction producing Principal Curvature 2 is called the second principal direction. It is a property of differentiable surfaces that principalDir1 and principalDir2 are orthogonal. A positive curvature by convention implies a centre of curvature on the side pointed away from by the surface normal (convex). See "Faux and Pratt Computational Geometry for Design and Manufacture" for more information.

Member.Name: GetBSurfParams2
Member.Signature: GetBSurfParams2( System.bool WantCubic, System.bool WantNonRational, System.object VP0, System.double Tolerance, out System.bool Sense )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.GetBSurfParams3">ISurface::GetBSurfParams3</see>.

Parameter.Name: WantCubic
Parameter.Description: True if cubic is needed, false if not; specifying true converts any surface type to a cubic Bsurface

Parameter.Name: WantNonRational
Parameter.Description: True if non-rational is needed, false if not; specifying true converts any surface type to a non-rational Bsurface; if you specify true, then you should only use this method for surfaces that are Bsurface or blend surface; otherwise, the underlying call is not made and the values returned from this are not initialized or contain the values from the last call

Parameter.Name: VP0
Parameter.Description: Array of values describing the UV range of the surface to be output; you can obtain these values by using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Parameterization">ISurface::Parameterization</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IParameterization">ISurface::IParameterization</see>

Parameter.Name: Tolerance
Parameter.Description: Tolerance, in meters, between the approximated b-spline surface and the underlying surface; the default value is 0.01 and should generally be reduced to the tolerance desired

Parameter.Name: Sense
Parameter.Description: Approximated b-spline surface is not always in the same direction as the original surface; if sense is true, then the underlying surface and the b-spline surface are in the same direction

Member.Returns: Array of values giving the b-spline surface parameters
Member.Remarks:
The VP0 parameter contains the following values, which you can obtain by using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Parameterization">ISurface::Parameterization</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IParameterization">ISurface::IParameterization</see>:
vP0[0] & vP0[2] are the lower bounds of the U & V surface parameters, respectively
vP0[1] & vP0[3] are the upper bounds of the U & V surface parameters, respectively If you want to use the Bsurface in combination with its trim curves, you should use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.GetTrimCurves2">IFace2::GetTrimCurves2</see> method to extract the trim curves and the Bsurface. The IFace2::GetTrimCurves2 method provides much better alignment of the trim curves with the Bsurface because they are both generated at the same time. Evaluation is as follows: Number of returned double elements is (4 + NumUKnots + NumVKnots + NumControlPointDoubles), where NumUKnots = (NumColumnsControlPoints + Uorder) and NumVKnots = (NumRowsControlPoints + Vorder). The returned data are arranged in this order:
Uorder, Vorder - These are two ints packed into a double
Uorder - Order of surface in U direction
Vorder - Order of surface in V direction
NumColumnsControlPoints, NumRowsControlPoints - These are two integers packed into a double
NumColumnsControlPoints - Number of columns for the control points
NumRowsControlPoints - Number of rows for the control points
Uperiodicity, Vperiodicity - These are two integers packed into a double. Since you may be generating a Bsurface with this function, the U,V periodicity values may be opposite from the original surface. Refer to ISurface::Parameterization or ISurface::IParameterization.
Uperiodicity - True if surface is periodic in U direction
Vperiodicity - True if surface is periodic in V direction
DimensionControlPoints, dummy - These are two integers packed into a double
DimensionControlPoints - Dimension for control points.
DimensionControlPoints = 3 for non-rational surfaces and control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........].
DimensionControlPoints = 4 for rational surfaces and control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........].
dummy - a system-used filler.
UKnots - Knot vector in the u direction. There will be (NumColumnsControlPoints + Uorder) knot values. If the surface is periodic in the U direction, then data is converted and returned in a non-periodic form with additional knots added to the surface ends.
VKnots - Knot vector in the v direction. There will be (NumRowsControlPoints + Vorder) knot values. If the surface is periodic in the V direction, then data is converted and returned in a non-periodic form with additional knots added to the surface ends.
ControlPoints - This is a list of control points output in (NumColumnsControlPoints*NumRowsControlPoints) vectors of dimension DimensionControlPoints. The vectors are output row by row. The U direction of surface is in the row direction. The V direction of surface is in the column direction.
For non-rational surfaces, control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........].
For rational surfaces, control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........].
For example:
Row1, Column1 Row1, Column2
x0, y0, z0 x1, y1, z1 = 6
Row2, Column1 Row2, Column2
x2, y2, z2 x3, y3, z3 = 6
Row3, Column1 Row3, Column2
x4, y4, z4 x5, y5, z5 = 6
= 18

A surface of revolution is constructed by revolving a profile curve (line or arc or b-spline) about an axis. The profile curve for the surface of revolution can be retrieved with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.GetProfileCurve">ISurface::GetProfileCurve</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IGetProfileCurve">ISurface::IGetProfileCurve</see>. Eight doubles of parameters returned.
Point [3] - X, Y, Z coordinates of the start point of the axis of rotation.
AxisDir[3] - Vector showing the direction of the axis of rotation.
Params[2] - Parameter range of the part of the profile curve that was used to create the surface.

Member.Name: IAddTrimmingLoop
Member.Signature: IAddTrimmingLoop( System.int CurveCount, ref System.int Order, ref System.int Dim, ref System.int Periodic, ref System.int NumKnots, ref System.int NumCtrlPoints, ref System.double Knots, ref System.double CtrlPointDbls )
Member.Description: Obsolete. Superseded by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IAddTrimmingLoop2">ISurface::IAddTrimmingLoop2</see>.

Member.Name: IAddTrimmingLoop2
Member.Signature: IAddTrimmingLoop2( System.int CurveCount, ref System.int Order, ref System.int Dim, ref System.int Periodic, ref System.int NumKnots, ref System.int NumCtrlPoints, ref System.double Knots, ref System.double CtrlPointDbls, ref System.double UvRange )
Member.Description: Creates a trimming loop out of specified surface parametric (UV-curves) and adds it to a list of such loops.

Parameter.Name: CurveCount
Parameter.Description: Number of surface parametric (UV) curves constituting the loop; the size of Order, Dim, Periodic, NumKnots, and NumControlPnts arrays

Parameter.Name: Order
Parameter.Description: Orders of the curves; array of CurveCount longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++)

Parameter.Name: Dim
Parameter.Description: Dimensions of the curves' control points; array of CurveCount longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++); if you set the first value in this array to negative of its absolute value, then 3D trim curves are expected

Parameter.Name: Periodic
Parameter.Description: 0 for non-periodic or 1 for periodic; array of CurveCount longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++)

Parameter.Name: NumKnots
Parameter.Description: Number of knots in the curves; array of CurveCount longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++)

Parameter.Name: NumCtrlPoints
Parameter.Description: Number of control points in the curves; array of CurveCount longs (VBA), Integers (VB.NET), or ints (C#, C++)

Parameter.Name: Knots
Parameter.Description: Knot vectors of the curves; array of doubles, where TotalNumKnots = (TotalNumKnots + NumKnots[i]) for i = 1 to CurveCount

Parameter.Name: CtrlPointDbls
Parameter.Description: Control point coordinates of the curves; array of doubles, where TotalNumCPCoords = (TotalNumCPCoords + (Dim[i] * NumCtrlPoints[i])) for i = 1 to CurveCount

Parameter.Name: UvRange
Parameter.Description: Array of four doubles defining U Low U High V Low V High

Member.Remarks:
The list of trimming loops is created by a previous call to one of the base surface creation functions, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateRevolutionSurface">IBody2::CreateRevolutionSurface</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreatePlanarSurface">IBody2::CreatePlanarSurface.</see> The information on each UV-curve is in b-spline form (knots and control point coordinates) and is compacted into two arrays, VKnots and VCtrlPointDbls. Order of each curve in Order is, at a minimum, 2. A second order curve is a linear curve. For each curve in NumCtrlPoints, Order, and NumKnots, (NumCtrlPoints >= Order) and (NumKnots = NumCtrlPoints + Order). Dim for each curve in Dim specifies the dimension of each CtrlPointDbl set in CtrlPointDbls. This method expects 2D-polynomial (X,Y) or 2D-rational (X,Y,Weight) curves to be passed as trimming curves. However, you can set a flag so that this method accepts 3D-polynomial (X,Y,Z) or 3D-rational (X,Y,Z,Weight) trim curves. To do this, negate the absolute value of the first value in the VDim array. For example, if the first VDim value is 3, set it to -3. When you do this, 3D trim curves are expected. If Dim is:
2, specify (X,Y) control points in each CtrlPointDbl sub-array. -2, specify (X,Y,Z) control points in each CtrlPointDbl sub-array. 3, specify (X,Y,Weight) control points in each CtrlPointDbl sub-array. -3, specify (X,Y,Z,Weight) control points in each CtrlPointDbl sub-array. Multiplicity of a knot is the number of times it is repeated in the knot vector. There are specific rules around number of knots, knot multiplicity, and curve order. For example, if a curve's Periodic value is:
0 (non-periodic), there must be (NumCtrlPoints + Order) knots and the maximum multiplicity of any knot is Order. 1 (periodic), there must be (NumCtrlPoints + 1) knots and the maximum multiplicity of any knot is Order. If a knot has multiplicity greater than 1, repetitions must occur at the end of the knot vector. If you do not want to specify a UV range, use null or Nothing in the UvRange array elements. After calling this method to add a trimming loop, you can generate a trimmed surface by calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateTrimmedSurface">IBody2::CreateTrimmedSurface</see>. You can create a body from trimmed surfaces using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IBody2.CreateBodyFromSurfaces">IBody2::CreateBodyFromSurfaces</see>. NOTE: It is highly recommended that you consult other resources for the mathematics behind b-splines, knots, knot multiplicity, and control points before attempting to use this method.

Member.Name: IEvaluate
Member.Signature: IEvaluate( System.double UParam, System.double VParam, System.int NumUDeriv, System.int NumVDeriv )
Member.Description: Evaluates the surface, given the u and v parameters of the surface.

Parameter.Name: UParam
Parameter.Description: Value of u parameter

Parameter.Name: VParam
Parameter.Description: Value of v parameter

Parameter.Name: NumUDeriv
Parameter.Description: Number of u derivatives required

Parameter.Name: NumVDeriv
Parameter.Description: Number of v derivatives required

Member.Remarks:
This method returns the evaluated point, normal, and derivatives with respect to u and v up to order NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs, respectively. If NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs are 0, then no derivatives are returned. For more information on the valid u and v parameters of the surface, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Parameterization">ISurface::Parameterization</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IParameterization">ISurface::IParameterization</see>. Also, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.FaceInSurfaceSense">IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense</see> to check to see if the normal of the face is in the same direction or in the opposite direction of the surface normal. The evaluation returns the following array of (3 *((( NumUDerivs +1) * (NumVDerivs + 1)) + 1 )) doubles: [ evaluatedPoint[3], evaluatedDerivatives[xx], evaluatedNormal[3] ] where: evaluatedPoint[3] = point representing the evaluated X,Y,Z point in meters evaluatedDerivatives[xx] = array of vectors representing the derivatives where the nth derivative wrt u (i NumUDerivs) and the nth derivative wrt v (j NumVDerivs) would be vector number ( i + (NumUDerivs + 1) * j ) - 1 in the evaluatedDerivatives array. If NumUDerivs and NumVDerivs are 0, then no derivatives are returned. evaluatedNormal[3] = a vector representing the evaluated normal The following table describes the number of derivatives that can be requested based on the surface type. If you request more derivatives than allowed, then this method returns all data as zeros. To determine the surface type, see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Identity">ISurface::Identity</see>.
U Derivatives
0
1
2
0
a
a
b
V Derivatives
1
a
a
c
2
b
c
d
where:
a - All surface types
b - All surface types except blend surfaces
c - All surface types except blend surfaces and offset surfaces
d - All surface types except blend surfaces but offset surfaces will only return 0th, 1st, and 2nd derivatives (the uncalculated 3rd and 4th derivatives are returned as 0 vectors). For example, if you specified 2 derivatives in both u and v, then an array containing 10 vectors is returned. The returned data is in model space coordinates. [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du P(u,v)/dudu] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv P(u,v)/dududv] [P(u,v)/dvdv P(u,v)/dudvdv P(u,v)/dududvdv] [N(u,v)] where:
du the partial derivative in the u direction
dv the partial derivative in the v direction
N(u,v) the normal vector
Each P() represents a model space point or vector depending on the entry in the array If you request 2 derivatives for u and 1 for v, then an array containing 7 vectors is returned: [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du P(u,v)/dudu] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv P(u,v)/dududv] [N(u,v)] If u = 1 and v = 2, then: [P(u,v) P(u,v)/du] [P(u,v)/dv P(u,v)/dudv] [P(u,v)/dvdv P(u,v)/dudvdv] [N(u,v)]

Member.Name: IEvaluateAtPoint
Member.Signature: IEvaluateAtPoint( System.double PositionX, System.double PositionY, System.double PositionZ )
Member.Description: Evaluates a surface at the specified XYZ point.

Parameter.Name: PositionX
Parameter.Description: X position

Parameter.Name: PositionY
Parameter.Description: Y position

Parameter.Name: PositionZ
Parameter.Description: Z position

Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: This method calculates the normal, the principal directions, and the principal curvatures, of the surface at the specified point. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.FaceInSurfaceSense">IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense</see> to check the directions of the face normal and surface normal. IFace2::FaceInSurfaceSense returns true when the face normal and surface normal point in opposite directions, and false when they point in the same direction. The return value is the following array of eleven doubles: [surfNorm[i, j, k], principalDir1[i, j, k], principalDir2[I, j, k], principalCurvature1, principalCurvature2 ] where: surfNorm[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the surface normal principalDir1[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the first principal direction principalDir2[i, j, k] = normalized vector describing the second principal direction principalCurvature1 = first principal curvature principalCurvature2 = second principal curvature Principal Curvature 1 is the minimum normal curvature at the point (largest radius). Principal Curvature 2 is the maximum normal curvature at the point. The tangent direction producing Principal Curvature 1 is called the first principal direction, and the tangent direction producing Principal Curvature 1 is called the second principal direction. It is a property of differentiable surfaces that principalDir1 and principalDir2 are orthogonal. A positive curvature by convention implies a centre of curvature on the side pointed away from by the surface normal (convex). See "Faux and Pratt Computational Geometry for Design and Manufacture" for more information.

Member.Name: IGetBSurfParams
Member.Description: Gets the b-spline surface parameters for the surface.
Member.Returns: in-process, unmanaged C++: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks) VBA, VB.NET, C#, and C++/CLI: Not supported See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/In-process_Methods.htm">In-process Methods</see> for details about this type of method.
Member.Remarks:
For COM applications, the following values must be set up in a previous call to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IGetBSurfParamsSize3">ISurface::IGetBSurfParamsSize3</see>:
vP0 [0] & vP0 [2] are the lower bounds of the U & V surface parameters, respectively. vP0 [1] & vP0 [3] are the upper bounds of the U & V surface parameters, respectively. If you want to use the Bsurface in combination with its trim curves, you should use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.GetTrimCurves2">IFace2::GetTrimCurves2</see> method to extract the trim curves and the Bsurface. The IFace2::GetTrimCurves method provides better alignment of the trim curves with the Bsurface because they are both generated at the same time. Evaluation is as follows: Number of returned double elements is (4 + NumUKnots + NumVKnots + NumControlPointDoubles), where NumUKnots = (NumColumnsControlPoints + Uorder) and NumVKnots = (NumRowsControlPoints + Vorder). The returned data are arranged in the following order:
Uorder, Vorder - These are two ints packed into a double
Uorder - Order of surface in U direction.
Vorder - Order of surface in V direction.
NumColumnsControlPoints, NumRowsControlPoints - These are two ints packed into a double
NumColumnsControlPoints - Number of columns for the control points.
NumRowsControlPoints - Number of rows for the control points.
Uperiodicity, Vperiodicity - These are two ints packed into a double. Because you may be generating a Bsurface with this function, the U,V periodicity values may be opposite from the original surface. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.Parameterization">ISurface::Parameterization</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IParameterization">ISurface::IParameterization</see>.
Uperiodicity - TRUE if surface is periodic in U direction.
Vperiodicity - TRUE if surface is periodic in V direction.
DimensionControlPoints, dummy - These are two ints packed into a double
DimensionControlPoints - Dimension for control points.
DimensionControlPoints = 3 for non-rational surfaces and control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........].
DimensionControlPoints = 4 for rational surfaces and control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........].
dummy - a system used filler.
UKnots - Knot vector in the u direction There will be (NumColumnsControlPoints + Uorder) knot values. If the surface is periodic in the U direction, then data will be converted and returned in a non-periodic form with additional knots added to the surface ends.
VKnots - Knot vector in the v direction. There will be (NumRowsControlPoints + Vorder) knot values. If the surface is periodic in the V direction, then data will be converted and returned in a non-periodic form with additional knots added to the surface ends.
ControlPoints - This is a list of control points output in (NumColumnsControlPoints*NumRowsControlPoints) vectors of dimension DimensionControlPoints. The vectors are output row by row. The U direction of surface is in the row direction. The V direction of surface is in the column direction.
For non-rational surfaces, control point coordinates are output as [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,.........].
For rational surfaces, control point coordinates and the weight are output as [x0,y0,z0,w0,x1,y1,z1,w1,........].

Member.Name: IParameterization
Member.Description: Gets the parameterization of the surface.
Member.Returns: Pointer to an array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: The return value is the following array of 11 doubles: [ uRange[2], vRange[2], uBoundType, vBoundType, uProps[2], vProps[2], numProps ] where: uRange[2] = array of two doubles describing the low and high range, respectively, for U. vRange[2] = array of two doubles describing the low and high range, respectively, for V. uBoundType = two integers packed into a double. Each integer describes the behavior at the start and at the end of the U range. Valid values and their meanings are: 13733 - Infinite 13734 - Extendable 13735 - Not Extendable 13701 - Periodic 13736 - Periodic, but not continuously differentiable across the boundary 13741 - Degenerate If the behavior at the start of the U range is Degenerate', then the V parameter is degenerate when U = urange[0]'. The derivative of the parameterization function with respect to v is 0whenever u = urange[0]', for all values of v, and the parameter curve corresponding to u = urange[0]' degenerates to a single point. A parameterization can only degenerate at the end of its range, unless the surface is a type of Bsurface. vBoundType = two integers packed into a double. Each integer describes the behavior at the start and end of the V range. For valid values and their meanings, see description of uBoundType. uProps[2] = four integers packed into two doubles representing U parameterization properties. The uProps array of two doubles will contain a total of one or more integer values with a maximum of four. Valid values and their meanings are: 13701 - Periodic parameterization. 13737 - All derivatives continuous. 13738 - All derivatives non necessarily continuous. 13739 - Linear. Corresponding parameter is proportional to the distance along a straight line. Straight line corresponds to a constant value of the other parameter. 13740 - Circular. Corresponding parameter represents an angle around a circle. Circle corresponds to a constant value of the other parameter. 13746 - Bounds at the ends of the parameter range are coincident. vProps[2] = four integers packed into two doubles representing V parameterization properties. The vProps array of two doubles will contain a total of one or more integer values with a maximum of four. For valid values and their meanings, see description of uProps. numProps = two integers packed into a double. Each integer represents the number of properties returned in uProps and vProps, respectively. If a surface is periodic in one direction (that is, cylinder, cone, torus (apple and lemon shapes), spheres), then U is the periodic direction. The -10000 to 10000 parameter range is the modeling limit for the modeler. This means that the values are effectively infinite in size. To get the parameter range from a given face, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.GetBox">IFace2::GetBox</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2.IGetBox">IFace2::IGetBox</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.GetClosestPointOn">ISurface::GetClosestPointOn</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IGetClosestPointOn">ISurface::IGetClosestPointOn</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.ReverseEvaluate">ISurface::ReverseEvaluate</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurface.IReverseEvaluate">ISurface::IReverseEvaluate</see>. These methods provide a true parameter range that the face is using on the surface.

Member.Name: ITorusParams
Member.Description: Gets the parameters of a toroidal surface.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles describing the parameters of a toroidal surface
Member.Remarks:
Returns an array of 8 double values: center.x center.y center.z axis.x axis.y axis.z major radius - the distance between the center of torus and the center of revolved circle minor radius - the radius of the revolved circle
NOTES:
The real major radius (the outer radius) of the torus is major radius + minor radius.
The center, major radius, and minor radius are in meters.
Possible values that indicate a type of self-intersecting torus:
Apple - when the major radius is positive and less than or equal to the minor radius.
Lemon - when the major radius is negative and the sum of the radii is positive.

Member.Returns: Array of the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see> to control the shape and length of the flattened surface

Member.Name: KeepInternalControlCurves
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to keep internal control curves for this surface-flatten feature.
Member.Returns: True to keep internal control curves, false to not

Member.Name: MapEdges
Member.Description: Gets or sets the map edges for this surface-flatten feature.
Member.Returns: Array of entities that lie on the selected faces or surfaces to flatten (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Map edges:
are entities to map to the flattened surface. By default, any entity that lies on top of a face or surface to flatten is ignored unless the user selects the entity as a map edge. are useful when users want to see where a selected entity on the original body would lie on a flattened surface. For example, users might select edges as map lines to serve as bend lines in the flattened surface. can be any of these types of selected entities:
edges, reference curves, 2D/3D splines, sketches, and sketch text. The SOLIDWORKS API returns <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see> for the entities selected for the map edges in a surface-flatten feature.

Member.Name: ReleaseSelectionAccess
Member.Description: Releases access to the selections for this surface-flatten feature.
Member.Remarks: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISurfaceFlattenFeatureData.AccessSelections">ISurfaceFlattenFeatureData::AccessSelections</see> puts the model in a rollback state to allow access to the selections that define the feature. Use this method to restore the rollback state if you did not modify the feature, or use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> if you did modify the feature.

Member.Name: ShouldMakeTears
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to enable relief cuts for this surface-flatten feature.
Member.Returns: True to enable relief cuts, false to not
Member.Remarks: <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISurfaceFlattenFeatureData.TearEdges">Tear edges</see> identify where to make the relief cuts before flattening the face or surface.

Member.Name: TearEdges
Member.Description: Gets or sets the tear edges for the relief cuts for this surface-flatten feature.
Member.Returns: Array of entities that lie on the selected faces or surfaces to flatten (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Tear edges:
indicate where to make relief cuts before flattening the surface. During flattening, regions of the flattened surface are stretched while other regions are compressed. Adding tear edges through regions of high stress can reduce these deformations, which increases the accuracy of the flattened surface. allow users to flatten closed surfaces, such as spheres or entire solid bodies, that would otherwise not be flattened. See the Example section. can be any of these types of selected entities:
edges, reference curves, and 2D/3D splines. must each intersect the face or surface being flattened while touching one boundary edge, which is an edge adjacent to exactly one face or surface. are only applied when <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISurfaceFlattenFeatureData.ShouldMakeTears">ISurfaceFlattenFeatureData::ShouldMakeTears</see> is true. The SOLIDWORKS API returns <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edges</see> for the entities selected for the tear edges in a surface-flatten feature.

Member.Name: UseTryToFormSolid
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to try to form a solid body when creating the Surface-Knit feature.
Member.Returns: True to true to form a solid body, false to not
Member.Remarks: If <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurfaceKnitFeatureData.UseGapFilters">ISurfaceKnitFeatureData::UseGapFilters</see> is true, then this property is automatically enabled or disabled depending on whether a solid body can be created from the input bodies. If you set this property to true, then <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISurfaceKnitFeatureData.KnitTolerance">knit tolerance</see> is automatically updated so that the Surface-Knit feature can be created as a solid body. Member.Name: AssemblyFeatureScope
Member.Description: Gets and sets whether this swept-cut feature affects only selected components in the assembly.
Member.Returns: True if the swept-cutfeature affects only selected components in the assembly, false if affects all components in the assembly (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Use this property, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISweepFeatureData.AutoSelectComponents">ISweepFeatureData::AutoSelectComponents</see>, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweepFeatureData.PropagateFeatureToParts">ISweepFeatureData::PropagateFeatureToParts</see> to insert sweep cuts into an assembly. This API works with ISweepFeatureData::AutoSelectComponents to configure the scope of an assembly sweep feature. This API performs the same configuration that is done in the Feature Scope section of the PropertyManager page of the sweep feature:
AssemblyFeatureScope setting AutoSelectComponents setting PropertyManager page Feature Scope setting
False Ignored
All components selected Auto-select not visible
True
If true, affected components are automatically selected If false, manually select the affected components before calling this API
Selected components selected If Auto-select is not checked, then manually select components
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details.

Member.Name: MaintainTangency
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to merge tangent faces in this sweep feature.
Member.Returns: True to merge tangent faces, false to not (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: If the sweep profile has tangent segments, true causes the corresponding surfaces in the resulting sweep to be tangent. Faces that can be represented as a plane, cylinder, or cone are maintained. Other adjacent faces are merged, and the profiles are approximated. Sketch arcs may be converted to splines. Parameter.Name: Angle
Parameter.Description: Angle of twist in radians in Direction 2

Member.Remarks:

<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweepFeatureData.TwistControlType">ISweepFeatureData::TwistControlType</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swTwistControlType_e">swTwistControlType_e</see>.swTwistControlConstantTwistAlongPath. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweepFeatureData.Direction">ISweepFeatureData::Direction</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swSweepDirection_e">swSweepDirection_e</see>.swSweepBidirectional. In the Sweep PropertyManager, you can specify revolutions, degrees, or radians. To specify Angle, you must convert revolutions and degrees to radians:
1 revolution = 360 degrees = 2*pi = 6.28319 radians See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details.

Parameter.Description: Angle of twist in radians

Member.Returns: Flange position as defined by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swFlangePositionTypes_e">swSweptFlangePostionTypes_e</see>

Member.Name: FlattenAlongPath
Member.Description: Gets or sets whether to flatten the flange profile along the sweep path of this swept flange feature.
Member.Returns: True to flatten the profile along the sweep path, false to not
Member.Remarks:
This property is valid only when not creating the swept flange on an existing sheet metal feature. If this property is true, then you can also specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweptFlangeFeatureData.MaterialInside">ISweptFlangeFeatureData::MaterialInside</see>. If this property is:
True, then when the model is flattened the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweptFlangeFeatureData.Profile">profile</see> flattens and is rotated parallel to the plane of the path. The <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISweptFlangeFeatureData.Path">path</see> is not flattened, and the result is a the shape of the path. False, then when the model is flattened the profile flattens and is rotated perpendicular to the plane of the path. The path is flattened, and the result is a rectangular shape.

Member.Name: GetCellRange
Member.Signature: GetCellRange( out System.int FirstRow, out System.int LastRow, out System.int FirstColumn, out System.int LastColumn )
Member.Description: Gets the selected table cells' row and column index ranges.

Parameter.Name: FirstRow
Parameter.Description: Index of row of first selected cell

Parameter.Name: LastRow
Parameter.Description: Index of row of last selected cell

Parameter.Name: FirstColumn
Parameter.Description: Index of column of first selected cell

Parameter.Name: LastColumn
Parameter.Description: Index of column of last selected cell

Member.Remarks:
The returned indexes are all 0-based. If you don't multi-select table cells before you call this method, then the cell row/column index range for the entire table is returned. Before calling this method, you can select the table cells in the graphics area whose row/column index range you want to get. How you make these selections determines what this method returns.
Selection Steps Cell range returned
Table cell
Place the cursor on the desired table cell. Click the left-mouse button. Selected cell
Hold down the Ctrl key and place the cursor on the desired table cell. Click the left-mouse button. Selected cell
Multiple table cells
Place the cursor on a desired table cell. Click and hold down the left-mouse button. Drag the cursor over the other desired table cells. Release the left-mouse button when the cursor is on the last table cell that you want selected. All selected cells
Hold down the Ctrl key and place the cursor on a desired table cell. Click the left-mouse button. Repeat steps 1 and 2 until all desired table cells are selected. Each selected cell
Table column Place the cursor just above the desired column and click the left-mouse button when the cursor changes to a solid arrow All selected cells
Table row Place the cursor to just left of the desired row and click the left-mouse button when the cursor changes to a solid arrow All selected cells Run any of the examples in the Example section to better understand the values returned by this method.

Member.Name: SetColumnWidth
Member.Signature: SetColumnWidth( System.int Index, System.double Width, System.int Options )
Member.Description: Sets the width of the specified column in this table.

Parameter.Name: Index
Parameter.Description: Index of column for which to set the width

Parameter.Name: Width
Parameter.Description: Width at which to set specified column, in system units

Parameter.Name: Options
Parameter.Description: Table's behavior after changing column width as defined by <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTableRowColSizeChangeBehavior_e">swTableRowColSizeChangeBehavior_e</see> (see Remarks)

Member.Returns: Width at which specified column is set (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Index is the column number for which to set the width. Thus, the first column is column 0. It can also be a value from the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTableCellRangeIdentifier_e">swTableCellRangeIdentifier_e</see> enumerator.
If Index equals...
Then the width of all of the columns...
swTableCellRange_All
Is set, if possible.
swTableCellRange_Current
In the current range (see <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.GetCellRange">ITableAnnotation::GetCellRange</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.SetCellRange">ITableAnnotation::SetCellRange</see>) is set, if possible.
When the width of a column changes, the rest of the table is affected. The Options argument indicates how the rest of the table should behave.
If...
Then...
Options = swTableRowColChange_TableSizeCanChange
The rest of the columns remain the same width and are shifted away from the table anchor to make room for the changed column.
Width of the entire table must remain the same, so that the table continues to fit properly on the drawing
Other columns must absorb the change in width. There are two possibilities supported by this method.
If Options = swTableRowColChange_AbsorbedByNext, then the first column to the right of the columns whose width has changed, is adjusted if possible. If that is not possible, then the first column to the left of the columns whose width has changed, is adjusted if possible. If that is not possible either, then no action is taken.
The other similar case is if Options = swTableRowColChange_AbsorbedByPrevious. First the column to the left is tried, then the column to the right.
Options = swTableRowColChange_AbsorbedByNext or swTableRowColChange_AbsorbedByPrevious
It may not be possible to get the desired results. If this is the case, you must determine the full width of the table yourself and set row widths individually using the swTableRowColChange_TableSizeCanChange option, making sure to end up with the original table width. The return value is the width that the column is set to. If you specified a range of columns, it is the width of the first column of that range. It is possible that the return value is different than the width value that you passed in. One possibility is that if you specify a column width that is less than the minimum column width, the minimum column width is used, instead of what you specified. Another possibility is that if you are trying to maintain a fixed table width, but the width of the adjacent columns is not big enough to absorb the width changes to the columns that you specified, then the return value is the same as the column's original width instead of what you specified. To get the column width, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.GetColumnWidth">ITableAnnotation::GetColumnWidth</see>. To get or set the row height, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.GetRowHeight">ITableAnnotation::GetRowHeight</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation.SetRowHeight">ITableAnnotation::SetRowHeight</see>.

Member.Name: SetHeader
Member.Description: Sets the header for this table.

Parameter.Name: Style
Parameter.Description: Header style as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swTableHeaderPosition_e">swTableHeaderPosition_e</see>

Parameter.Name: Count
Parameter.Description: Number of lines in the header

Member.Returns: True if header is set successfully, false if not
Member.Remarks:
Tables created internally by the SOLIDWORKS Design software, such as Hole Charts, Revision Blocks, and BOM tables, are created with a specific number of headers lines. This method cannot:
Change the number of lines in the header for these tables; thus, the Count argument is ignored. Turn off the header in these types of tables; thus, this method has no effect, and FALSE is returned. Essentially, the only thing this method can do with these types of tables is to change the header between the top and the bottom. If you are changing the header style and number of header lines in a single use of this method, the number of lines is considered before changing the header style. For example, if you are changing a table that had 1 header line at the top, by calling SetHeader (swTableHeader_Bottom, 3), the first 3 lines in the table are moved to the bottom of the table.

Member.Name: AddCustomButton2
Member.Description: Adds a custom button to the Task Pane.

Parameter.Name: ImageList
Parameter.Description: Array of strings for the paths for the image files for the custom button (see Remarks)

Parameter.Name: ToolTip
Parameter.Description: ToolTip for the custom button

Member.Returns: True if the custom button is added to the Task Pane, false if not
Member.Remarks:
This method supports scaling for high resolution screens with high resolution operating system scaling options. ImageList images can be:
20 x 20 pixels 32 x 32 pixels 40 x 40 pixels 64 x 64 pixels 96 x 96 pixels 128 x128 pixels The images should use 256-color palette. The size of the custom button displayed is dictated by both the monitor's or laptop's screen resolution and SOLIDWORKS icon size. You must set the custom button size before executing a macro or application that calls this method. For example, if running Windows 7:
To set your monitor's or laptop's screen resolution:
Click Start > Control Panel > Appearance and Personalization > Display. Select a different icon size. Click Apply. Click Log off now. Log back in. Start SOLIDWORKS and open a part, assembly, or drawing. Click Tools > Customize and on the Toolbars tab, click the Icon size that matches the size that you set in step 1b and click OK two twice.

<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITessellation.NeedErrorList">ITessellation::NeedErrorList</see> After using an ITessellation function, you can return error information about any of the tessellation data. The arrays returned by ITessellation::GetErrorList contains the tessellation entity IDs that have errors:
Face error: The specified face could not be faceted.
Facet error: The specified facet is disconnected from its neighboring facets.
Vertex error: The specified vertex does not match any vertices on adjacent faces. There may be gaps between facets.
Vertex normal error: The tessellate function could not calculate an accurate vertex normal.
Vertex parameter error: The tessellate function could not calculate accurate vertex parameters.

Member.Signature: GetSystemTextureName( System.string FileNameIn, out System.bool Res )
Member.Description: Gets the name of the texture that appears in the Texture PropertyManager.

Parameter.Name: FileNameIn

Parameter.Name: Res
Parameter.Description: True if the name of the texture that appears in the Texture PropertyManager is returned, false if not

Member.Returns: Name of texture as it appears in the Texture PropertyManager (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method only supports SOLIDWORKS-supplied textures.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITexture.MaterialName">ITexture::MaterialName</see> to get the value for FileNameIn before calling this method. ITexture::MaterialName returns an abbreviated path and the name of the texture as it appears in the Texture PropertyManager. For example, if ITexture::MaterialName returns install_dir\data\images\textures\plastic\brushed\bred.jpg, then this method returns Plastic\Brushed\Red.

Member.Remarks:
If the texture is a SOLIDWORKS-supplied texture, then the path returned is:
install_dir\data\Images\textures\texture_library\texture_type\texture_image_file
For example, install_dir\data\Images\textures\plastic\brushed\bred.jpg.
If the texture is user-defined texture, then the path returned is:
drive:\path_name\texture_image_file
For example, D:\MyTextures\gear.jpg.
Call this property before calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITexture.GetSystemTextureName">ITexture::GetSystemTextureName</see> to obtain a value for FileNameIn.

Member.Description: Gains access to the selections that define this thicken feature.

Parameter.Description: Top-level document

Parameter.Description: Component to which this feature is to be applied

Member.Returns: True if access is successful, false if not
Member.Remarks:
To modify a feature in a... Then...
Part
TopDoc argument is the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">IModelDoc2</see> for the part Component argument is NULL
Assembly

Member.Name: GetArcs4
Member.Description: Gets all of the information for all of the arcs added by a user in this drawing view.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
This method only returns arcs that were sketched by a user in a drawing view. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetPolylines6">IView::GetPolylines6</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetPolylines6">IView::IGetPolylines6</see> to access the solid model's projected display data in the drawing view. Return value is an array of doubles with the format: [ Color, LineType, LineStyleIndex, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, StartPt[3], EndPt[3], CenterPt[3], RotDir, ... ] where:
Color - COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value could be 0 or -1 for default color.
LineType - Line type. Valid returns as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see>. A LineType is a combination of a line style and line weight.
LineStyleIndex - Line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineStyles_e">swLineStyles_e</see> enumeration.
LineWidth - Integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>.
LayerID - Integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. The <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> object can be obtained by passing this integer value to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::GetLayerById</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerById">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerById</see>.
LayerOverride - Integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the Layer default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride was returned as 3, the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer.
StartPt[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the start point.
EndPt[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the end point. If the arc is closed, then EndPt[3] is the same point as the StartPt.
CenterPt[3] - An array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the center point.
RotDir - Rotational direction (CW = -1, CCW = 1) ... This set of data repeats for each arc in the view. The size of the array is (NumArcs * 16). To determine the number of arcs, use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetArcCount">IView::GetArcCount</see>. The data returned from this method is in terms of view space. If you want the data in terms of sheet space (for example, the 0,0 origin being the lower-left corner of the sheet), then you should combine this data with the three return values from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetXform">IView::GetXForm</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetViewXform">IView::IGetXForm</see>. The sheet must be visible. See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISheet.SheetFormatVisible">ISheet::SheetFormatVisible</see>.

If the break line style is swBreakLineStyle_e...
Then [ break line data ] is packed with...
swBreakLine_Straight
12 doubles (2 lines * 1 segment * 2 points * 3 coordinates)
swBreakLine_ZigZag
60 doubles (2 lines * 5 segments * 2 points * 3 coordinates)

One difference between this method and the now obsolete <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetCenterMarkCount">IView::GetCenterMarkCount</see> is that this method also works if this view represents the drawing sheet. The original method always returns 0 if this view is the drawing sheet. Call this method before calling <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetCenterMarks">IView::IGetCenterMarks</see> to get the size of the array for that method.

Member.Name: GetCenterMarkInfo
Member.Description: Gets information about each center mark that is a feature in the view.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks: Center marks are now annotations. Previously, center marks were features. This method is only valid for center marks that are features. The return value is the following array of doubles: [ numCenterMarks, [ numCenterMarkLines, lineType1, plus1StartPt[3], plus1EndPt[3], lineType2, plus2StartPt[3], plus2EndPt[3], [ lineType, lineStartPt[3], lineEndPt[3] ] ] ] where: numCenterMarks = is the number of center marks in this view. See also <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetCenterMarkCount2">IView::GetCenterMarkCount2</see>. The following set of data repeats itself for each center mark in the view. The number of times the information is given is numCenterMarks: numCenterMarkLines = number of centermark lines in the current center mark. Every center mark has at least two lines. These two lines represent the plus at the center of the circle. lineType1 = line type associated with the first plus-sign line. See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see> enumeration. plus1StartPt[3] = X,Y,Z start point of the first line in the plus sign. plus1EndPt[3] = X,Y,Z end point of the first line in the plus sign. lineType2 = line type associated with the second plus-sign line. See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see> enumeration. plus2StartPt[3] = X,Y,Z start point of the second line in the plus sign. plus2EndPt[3] = X,Y,Z end point of the second line in the plus sign. This set of data also repeats itself for the remaining centermark lines in this particular center mark. The number of times this information is given is (numCenterMarkLines - 2): LineType = line type associated with the second plus-sign line. See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineTypes_e</see> enumeration. lineStartPt[3] = X,Y,Z start point for this centermark line. lineEndPt[3] = X,Y,Z end point for this centermark line.

Member.Name: GetDatumPoints2
Member.Description: Gets all of the information about all the datum points in this view.
Member.Returns: Array of doubles (see Remarks)
Member.Remarks:
Return value is an array of doubles with the format:
[ Color, LineStyleIndex, LineWidth, LayerID, LayerOverride, ptLoc[3] ... ] Color = COLORREF returned as an integer. Return value can be 0 or -1 for default color. LineStyleIndex = line style. Valid line styles as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineTypes_e">swLineStyles_e</see>. LineWidth = integer value defining the line width. Valid width values as defined in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swLineWeights_e">swLineWeights_e</see>. LayerID = integer value indicating which layer holds this entity. This integer value is the array index value into the layerList array. The layerList array can be obtained using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.GetLayerList">ILayerMgr::GetLayerList</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayerMgr.IGetLayerList">ILayerMgr::IGetLayerList</see>. A value of 1 indicates that this item is not on a layer. LayerOverride = integer with bit flags set to determine which properties, if any, have been overridden with respect to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILayer">ILayer</see> default properties. If the bit value is set, then the specific property or properties have been overridden. The bit indicators are: color = 0x1, style = 0x2, and width = 0x4. Therefore, if LayerOverride is returned as 3, you know the color and style have been specifically set for this item and may not match the default values associated with this item's layer. ptLoc[3] = array of 3 doubles (X,Y,Z) describing the point location ... This entire set of data repeats for each datum point in the view. The size of the array is (NumPts * 8). To determine the number of points,use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetDatumPointsCount">IView::GetDatumPointsCount</see>. The data returned from this method is in terms of view space. If you want the data in terms of sheet space (for example, the 0,0 origin being the lower-left corner of the sheet), then combine this data with the three return values from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetXform">IView::GetXForm</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.IGetXform">IView::IGetXForm</see>.
